RUST SURVIVAL GUIDE:
1. Stick to the BUSHES as a naked, because you'll soon realize that everyone is out to get you.
2. once you have a SPEAR or BOW try to find another naked or low gear play who doesn't KOS.
3. form a simple alliance of peace and trading.
4. start a simple, non-ambitious base.
5. get a code lock, sheet metal door, upgrade base to stone, and maybe an airlock (second set of doors)
6. craft better armor, weapons such as crossbows, waterpipe shotguns, and wood armor.
7. Farm for hours, animals, for animal fat to make a furnace. wood to keep your base and furnaces going. ores for constant production of materials. (gunpowder, bullets, better tools, weapons, etc...)
8. scan your area, don't KOS un less they do first, try to find allies. make sure to find out where your enemies live to be cautious in that area.
9. when you notice people have better gear than you start to gather scrap. hit barrels, boxes, ammo crates. anything you dont need, go to your local rad-town and recycle it for scrap. then craft a research table and use your scrap to research items you want to be able to craft.
10. if you have any friends, get them to play with you, because playing solo makes people want to die, it's so hard.
11. by this point you will probably have enemies.
12. they might try to raid you if they have better gear, be WARNED!
13. if your still alive, try to figure out when wipe is. (when the server wipes and everyone resets)
14. REPEAT 1-13.

SMITE had potential, but because Hi-Rez has given up innovating SMITE, it is pretty stuck where it is.
The game lacks any type of balancing or "rubberbanding" mechanics. There are only a handful of competitive gods and if someone on your team starts to lag behind in level, you might as well count them as dead because level differentiation will always outway skill. Once 1 or two players on one team start to pull just a little ahead of the others, it's game over.
The game also lacks a lot of things MOBAs have evolved to include. Like mounts or fast movement out of combat. Hope you enjoy slowly walking long distances because there is a lot of that in SMITE. Which you'll be doing a lot of because the game uses the outdated mana system. With mana regenning extremely slowly, you need to take a break from the fun part of the game and port back to the start. After you're done waiting (because that's always fun) you'll need to slowly make your way through the map toward the front line.
There are only 5 maps and 2 game modes. There's the standard deathmatch map, and 4 maps that vary on "Kill the objective at the end of the lane". This gets VERY boring after awhile.
SMITE is a MOBA that uses all of the old rules and didn't try to innovate or change anything. There are currently MUCH better and more modern options out on the market.

=== FIRST, A WARNING===
As has been stated by many reviewers here already, if you play with a keyboard and mouse either get an Xbox Controller for PC (or if you have an Xbox you can order a PC USB adapter thingy and then you can just use that control for your PC.) I won't go into why you need this controller simply because everything that needs and can be said about that has already been stated here.
Also, if you get frustrated easily or have anger issues, then I don't reccomend a Souls game at all. Why are you even looking here?
===THE REVIEW===
Apart from the current issue with the KB+M this game is amazing both visualy and from a player point of view. When you start off you feel like its just the first one over again and that you've wasted some money on another bad PC Souls port. This is true to an extent. The overall feel of the game is very similar to the original Dark Souls, however it's a welcome return to that universe. From the little I've played I see that the story feels slightly stronger (that is to say: it exsists) in this over DS I, and that the NPC's nearer the begining are stronger in character and marginally better in helpfulness. The look of this game is amazing. In the first hour of me playing, I've already had my breath-taken away numerous times and been forced to do something which I rarely do - take screeshots of the game. Since I am a PC Gamer, I have neither console to compare the look to, but if you search on the internet I'm sure you can find some comparing shots.

Astroneer suffers from a pretty fundamental problem: I am encouraged to spend my time and resources to create a base from which the ultimate reward is to build a basic spaceship and leave. The only tangible benefit to leaving the starting planet and journeying to a new planet, is the opportunity to start the entire process over again. That is it.. There is no gameplay beyond that. There is no AI interaction (beyond some static enemy plants that are no challenge), no strategic challenges to the player beyond finding a resource, and once you have basic power and oxygen generation, no real risk behind any decision the player makes.
The development roadmap does allude to future content updates, but even then it is very hard to envisage changes to affect the game which could mitigate the extremely shallow gameplay.
Unlike games like Elite Dangerous or Star Citizen which afford decent scope for challenging exploration and navigation; Astroneer does not provide: customisable or upgradeable space ships, distinct nodes to travel to beyond different colored planets, any combat or real basis for interplanetary travel (the only reason to even use a spaceship is just to get to the nearest planet). There is no reason to hang around in space, you are simply driving from point A to B with limited fuel.
As for base-building, the only objective of the game, Astroneer compares pretty poorly to other games with a similar focus. The most crippling shortcoming to Astroneer is the lack of any and all automation. If you need resource x, you have to go find resource x. Once you have it you have to manually provide to the relevant part of the manufacturing cycle. Factorio and Minecraft, two games which create arguably the best base building and production management gameplay, provide a strong incentive to progress with base development. Not only does each development stage provide a tangible reward and chance to further relieve the player of the laborious task of obtaining resources, but both games provide extreme customization and personalization, so that the player becomes personally invested in mainting and creating better and better bases. Base building in Astroneer is aimed at only a handful of objectives: oxygen (to keep the player alive), transport (a rover/truck to reach more remote resources, and a spaceship to leave the planet), and power (which keeps the base/rover running). There is no personalization to speak of, and therefore absolutely no reason to build any but a handful of base buildings. There is a decent level of detail in the sandbox nature of the planets; sculpting the landscape can be a relatively rewarding diversion from the mundane task of retrieving distant resources; but it is only a brief respite. But again that is it. No AI to really speak of, so no challenge, and no risk of finding anything of note on the planets other than a small number of distinct resources and some randomly generated terrain.
On a more personal level, I am not entirely sure that this game has got much more time left to keep attracting new users. At time of writing the devs have conceded that many of the game's owners are frustrated at the rate at which new gameplay content is being patched in. While they do provide a 'roadmap' of new content, it is unfortunate that this came some time after an update post which excitedly promised a chance for owners to buy merchandise related to the game. Whilst this certainly isn't unethical, it might not have been so prudent to push that notice out to people who had already bought in to the alpha. As far as publicity on Steam goes this game is 'out'. People can buy it and play it and then move on. Hopefully this doesn't begin to create financial pressure on the dev team to suddenly release the game as is.
Final summary: Astroneer is competent (in that the game runs and is stable), but man is it boring.

I really didn't want to spend any money in fear of getting stuck with some crap indie game that some developer thought was amazing while making and didn't hold back on letting you know in the script. So when I found a game called, No More Room in Hell, I thought to myself,"This might be fun." Well, now I know what boring really is.
It might be free, but the novelty wears off pretty fast. The few character you have to choose from are charming and the gameplay runs like every other Half~Life Mod. There really isn't much to cover here since the game is very shallow and really only consists of killing zombies while stocking up on weapons.
The levels are very clustered and ugly. At first glace the game seems just like every other shooter based around the idea of keeping your character alive during wave after wave of the undead. The reason the game looks like that is because that is all there is to it. You never really feel like anything is ever going anywhere.
The entire game feels like one boring, neverending game of kill stupid zombies that come from the same places over and over again. It brings nothing new out of an already tired idea. I do understand this is a free game and you get what you want out of it. I for one do not have the time to just blast away at something for no real reason.
It is not the worst thing out there and with that in mind you might get an hour out of it or more. Despite the fact that I did not enjoy it, should not by any means stop you from trying it. I would just like to think that if you are reading reviews that are negative that you might want to save some time by not putting anymore into this.

There is, I must admit, a niche for games that are harder than hard. A game which is not gentle, that does not have a learning cure so much as a learning cliff. A game which shows nothing but brutality to it's players. This game is a labour of love, with many, many hours obviously put into it to make as best a game as the developers could. They knew what they were going for, a semi-realistic zombie apocalypse that shows no mercy and they went for it.
Of course, this introduces problems.
Let's start with the learning curve. As mentioned before, this game has not so much a learning curve as a learning cliff, so you might expect a short moment on how to explain game mechanics, or at least, hints and tips while the game loads for you? Reasonable to expect, isn't it? Well, no. You don't get that at all. There is no kindness, no compassion, no one or nothing to give you a holding hand; this game chucks you in the deep end, then expects you to know breast stroke. Now other games have done this, Dark Souls being the most infamous, but Dark Souls took a moment to explain what was going on. It told you how to raise your shield, explained how to equip, and how to use the bonfies. No such luck here. You're in a bulding that is secure, and the moment you walk out that door, zombies. Lots and lots of zombies.
Now having one or two zombies at first to get used to them, to know how to deal with them, again, would be standard fare. Nothing wrong with being exposed to a new enemy type slowly, to let you understand and get used to. Not so with this game, oh no. Try a few dozen. And you don't know what to do beyond kill. You might have a few weapons, but they float through the air, seemingly not connecting to anything, which means that you have to spend a few swings getting used to weapons. And in a game this lethal and unforgiving, those few practice swings will cost you dearly. And you will die.
Now one mechaninc that you might know is that being grabbed can only be resolved by pushing (which is V by default). What you may not know is that zombies can grab through wire fences and windows (wether or not this is a bug is something else entirely) and if that happens, you are beyond all hope. Another thing that you might guess that being grabbed and then bitten is bad, and it is, but being bitten is not well shown. Beyond the zombie jerking a bit, you may not even know you've been bitten until you begin to show the signs. And if you are bitten, death is inevitable. You have two minutes. Spend them well by either finding pills to buy you more time (no cure here), jump off a ledge, or simply beg someone to kill you.
Now the inventory may take some getting used to. You have two inventory wheels, one for ammo, one for weapons. The bigger, bulkier, and heavier something is, the more space it takes, and you don't have many pockets. So of course you need to manage inventory space, which is perfectly fine, this is a horror survival game after all. Nothing wrong with that. In fact, I applaud it. I don't want to be carrying two rifles, three pistols, and a big ♥♥♥ sledge hammer. I'm not a ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ space marine here, and this isn't the game for them. Ammo is counted in weight and mass as well, which makes sense.
And, of course, the zombies. Oh, the Zombies. These are standard Romero-Zombies. Undead who feel no pain, fear, or emotion and operate entirely on instinct. Woth noting, hwoever, that the eyesight of a zombie is perfect. I'm not kidding; they have perfect, near 360 degree awareness of everything that not even you or I should be able to see. Two stories directly overhead? They can see you. Small dot on the horizon in a darkened room? They know you're there. Pitch blackness? Sure as ♥♥♥♥ they know you're there.
And while this does make for a fun and entertaining horror game, there is one more flaw. Multiplayer. Now, I know what you're saying: But Left 4 Dead and Payday did it perfectly! How can this be possible!? Well here's why. For starters, Valve knew that players can't communicate well with strangers on the other side of the world. They knew that coordination was next to impossible. They knew that players naturally deviate from each other at all times. So how did they solve this? Simple. You always knew, at a glance, how your fellow players were doing, and where they were. They had glowing outlines that showed at any distance, and maps were linear to prevent fanning out by players. Maps in valves games were funnels, and even Overkill understood this by making the map around easy to navigate and open buldings made as simplistic as possible.
Multiplayer is a mess. Players do not communicate well with others over large distances. Most players don't even have microphones, so that idea with walkie talkies where players far away can't talk without them? A waste of time since text speech does not work with walkie talkies, so you must be right next to them to work. Maps are cramped, narrow things that while linear, often curve in on themselves and encourage exporation. Again, not a problem, except that players naturally do not drift together, they drift apart because they have no sense of surroundings at the best of times and are given no way to drift back together.
This game strikes me as a single player game trying to do the work of multiplayer. It just can't work. It doesn't work. Bad bugs (or bad mechanics, that's unclear), an extreme difficulty curve beyond any sane resembelance and poor combat mechanics and jerky, overwhelming numbers of undead at all times mean that players will only have an experience of death, more death, and of course death, all without any real progression. This game isn't just hard, it's near unplayable through it's obscene diffculty spikes and poorly designed multiplayer maps.
This is not to say that it's bad, but it is very much a niche game. If you don't want to play this sort of game, skip it over, but I reccomend playing this game just for the experience.

*Please note that this review is for early access. This game is VERY early in development, but is off to an excellent start*
Slime Rancher is a really laid-back, casual sort of game. The entire objective is to simply play it how you want. Slimes are obviously the focal point of the game; but there are many different kinds of slimes including combinations, and it's up to you to choose which slimes you want to keep around your ranch.
Gameplay: 9/10
The gameplay is very smooth and easy to get used to. At first the mouth scroll speed is extremely high, but turning that down under the settings quickly fixes that. Movement is quick and flows like liquid. The main tool is easy to use and very responsive. There are virtually NO bugs as far as I can see, just some clipping issues when attempting to run into a wall. You occasionally get stuck for a few seconds.
Graphics: 9/10
The graphics are good for the style. It's obviously not realistic looking, but everything is very well polished and there is a good bit of detail added in.
Storyline: N/A
Currently, there is no storyline.
Replayability: 7/10
The game isn't yet finished, so there really isn't any way to beat it. You do have the options of changing up which slimes you'd like to interact with simply by capturing them though. Easy.
Difficulty: Very easy
The only times I actually died are via falling off the cliff into the ocean. Yes, this game does have multiple dangers to keep you on your toes, but they are practically harmless. Even without upgrading my health at all, I've only taken 3/4ths of my total hp in damage. If anything, I think the game could benefit from a higher difficulty or at the very least, several difficulty options.
Estimated Playtime: >10 hours.
As it is currently, this game is short and to the point. It throws you out there and expects you to learn on your own (for the most part). I've spent about 5 hours in so far and I believe I am coming to the end of the game as it stands right now.
Final comments: This isn't a game for those who want constant action. If you like casual games that include farming and caring for various entities, this is the game for you. I look forward to more updates, new areas to explore, and especially more slimes!

That, however, is where the good ends. Technical problems plague the launch of this game, some of the them egregious enough to warrant suspicion that they cannot have happened in good faith. Why, why, why would you make a competitive FPS run on p2p servers in 2014? It's just illogical. When you add the fact that they confirmed that the game would run on dedicated servers pre-launch, it becomes disrespectful. As anyone could have predicted, using p2p servers combined with grotesque lag compensation designed to falsely level the playing field has left many people so frustrated that they have LEFT THE GAME until dedicated servers make their way to AW.
On AMD cards, you can expect (with a reasonable degree of likelihood) slowdown on certain large maps. Slowdown that, if you meet (or exceed) the recommended systems specs, simply should not happen. Mouse problems exists too--it took me quite some time to figure out a set -up that worked for me. Expect to do the same. These kind of optimization issues exist often on ports of console games that simply don't have enough care put into them. The logic, the only possible logic, is this: "PC isn't a big enough market, therefore no matter how longly and loudly they complain, we will remain essentially aloof from it". The irony is that the PC launch of AC: unity makes AW look positively saintly in comparison.
Therefore, I can sum up by saying that, firstly, this is a terrific game and anyone who has the proper system and is interested in competitive shooters should get this. It is truly, honestly, a good game; something I didn't think I'd ever say again in the COD franchise. Ghosts was one of the worst games I ever played. The more this community grows, the better this game will become. Who knows, maybe in time it will become a seriously competitive game on PC like CS:GO is, although there will be many who scream at the thought.
There are technical errors, as mentioned, and even worse than mentioned, but if those don't phase you, you will find an amazing game that gets better and better the more people that play it!

I thought Questerium would be a fairly standard Hidden Object/Puzzle game from Eastern Europe. That meant there would be some translation/dialogue problems, a story that would require magic mushrooms to comprehend, and a fair amount of random clicking to find the single, off-center pixel required to make two objects interact. What I did not expect was that the game would be an intentional?/unintentional? journey into full-motion-video game camp.
It all started when that guy on the cover art, the guy with electricity coming out of his eyes, used his awesome god-like powers to perform one of the most over-the-top pantomimes ever shot for a video game. Imagine Emperor Palpatine using force lightning to toast a waffle and you will come close to the utter pointlessness of his act.
Later, the bald-headed guy in the video advert leans out of a cartoon window and engages in a moment of villany that is more commonly associated with moustache-twirling, a top hat, and a black cape. Snidely Whiplash should sue this guy for stealing his act.
And there are plenty more moments with these two that left me howling at how "tragically ludicrous" the whole thing was. If it was intentional camp, then bravo! If this was not intentional camp, it only makes it even funnier. I recommend the game based on how much enjoyment I got laughing at the full motion video.

The game's full title is
but let's refer to it as
for short.
is a Hidden Objects Game (HOG) combined with Full Motion Video (FMV). It's not the best HOG I have played but it is worth playing. The puzzles are fun and even though (or maybe: because?) the acting is cheesy, the FMV really adds something special to this game.
A meteor has struck near a town. It's emanating an unearthly energy and the resident scientist, Dr. Gustav, starts experimenting with it. Something must have gone wrong, as the meteor's energy has suddenly manifested itself as a huge but inert whirlwind just outside of the town, causing the townsfolk to flee in chaos. Two children are unaccounted for. You play an investigator who's asked to go look for the children in the abandoned town.
The story is rather thin. Dialogue is scarce. You do learn some background stories about the main characters by reading journals, newspaper articles and other texts you find while exploring the town. All in all, the narrative is enough to keep a HOG going but not much else. This is one of the many HOG that relies on a lot of puzzling and just a basic story to keep the player interested.
At the start of the game, you select a difficulty to determine the challenge
will offer. You can adjust the difficulty at any time while playing.
At the easiest difficulty, you occasionally see a small sparkle on all the objects you can interact with. The hardest difficulty mode is meant for people who want to click on everything to check if it does anything, and who don't mind resorting to some pixel hunting. The difficulty modes in between don't have the sparkles but you can use a hint button to lead you to the next object to interact with, if you're stuck.
The hidden object puzzles in
are what I'd like to call 'the advanced type', meaning you don't just need to look for items hidden in a scene and click on them, but you also need to combine items and use some items on other items to find hidden objects. It's a small step up from the basic hidden object puzzles seen in some other HOG, but a step up nonetheless, making the hidden object puzzles a bit more challenging and interesting.
The other puzzles are varied enough. There are some classic puzzles and there are some original ones. The difficulty of the puzzles is never too high to be frustrating, but overall they are challenging and most importantly, they're fun to tackle.
Optionally, there's some collecting to do while playing the game. In
, you can collect money and plants. The plants are easy to spot but the money is hidden very well. Spots where there is nothing but hidden money don't even 'sparkle' on the easiest difficulty mode, so you either need to click around a lot or keep one eye on a guide.
At any time, you can click a button to travel to your own personal place in the world of
. There you can use the money you've gathered to buy fountains and trees to make your garden look more impressive. The small building leading to your garden contains a book that keeps track of the plants you've collected. The rest of the room automatically gets filled up with all sorts of decorations while you complete achievements in
. All this is completely optional and not relevant to the game at all, but it's there for people who like trophy rooms like that, and it's a fun addition to check out once in a while if you're an achievement hunter.

The graphics are as good as you'd expect from a decent HOG. In the case of
, of course, it's the FMV that makes the game look special and different from other HOG. Graphically, the FMV looks great. The FMV is used only for the four characters you meet in the game, though, so it's only a small part of the whole game.
The acting is very cheesy. This is a word us FMV afficionados use to avoid calling the acting terrible. But we use the word affectionately. The quality of FMV acting has known extreme highs and lows over the last 25 years, but the appeal of FMV is that when the acting is ok, the FMV is called great, and when the acting is bad, it's called typical charming FMV. Or indeed, called 'cheesy'. The fact is, the FMV in
adds a lot of atmosphere. And after playing
I have to say it baffles me that this is the first HOG with FMV I've ever seen, because FMV goes really, really well with the HOG genre. I hope to see more of that combination, although preferably with a slightly higher standard of acting, if at all possible.
The music and sound effects of
are fitting, atmospheric and clearly of high quality.
has 5 Steam Trading Cards. You'll get 3 while running the game.
The 23 Steam Achievements, which are also tracked ingame, consist of story-related achievements, puzzle-related achievements (for solving them without skipping or using hints) and collection-related achievements (for collecting all the plants, finding all the money and buying decorations for your garden).

The terrible FMV just adds to this cheesy game. Occasionally it fails to register a click or has an inconveniently small hotspot, but that aside, it seems to be bug free for me. Puzzles are quite original and the HOG scenes are well themed, with fewer random junk heaps than most games. The story makes very little sense, so a typical HOG in that respect. Anyhoo, I had 6.8 hours of fun and consider this thing a bargain.

Cons:
- The acting. Oh, man. Now I'm a big fan of the HO genre, and am used to mediocre acting, but this was a whole new level of bad. Someone decided that this game needed live action characters, but then apparently didn't know where to find people who know how to act, or people who know how to animate the live action bits into the scenes. It would have been so much better with more standard characters. The voice acting wasn't bad, but the movement... seriously. If this were a comedy game, maybe I'd think they're trying to be ironic, but it's too serious for acting this bad.
- Some of the puzzles are not well explained. I had to skip a couple of them because I couldn't figure out what to do and the instructions were useless.
- A few very slow and frustrating animations. For example, there's a pyramid minigame, which is simple and shouldn't take a long time to solve, but the animation for moving the blocks... it makes you click on the one you want to move, the arm moves over, picks it up, and you nca't click destination until that's done. It gets frustrating really fast.
- Unlike every other collector's edition game I've played, this one doesn't have a strategy guide.
But, despite the painfulness of sitting through the cutscenes, I did have fun playing it. So, get it on sale, it's a decent way to spend a few hours.
Edit:
I've played the bonus chapter. The map and hint are broken, in that they always point to the very first task, but it's still playable, you just won't have the help of hint and map.
Amateurish, clunky game. Some decent graphics and scenes are ruined by game play and 'acting'. Bonus chapter is very buggy and appears to be unfinishable due to bugs.
Well worth the price.

Phil Ochs songs helped to end Bloody wars
By: Cole Shrader
Phil Ochs was a small time American songwriter who lived from 1940 to 1976 and who wrote songs and participated in rallies that protested against the cruelties of the vietnam war that the USA was participating in. Phil made several songs including “I Ain’t Marchin’ Anymore” in which he spoke out against not only the war in Vietnam, but in the idea of war in general. This songs motive of protest is pretty obvious, as most of its lines like, “I ain't marchin anymore” the most repeated line in the song, are directly stating that he was opposed to war by saying he wont march to war or follow any orders. I believe that the songs made by Phil in connection with peaceful protests and other songs by many other artists helped convince the United States government to stop their direct involvement in the vietnam war.
First of all, these songs Showed more and more people the atrocities of the Vietnam war and slowly managed to pull public support from the american government and helped make more people join in on protests and peaceful rallies. By doing this the american population gave corporations the problem that if they supported the vietnam war with arms,supplies, or funds, their public image would be ruined, people would no longer buy their products and investors would no longer give them funds. The US army spent 168 billion dollars to fund the Vietnam war, boycotts of factories and corporations funding the military and of the government itself substantially decreased the amount of time the war could go on without the USA losing so much money that their country went into a economical depression again.
Additionally, the coverage of the failures and horrors of the war by this song and many others reduced public approval of the military efforts the US government. Many parts of songs drew emphasis to the problems of war and questioned there means to gain their goal of ridding the world of communism. The chorus of “I Ain’t Marchin’ Anymore” is: It's always the old to lead us to the war It's always the young to fall Now look at all we've won with the saber and the gun Tell me is it worth it all”. In this section of the song there are several parts worth mentioning that might have swayed the public opinion. Primarily the line “Now look at all we've won with the saber and the gun Tell me is it worth it all” questions the audience whether or not any fighting or war is worth it if we gain so little and this works especially well with the war that was going on at the time as the US wasn't defending its own land and it wasn't attacking someone else so there was no real end game benefits for the country besides the prevention of communism. Secondly the line “It's always the old to lead us to the war It's always the young to fall” is in reference to how the older government started the war but it was primarily 19 year olds who died during the Vietnam war.

In conclusion, the song “I Ain’t Marchin’ Anymore definitely helped end the cold war in a small but effective way. And though many people say that the vietnam war was ended because of other factors, which i admit to a point, the US had ample military strength and technologie but was held back by its own people who opposed this war because of songs like “I ain’t Marchin’ anymore”. Thank you for reading this, and i hope that in some way i have informed you on the strength of songs in changing the world.

I Giochini consolosi di botte dei Cavalieri dello Zodiaco ci girano tra le palle dal 2005 quando uscì per PS2 Saint Seiya The Sanctuary, almeno i giochi di questo stampo... in realtà c'è anche un mare di robaccia per cellulari, un gioco a quiz per pc, merdate per le console retrò ecc...
Diciamo il gioco dei Cavalieri picchiaduro 3D post 2000 così come lo concepiamo adesso ebbe la sua prima epifania in quel periodo con quel titolo.
E da fan sborsai subito i soldi per acquistarlo ritrovarmi tra le mani... una merdata colossale. Però era bello. Era strabello poter sparare i colpi finali sul muso dei cavalieri d'oro, rivivere la storia, fare le mosse. Era una figata.
Il tempo passa e esce Hades nel 2006 che è identico a quello del 2005 ma con personaggi nuovi, e poi? Il silenzio. Quanto tempo passato a sperare che la Bandai sfornasse un giochino dei cavalieri decente, un piacchiaduro decente magari simile ai Dragonball Budokai Tenkaichi che non erano nulla di eclatante ma che almeno funzionavano. Non chiedevo tanto. Almeno la decenza di avere un sistema di movimento soddisfacente e una grafica che non sembrasse una vomitata su un cadavere.
Escono in sequenza 2 titoli per PS3 che ho saltato a piè pari e poi Soldiers' Soul, che pochi giorni fa è vittima di uno sconto gargantuesco e che quindi finisce al volo nella mia libreria Steam.
12 euro? Una pizza farcita e acqua minerale al ristorante in centro, se fa schifo non ci ho rimesso molto.
Lo scarichi, installi, lo fai partire e ti ricordi di 11 anni fa. Ricordi come mai giocavi ai giochini dei Cavalieri della PS2, delle cagate enormi, e ricordi anche come mai giocandoci piangevi in preda al terrore e alla rabbia. Il pianto di un fan distrutto: "perché fallire tremendamente un gioco con un tema così facile? Come è possibile?"
Questo effetto amarcord è stato devastante ma mi ha fatto realizzare che forse dopo 11 anni sono riusciti a tirare fuori dal cilindro il primo gioco di Saint Seiya decente correggendo 11 anni di disastri indigeribili e mazzate nello stomaco al povero fan ignaro.
Soldiers' Soul corregge i 3 errori più osceni e imperdonabili degli altri titoli (almeno quelli che ho giocato io):
1) Pochi personaggi in un brand che ha tipo 500.000 personaggi.
2) Gameplay mortale, lento macchinoso non funzionale.
3) Grafica oscena anche per il periodo.
La prima cosa che mi gasa di questo titolo è che finalmente ci hanno messo la gente dentro! Ci sono più di 50 personaggi, molti dei quali unici come i cavalieri di nettuno o quei debosciati anni 80 degli asgardiani. Hanno capito che va sfruttato tutto Saint Seiya e non a pezzi e bocconi, che te ne frega se li fai tutti identici, tanto basta dargli un colpo figo da lanciare e delle combo sceniche e ci sei. Diciamocela tutta ma chi ha preso questo titolo non lo ha fatto per il gameplay o perché sicuro di trovare un picchiaduro tattico, si sa perché si compra una cosa del genere: Vuoi vedere la gente assurda che si spara le stronzate sul muso.
E qui ci sono 48 imbecilli che smanaccano strillano e ballettano e poi: BIGUUU TUORNEDOOOO
E ti basta. Vuoi la gente e vuoi le mosse fighe. Punto. Qui ci sono.
Sempre rimandendo in tema di mosse quanto sono belle? La esegui e lo schermo vira verso una colorazione e una luminosità da tubo catodico fine anni '90, i personaggi si vestono di texture disegnata in stile Anime, quello originale, e BEM. Una veloce e scenica cinematica per farti sentire la potenza del colpo. Bello.
Il Gameplay stavolta è solido, veloce, facile da imparare. Forse offre troppe poche scelte tattiche e la sua semplicità lo rende un po' ripetitivo, comunque funziona bene e supporta perfettamente le fantasiosissime combo dei personaggi che eseguono tutti colpi unici e personali.
Grafica mediocrissima negli scenari ma ottima sul modelli dei personaggi, con eccezione delle armature divine dei cavalieri d'oro che sono pacchiani ingombranti di cattivo gusto e con delle textures allungate e strecciate da far schifo. Inguardabili.
Il gioco ci offre anche un single player longevo con un sacco di modalità e obiettivi da compiere, ha l'ovvio multiplayer, sia online che in locale e un sacco di stronzate galattiche da sbloccare e acquistare in game.
Però in tutto questo ci sono sempre delle cose che mi fanno incazzare, soprattutto se si conta che stavolta sono quasi riusciti a fare un prodotto perfetto nella sua consolosa pochezza. Bastava così poco per fare il centro perfetto... e invece:
1) Ci sono ancora i pergonaggi "nuovi" che sono gente che hai di già ma con armature differenti. Qui c'è un pasticcio evidente: Sblocchi il personaggio che in alcuni casi ha vari costumi, ma per certi costumi quel personaggio è contanto come un "nuovo" personaggio. Tipo c'è Seiya con l'armatura divina, ok è li tra i possibili vestiti per il personaggio Seiya. E poi c'è Ikki con l'armatura d'oro, e voi direte: E' un costume. No. E' UN PERSONAGGIO NUOVO! Non è vero! Decidetevi o il costume è un nuovo personaggio o nessun costume è un nuovo personaggio. Una delle due, non un mistone.
2) I menù sono disastrosi: Le modialità single player sparpagliate per 3 menù differenti, shop confuso che si naviga male con un sistema di acquisti multilpi da seggiolate nel muso, menù online con 34mila opzioni inutili. No. No. Date un senso alle cose e catalogate la roba.
3) Basta con i match online dove devi creare la stanza e aspettare la gente che si unisca, non funziona mi fa perdere tempo e nel 2016 non si pole vedè.
4) Garuda non ha il Garuda Flap. No devo continuare? GARUDA non ha il GARUDA FLAP. Boh. C'è gente come Seiya o Virgo che hanno 784 mosse differenti e Garuda, che ha 2 mosse di cui una porta il suo nome... no. E' anche una figata di colpo e comunque non ha senso non aggiungerlo. Il cavaliere della Sirena di Nettuno ha 2 mosse! Ed è un tizio a caso come poteva essere benissimo Garuda. Si ok, la presa è un mini Garuda Flap ma io volevo il colpo serio. Andate in♥♥♥♥♥♥
5) Perché si continua a non inserire dei cavalieri bellissimi? Questa volta non c'è giustificazione perché il gioco ha un mare di personaggi e certi anche deprecabili come quell'imbecille dell'unicorno o quello dalla carnagione viola... come si chiama? Ichi dell'Hydra (Hail Hydra)! Che oscenità. Dei cavalieri d'Argento nemmeno l'ombra... Lizzard, Auriga, Cerberus. So straganzi. Ci poteva essere una piccola rappresentanza. Quello della balena. No. Degli Spectre ci sono sempre i soliti 3 generali, ok, stavolta hanno messo gli dei del sonno e della morte che sono ganzissimi, bravi però... cioè... sono 108 porco cane! Se ne vedono TRE! Ci sono dei personaggi bellissimi! Sphinx Pharaoh è stupendo e potevano farci dei colpi sceneicissimi, Lune è splendido! Nulla. Nemmeno il puzzo. Un DLC... non lo so. E sono tutti personaggio con un certo peso nella trama, c'è Orfeo della Lira ma Lune no?
6) Ma certo le musiche originali dell'anime potevi inserirle, brrutto ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥o. Magari come sbloccabile!
7) L'IA fa schifo. Tre livelli di difficoltà sono troppo pochi e giocare contro il PC dopo poco diventa una stupida routine. Doveva essere più flessibile in questo aspetto, avere più livelli di difficoltà e una IA più dinamica.
Difetti superficiali è vero, ma che denotano una certa ingenuità nella creazione del gioco e che spero vengano corretti in un possibile seguito.
----------
Comunque. Alla fine una consolata senza particolari pregi ne difetti, ottimo prodotto se siamo fan del brand da cui è tratto: Si fa giocare bene è piacevole da vedere e ti catapulta nell'anime in modo perfetto. Se non si conosce o non si apprezza il brand da evitare, ci sono giochi di botte migliori in giro. Anche su Steam.

So looking at the time I spent on this game probably indicates that I'm probably addicted to this game.
Well you'd be right.
I just stumbled upon it by chance and thought, eh, why not? Seems nice.
I have no regrets.
In reality, this is a very short but lovely visual novel that can be completed in about an hour and a half, but my God you'll have so many feels for it, you'll wish it was longer (Mind you the extra unlockable content can add about another 30 minutes or so, but it's still very short nonetheless).
This is a very short and simple story of this kid named Cantus, and he's a bit of a black sheep because he likes to hang out by the ocean all the time and doesn't want to go off and play video games like any other 13-year-old. He's not exactly the fun-loving type or the talkative type either so he's not apart of a clique of friends to say the least. At first, I thought I'd hate him because he kinda seemed like a bratty loner trying to be emo. But then he slowly changes because he meets a girl named Maris. And Maris is very strange in comparison to Cantus because she is very chipper, cheerful, friendly, easy to get along with, you have no idea where she came from or why she's talking to Cantus, etc. As Cantus hangs out more with Maris, he begins to slowly be more friendly and opens up more. The two have the cutest moments and conversations due to their different personalities, which makes both characters lovable and fascinating to watch and listen to.
One thing I want to mention as well is the music. I think the whole reason why I put so much time into this visual novel is because of the music. It's so relaxing and soothing, and the tracks, while there isn't a lot of them, it's still a very good soundtrack and they all set the tone for every moment very well. The only gripe about it I can think of is that there's no transition to the music tracks, like no fade in or fade out when the tracks have to change. But that's just nit picking.
The next thing is the voice acting (Only available in the DLC). While not professional by any means, it's pretty decent. It's nothing groundbreaking but it won't urge you to stab your eardrums. One thing I will say about the voice acting is that when the characters have to be loud, the voice actors don't really shout or raise the volume that much. I understand if the visual novel is meant to be a bit quiet or subdued but there is a certain part of the game when Cantus gets very upset/fed up. When it comes time for a him to express this, he's not very loud about it. I'm not saying you need to be loud in order to vent frustration, but it would make more sense if this was the case since, given you've seen the story up to said point because it's very relatable.
I also love how every time you get a new sea shell Maris and Cantus always have something different to say about the shell you pick which then branches off into a full conversation, and it all sounds and feels so natural. Except how Maris refers to herself in the third person. I thought I would hate that she did this, but I oddly didn't mind. I mean, Maris was already kinda strange so it makes sense that she would talk weird, but she's also really cute so it didn't really matter in the end. You kinda just accept it as a normal thing.
Now I also want to say things about the art style. It's super cute and even very beautiful. I love the way these characters are drawn, and I also love how blue the sky and water always is. I especially like the last part of the game art-wise because of how the scenery changes.
Also included in the DLC is a gallery where you can unlock wallpapers to change the image of the title screen. There's also character images and small profiles, a music gallery to the soundtrack, a theatre which unlocks a 3 part little story, and 2 side stories that are both very nice to watch through. Both side stories are only about 10-20 minutes long.
This visual novel is adorable.
Other than that, Voices from the Sea is an adorable visual novel. The writing is simple and lovely, and if someone can take a simple story and take you on emotional roller coaster in 2 hours, then you're a genius. Granted there's no serious decisions nor multiple endings, but it's still a nice experience.

I thought this was a good port of the original at first, but as I continued to play the game, there were clearly some details that probably have been adressed before, but I will complain about them anyway.
- There is a scientist at the beginning of the game that is not sitting in a chair, but is standing on a chair.

- Some guards and scientist, when they get hit their hit sounds never stop. They continue to make hit sounds even after they have been hit.
- The gravity in Xen is terrible compared to the original version. I had to get better distance by grenading myself to some platforms.
- When I'm done with all of the chambers Nihilanth takes me to, he appearently stops using the attack that takes you there in the original version. However, in this version, he keeps ♥♥♥♥ing using the attack even after I've completed all the chambers. This makes it take a super long time to kill this ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥. - This might be unfixable, but when you're battling the big water monster things, the environment is not as scary compared to the original version. The water is chrystal clean and it's just not fitting.
The only thing about the experiance that makes this version better than the original version is when you go outside of the laboratory in this game. Specifically, when you go out of the pipe and see the canyon. It's way better than the original one, which wasn't meant to be seen on bigger screens with better quality. The ragdoll physics are also better, but it doesn't make much of a difference.

After Call of Duty Black Ops, I have had zero interest in the franchise afterwords as Activision began pushing out Call of Duty year after year after year becoming less awesome than it used to be (although Black Ops II does get an honourable mention of Treyarch trying to keep the franchise interesting). Last year's Ghosts was by far the worst in the franchise, not helped by the ♥♥♥♥♥♥ optimization on PC.
This game by Sledgehammer have managed to re-kindle my interest in the series by taking the game far into the future and introducing exo suits as part of the mechanics. As for the story, it's decent but at times predictable; you go from shooting North Koreans, to terrorists, to corporate soldiers. As for the multiplayer, the exo mechanic actually helps reduce the amount of frusturations I have had with the CoD franchise, particularly campers as verticality becomes key.
In terms of the PC Options, the game does contain full fledged options from texture quality to anti aliasing to shaders, etc. The one problem I have had is the lack of a Field of View slider in the single player campaign (while FOV is allowed in multiplayer) where in I did not get sick up until playing more than two and a half hours. It has to do with the developer wanting you to experience what they have without clipping like how FOV can do at times for certain games, it still was not healthy when playing up close with the mouse and keyboard (I recommenend using a controller if you have one). Though when optimizing the game for me, I tried getting the same graphical fidelity and performance at least on the same level as the PS4 and the Xbox One, however I soon learned that playing the game on 1080p with texture resolution high and everything else set to medium and/or low the frame rate (with V-Sync on) kept on tanking within certain points around the game, forcing me to have to down scale the resolution to 900p in order to make it responsive enough for me to enjoy (keep in mind my rig is mid-ranged with a Radeon 7870 and i5-3070).
Overall, I find it to be decent enough for me to enjoy and recommend, if you like to see some change in the CoD franchise.

I remember when I was a kid and thought to myself "This timer in Super Mario Bros that kills me if I don't finish the level quickly enough should threaten to kill me in about one minute, multiple times per level, unless I manage to grab items in time! That's what this game is missing!" Oh wait, I don't remember that at all, because that's a terrible idea, and even when I was a dumb kid, I didn't have ideas that were that awful.
You see, in Dinocide, as with Super Mario Bros, you move from the left side of the level to the right. However, in this game, you grab food along the way. If you have trouble lining up an enemy to kill, or have to wait for a moving platform to get into position, chances are you're already dead, because you won't get to the food in time. Then you rush, trying to get to the food, which just makes you take damage...oh, and your "health"
your hunger, so getting hit just means you starve to death even faster.
I did like the two boss fights I completed, but the hunger meter is a huge turn-off which I really gave a chance, but ultimately did not enjoy, and it's too annoying for me to want to finish the game. Without that, the game would just be a middling title that is less entertaining than an NES Mario game, which is rather disappointing, considering decades have passed with which new features and blending of genres are now possible. This game's hunger meter and lack of anything to modernize the game in a positive way made this a title I would not recommend to anyone.

I love caveman / Dinosaur genre games, in my opinion, there is not enough of them and it is a genre that is way overlooked.
Here comes along Dinocide with some really cool game mechanics, mostly familiar from the NES era.
The game feels like not so much a throwback but more of an homage to the past.
However the game is poorly put together, there is no structure to the overworld map, and this feels clunky, I would have much preferred clear stages such as desert, forest, ice, instead we are given a roulette style level system, I have no idea who thought that was a good idea.
Also, the game is very repetitive, some of the level design feels rushed and the enemies seem as though they were taken from previous projects the team had worked on, for a game called Dinocide there are very thew dinosaurs, which is a shame, instead we have Mexican skeletons and zombie pig-men !!!
There are some good secrets hidden away, and the boss fights are inventive, I kind of wish the team had spent more time on creating more bosses and actual dinosaur enemies than trying to pad out the game with convoluted levels.
Dinocide does have some charm, it's hard to find but it does exist within the game, surprisingly with everything said the game is fun and does give the player some challenges, even if some of them seem unfair at times.
I believe this is a game aimed at little children, who have very short attention spans. Dinocide is a bad game, it is not a good game, but it is  fun and very random.
I am giving it a thumbs up because I do believe people should play this if only to learn what not to do while developing a game, and how to avoid the trappings of poor development.

Recently, we are witness the new wave of popularity of prehistorikal theme in media. Dinosaurs tiring apart boxoffice in theathers and three of biggest videogame companies simultaneously developing the big budget titles aboout cavemen and their savage and dangerous surroudings.
And while we're looking on FarCry: Primal, Wild and Horizon: Zero Dawn with all of it's serious mood, pathos and drama, the same time we're began to remember what kind of games we played in this setting in the beginning of the 90-s.
Ofcause, there was a period of Prehistorical slash Fantasy RTS in the early 2000-s, but some of us the most vivid memories were related with platforming arcade hits inspired by the desing of everyday life of cavemen presented by The Flintstones.
Reckless and carefree master of belly-fu Chuck Rock with his bubblehead son, constantly hungry Sam from Prehistorik, professional rescuers of Damsels-in-Distress Joe & Mac and, ofcause - humans, The Humans. Not to mention about a bunch of games about The Flintstones themselfs!
Anyway, I just wanted to play in something similar to this classic arcades. Not replaying the same games, but rather in somthing fresh, made by the people who remember this games too, and be able to create a game inspired by, let's say, the same Prehistorik 2 - the game easy to play, but not so easy to win.
Dinocide - is this kind of game! It has very cute fauna representatives and bearded manly-man, who about to rescue his girlfriend/wife/sister from the giant Godzilla-like dino... I wonder, it has a level inside the dino's guts, like in Joe & Mac or Chuck Rock... and nothing will stop him! Unless, miss some fruit and dying from starvation.
Yeah, you will travel on the various Prehistirikal locations, like rainy forests, woods, deserts, caves, lagunas and even American West prairies and canyons infested with undead mexican outlaws armed with bumerangs (don't ask), but if you will keep to your diet - the hunger will kill you before tusks and claws... or bumerangs.
But, the swifty hunger protagonist is the only devoloper's flows about this platformer: jump, throw sticks-n-stones (and bumerangs) at dinos, giant lizards, spiders, scorpions, snakes (you can't deal without them), rainbow spiting bears, muchachos in ponchos (?) and more than expected giant bosses.
Good game to spend the evening and remember the countless hours of beating the Prehistorik around 1993))
P.S. also, here you ride on the back friendly dinos... and drive the real Mech Warrior!

The music, sound effects, and narrations were produced very well for what the game is going after. Cutscenes although used minimally provide a great structure in giving a back story as well as furthering questions about the plot.
This game is worth playing and is a nice refresher in what horror can actually shape up to be like without the use of fantasy elements.

Currently one of my favorite "fighting" games!  If you are a fan of the anime or a fan of fighting games as a whole this game is great to own!
This games roster is huge, with a just as impressive selection of game modes. Story, Survival, Tournament, etc.
Game play wise if you've ever played a Naruto Ultimate Ninja Storm game then this will seem oddly familar. Take the usual dash and combo system from that and turn down the speed and there you go, Saint Seiya. I'm not saying that's a bad thing. Surprising it works really well. A slower space to compliment the extra supers you can use.
The Story is pretty good too. Don't expect any Nuns level cutscenes. This is alot more simple. But is steps above its predecessor which only used pictures and text boxes.
Lastly there's alot to collect in this game. So If you like having everything with no effort then this isn't for you. Stages, characters, and costumes can only be unlocked after hours and hours of massive grinding. But if you can bare with it, you'll find a fun combat system, with an even better cast.

From the first battle I've played in this game, I couldn't stopped thinking that I've already played game with familliar gameplay. And yes, I was right - "Naruto Shippuden Ultimate Ninja Storm 3" and "...4" have very simular gameplay. Unfortunately, when compared, this game loses almost in everything.
The first and main problem for me is story. God damn, it's BORING. I didn't watch anime (if there is) and never played any games from this universe (if there are any) and, if you think, that I shouldn't even started playing this game without doing these things, then you will be wrong. In Naruto games (which I mensioned earlier) I also haven't any information about story, characters, etc., but I still had A LOT of fun playing story mode in both of those games. I understood everything, I was involved in plot. I didn't think "WTF is going on?" or "Why are you saying/doing this?". This game does not do this. In every cutscene I have to break my face with facepalms, caused by unbelievably unrealistic, epic (or, more accuratly, "epic"), empty and, sometimes, just stupid phrases (with each 2nd of them ending with god damn exclamation point).
The second is graphics. They are mediocre, at best. According to Steam this game was released in November 2015. Naruto Shipudden 3 was released in 2013, and it somehow looks better, with better faces, than in this game.
The gameplay is, probably, where Saint Seiya is better than you-know-what. In Naruto you just mash one button to attack, sometimes turn chakra mode on and maneuver around enemy. Here... well, you do the same, but here you have not one button to attack, but two! Not much of a difference for me, but point for trying. Except for it, everything is the same: projectiles, blocks, rushing to enemy, using a bit of "mana", throws (which you made exactly the same way: by attacking, while blocking), special mode and special super attack. About super attacks. They suck. After Naruto, where special attacks were colourful, diverse and overall beautiful, here we have several attacks, made by hero, after standing for several seconds with some constellation as a background and, of course, shouting out the name of your attack, while doing it...
In the end, I can give this game 5/10. Very mediocre game with "not bad" battle system, "very bad" story mode and outdated graphics.
P.S. I've used Naruto, not because I'm some kind of fanboy (as I said earlier, I haven't experienced anything from this universe, aside from 3 games in Steam), but because it's an excellent example of how to make a game, based on anime that will be interesting, immersive and fun to play for everyone, not just those, for those, who know, what they're buying.

Half Life is a brilliant game. Before playing, I was unaware of the preeminence of this game. I had only heard that HL2 was amazing, so I figured I'll play the series sequentially. I had done the same for the Portal series and for no reason at all, assumed that HL would likewise be short (just as Portal 1).
It isn't. The game is pretty long (~ 12-14 hours). It's got a lot of action, is challenging, has few puzzles, has a decent story, and a really engaging gameplay experience! The continuous storytelling is superb, and I can imagine the reverberations it would have created in the gaming world back then.
I played for a few hours on HL engine before switching to Source. (All chapters were fortunately unlocked, so I could pick up where I had stopped.) I was expecting to see a massive graphics overhaul, the likes differentiating Counter Strike Source and Counter Strike 1.6, but was let down. Visibly, I could discern nothing much except maybe that the water looked better. That's all.
While the port didn't do much justice to the graphics improvement, the gameplay remained smooth and bug-free.
Black Mesa would probably replace it however.
As for Half Life, it's an amazing game. Whether you play the original HL, or HL Source, or Black Mesa, just make sure that you DO experience the game! It's a classic that cannot be missed!

I really wanted to like this game. I like platformers, and don't mind the nostalgia look. Unfortunately bad design decisions and finnicky platforming ruin it. You go forward through stages and collect upgrade weapons to use, as well as mounts. The mounts give an extra health bar, which is greatly needed. The problem is you lose everything on you if you die or fall down. Which you will do a lot due to the poor game structure. For no apparent reason, you constantly lose health throughout the stage. This forces you to run forward at all times, meaning you can't really fight enemies well, and usually just have to try and rush through them. This is by far the worst of many bad design decisions and ruins the game. If enemies hurt you, and they do way too much damage coupled with constant health loss, you have to try and rush even more, forcing you to more likely get hurt by more enemies. Items also restore barely any heath, and less than even what 1 enemy hit does. It is this vicious cycle. If you are at half health rushing and a guy hits you you basically will die bc you'll be too low before next health. You are at mercy of game designers for next health. Also health placement is super hit and miss, some being way too far while others are close or decent.
With the mount, for some reason, if it dies, you remain, but only with half health, which makes no sense. The jumping isnt well down, when you jump, you go up super fast all of a sudden and go really high, but barely move horizontally at all, meaking some deaths from trying to reach the next platform, making you lose everything. Enemy design is also poorly done in some aspects. Enemies like vultures suddenly fly in from nowhere off screen, giving you no warning sign nor time to reach, leading to cheap damage. Enemies like the snake are also super fast and jump around, making them near impossible to dodge, and unable to run from. This is compounded by the fact there is no running, and your guy moves at .5 mph for some odd reason.
There is no backtracking or ability to get more upgrades, meaning if you lose with them, you have to replay the next level without them. This come to the head later on. In one level I kept dying because of poor health placement. Coupled that with vultures doing cheap damage, and this giant sand worm that comes out without warning and even hits you if you aren't close to it. You are unable to get past it and have to kill it, but it has way too much health and you constantly lose yours. So i kept dying and then i was left without items and pets, and just my weak normal attack. This basically means you're screwed and you can't do anything about it. This is where all the poor game design comes together in one terrible mess. I have no items, I have to fight this guy that I can't run or get past, who has way too much health, who I do no damage, to, as I constantly lose health. Because he's at the end of a section, I have little health already, so I just die and have to constantly repeat entire level, only to die as this poorly designed part again. As the game gets harder you are forced to use less items as you lose them, which is the opposite of how it should be. Thanks for nothing game.
3/10.

I can't recommened this game in its current state...
Nobody in casual matches has a proper grasp on how to play, and almost everyone is plain toxic.
Furthermore, Matching-making is a nightmare. The Dev team recently added "prestige levels" for players to level up passed the previous level 30 cap, but I just use it to see who I'm being put up against in a match. Myself, a level 127 player, has constantly been placed against people below level 100, and it gets a little bit frustrating.
Smite's main gamemode, Conquest, is the least played gamemode because of it's drastic and impossible learning curve. Only players who have been playing since day one, and have been evolving with it can properly play. Conquest in it current state is much too "snow-bally" to be an enjoyable experience, and the worst thing is. Most of the people on the deisgn and balance team don't even play Ranked! It's absurd! Not to mention too much time and effort goes into skins...
Also, every other God release is♥♥♥♥♥♥poor. A lot of them end up being eye-candy Godesses, to pander to the new, younger men playing the game. And their ability kits suffer because of it, with little to no synergy in them at all. It's just heartbreaking that it's gotten this bad, compared to the old design team's releases.
Lastly, Osiris hasn't been nerfed yet. A character that has been overpeforming at the mid and highest level of play, hasn't been nerfed yet because of his underperformance in casual matches.
So, yeah... Maybe wait until it gets a new Lead Designer, or until Season 5. It's supposed to be great! But I'm not getting my hopes up.

Romero's Aftermath is the spiritual successor to Infestation: Survivor Stories...That should probably tell you something.
Like the game before it, Aftermath is basically a DayZ clone but free to play. All I'm going to say to that, is you get what you pay for. You're dropped into an open world with other players and you need to survive. One thing that I will praise Aftermath for is that it is challenging. You need to get food so you don't die of hunger. You need water bottles for water, because your character can't drink ou of lakes for some reason. Don't try and say "The river's dirty" or anything like that as an excuse, because dirty water is a consumable in the game. But, the game does bring a big challenge o anyone but then again, that's soething DayZ has already done. Aftermath does nothing to make people choose this over DayZ except for 3 things:
1) Take everything that was good about DayZ and make things 10X worse
2) Free to play (which is one of the few praises I have for this game)
3) Add in a micro transactions element to the game and make everything that's incuded in the in game store incredibly hard to find in game so you try and make tons of cash from it.
It also doesn't help that around 60% of the servers in this game are servers where barely anything functions.
Graphics in this game are decent to say the least. The game could have looked worse, but it easily could have looked alot better.
This game is better than Infestation: Survivor Stories bu that isn't really saying much. I don't even think tht this game is worth picking up even when it's free. There is already an infinately better version out there called DayZ. The devs are going with the tactic "It's free, it's meant to be sh*t" In my opinion, that's not a valid excuse. If you're putting a game onto an insanely popular market and it's free to play, then it has to at least be half decent. Look at Team Fortress 2, that game is free to play and that game is amazing and tons of people are still playing it to this day, I doubt anybody will remember this game any time in the near future.
Pros
+ Decent graphics
+ Challenging
+ Better than Infstation: Survivor Stores
Actually you know what, forget about that last pro, that isn't something to be proud about
Cons
- Boring gameplay
- Half broken servers
- Bugs and glitches
- Terrible animations
- Micro Transactions
Final verdict: 2/10

Death. Over and over again, death. Now that we have this game's main aspect covered lets get to the review. dark souls 2 is a third person RPG in a fantasy world. keep in mind fantasy just means the world never existed in our history. the world is a very harsh, lonely, unforgiving and downright ugly place. all of this was done on purpose by the devs to make a gritty atmosphere just as in pervious games.
The combat is very difficult to get, but once you play the game more and more you'll realize your deaths are mostly nothing but your fault. Few enemies can qualify as "cheap", as they are made to be hard for some and easy for others. You could fight this big fat dude in heavy armor with nothing but a giant axe. for a melee character this would be hard, or at least a challenge. but if you have range weapons of any type he could be a giant joke. (no pun intended)
but the main thing in this game you need to realize. you are not alone. for those of you newbies reading these reviews you never experienced dark souls 1 invasions. in my, say, twenty+ hours on my first character i've been invaded twice, and only one of those succeeded in killing me. Dark souls can be very much so multiplayer based if you let it. just keep in mind very means summoning two people to fight alongside you. there is even a ring that lets you more efficiently play with your friends, and i commonly help my friend through the game.
Point is, dark souls, any one in the franchise will make you mad, angry, and even make you want to quit. you'll find yourself ranting about how the game is flawed and doesn't work. But..... if you play more despite this, you will find one of the most rewarding experiences in video gaming ever.

Two things. First the game - then early access.
THE GAME
Great concept, nice art style. It's basically a fun exploring game with base building (eventually small space craft building) and research and resource elments that are largely there as obstacles to exploration and survival. Action junkies will hate this. People with patience and imagination will most likely enjoy this very much. It's good fun on multiplayer too with friends. I recommend it. If the vids appeal to you, it'll probably be a safe purchase even in early access. Just remember that this still has a ways to go before it's finished and the amount of additional content we can expect to see is anybody's guess.
So why the sudden run of negative reviews when the overall score remains very positive? Simple - a lot of people seem to think early access games should all be like second year of ARK's early access. That is simply not realisitc.
EARLY ACCESS
For those that don't realise, means that the dev's focus is usually not on new content but on refining and stabalising what is already available in the early access package. That content will almost always be in a primitive and buggy state. There's no point throwing more content on top of unsteady foundations.
If you buy an early access game and complain about the need for more content before the game is stable perhaps the problem isn't with any particular game but with early access itself. It's not pre-sale. It's exactly what it says on the tin - access, long before the product is market ready. You make this choice going in. Moreover, the absence of new content in the early access release does not mean that new content is not being developed and made ready.
Just look at the content of the 199 patch. I'd rather have that than more content before that lot was fixed. And it points to new content that is actively in development.
There's a sense of entitlement about early access gamers that seems to mistake early access for pre-order. They really are two different worlds.

My friend lived in Mexico for a while as a child and his first introduction to animé was Saint Seiya.  Years later, we met and he introduced me to it.  It wasn't my favorite thing, but it was in a spirit similar to Dragon Ball, and it was fun watching this very dated show go about making us grow more fond of its wide cast of characters.  I became very familiar with the most used quote in the entire series: "Nani?" "Que est esto?" or "What?" depending on which language you preferred...
Now, here.  When I saw the game released, I thought, "I want to play this, but I definitely don't want to pay full price.  I didn't LOVE Saint Seiya."  Now playing the game, I find a new fondness for these now-familiar characters.  I enjoyed familiar elements of the plot, and gaining my own nostalgic moments.  For story, I definitely love this game.
Visuals are incredible, but I wish more of these newer games had low-end options.  It seems like everything is making a push to cause 2-year-old laptops unable to even play at Middle-option visuals.  As it is, I have most of the visual options turned down as far as they can go, and I have my screen set to viewing about the same size as your average Kindle or tablet...and it still has a little lag.  I would love to be able to turn off the shining and reflecting features of the armors...
And for combat, I love and hate it.  Maybe we can say it's sort of like the show?  There are times when I have the upper hand for a while, then I get my butt handed to me in a similar way.  However, I love to Dominate combat, so it really sucks to have a combat system where it seems the only escape is to always have a little bit of energy ready to make an escape.  I never have that, and over half of the time I end up escaping the opponent's onslaught, he just re-targets me where I teleported and now I can't get out.  And while all the moves are things we've seen in the show, and there are variations of characters you can use to pick different combos of special attacks, they are ALL completely telegraphed.  It seems like every time the enemy wants to pull off a special, I'm right in the path of it and can't escape, but many of the times I pull one off, it's blocked or dodged or I just get attacked and interrupted.  It feels unfair.  As for the Big Bang attacks, I'm lucky to hit with 1 out of 10 attempts for the previous reason.  There is so much delay for our attacks, the enemy has all the time in the world to react.
So, I recommend this game, but have patience.  If you're a fan of Saint Seiya, this is a great game.  If you have a high-end computer, it is also great.  If you aren't very good at fighting games, this will be frustrating...or I'm just an exception...

So, Dishonored 2...
This review is work in progress, and I will be updating it accordingly. However, after seeing so many negative reviews here I decided to give my two cents to those on the fence about buying it.
In one sentence, the game is great. I loved the first one, and everything is turned up to eleven in this sequel. First one always lacked some soul to me, but that didn't mean much since the game was so fluid and fun to play. And there's even more of that here than before, skills now have more depth, no killing playstyle is now more interesting than ever before, and because of superb voice acting characters finally have depth that first game to me always lacked. I haven't finished the game as you can propably guess, but if 4 hours is any indication this is in every way the kind of sequel that every fan ever wanted. There simply isn't many options if you want to play something like Dishonored.
However, if the game itself cranks it up to eleven in it's systems and gameplay, so do the system requirements. And even with high end rig you can expect to have framerates that are not what you want to see in AAA release in 2016. My rig is i5 4670K, GTX 1080 and 16GB's of memory and at times the game has the nerve to drop even below 40 fps. To some this might not matter but having spent over 1000€ for a gaming PC I find this a bit offensive.
Still, the game is so damn fun that I simply can't hate it for it's shortcomings. I hope they fix the framerate in upcoming patch (rumors are talking about patch coming in next few days), because if/when technical side is fixed this game is simply a must buy.
I recommend it to everyone who enjoyed first Dishonored, but only if you feel lucky enough to not get affected by possible technical issues, or after a patch that fixes the game. In the mean time, if you haven't played Dishonored the first go get it and enjoy youself. If you have it already, go play it and wait for the patch.

I had my doubts Dishonored 2 was gonna live up to Dishonored. UNTIL IT DID.
For one the fact you can switch between Emily and Corvo really lets you get into their mindset, which adds to replayability besides just playing the other character, or you could just play how you want still good replayability. Not to mention Emily and Corvo do have different abilities, even if some of their powers are meant to mirror eachother they are still different even a bit slightly. Corvo is classic mode you could say.
The second: The maps are so much bigger, it's much more open world, there's more nook and crannies to explore, and that's all something I really enjoyed about Dishonored, there were a lot of locations I missed until I made a second walkthrough and thought "Hey, that's cleverly hidden."
Another big factor is the fact you can now drop on enemies from above with the choice of knocking them out, Dishonored only you do drop assassinations, you can now drop knock out people. In addition in sword fighting if you get someone off balance you can outright knock them out, so that's a good incentive to try and sword fight with the purpose of getting someout cold rather than just running away.
Did I mention you can also outright reject the Outsider's offer? Rejecting his offer of giving you powers turns on No Power mode, so if you feel like powers a little too easy, that's an option. I thought that was neat.
I've found no hiccups really, just improvements, all in all this is my pick for GOTY 2016.

Is that dishonored 2 is an amazing game, and if you liked the first one you will love this one. It improves upon every fault of the first one and then some. While it may not be perfect, no game ever is really. This is a giant leap into the right direction in terms of gameplay and listening to the community.
I can't tell you exactly how long I spent just walking around with the heart and listening to what everyones story was. A tough yet gentle fisherman offered me advice on how the guards treat new comers. So I thought he was a good guy. Yet the heart gave truth to his actual nature; a liar, a cheat, and a killer. And then not five steps away from him was another fisher. Sitting on the edge of the dock trying to catch a fish. The heart spoke of how ever since his wife died, he stays up with his daughter reading her stories until she falls asleep. Every, single, night. -- It makes you feel like there's a whole world going on around you. That these people actually matter, you don't want to seem them come to harm. As you do whatever it was that you were doing.
The guards(I play on very hard. which is the highest I believe.) spot you like how you would think someone in the real world would see you. I rattled my sword against a metal gate to lure some of them away then made my way into the locked door they were guarding. Once they came back, they tried to open the door to see if it was tampered with. After they found it to be unlocked, they alerted every other guard in the vicinity that this happened. they even get alerted when one of their squadmates don't come back from patrol in a timly manner.
While this is the first iteration of upgarding powers and the like. I wish they really changed how you would use that power. Instead of it being a straight upgrade. Bonecharms however, seem to fix this issue. The corrupted ones at least; for example, there was one that made Far Reach be able to stealthily pull someone at the cost of needing more mana to cast.( I believe you still need the upgrade however.) things like that really change the way you play. Suddenly I couldn't spam Far Reach anymore, but it gave me this new option to deal with enemies.
I wouldn't recommend buying dishonored 2 right now until the optimisation patch comes out. But when it does, you are in treat for a real gem of a game.
