Dinocide is a game heavily inspired by the Adventure Island games.
A lot of the core mechanics are almost identical to Adventure Island, although the game does add its own stuff to the mix.
The game consists of basic platforming. To kill enemies, you can use a variety of projectiles.
You start off with rocks. They don't do as much damage as later weapons, and launch in an arch pattern.
As you progress through levels, you can pickup new types of weapons with varying damage and launch patterns.
You may also hatch a dinosaur egg, that will then mount you ontop of said dinosaur. These guys play the same for the most part, but allow you to do subtle differences like walk through lava safely, or destroy obstacles.
The main stand-out feature, is the fact that you have a hunger meter, that is constantly depleting. As you progress through the level, you'll find food items that fill it back up.
Along the way, you'll also find gems that you can spend in shops to buy weapons, or dinosaur eggs.
The graphics are pleasant to look at, and the music is quite good for the most part. It's a good replication and twist on the type of atmosphere it's trying to recreate. I wouldn't say the game innovates as much as it should, but if you really enjoyed Adventure Island, then you'll probably have quite a lot of fun with this one.

Questerium: Sinister Trinity HD is a well-made hidden object game that I'd put up near my top recommendations in this genre. While the formula is familiar -- a mystery unfolds and is solved through a combination of cut scenes, hidden object hunts, solving mini-game puzzles, and finding necessary objects to progress through the story -- the execution is good and the game is fun.
The use of live actors in the animated setting was an interesting choice that certainly sets this game apart. It's a little jarring at first, but it blends a little better once you get used to it. The acting's pretty over-the-top campy, and it made me laugh more often than not, like a cheesy B-movie performance. I'm not sure if that's quite the result that was intended, but it amused me and it worked with the game.
I really like the addition of findable money in the scenes, and that you can use the money to upgrade a garden patio (though I kind of question the desire to buy plants while encountering the plants throughout the story!) I also like the collectible plants that you pick up in different locations, and the way the achievements unlock objects in a virtual trophy room.
The story is decent, and though it is somewhat predictable, the journey is still fun. The artwork is good, and very colorful. The hidden object scenes are nice, and most involve multiple objects where you have to piece things together or uncover them first, making them a bit more challenging than a simple point-and-click thing. Where Questerium shines, though, is in its mini-games. Some of the puzzles are really clever, and I had a lot of fun working them out.

So I'm here to throw my ten pence into the pot as it seems like a lot of people are just salty about optimisation issues and such and are ruining the image of what is, to me and apparently my pc, a perfectly fine and beautiful game.
I have finished my first run of the game (Low chaos) And I am currently partaking in my no kills, ghost playthrough, so my review will be based off a very low chaos angle, maybe optimisation is poor with a lot of bodies around or something.
OPTIMISATION ISSUES: Now I have an i7 processor and a Nvidia GTX 970, and I have played through the entire game without a single drop below 60, which is curious to me as people with hardware much higher than mine are reporting issues. It's hard to call in this situation, but I have had no issues with optimisation myself, so it's worth giving it a go and if it's absolutely atrocious on your pc then you can refund it, I'd guess. A neutral point.
STORY: So with optimisation kerfuffles out of the way, let's focus on the first major thing about this game, the story and the world surrounding it. I think it's pretty marvellous. I won't put any spoilers or hints at the story as it's one of those that you really wouldn't find engaging if people told you what's going on. Is it as strong as dishonored 1's story? I wouldn't say so, however it is not far behind at all, and is still great. So it's a thumbs up from here!
GAMEPLAY: The gameplay on this is sublime. It's just as good as the first game's gameplay, and I have quicksaved a few times to give combat a go, and the gorey and horrific deaths you inflict onto people doing their jobs and duty guarding a helpless city are ever so satisfying. (Especially if that guard spotted you the last five attmepts you tried to sneak past him, forcing you to reload). Powers are good, however, without trying out Corvo, many of Emily's powers seem a little useless, at least to a low chaos run, with only far reach, dark vision and occasionally shadow walk coming in handy. Many aren't a neccesity to play through the game, and are simply a way of spicing things up. I don't know how I feel about that exactly, yet this technically the case in dishonored 1 too, however a little less so. When I've done a high chaos run I'm sure I'll have a more firm idea on how I feel about it, but for now mark me down as skeptical. Yet gameplay as a whole is great, and par the powers it's a big thumbs up from here!
The game is great. I'm sure if you've had optimisation issues then it would be horribly frustrating, but from somebody who hasn't had that problem, I must say it's very good, and I would have to recommend. You might as well give it a go, no? The worst thing you'd have to do is send for a refund.
Go play this! Maybe wait for a patch! Who knows? Who cares?

I've not had any issues by a graphics standpoint on either of my GPUs, so I can't speak to that, but I can speak to the game's content itself.
Dishonored 2 has rocketed itself into my favorite game of all time. There's new mechanics, deeper lore, more intriguing characters with better design, and above all, it keeps the same Lovecraftian feel as Dishonored 1. The gameplay has greatly improved, and level design has soared into an incredible level of detail in wide environments. As far as story goes, it is fairly straightforward, but the lore deepens a seemingly simple world into an ocean of history.
I also nominated this game for the 'Villain Most In Need of a Hug' award. So there's that.

To be quite frank, alot of reviews talk about poor game optimization and bad frames. Yes, sometimes my frames go a bit off, going to around 30 fps at high intensity situations, however, it is NOWHERE NEAR unplayable. I have a 960 and i5-4460 so my rig is very average.
So far I have played 5 missions and each and evryone is filled with difficult objectives and many different ways to do each one. This is much more challenging than the first game which I have played 10+ times over on every difficulty, so be prepared for a leap in skill. Emily is very fun to play with her new abilities like shadow walk and dominoe which I will have fun testing as I am currently doing a ghost playthrough. I haven't had chance to play Corvo but I cannot wait to blink everywhere.
The graphics, gameplay and difficulty are all very good and Bethasda have done an amazing job with this sequel. I strongly reccomend it, but play the first game beforehand.

(THIS REVIEW DOES NOT CONTAIN THE ISSUES ON PC AND IS COMPLETELY BASED ON THE PURE GAME) So, starting off let's talk about the stealth. The stealth is what you would expect from a Dishonored game, the AI is very much improved with the "stupidness" of the Dishonored 1 AI removed. The enemies have realistic vision cones and can see you pretty well and they can actually see you if you are above them now. Let's just say trying to get past guards is much harder now and takes planning and patience. The stealth is excellent but is optional like most stealth games. Next we have the graphics which I believe has been drastically improved from the first game. There are some parts of the game that make you stop and stare and it keeps the cartoon-ish look of the first one. Moving on, we have the character choices. In my playthrough, I chose Emily and I enjoyed her 100%. Her new powers are insanely cool to use but can be a bit overpowered at times but that's leveled out by the difficulty of the missions. She has a great variety of spells and are all very useful. With Corvo, his powers are the exact same as the original. Moving on to the story, if I'm being 100% honest, isn't the best... It's good at times but feels rushed and is explained quite badly. Delilah is a great antagonist but the game sort of makes her look like the victim which softens your view on her ultimately softening the multiple endings. With the level design, I can say it's great. Each level is crafted carefully to give you multiple ways of getting to your objective. There are many sidequests to occupy you during these levels and reward you very well but the game's weakness is definitely the bloodflies... They are nothing less of a nuisance that can be taken care of easily and are rarely ever mentioned throughout the game. I was hoping that they would be as dramatic as the rat plague but they really weren't (They are pretty ♥♥♥♥ing terrifying though). The game feels like Dishonored, plays like Dishonored, looks like Dishonored and definitely sounds like Dishonored and to end the review, I'm giving the game an 8/10. Although there are quite a few flaws, the fantastic stealth and gameplay overcomes it all. You won't feel the flaws during the game until you really think about it and in the end, you should buy this game if you are a stealth fan.

Well the fighters all have pretty unique styles and feel like the original characters, so that's cool.  However, this also seems to make a few of them just completely unstoppable.  I'll admit I've only played the single player, but for instance I have yet to actually take a hit while playing Andromeda.
Speaking of which, the singleplayer is pretty good with quite a bit to do.  The AI plays pretty aggressively from the outset, which is nice compared with other fighting games where you've always got a few rounds of way-too-easy opponents before any difficulty kicks in.  The cutscenes are godawful though.  I mean okay, to be honest Saint Seiya was never great story/character material to begin with; the characters were always painfully cliched manime archetypes, but absolutely zero time has been put into animating the models or faces for cutscenes in this game, so what you get is a character standing in his respective fighting or standing stance, and moving his lips while the rest of his face remains perfectly still.  Come on guys, it's a sixty dollar game, make the faces expressive.  I also would have liked it better if we could change the stories like in some of the Budokai games.  I find myself just skipping all the story stuff, which is something I generally don't like to do.  Story mode also does that thing where it makes you play all the characters instead of just playing through one's story, which I find aggravating.
Anyway, the fights are fun and a lot more interesting than fights in Saint Seiya ever were, and there's a pretty robust single player mode, so that covers the two major areas for my dollar.

Alright, so having finished with this game, I do have a few choice words for it.  For one, this being a game where you'd have to rely more on strategy than just straight going toe to toe, this works in a fighting game.  For the most part, it's a fighting game where you'd have to anticipate attacks constantly whereas in other games is more who combos first.  Since I relied mainly on both for certain characters, it draws a learning curve more of how you should fight than who to fight with.  There are characters who are fast enough to flat out chase their enemies and catch them offguard with either melee or cosmo attacks, characters who strongly rely on cosmo alone then those who have short ranged melee attacks or just slow with melee but cosmo attacks are just that powerful. The Cosmo Attacks are pretty lengthy and can sometimes cost you the battle but again, it comes down to strategy.  This is a thinking man's fighting game so it's not as spam happy as Street Fighter is. So for those who have it and don't like due to lack of speed and whatnot, it's not that kind of game.  For someone like me, it works.  I'd say this: if you like Saint Seiya or you're a devoted fan of the series, get it for that reason alone. The story cuts it down to where it matters and worth playing through.  Try it if you like it, that's all I can say.

I have been an avid fan of the Borderlands series since I first played the original installment back in 2008. Below is my personal impression of its pros and cons:
+ Engaging, immersive gameplay.
+ Fun and worthwhile cooperative multiplayer experience.
+ Graphics and art-style is timeless, aging through the generations remarkably well.
+ Creative characters, both playable and NPC.
+ Great level design and set-dressing. There are lots of little details to find and explore.
+ Detailed universe, with a captivating storyline that further motivates you to keep playing.
+ Great gameplay balance with the leveling system, making progress feel rewarding.
+ Varied characters with a range of possible play-styles.
+ Excellent compatibility in terms of your computer's performance. Even low-end computers with generic graphic cards can comfortably play (with reasonable quality adjustments).
+ LOADS of extremely entertaining and creative DLC to play after you've finished the main story. DLC campaigns are also fairly priced.
+ Tiny Tina.
+ Meat Bicycles.
- No evident compensation for high latency in network play.
- No in-game method to view your ping. I often try judging my latency by how long it takes a bullet to leave my gun after firing.
- There's an anticlimax once a character has reached the highest possible experience level. Each subsequent kill and other progress after that, comes accross as less rewarding.
- A character becomes progressively more difficult to fully level up. Less experienced FPS players will likely find the tougher play-through modes more frustrating than fun. Playing with friends, especially in
or
is definitely recommended.
- Relatively predictable storyline for the main campaign, but still worthwhile.
Ultimately, I fully recommend this game, as well as the other titles in the series, despite their shortcomings. It's an experience I always look forward to, whether I get to play with friends, or when I just wing it solo. There's a unique joy in finding that occasional super-rare item, or popping the head off a cheeky psycho that wants to be buried upside-down!

So I'm here to throw my ten pence into the pot as it seems like a lot of people are just salty about optimisation issues and such and are ruining the image of what is, to me and apparently my pc, a perfectly fine and beautiful game.
I have finished my first run of the game (Low chaos) And I am currently partaking in my no kills, ghost playthrough, so my review will be based off a very low chaos angle, maybe optimisation is poor with a lot of bodies around or something.
OPTIMISATION ISSUES: Now I have an i7 processor and a Nvidia GTX 970, and I have played through the entire game without a single drop below 60, which is curious to me as people with hardware much higher than mine are reporting issues. It's hard to call in this situation, but I have had no issues with optimisation myself, so it's worth giving it a go and if it's absolutely atrocious on your pc then you can refund it, I'd guess. A neutral point.
STORY: So with optimisation kerfuffles out of the way, let's focus on the first major thing about this game, the story and the world surrounding it. I think it's pretty marvellous. I won't put any spoilers or hints at the story as it's one of those that you really wouldn't find engaging if people told you what's going on. Is it as strong as dishonored 1's story? I wouldn't say so, however it is not far behind at all, and is still great. So it's a thumbs up from here!
GAMEPLAY: The gameplay on this is sublime. It's just as good as the first game's gameplay, and I have quicksaved a few times to give combat a go, and the gorey and horrific deaths you inflict onto people doing their jobs and duty guarding a helpless city are ever so satisfying. (Especially if that guard spotted you the last five attmepts you tried to sneak past him, forcing you to reload). Powers are good, however, without trying out Corvo, many of Emily's powers seem a little useless, at least to a low chaos run, with only far reach, dark vision and occasionally shadow walk coming in handy. Many aren't a neccesity to play through the game, and are simply a way of spicing things up. I don't know how I feel about that exactly, yet this technically the case in dishonored 1 too, however a little less so. When I've done a high chaos run I'm sure I'll have a more firm idea on how I feel about it, but for now mark me down as skeptical. Yet gameplay as a whole is great, and par the powers it's a big thumbs up from here!
The game is great. I'm sure if you've had optimisation issues then it would be horribly frustrating, but from somebody who hasn't had that problem, I must say it's very good, and I would have to recommend. You might as well give it a go, no? The worst thing you'd have to do is send for a refund.
Go play this! Maybe wait for a patch! Who knows? Who cares?

I've not had any issues by a graphics standpoint on either of my GPUs, so I can't speak to that, but I can speak to the game's content itself.
Dishonored 2 has rocketed itself into my favorite game of all time. There's new mechanics, deeper lore, more intriguing characters with better design, and above all, it keeps the same Lovecraftian feel as Dishonored 1. The gameplay has greatly improved, and level design has soared into an incredible level of detail in wide environments. As far as story goes, it is fairly straightforward, but the lore deepens a seemingly simple world into an ocean of history.
I also nominated this game for the 'Villain Most In Need of a Hug' award. So there's that.

(THIS REVIEW DOES NOT CONTAIN THE ISSUES ON PC AND IS COMPLETELY BASED ON THE PURE GAME) So, starting off let's talk about the stealth. The stealth is what you would expect from a Dishonored game, the AI is very much improved with the "stupidness" of the Dishonored 1 AI removed. The enemies have realistic vision cones and can see you pretty well and they can actually see you if you are above them now. Let's just say trying to get past guards is much harder now and takes planning and patience. The stealth is excellent but is optional like most stealth games. Next we have the graphics which I believe has been drastically improved from the first game. There are some parts of the game that make you stop and stare and it keeps the cartoon-ish look of the first one. Moving on, we have the character choices. In my playthrough, I chose Emily and I enjoyed her 100%. Her new powers are insanely cool to use but can be a bit overpowered at times but that's leveled out by the difficulty of the missions. She has a great variety of spells and are all very useful. With Corvo, his powers are the exact same as the original. Moving on to the story, if I'm being 100% honest, isn't the best... It's good at times but feels rushed and is explained quite badly. Delilah is a great antagonist but the game sort of makes her look like the victim which softens your view on her ultimately softening the multiple endings. With the level design, I can say it's great. Each level is crafted carefully to give you multiple ways of getting to your objective. There are many sidequests to occupy you during these levels and reward you very well but the game's weakness is definitely the bloodflies... They are nothing less of a nuisance that can be taken care of easily and are rarely ever mentioned throughout the game. I was hoping that they would be as dramatic as the rat plague but they really weren't (They are pretty ♥♥♥♥ing terrifying though). The game feels like Dishonored, plays like Dishonored, looks like Dishonored and definitely sounds like Dishonored and to end the review, I'm giving the game an 8/10. Although there are quite a few flaws, the fantastic stealth and gameplay overcomes it all. You won't feel the flaws during the game until you really think about it and in the end, you should buy this game if you are a stealth fan.

After nearly 3,500 hours I finally decided to review one of my favorite games on PC. In fact, it was the reason why I bought a gaming PC in the first place.
Pros:
- RAIDING - Raiding other groups, clans, or enemies provided me with many hours of tactical, engaging, and intense fights. It is one of the core aspects of the game, and is what kept me hooked for so long.
- PVP -Rust is one of those rare games that gets your heart rate pumping after killing a couple of enemies, and trying to loot all of their bodies while zig zagging your way to safely deposit your loot back home. All while your hands are shaking.
- BUILDING - The way that people build bases is constantly being changed through certain forced updates. You used to be able to build huge castles and compounds, but now the game has switched to a more bunker base style build. This change in style every once in a while is refreshing in the form of you aren't seeing the same base build over and over again from YouTube tutorials.
- ROLEPLAY - Facepunch has implemented many items that encourage friendly player to player interaction. From shop fronts and vending machines, to mailboxes and notes, and to the new furniture being added to the game, there is certainly a place for your casual gamer.
Cons:
Don't get this game if you won't treat it like a full time job. You will be disappointed every time you login to find that your base has been raided by a bunch of high schoolers who can spend almost 12 hours a day on the game.
Unfortunately, many Rust players are way too serious about their loot. Meaning, they would rather offline raid a base in 30 minutes, than be challenged in an online raid that provides multiple hours of fun for both sides. Also, a lot of♥♥♥♥♥♥talking and bragging about loot in the public chat.
Hackers, scripters, and ban evaders are everywhere.
FPS Stutters. The game on the highest setting looks beautiful, but expect to take a huge performance hit once you are in a gunfight. I run on potato settings with a high end PC to make sure I don't dip to 10 fps if I get in a big gunfight.
Overall, the gameplay in Rust is extremely addicting and you forget what time it is in real life while playing. However, the fact that you have to treat this game like a full-time job and the terrible performance hits is what will kill the game. Still, it remains my favorite.

Main issue with this game is as follows:

Certain puzzles are almost unsolvable not because I don't know how to solve it but because those puzzles requires you to use your gauntlet to hit the ground trigger button and you need to be very precise and accurate. You'll miss your hit even if its only 1mm away considering the controls are already extremely bad in this game when it comes to precision. It took me several tries to try to hit just one ground button. The problem with the puzzles are not the puzzle itself but its the controls.
2. It is extremely easy to get lost and not know where to go and if it takes players more than 5 min roaming around the same area over and over just to find out where to go, then its a very bad level design.

4. Combat feels more like god of war style rather than the old school castlevania but that's not the bad part about the combat. The bad part about the combat is that it can get tedious cause most of the time you can only hit twice and dodge, rinse and repeat because the enemies here does not get staggered as much as the previous castlevania entries and because they have tons of hp, hitting and dodging becomes a chore rather than playing.
5. The forgotten one in this game is no doubt the WORST boss design ever out of all the castlevania series. To beat this boss, you need to jump and hit most of the time which in doing so causes you to constantly take damage because you cant dodge mid jump. There's no other way to damage the boss other than jump hit. Basically if you wanna do damage to the boss you're gonna havta eat 5X the damage you do and by the time you dealt about 5% of his hp you're dead. Other castlevania entries you still have time to land on the ground and dodge after hit jumping any of the boss but this one, there's no time at all but that's not the worst part about this boss fight. The worst part about this boss fight is the final phase where you have to double jump just to land a hit on him but because of how ♥♥♥♥♥♥ the camera and controls are, you'll spent most of your time double jumping into the wrong direction. Hit and jump is already making you prone to getting hit by the boss but the fact that the designers wants you to double jump and hit!? just shows that they hire the wrong designer. All this does not make the fight difficult, it makes the fight near impossible, if the fight is near impossible then its a really ♥♥♥♥♥♥ boss design, end of story. Also the hint that tells you what you should be doing for certain attack patterns only appear after your first failed attempt. I don't mind a challenging boss battle but this boss is not considered challenging, its considered sh!t. Literally the worst ever boss design.
Overall, here's the most important question, is the game fun? Hell No.

This game gets a lot of hate (though not as much as its sequel), and some of it is deserved. It definitely has its problems, but at its core, it has a lot of awesome things going for it.
The rest of this review will contain spoilers, you have been warned.
The biggest problem I found with it was the storyline's emphasis on telling over showing, which may just be an inherent problem with relying on narration for 90% of your narative. Almost every mission starts with Zobek telling us how Gabriel is becoming consumed by hatred, but we don't really see much of that in game. Sure, he's a brutal protagonist, much like that other protagonist that murdered a bunch of mythological creatures with a chain weapon after his family was murdered, while in search of a way to bring them back, but we don't really see him becoming the Prince of Darkness until the DLC, and even that is solely through narration, with the exception of one dialogue exchange where Gabriel admits that he doesn't really care any more. It feels forced in a way, which is a shame because there are a lot of good hints at what Gabriel is going to become. Many of the bosses end up impaled, which would have been a subtle hint towards it had we not been beaten over the head repeatedly about how he was becoming consumed by darkness, and by the time you get to the Land of the Dead, just about every Brotherhood knight you find has written something about how they're all becoming crazy murder happy killers due to over using the power of shadow that they pretend is mandatory for fighting monsters.
On the other hand, as far as a Castlevania reboot goes, this was a solid attempt. The gameplay is pretty good all around, despite kinda feeling like a buffet plate of what worked in other games. You've got your Shadow of the Collosus boss battles, God of War combat, some Portal puzzles (even going so far as to describe it as Aperture magic). The idea of Dracula being a fallen Belmont is pretty cool, and were it not for the over use of narration turning it all into telling over showing as described above, would have been one of the coolest reboot ideas I could think of. The voice acting is pretty good for the most part, a few hammy scenes notwithstanding, and the game looks beautiful and plays solidly. It's no Symphony of the Night, but it's definitely not Castlevania 64 either (though they did bring back a character from Legacy of Darkness as a boss fight). The boss fight with Satan in specific is a really fun mix of a lot of the concepts that you've been learning throughout the game, requiring you to constantly switch back and forth between the power of light and shadow in response to what the boss is doing, which felt really good. And on top of all that, there're a lot of battles that while maybe frustrating, never feel overly unfair, and do a good job of rewarding the restraint from throwing your controller through the monitor by giving extremely cathartic conclusions, such as the time Gabriel punches a Dracolich back to death out of the sky.
In summary, it's a fun game that had a lot of potential, but seems like a lot of that potential might have been cut due to time or budget constraints.

The Call of Duty franchise routinely gets bashed for it's yearly entries and what's perceived as rehashed material. Whether or not this is in regards soley to the multipleyer or the overall game as a whole, I cannot say as I'm the oddball who plays these games for the campaigns (sans BLOPS 2 and Ghosts). I've dabbled some in the multiplayer, yes, but the campaign is what I enjoy about these games. Are the stories amazing? No. Are there memorable characters? Not particularly. Are they fun? Hell yes.
I don't play these games for anything else than the unadulterated pure action that it provides, and boy does this entry give you that in spades. Advanced Warfare's campaign is slam packed with awesome set pieces and great spectacles for you to fight in. The gun play is good as ever and there are just the right amount of specialty mission sprinkled in to keep you constantly wanting to see what it will throw at you next. The skill system is a neat idea, if somewhat shallow. Add to all of this probably the most breathtaking and life-like cutscenes I have ever seen. I mean, the motion capture in this is just incredible.
So at the end of the day, yes, I absolutely reccomend this game. Why? Because it is some of the most fun you'll probably have playing a shooter this year. And frankly, having fun is why I love to play games.

As a Saint Seiya's fan I recommend this game if you feel nostalgic about the series. As a fighting game however, there are better games out there. Overall I'd give this game a 6/10, maybe a 7 on a generous day. The fact that most moves are the same on all the characters is a bit of a downer, but it's also nice if you don't have the patience to learn new combos.
Let me clarify: the special moves are all triggered by the same combo. Even though you get different cut scenes and different moves. So you the timings are different and the situations you might use them in are different (somewhat). There are some minor combos that differ, too.
They attempt to tell the anime's story, but they leave a lot out. For a beat-them-up though, the story is as good as it's going to get. No English dubs, but then I have never seen the anime itself dubbed in English, although it was dubbed in my native language back in the 80s. You do get subtitles but the translations leave somewhat to be desired in places.
You do get to play the Sanctuary saga, Asgard, Poseidon and Hades, you unlock a lot of characters with their gold or god cloths. That is bound to wet the apetite for the hardcore fans.
TLDR: If I wasn't a Saint Seiya's fan I wouldn't have bought this. I do enjoy it for what it is, and for the fans I'd say it's worth getting but perhaps when a sale is on.

this is not a souls game.
the world is completely uninspired and very few locations have the mysterious atmosphere pulling you along. you're able to travel between bonfires from the very start, which i'm not sure if this is a cause of or caused by the fact that the world is nothing more than four Y shaped paths out of the main hub.
the "storyline" of this game makes no sense, from the first cutscene you're looking for a cure to the curse, then after the tutorial "seek the king, you'll do this without knowing why!" while the first game gave pretty clear instructions on where to go as long as you spoke to people ("one of the bells is UP above! [this one is stated first so you can assume it's the easier path] the other is BELOW in BLIGHTTOWN"). in dark souls 2, the directions given by npcs are far less specific. you're told all four paths, even though two are gated at the start, and aren't given any idea as to which of the two are easier.
the friendly npcs are entirely forgetful. the only one that stays in mind is the poison arrow vendor.
trash is long, tedious, and poorly placed. while there were times in dark souls 1 where you'd be forced to fight multiples, they were rare and were usually creatures that could be easily handled (eg, the group of 7+ naked hollows with the channeler in the parish). this game, it seems every single trash section has at least one if not several pulls where 2-3 enemies is being gracious. additionally, these monsters spam multi-hit combos, have infinite stamina, and perfect tracking (ie, if you move left or right, they turn on a dime to stay facing you). your major options for smoothly clearing trash are either: a. be a magic user or; b. use a bow and poison arrows. after awhile, sitting around letting the poison arrows tick gets very frustrating.
none of the bosses are very memorable. infact, the ones that i do remember almost vividly, were actually just rehashes of bosses from the first dark souls. old dragonslayer is ornstein with a different color palette and one new attack (the fight is a joke because smough isn't there). belfry gargoyles make their return, again with a different color palette, the difference being you fight 3 at a time. royal rat authority is a reskinned sif with 4 adds at the beginning of the fight. lost sinner was a slower version of artorias. the scorpion woman is quelaag reskinned with one new attack, and a few soul arrow variations to replace the fire attacks. every boss in the game has 3-4 moves and possibly a gimmick, but otherwise have no difficulty factor aside from clearing the trash to them.
on top of all this, there are a myriad of engine based bugs. these range anywhere from being able to see reflections in water through solid objects (WarZ beta style) to weapons swinging in the wrong direction, all the way through to weapons simply not scaling (seriously, a +10 axe with A str scaling doing 200 damage less than a +7 sword with C str scaling? give me a break.) beyond this, there were a variety of issues early on of people being unable to even start the game, which i am unsure if this has been fixed.
all in all, this game failed to live up to the name of the souls series. the first game was challenging in that you had to play smart to not be overwhelmed. in order to not be overwhelmed in this poor sequel, you'll be spending lots and lots of souls on poison arrows.
if you're planning on buying this, i would highly recommend saving yourself a few bucks and buying the first game. you'll get a much more enjoyable experience.

Very well constructed with a great eye for detail.  It's a genuinely creepy experience that plays up a variety of horror tropes well.  There was never a point where the haunted house trope dragged on or relied on cliche.  Of course it helps that the game is short.
The voice acting was surprisingly good, but the editing and script were not this games strongest feature.  There were a number of elements that were unnatural in English, with a few interesting word choices that might have worked better in other languages, but made the protagonist feel like an alien.  The inclusion and mispronunciation of the word 'banal,' made me laugh, which was probably not the intended effect.
There were also several instances where dialogue overlapped, or very nearly overlapped, leaving the character sounding as if he were rushing to tell his story.  This would be fine, except for it standing at odds to the rest of the delivery.
I thought this was an excellent experience, one that goes to show how much you can accomplish with limited space and an eye to detail.  If the script were better, the editing a little tighter, and the puzzles a little less oblique (the keys, oh the keys!) this would be excellent.  As it stands it's very good, and I would recommend it to anyone.

I don't usually write reviews, but this game deserves it, as it's so gravely misunderstood.
The greatest issue I believe is that people expected a game like the old Castlevania titles, but this one is vastly different from those, therefore it fell victim to expectations.
However, if you head in with no prejudice and a clear head, you will find a greatly enjoyable game, full of action and in my opinion an engaging story. It's no masterpiece, but you actually feel for some of the characters, which by today's shoddy standards is good. The graphics are also gorgeous, though I never really cared much for them, gameplay makes a great game, in my opinion. Some cinematics appear a little blurry which I guess is due to the port.
The PC port is also solid, I played with mouse and keyboard, which worked perfectly after I found out what kind of keybinds work best for me. I imagine it's even better with a controller. This game has a definite learning curve, if the player wishes to complete it on higher difficulties, they need to observe enemy movement and abilities. The vast majority of times, it is the player's fault if they die. Rare expectations are the few encounters with RNG elements and the occasional bad camera angle. Overall, it has an amazing satisfactory feeling when you defeat something you've been struggling with.
It took me roughly 55 hours to complete the game including all achievements that naturally calls for a second playthrough. The collectibles are helpful, non-arbitrary and actually help a lot if you keep an eye out for them throughout the game. To me this game felt like one of the old Prince of Persia games, with better combat, and the same kind of puzzle solving and platforming.
It's really a steal if it's on sale, go get it!

I'm writing about my impressions of Voices from the Sea as an avid VN reader. tl;dr is there is much better material (free or otherwise) to be reading. Granted, this is both free and very short so there is little cost to you whether you end up liking it or not.
The most to like about this one is the art and the music, which evoke a calm and contemplative mood, and there are a good number of CGs for its short length. Unfortunately, however, it fails to capitalize on its almost surreal setting, as its other departments are painfully inadequate. It might be that the game has a very low development budget, and free VNs tend to not be as well-written as the ones you have to pay for, but even then, there are much better examples free VNs for PC out there, like the Narcissu series [Stage-nana 2005], or True Remembrance [Shiba Satomi 2006]. The characterizations, motivations and themes here are much too shallow and generic to be memorable, and there is almost no story or scenario to speak of, whereas in the other examples, while they may not necessarily be the pinnacle of writing, they are unique in their own way.
If we don't consider only free titles then you get phenomenal works like Ever17 [Kid 2002], Little Busters! [Key 2007], Symphonic Rain [Kogado 2004], White Album 2 complete [Leaf 2010]. I do realize that Zeiva (the developers) are an independent group, but they need to try harder to make a favourable impression or to distinguish themselves. For me at least, 'disappointing' best describes the experience.

A buffet of violence.
Become a vault hunter on Pandora. Shot enemies. Get loot. Repeat.
Borderlands 2 is an FPS with a touch of RPG. There are 4 playable characters (6 with DLC) to make your way through Handsome Jack's minions. Each character comes with their own powers; a single active ability as well as some passives. There are literally billions of guns and items for you to farm and create your perfect build, though as the enemy levels rise, there is more importance in obtaining unique or legendary items (and good versions of those items). There Salvador whose ability allows him to wield 2 guns at once. He's blatantly overpowered. Maya is a siren that can phase lock enemies and is the only character with skills that directly benefit allies. Zero the assassin who can clock is the character I found the most interesting. He can melee or snipe so there is a wide variety of styles and builds for him. Axton has a portable turret and favors assault rifles and grenades.
Borderlands doesn't take itself very seriously. Pretty much everyone in the game is insane and bloodthirsty. There isn't to much of a story, though Handsome Jack is a solid villain who with throw insults and taunts your way. Personally I would have liked a more personal touch to the story. No matter who you play as, your character is just referred to as Vault Hunter and there is no difference in dialogue. So you never really have a sense of personality. Enemies have a decent variety of quips, though if you plan on maxing out and pouring in hundreds of hours it'll get tedious. But there is 4 person co-op to break up the monotony (though I only solo'd the game as of this review).
There are some issues out side of whether you like grinding for loot or not. The loot itself is pretty bad. I understand their needs to be bad items in the game, but the sheer amount of worthless loot is crazy. By the time you've unlocked your power, 75% of what you pick up is simply fodder. I don't find the game to be particularly nice to look at. Most area's are huge, but the muted colors makes it all blend together. Also enemies can be tough to see against the background or from distance. There are a lot of invisible walls and some clipping issues. Most fights come down to DPS and health regeneration. This isn't really about strategy or tactics; it's just how solid is your build.
There are some scaling issues as well. Missions scales their levels to the level of the player when the start the mission (except dlc missions which always scale to the player's level). So outside of the dlc, you cannot continuously farm an item you like as it won't scale to your current level (until ultimate vault hunter mode). The level discrepancy between you can enemies effects the amount of damage you deal. Enemies 3+ levels higher than you take significantly less damage (to a point that some are literally unkillable). In harder difficulties, enemies have so much health and regeneration that several skill abilities become nearly worthless thus limiting the diversity in viable builds.
There is a ton of DLC and should be talked about. There is a season's pass that is missing a lot of the DLC (it doesn't have the 2 dlc characters for example) The game of the year edition doesn't come with the final level pack (Level 62-71) nor any of the head hunter DLC. Tiny Tina's DLC is the best in regards to story and items. Captain Scarlett and Torgue's are solid contributions of the same quality as the game. Hammerlocks is the weakest of the story DLC. Creature Slaughterdome is little more than a save point for farming loot. There are also 2 new characters; Gaige and Kreig (haven't played him yet). Gaige's main feature is anarchy which increases damage and lowers accuracy with every kill. But you have to build it up each time you reload the game.
If you like hunting for loot and juvenile humor you can play with your friends, Borderlands 2 GOTY edition is the way to go. I don't feel like it does anything amazing, but it does a lot of stuff well enough to be enjoyable for the time you put into the game.

I love Dark Souls, its a game that I enjoyed from start to end. Dark Souls II has finally come around which take place thousands of years later, what is known of The Chosen Undead from the first game is left unknown but to imagination. The set for the sequel is what they now call Drangleic, a land where many civilizations have fallen and what's left is in ruins.
As expected from the previous installments, the game does not tell a story, just the plot that unfolds before the player's eyes, lore is told from descriptions, environment, and dialogue, the rest is up to how you piece it together.
Drangleic's entangling areas each have their own unique setting, some small and others immense, but all visually pleasing. The only setback is the soundtrack, every song in Dark Souls is great but also unique, which happens to be the problem with Dark Souls II, most of it is forgettable or generic. Gameplay is solid, classes are split up by types, weapons still give different attack styles with the addition of being able to duel wield weapons now. The difficulty is about on par if not more than the first game and it can be for any reason but it's usually for being unprepared, which you will be more than often. Still even if you have a hard time progressing you can always summon a fellow shade (another player) to help you, Jolly Cooperation! Note that with the benefit of being able to summon help, there are other players that can invade and kill you, so its quite bittersweet. Don't let that deter you from playing the game, its very demanding and overwhelming at first but once you get off your feet a few times, you will learn and appreciate the world of the Souls games.

(Please note: I played through both NG and NG+ as a pure strength character on PS3, and am currently well into my third playthrough as a Faith/Strength hybrid now on PC. I say this because your choice of build can dramatically alter which bosses you find difficult.)
This review will be split into three parts: The good, the iffy, and the bad. Let's do dis.
-Just to get it out of the way: the quality of the port. No worries here. Support for any resolution and 60fps right from the get go. Just beautiful. You'll still have to stay away from mouse+keyboard controls, though.
-The combat. Just as good as ever, if not better. Dual weilding and bows are now super-viable, which is awesome. I love me some bows.
- The aesthetics. This game NEVER stops impressing visually. Heide's Tower of Flame is one of the most beautiful areas in the entire Souls series. Special shout-out to the cloth physics.
- Some of the bossses. Smelter Demon and the Rotten are some of my favorite boss fights in the series now. Two of the post-game optional bosses are also amazingly difficult, for anyone who is disappointed with the last boss.
- The UI and menus. SO much better. It's a little hard going back to the menus of Dark Souls after playing this one.
- NG+. I never really got all that far into New Game+ in the first game because it simply increased all enemies health and damage, which didn't seem all that interesting to me, but Dark Souls 2 changes up a lot of stuff. There are entirely new enemies which make some areas considerably harder, and some boss fights have even been changed (most notably Lost Sinner, which goes from being one of the easier fight to being controller-breakingly hard).
-Some of the covenants. I only ever really enjoyed my time in the Sun covenant in the first game, but this time around I have a hard time deciding just which covenant I want to stick with for any given amount of time. The bell covenant, rat covenant, sun covenant, and blood convenant are all great fun. ESPECIALLY the bell covenant.
-The stats. Yay, no more useless stats! Level up without fear! You can even respec your character this time around, which I don't think will complain makes the game to "casual" or whatever. It's amazing to be able to completely change your build halfway through if you feel the need, instead of being forced to start over.
-Bonfire Ascetics- Such a cool item. Basically, you can burn one of these to respawn the nearest boss and all enemies (yes, enemies despawn, more on that later) AND make them all more difficult in the process. Specifically, it bumps them into NG+ difficulty if you're in NG, NG++ if you're in NG+, and so on. This is great for a number of reasons. A) it's great way to allow players to make the game harder for themselves. B) It's a cool way to allow for the farming of souls. C) You can fight your favorite boss as many times as you want, yay!
- Bonfire teleportation. You can now travel between any bonfires from the start of the game. While incredibly convenient, Dark Souls has never really been about convenience and this has some unfortunate side-effects on both exploration and world design.
- Enemies despawning. This has been controversial and I'm not too sure where I stand on it. When you kill any enemy around 15 times, it stops coming back for good. On one hand this could be seen as making the game easier, but on the other hand if you've killed something 15 times I think you've probably got a handle on that enemy so it's almost like a reward. I dunno. Some areas seem stupidly hard, and the only justification is that if you suffer through it enough times it'll become easier. Hm.
-The torch mechanic. It's a shame it's not put to use very many times since the lighting system was gutted. The only area where it's "necessary" (the gutter) is incredibly fun and puts the torch to perfect use.
-Holy jesus those hitboxes. They can be really unreliable, which is unacceptable in a game this difficult and so reliant on it's battle system. Dark Souls had it's hitboxes mostly in check so it's disappointing to see this step back. I can no longer say "if you died it's probably your fault" because of this.
-Some of the bosses. A very large percentage of the bosses of DSII fit the description "overly large humanoid with a sword". Now, some bosses like the Demon of Song have some of the most interesting designs i've ever seen but they're unfortunately few in number.
-The world design in some areas. There's one area that seems to be a large stone tower. You progress up said tower and fight a boss seemingly at the top of the tower. Then you take an elevator... up, and end up in... the center of a volcano? What? There are a few examples of this and it's sad to see, especially coming off of Dark Souls' amazing world design.
-The last boss/ending. Just generally anti-climactic. Ain't no Gwyn, that's for sure.
Overall, though the bad section looks pretty big now that I look at it, Dark Souls 2 is still one of the best games I've ever played. Yes, the absence of Miyazaki's creative genius is painfully evident in some areas, but the new guys have created a game VERY worthy of the "Souls" title. It's ridiculously replayable thanks to the tweaks to NG+, the covenants, and the ability to respec, so you'll get way more than your money's worth no matter what price you buy it at.

Another series in the souls franchise. Rather, the another game in the dark souls universe.
This game is immensely difficult for first timers as the play style do not give second chances when mistakes are made. I.E. when you strike a friendly npc, when you miss your strike against an enemy, when you failed to successfully dodge, spend too much of your stamina, making the wrong choice to block or dodge, etc. Not to mention what kind of unfairness the game has in-store for you, such as dying, invasion, curse, enemies' position, etc. Though the game has a mysterious lure that always bring you back despite much of the difficulty.
Minus the invasion of online play, the game has JOLLY CO-OPERATION. These players who drop their summoning signs are anxious to join your world to help you on your journey. Most of them are very friendly and helpful, pointing the way and taking out the enemies or traps that may befall on you if you make the wrong step. And of course you don't lose anything when they die except maybe your pride if it's your fault. With co-op signs, there's also invasion signs for pvp action.
Dark souls 2 PVP has not many changes compared to the first one. It is nearly the same except that poise doesn't seem to work as effective as it was in the previous dark souls. Regardless of poise, players still have the mind games against each other. Do the player have stamina after that attack? Is the player going to run to heal? Is the player going to cast magic? I wonder if the player is going to hold block... etc. Skill is also a crucial factor in Dark Souls 2 as the previous game did. Parrying, dodging, striking, backstabbing, efficiently using all your abilities.
Because the game is not friendly when mistakes are made, the game will have that same difficulty. Got a nice upgraded armor and weapon? Who cares!? Enemies are going to hit harder in the next area and almost as agile! Don't fret however, you will always return if you fail. Learning comes from defeats. Many defeats will befall on you.
Remember, you will die. You will learn every time death comes. You will be stronger. You will die again. Welcome to Dark Souls. 2.

A solid combat system, combined with epic boss battles and an amazingly beautiful and diverse scenery combine to create the best 3D Castlevania game by far, and a must buy. Really hard to understand all the flak it took back in the original launch.
Pros:
-The combat is really consistent and fun to play.
-Quite inspired in Shadow of the Colossus, the boss battles are creative, fun and have an epic sense of scale.
-The locations are very diverse, with amazing, immersive scenery. You fight through swamps, abandoned cities, dracula's castle and even supernatural locations, and all of them look gorgeous.
-The platforming parts are really fun, giving you a time to cool down between fights and enjoy the awesome views.
-Quite a long game, even more if you include the two DLCs.
Cons:
-I know some people like it, but the story is quite messy in my opinion.
-Some of the puzzles are a little bit too much, even though some are quite good.

I don't mind a game to be challenging, for as long as it is skill that is required for you to overcome any obstacles. Castlevania however, is a very frustrating game that would have potential to be okay if the developers bothered working on its very obvious flaws. For example, this game has platforming mechanics that will make you want to place a toothpick under your toenail, and boot a wall out of sheer anger - and this game is mostly platforming. I was hoping for a nice hack'n'slash type game, but you only get drip fed these moments as you fumble and fall and fail your way around jumping over (seemingly) simple ledges and cliffs. Even the epic boss fights require you to climb and jump, instead of block, dodge and fight. It's frustrating. Dull. Horribly placed. The checkpoints are at really inconvenient moments. The camera angles are as if they're straight outta Resident Evil 1. I got this game for under £5 and I still wouldn't recommend it. Avoid.

A really short but wonderful game.
The story is about a lonely boy called Cantus. He sits around at the beach listening to the waves, when suddenly a girl shows up. She is rather excentric and clings to Cantus. She will be his first friend and make him happy.
The story and plot are short but wonderfully done. While you can pretty much guess the outcome (specially as it is quite a linear story), it is fun to read. It's funny and also a little sad at some points.
The characters are also nicely done with the girl being quite random and Cantus being quite silent/serious.
The graphics/art style are nicely done, though don't change much, as there is only 1 setting and a few characters.
Still, they are drawn really nicely and the backgrounds are nicely animated as well.
The music has the same problem as the graphics. They are wonderful to listen to and really set the mood of the story and characters but there are around 3 songs in total.
Verdict: If you want to read a visual novel with a good story, fun characters in a nicely drawn fashion, this is really for you. While short, I reckon it would make you smile.

Still, the game only lasted me 12 hour play time (it tells you ingame, steam hours isn't actual playtime). On top if that the optimization is... okay... I have not had any of the massive FPS drops that some other people are reporting. I did however have some drops while looking at certain objects, for example a boat in a glass cage the FPS would jump from 60 all the way down to 25-30. Weird.
Pro's:
-Lots of different ways to complete objectives.
-Very cool mechanics.
-Emily's skills are a nice breath of fresh air from Corvo's abilities. For example the blink, if you jump right before you blink, you launch yourself in the air. This has also killed me numerous times though...
-Very well crafted levels with lots of secrets. The clockwork level is just awesome.
-Voice acting is exellent.
Con's:
-Short. If you rush it in the slightest you'll be done before you hit the 10 hour mark.
-Lots of places to get stuck with blink. You can always blink out of it but still. Annoying.
-The game is rather slow in letting you assassinate NPC's stealthly, when you blink to a NPC you have to wait a second before the game lets you stealth kill them.
-Story was kind of lackluster.
-Later levels become very easy with all the powers. Would've liked better/stronger enemies in late game.
-Optimization is rather poor.
All in all, it is a very fun game with an okay story and in pretty much every aspect a upgrade from the first one.

Another series in the souls franchise. Rather, the another game in the dark souls universe.
This game is immensely difficult for first timers as the play style do not give second chances when mistakes are made. I.E. when you strike a friendly npc, when you miss your strike against an enemy, when you failed to successfully dodge, spend too much of your stamina, making the wrong choice to block or dodge, etc. Not to mention what kind of unfairness the game has in-store for you, such as dying, invasion, curse, enemies' position, etc. Though the game has a mysterious lure that always bring you back despite much of the difficulty.
Minus the invasion of online play, the game has JOLLY CO-OPERATION. These players who drop their summoning signs are anxious to join your world to help you on your journey. Most of them are very friendly and helpful, pointing the way and taking out the enemies or traps that may befall on you if you make the wrong step. And of course you don't lose anything when they die except maybe your pride if it's your fault. With co-op signs, there's also invasion signs for pvp action.
Dark souls 2 PVP has not many changes compared to the first one. It is nearly the same except that poise doesn't seem to work as effective as it was in the previous dark souls. Regardless of poise, players still have the mind games against each other. Do the player have stamina after that attack? Is the player going to run to heal? Is the player going to cast magic? I wonder if the player is going to hold block... etc. Skill is also a crucial factor in Dark Souls 2 as the previous game did. Parrying, dodging, striking, backstabbing, efficiently using all your abilities.
Because the game is not friendly when mistakes are made, the game will have that same difficulty. Got a nice upgraded armor and weapon? Who cares!? Enemies are going to hit harder in the next area and almost as agile! Don't fret however, you will always return if you fail. Learning comes from defeats. Many defeats will befall on you.
Remember, you will die. You will learn every time death comes. You will be stronger. You will die again. Welcome to Dark Souls. 2.

Greetings everybody my name is Tommy the game master and welcome to my channel. Well Halloween is over but I did pick up a few games for myself on the steam Halloween sale. One of the games I bought was a game I’ve been meaning to talk about for a while, Castlevania the Lords of Shadow. I already reviewed one of the sequels several years ago when I reviewed the downloadable Mirror of Fate. So lets start actually talking about the orginal Lords of Shadows.
So what was Castlevania Lords of Shadows, it was an attempted reboot of Castlevania. And when this reboot happen Konami took the series away from Koji Igrashi director who had been doing Castlevania games for almost a decade and had several portable hits under his belt and gave too Hideo Kojima and the Spanish studio Mercury steam, too see if they coulden’t make the franchise successful again on console, shame of it despite the fact that Lament of Innocence and Curse of Darkness are decent games Konami coulden’t get past the fact that there 3d games on the N64 were a bit lackluster. Now too be fair here Igrashi even said the series needed a reboot after 20+ years in the market, there was no place too really put in another one, it was for the most part complete. I agree with that except for one more game they could make, I think gamers would have loved a game where Julius Belmont was the main character and we see him get rid of the evil count once and for all, or at least see his next incarnation be more human then vampire. Anyways with Mercury Steam and Kojima at the helm they kind of made a Castlevania game that wasen’t really a Castlevania game. Does that make it a bad game, not really but it is different.
Story
The story follows Gabrieal Belmont has he tries to figure out who put up a barrier between earth and heaven causing spirits of the dead to wonder the earth unable to find peace. His wife is trap like this having been mysteriously murder just a few days before. He finds out from the mysterious Zobek that in order to restore the balance he must find and defeat the Lords of Shadow and restore the god mask they manage to posses, and with that power he can not only restore order but bring his wife back to life.
Ok that is the simple virtually no plot spoiler version of the story, the story is thick and has some ups and downs to it but I am going to do a plot analysis videos because some parts are clever, and some especially being a reboot of a series just sucks and shows the Lords of Shadow spin offs were going down the wrong path pretty much from the get go.
Gameplay
I have got start my asking, can a game be too big? And I don’t mean like artificially large by making you collect stupid mcguffins that you don’t need. But just too big on it’s own that your sick of playing before you get to the end of the story. Because that’s a problem I have with this game, I was exhausted by the time the final boss got here. It’s not bad, but it could have actually been better being shorter. Let me explain first lets just say there are 3 types of gaming in here. Platforming, combat, and puzzle solving.
So lets begin with the platforming, it’s more Prince of Persia then classic Castlevania. You can climb up walls, swing using your whip, and basically have to figure out how to get around and up tall obstacles. I find this type of thing very satisfying and with the exception of a few small areas where what I could grab wasen’t made clear to me this part of the game was actually pretty fun.
Combat is the next type of gameplay your going to find, and these are a bit of a mix bag. To be honest I enjoyed the combat in Lament of Innocence a little bit more even if it was a lot more simple. The amount of moves Gabrieal can learn is abslotuey stunning. From heavier attacks, to air combat, or even just spinning his whip like a chain. Hitting enemies rapidly without getting hits increases your focus gage and when full enemies drop magical refill orbs like crazy which you can by hitting an analog button decide which one you want to fill light or dark magic. Activating the light magic will allow Gabrieal too heal when he strikes an enemy, while activating the dark magic will greatly increases Gabrieals attack, however regardless of the mode your in you won’t get any refill magic orbs to appear while using it, and your focus will never fill. So your main focus in battle is often times trying to make sure you got a balance approach of making sure your hitting enemies in a way to cause magic orbs to appear, deciding which magic type you need, and making sure you don’t use to much of it that you run out of it. It’s actually kind of fun and make it even more satisfying when you get a large combos and magic orbs just fill the screen waiting for you too fill your magic tank up. Along the path of the story Gabrieal will gain a few new abilities like the ability to run or double jump through Relics he finds. The only bad thing I can say about these is they often time lead to run ins with Cubachabra who steals these abilities temporaily so you can play a game of hide and go seek and these events are aggravating because they always screw up the pace of the game. But the chubachabra encounters aren’t the worst ones. There are puzzles and whenever you encounter one of these the pacing goes out the window.
Ok two types of puzzles first are environmental puzzles that do fit a game like this and most aren’t too frustrating, no more then the churchbras and some can be quite fun and they fit action games like this so no real complaint that they put these in here. However there are also professor Layton type puzzles jammed into a game where your main goal is to whip vampires into bloody smears and oh boy do they not fit. And there always in the worst freaking area possible. Sometimes you know after you beat a tough boss to a mutilated mess you just want to go on the elevator that was obviously activated and not play a stupid freaking puzzle trying to get his blood all the way to the correct area in order to complete the stages. These things are always frustrating and just stop the pace and it would have been better if these puzzles were left out completey, and yes the game does often times give you the option of peaking at the answers in order to finish them faster, still doesn’t mean it won’t stop the game completey because of it.
In fact because the game just jams so many different types of gameplay elements together with the combat, and the platforming, and the puzzles all together the game actually feels like a bit too much. This game is the most exahausted  I think I have ever been from playing a game, not bored, or frustrated but exhausted. This one game where I can say when it comes to the gameplay less would have been a hell of a lot more.
Has far has the DLC is concern I woulden’t pay 20 dollars for it. The first pack is pretty interesting from the gameplay wise and it has a few different levels of the castle with some new monsters and platforming areas, and puzzles. It’s more of the same gameplay found in the main game but what I found was good, even some of the professor Layton puzzles were fun. Unfortuantley the 2nd pack was a dispointment basically stalk a giant demon around this volcano area, find it when it’s weak beat the crap out of it and continue.
Graphics
The graphics in this game have held up really well over the last several years. The charecters faces look pretty good for the most part are good and the envoirnments look absloutley great. Now the enviornments themselves are something to be a bit of a nit pick. Most of them don’t really feel like Castlevania very much. Yeah some of the monsters may have a Castlevania motif but the forest areas and the ruins of the lycans don’t really strike most people of there favorite memories of

With just under 10 hours of playing this game I can safely say that this is not a title for people who are not familiar with the Saint Seiya universe and lore.
The game does not take the time nor apologize for simply narrating the very big overall plot points of the series.
This game is, however, a
for hardcore Saint Seiya fans who were lamenting the lack of a PC version to play with.
Falling in this category, I am having the best of time rediscovering the main fights from the this beloved series.

I really recoomend it if you are a fan, or at least know the history of the anime and enjoy a fun fighting game
PROS
* original voices - excelent voice acting, well synced
* lots of characters (although they could have inclued some silver saints and more specters)
* fun to play
* gameplay improvement compared to the previous games
* nostalgia
* multiplayer works just fine (I have NOT experienced lag)
* almost all sagas of the anime was covered
* no bugs - yeah, it would be mandatory, but lately all games are released with bugs (some major and big annoying ones) so this is (sadly) becoming a diferential
* MODS! the game looks like really easy to MOD, and some MODs are already on the scene, with new custom models/ sounds
* special moves animation are really similiar to the way saints perform it on the anime series
CONS
* no OST ( can be fixed with a MOD that puts the original musics in the game )
* no intro movie
* no bonus stage
* no animation of any saint dressing the armor, one thing that i really enjoyed watching on the anime
* lame cutscenes - almost no animation, saved by the voice actors that did a great job
* history is resume to a point that if you dont know it already you will be lost
* graphics could be better (worse comparing dbz/naruto games)
* fighting could be better too (comparing what we can get from dbz/naruto games)
* characters not really well balanced - there are some Saints that are a little stronger/easier to use then others (but all games have balance issues and maybe a patch can solve this)

I have been an avid fan of the Borderlands series since I first played the original installment back in 2008. Below is my personal impression of its pros and cons:
+ Engaging, immersive gameplay.
+ Fun and worthwhile cooperative multiplayer experience.
+ Graphics and art-style is timeless, aging through the generations remarkably well.
+ Creative characters, both playable and NPC.
+ Great level design and set-dressing. There are lots of little details to find and explore.
+ Detailed universe, with a captivating storyline that further motivates you to keep playing.
+ Great gameplay balance with the leveling system, making progress feel rewarding.
+ Varied characters with a range of possible play-styles.
+ Excellent compatibility in terms of your computer's performance. Even low-end computers with generic graphic cards can comfortably play (with reasonable quality adjustments).
+ LOADS of extremely entertaining and creative DLC to play after you've finished the main story. DLC campaigns are also fairly priced.
+ Tiny Tina.
+ Meat Bicycles.
- No evident compensation for high latency in network play.
- No in-game method to view your ping. I often try judging my latency by how long it takes a bullet to leave my gun after firing.
- There's an anticlimax once a character has reached the highest possible experience level. Each subsequent kill and other progress after that, comes accross as less rewarding.
- A character becomes progressively more difficult to fully level up. Less experienced FPS players will likely find the tougher play-through modes more frustrating than fun. Playing with friends, especially in
or
is definitely recommended.
- Relatively predictable storyline for the main campaign, but still worthwhile.
Ultimately, I fully recommend this game, as well as the other titles in the series, despite their shortcomings. It's an experience I always look forward to, whether I get to play with friends, or when I just wing it solo. There's a unique joy in finding that occasional super-rare item, or popping the head off a cheeky psycho that wants to be buried upside-down!

I remember when I was a kid and I had to struggle to stay awake to watch Saint Seiya and other anime series on TV. I know all their names, constellations, techniques, fighting stances, remarkable phrases... Everything. When I look at the series now they seem a bit silly. But still, I am a die hard fan, and I vowed that I'd never buy another anime game if this one sucked. Thanks be to Athena it did not come to that...
The game follows a very similar style as DBZ Xenoverse (same game engine I suppose), with graphics going heavy on the idea of preserving the anime-feeling in the air and simple fight mechanics with simple button smashing and timing strategy. I could not find any of the original songs from the series, don't know if I still need to unlock them, but what I heard of BGM on the stages pleased me.
But of course, the objective here is not a complex fighting game like KoF, SF or MK... This thing shoots at the series' fans, so I'll tackle the matter from this angle: the game is a jab of nostalgia right in the kisser. Seeing those old friendly (and some not THAT friendly) faces again almost brings a tear to my eyes... But what got me were the voices. I am Brazilian, and voice-acting around here back in the late 80's and early 90's was, at least for me, top-notch... And the ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥s brought back almost all the voice actors from the original series. I laughed with joy like a child at every technique name they cried. I admit that it is not what it used to be. I don't know if the quality really dropped or it is because I remember the voices differently... But still, it touches me (in a decent way, pervs).
So, if you are a fan of the series, I really recomend it. It is a ticket to the Nostalgia Train.

Broforce is a fun, 16-bit arcade-style shooter, featuring a bunch of 1980's action stars rotating through the protagonist's slot. Each time you meet with your demise, you get to play as a different 80's action movie star. Each Bro has different and specific power-ups.
The game play is fun and fast-paced, requiring the KBO (keyboard operator) to take it slow when needed to plan what to do. You don't necessarily need to shoot everything because there is always a stealthy way to take something, even though it might involve an explosion or two.
Broforce is a great game that you will return to play a lot if you like your shooter action arcade-style and 16-bit. Definitely well worth the price. Looking forward to more from the developers!

I rarely play simulation games because I don't really understand their appeal. However, Euro truck simulator has successfully won won my approval. Playing this game invokes a number of feelings. It reminds me of a cross between having a sedative and being woken up being trolled by a bunch of gamers who just can't bear to see a bad review you've posted about a game they are oh so loyal to, and then finding their overreactions rather amusing. But let's contextualise these feelings within the events of Euro Truck simulator 2.
You can be quite happily driving along the motorway in your own sedate way, admiring the countryside and the occasional whistful mooing of cows. You've almost reached your delivery point. But suddenly, when changing lanes and you realise a damn vehicle has arrogantly occupied the lane that you were about to occupy in order to exit the motorway. The motorist scrapes into you and damages the precious cargo you were carrying. Enraged, you abandon your serene mood and start to ram the obnoxious twit so that he crashes into another lorry, hopefully causing a huge pile up. You smile as you drive up and out of the motorway knowing that although your cargo has been damaged justice has been served.
Good game.

If you are looking for a game when you are feeling down and need something to smile, just install this game and play a bit to get infected by the humongous ammount of happiness. The slimes seem mathematically designed to produce cuteness on industrials levels inside your brain; big eyes, big mouth, soft look, smaller than you, constantly emitting high pitched sounds...
This is not say that there are not mechanics involved, therey are similar to the ones you would find in "viva piñata" and so its more about constructing something slowly but constantly, while exploring the world and new slime species, so the game is dependent on content since you would see that it gets into a point where you reach your "apex farm" and there is not really much to do, thankfully the developers are still adding content around.
Don't expect much oposition in the game, slimes eat other slimes or die from hunger and sometimes they can go over your fence and scape, but once you get into the game they become minor annoyances and these fall more along the lines of carelessness than than actual challenges from the game.
So, as you see, the game is more about relaxing and feeling involved in a colourfull, fun and happy world, maximum escapism if you prefer.

Singleplayer is awesome, although it´s still only 6/7 hours playtime. It has a good story, but not completely new. Actually it´s the same story as Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 2. To keep it short: Good guy become bad guy.
A lot of new characters, better graphics and the cutscenes are just amazing!
Multiplayer is really good too, I did not have this 'CoD'-feeling since Modern Warfare 2 Multiplayer. The feeling that I could be playing this for a long time. The feeling that I could actually turn the tide and win the match with me team.
Besides the Ray-gun, the game is pretty balanced. Lot's of gamemodes, even a couple 'classic'-games, without the extra options. The new gamemodes in the game are things like: Uplink and Momentum. you can compare Uplink with the Unreal Tournament Bombing-run. Momentum is similar to Capture and Hold.
Lots of guns, lots of outfits. Everyone can customize their character to their own likings. Even the logo is completely customizable. Too bad that not many people make their own logo, as I see in-game, when I check other people's characters.
There is also an 'Exo'-ability. Exo is used for a special ability, abilities like: extra movementspeed, (almost) stealth, shield, health regen, etc.
Exo Survival is a coop-game. A maximum of 4 players fight off waves of enemies. Upgrade your weapon's damage, your armor, etc. etc. Upgrading can be used for anything, guns, armor, exo, scorestreaks, grenades, etc.
It's a fun gamemode, although it takes quite long before it gets really difficult. There is also a bonus wave, around wave 100, zombies. That's the only thing with zombies at the moment, there are rumors of a zombie-DLC coming soon.
Wave 100 is easy to reach, it's not that hard to stay alive.
- Customizable logo's
- Customizable characters
- Balanced gameplay
- Lot of actions
- (almost) No noobtube.
- Lots of gamemodes
- Exo survival upgrade opportunities
- Ray-gun is too OP, needs to be balanced
- Singleplayer same story as Modern Warfare 2
- Zombies only in Bonus round Exo Survival
8/10

At the moment, there's a lack of dedicated servers and severe lag/framedrop issues on the PC;  Particularly for AMD users.  This often makes the multiplayer portion of the game almost completely unplayable, especially on certain maps.  Some maps also take an unusual time to load even with RAM/CPU way above the requirements listed.  This includes certain single player maps for the main storyline.
If these issues can be fixed, then I can fully recommend this game and judging from the other reviews, it looks like a lot of people feel the same.
