Eh, theres not really much to say about this one. Really, there isn't... I think. Here we go:
Meet Cantus, a reclusive thirteen year old chap. For him, he perceives the motion of life as nothing but a drag, and everything that doesn't constitute remote significance to him is dismissed as "noise", and his only passion resides within the virtues of seashells. He refrains from having any unwarranted interactions with other people, even with his own Mom. Overall he views his life devoid of any happiness. What an♥♥♥♥♥ because you know, God forbid the MC of a visual novel isn't a pretentious snob, right? To be frank, he is by far the most insufferable brat I have witnessed being shown in a game for a while. Though Cantus' views are relatable to
degree, players like me will not be able fathom how his character got past the scripting stage of development, as I sporadically pulled my hairs in frustration of his unimaginative demeanor in-game. During one decisive day in one of the beaches of our aquatic/tropical setting, he encounters the main plot device of this narrative, Maris. Over the course of a week, she tries to make Cantus' smile at least once with promises that she will do so, and maybe pry open the door of opportunity for him to be a more sociable person. One can consider Maris to be the polar opposite of Cantus, as her exuberant, loquacious nature proves so, and with that said the contrast between these two characters is perhaps the only redeemable aspect about this game other than the art, but practically anyone can construct and recognize contrast between two different entities, so this isn't all that special.
This narrative in general follows a very linear template. There are 7 days in this game, and for a good 5 or so the player/reader will find themselves following the format of having a momentary mischief with Maris, picking up one of the three seashells, sitting through MC's reminiscence of his early days, rinse and repeat. Perhaps the creators made this monotonous pattern with some sort of intention, but as a result of me being so dense as to not figure out why that is I will propose a certain notion: THERE WAS A BETTER WAY TO GO THROUGH WITH THIS. It must take the most absurd   reasoning to so much as presume that your audience
find this redundant. To cap things off, during Cantus' little reflection, the last few words of the day usually appear after the screen's fade to black. For that
. It's as if the writers really wanted to impart some sort of idea to me by the end of each of these days, and I have no inhibitions to claim that these guys...
.
This one isn't too much of an issue, but the choice-making features this game brings was also a let-down. There is no bad ending for making the wrong choice, but rather that
choice can only be made once, to add some extra dialogue, and should the player make that same choice again instead of commencing the daily search of seashells, the MC blatantly denies, DENIES your choice, holding you at an inextricable bind until you make the correct choice that proceeds the plot. It's silly, but at least the choices were there to be made, and honestly the game has the prospect of being worse if there were more than one route.
In the nitty-gritty of things, it is imperative that a story well expresses it's themes if it wants to have any creditable substance in any form. This is my biggest gripe with this game, as it fails to preserve it's themes of social isolation for the entire game. I wish not to adorn my review with long spoiler bars, so I'll keep it simple. What it does wrong it that it manages to ignore the entire emotional (I use this term lightly) drive of the game, and turns the entire quintessence of the plot on it's side by the end of the reading. This was something I witnessed in a more famous novel, Tomoyo After, and it nettles me to no end. To my interpretation, the entire main idea of the game was turned into a more concrete one just for the sake of players not screaming at their screens saying "WTF WAS THAT EDGY TRASH?". I can't stress how disappointed I am by this, just like everything about this game.
It's free and all, but I implore you, no. It's a waste of time.

So, i'm setting this on recommended - but i'm very conflicted as the game technical difficulties pull it down immensely from what is a VERY good stealth/action sequel to the original game.
The game was gifted to me by a viewer of my content, so thanks be to him.
Video:
Text:
Lets start of from the top - The technical issues with the game are not excusable. From shaders that mess up, to collision detection that fails, models that clip into terrain and objects... none of that is okay, and beyond that there are issues with the sound mapping AND the FPS is fluctuating wildly. I'ts not Arkhem Knight levels bad, but it is bad.
So on those reasons alone, it is very valid to hold of purchasing the title.
But, why did i put it on recommended then?
Dishonored 2, for all it's technical issues, does everything else extremely well.
To start with the meat: the stealth/action gameplay is extremely enjoyable with varied options for each route and mission and tons of little bits of content to find and enjoy everywhere. From the extra bits of lore, to entire side-objectives that you can stumble on if you look around.
This applies for both characters... while both play the same missions, the difference is staggering in terms of abilities they have (and thus, how to complete objectives) and the way the world reacts to them. It's not quite "two games" but it feels very different while playing. Part of this is the EXCELLENT voice talent on display. While not perfect (especially corvo) its damned good regardless from the scullery maid to the big-bads.
The enemy Ai has received a bit of an upgrade from the first game as well, with more nuance and a bit more smarts (depending on difficulty). The game still lets you customize your experience extensively, going so far as to offer a "no powers" mode - which is really cool in and of itself.
Now, even with the various issues with the games performance: it looks very good. Especially the various details of constructs and buildings look great, and even when you are nose-to-nose with a crate you're hiding behind, it still look nice. Were only that the performance could match up.
Lastly, a minor critique is that the games missions feels disjointed and less of a cohesive whole and more of a somewhat-laced-together set of missions. Its not like HITMAN, there is overlap and continuity - but it is there.
So, decide for yourself - will you brave the technical issues for the great gameplay, or hold of on fixes... that i leave to you.
Also: ♥♥♥♥ Bethesda's new review "policy".

I'm not one to write reviews for many games, but Castlevania: Lords of Shadow
I must say, has some interesting designs.
I was actually surprised when I saw that Hideo Kojima, (The man behind some of the Metal Gear Series)
had his hands in this game, as I knew it was going to be quite difficult, even for the easiest settings.
The game is challanging but takes time to master. This isn't one of those "button-mashing"
games, as you really have to focus on attacks and abilites that work on certain enemies.
Castlevania has been known to have some good enviromental designs, along with the music. It has
its low and high points, making some fights seem intense or just something as simple as a puzzle
that makes you concentrate on the goal you're trying to reach.
With most games, a storyline is also what makes the game stand out as well. Whoever wrote the story
for Castlevania: Lords of Shadow, to make it intertwine with the history of other Castlevania games,
did a pretty good job.
Controls to me seem fluid because of how it was designed, and even parts of the camera angles
aren't to bad. I have seen a few comments here that complain about the combat systems/controls,
but, growing up playing the older Castlevania games, this is a huge difference and seems a lot easier.
I do enjoy the upgrades you recieve throughout the game as it uses a 'credit' based setup that makes
you want to reach that goal to see the new move sets that are placed. (Hell, some of the animations
are pretty well done.)
All-in-all I think for anyone who is a fan of the older Castlevania series, (back on the NES and SNES)
this wouldn't hurt to much to try out. (Even if you're the type that's into the storyline.) I am rather impressed
and was not disappointed when I bought it. There are times when you'll get frustrated in fights and
constantly have to restart, but, if you're the persistant type, this game is for you.

Playing this game was like getting shot back to 1986 when Saint Seiya popped out from the void of an artist's imagination and turned into a popular Japanese anime. Finally, after 29 long years of countless manga, anime/movie adaptions and five game releases, it is good to know that we have yet again been blessed with a sixth addition to the video game series!
Saint Seiya: Soldiers' Souls is based on a very old anime where you take the role of four Saints of Athena; Seiya, Shun, Shiryu and Hyoga -- and sometimes Ikki if he's not too busy being a badass. The Saints' jobs are focused on the constant protection of the world from numerous perils along with safeguarding Athena who, despite being a Goddess of War and Wisdom, tends to get herself endangered quite often. Clad in Cloth -- magical armor blessed from the empyreal constellations above -- the four Saints (and occasionally five) must battle against strong foes and maximize their true potential!
The game, like the show, is a part of the fighting style genre. The game play mechanics has increased and improved drastically since its predecessors. These Gods are equipped with a variety of attacks ranging from basic to heavy attacks along with special moves; it’s easy to execute successful combos, making this a great pick for those who are not skilled veterans to the genre and would like to start somewhere light and easy. The controls for combat are smooth and definitely feel quick; I enjoyed the wide range of different fighting styles each character had to offer along with a player roster of 72, so trying them all out will be a task in itself but won't feel like a chore.
The cinematics and graphics aren't at its optimal level, nor is it chiseled to perfection, making the main campaign feel lackluster every time a character is perceived having a traumatic moment. While playing it, the player will come to think, "But is it sad? I don't know, his eyes are too damn pretty to look at!" But it’s to be expected, it’s a fighting game and most fans of the genre don't care much for the emotional rollercoaster, which is what visual novels are for! The price of $59.99 is steep but it's understandable for a big name title since most games standard point is $74.99-79.99, nowadays, so I shouldn't complain. There is quite a bit of replay value, with a campaign that’s long in duration, CPU battle arenas, as well as online battles and ranking systems! For the dedicated and the skilled, this game is definitely for you! However, for those with short attention span, and lack skills like myself, not so much to pay full price but good to try whenever it goes on sale. You never know, Saint Seiya: Soldiers' Souls may be the gateway game to draw you into the fighting genre scene!

I recommend on getting this game if you're  a fan of RPG's. One thing I love about the game more so than the elder scrolls series and some other RPG's is the fact that once again, the combat system is fantastic(although they are using xbox control pop ups instead of teaching you what does what with the keys unless you check the keybinding and learn some things and set it up for yourself). They brought back some of the older weapons, and they are even better, with a new animation to the chaos blade and the other classic weapons, you'll enjoy them even more this time!
The level designs look awesome although the graphics are passable, it's not next gen or mind blowing, but if you like dark souls at all, you'll love these new map designs. As for the enemies, they look pretty good, especially the bosses which by far are some of the best bosses I have seen lately in any game! Not only do they look cool, but they will kick your♥♥♥♥♥as well if you make the wrong move but anyone who has played dark souls one, or demon souls knows that learning their attack pattern and forming a strategy and not over button smashing will go a long ways, and to be honest, I find most bosses in Dark Souls 2 allot harder than the first one of the series although I have to say the last boss is easier to beat than Gwyn from the first game.
The flaws the game has besides xbox buttons being shown on the screen is far little to complain about. One of the cons I didn't like was needing to go back to Majula over and over to level up(tho you don't need to level at all if you're good) but I'm complaining about this just because there is hardly anything to complain about, I mean the graphics aren't next gen as you'd think they should be.  One thing that is a legit complaint is the possible story to the game. Just like the other Dark Souls,  the game doesn't have many cutscenes at all(which can be good to some) but with an RPG as good as Dark Souls, they should start throwing in more cincematic scenes to give you a better  description on what the lore is about being the enemies, and the player. I will say Dark Souls doesn't disapoint with the difficulty because once again, you are thrown into the game with almost virtually no help and no clue on where to go and speaking of that, the game is a little linear at first but gets tricky after the first two, maybe three areas and there is tons of secrets in the game, so  at some point, you going to have to find a guide.
Another thing I can complain about is the scaling of the enemies and bosses because it seems no matter how much vitality or  vigorance you have, all bosses which drop you dead in one or two hits, maybe three tops. So what's the point of upgrading these stats if they are irrelevant? Also mages are once again have a easier time although they are very slow at first because of there being no spells to buy at the start worth while, and you'd have to constantly be conservative and not waste all the spells before the boss. So I made a mage first, I noticed it was tougher at the beginning of the game because of this but balances out, or should I say becomes overpowered later on, and oh any faith build using lightning spear which is a OP spell that can be gained from contributing to the sunbro covenant. As for melee classes, they seem pretty steady throughout the game but can struggle on some bosses but by far in my opinion the best starting class at first until later where the mage will out perform, especially in PVP.
I like that you can dual weild swords or greatswords, or just allot of combo's like having a staff in one hand and a sword in the other, or a shield, but there isn't too many good weapons that is gained in new game compared to new game+.
Overall, the game is  a solid RPG, I personally think it's as good as Dark Souls, if not better than Dark Souls, and you all should pick it up sometime and try it.
Must-buy for anyone who likes RPGs.

I'll divide this into two separate short "reviews", for SP and MP.
SINGLE PLAYER:
I'll start by saying that it was mostly enjoyable, much like a big budget action film, but it has multiple technical issues and design flaws.
First of all the game can't deal with mouse polling rates of higher than 125Hz without it messing with your aim, by randomly giving you high mouse acceleration, so it's adviced to turn your mouse polling down to 125Hz, if it's possible for you to do so.
The game has FPS stuttering issues too, at times, and the prerendered cutscenes are running at 30FPS (for "cinematic feel", I assume), but they too keep stuttering, and on top of that they're unskippable. There's a loading bar for the next mission, but I suspect it's complete bogus, as it never finishes until the cutscene is already over.
The game is full of  these predetermined events where you're supposed to do exactly as told, or you're punished by instant death, no matter what your difficulty is set to.
You could be playing on the easiest, and sponge all kinds of damage, but if you fail to do what you're supposed to in the events, you're punished with instant death.
Here's a couple of examples of the above.
The white pickup truck with a turret in the alley, during the mission where you save the prime minister of [????].
You could take it out with ease, if it wasn't for the fact that the car plays a role in the mission a little bit later, so they made it kill you instantly.
Then during the mission where you have to escape from Atlas with Ilona, and you're running through the streets, being chased by Atlas soldiers.
I had reached a checkpoint near the docks, and I had to backtrack for intel, but it was made impossible with some kind of an invisible line, where if you crossed it, you'd get OHK'd by a random bullet every time.
The truth is, the intel collectables do not fit this cinematic style of gameplay.
The checkpoint feature causes you to get stuck in places, where it's impossible to backtrack for the intel you missed.
Sometimes when it should be possible, you're met with an invisible border, that when crossed, causes you to "fail the objective" and the last checkpoint is loaded.
In fact, sometimes these invisible borders are so strict, that you'll cross them just by straying a tiny bit from the intended path.
You see that alley there? Could there be a hidden intel there? Nope, just another invisible line.
Exploding helicopters were cool. Kevin Spacey too.
MULTIPLAYER
+The exo movement is a welcome feature, and it adds nice fresh variety to the stale COD MP.
+The map designs aren't half bad.
+Graphics are pleasant.
Now let me tell you why you absolutely SHOULDN'T bother with COD:AW MP, if you are looking for a quality MP shooter experience.
-P2P, complete with the good old host advantage, and associated goodies.
-Killcams never match what actually happened on your screen, and we can thank P2P, netcode and lag for this, I guess.
-Simply awful spawns, this becomes especially apparent in FFA mode.
-Loot weapons with varying damage stats is an awful design, and ruins any chance a game had with the competitive crowd.
-Certain maps are so awfully optimized, that I suspect they were never playtested on PC AT ALL, these maps will cause stupid amounts of FPS stuttering, which makes them unplayable.
-Time-to-kill in general is stupidly low, and often you'll have no chance to react to being fired at, because you get notification of the opponent's first bullet, by the time he's fired 4-5 bullets in you on his screen.
That said, I'll probably continue playing the multiplayer a little longer, because I'm a masochist.
I'll update the list of pros and cons if I'll think of something to add.

Man, what can I say? I'm basically playing my character from San Andreas, busted out of Federal Prison after 10 years!

Still playable with up to 60 on a map, but you better let someone closer to the server drive. Much past that and it's not great. If you take Dota and combine it with World of Warcraft.
That's what it feels when playing Arena in SMITE, atleast for me. Arena is 5v5 game mode and it's what you would expect from "arena" map. Pure, fast paced action.
Honestly, i don't really play other game mods, except events. If i want to play classic long game, i can play Dota. When you played so much of other moba games, you most likely look for something different. But there are also many people who play classic map (and it's really well done imo). To each their own, important is possibility of choice.
Of course there are other game mods, here is the list:
- Classic (3 lanes, 5v5, doto style)
- Joust (1 lane, 3v3, smaller doto)
- Assault (1 lane, 5v5, ARAM)
- Siege (4v4, 2 lanes, siege towers)
- Arena (5v5, try not to die, kill everyone, have more tickets in the end)
- MotD (different each day, some crazy stuff here)
Each mod is 100% playable, no imbalanced sh.t going on (except MotD) and people play them all.
You can buy these items:
- gods (heroes)
- god skins
- voice packs
- portraits, ward skins, border frames, announcers, pedestals... (all of these are the least important imo, save your Gems for skins and voice packs)
There are two ingame currencies: Favor and Gems.
Favor is used to buy new gods and some skins. You earn Favor by playing games and loging daily.
Gems are premium currency. You can buy them via real money, or you can get them for free during various events and also by loging daily. With Gems you can buy everything, naturally you should buy the things you can't buy with Favor.
Game itself is absolutely NO PAY TO WIN. Real money can get you only cosmetic items.
I can't but recommend this game. It's really great. Try it, you might like it. And remember to take the daily bonuses!

throws you into a dark world of suspense and mystery from the very beginning - that is, if you let it. The ambience is astounding both visually and audibly - rising music, sounds of the house shifting, shadows cast over the unknown territory; all of sound and sight leave you feeling lost and endangered. Even better (or worse), the sanctuary of city lights glow just past the property, giving you hope whilst simultaneously taunting you. Other than a few glitches with the visuals,
does a good job of pulling your attention.
The voice acting isn't really the best, but it has it's moments. While the tones sometimes don't carry the urgency necessary, it certainly isn't the worst and it still aids gameplay.
The plot didn't consist of much, and was actually a bit confusing. The characters aren't very developed, but there isn't much need for an involved storyline anyway. The whole objective is to escape somehow, and
becomes a "do this, to do this, to do this" kind of thing which is prevalent in video games, and I enjoy it a lot in shorter ones! Whereas I, personally, put a lot of emphasis on ambience, the easy-to-follow objectives make it easy to submerge yourself into the world and get things done. Solving problems as they come is understandable in gameplay and it does not require involved characters.
The controls were interestingly - and enjoyably - simple, especially considering the open-world feel of the mechanics. It uses the basic walk, run, flashlight, and interact abilities but offers a lot of interaction with other objects. As unnecessary as this capability is for completing the game, it makes the player more mentally involved without complicating gameplay or ambience.
Overall,
was very enjoyable. The scares were well-timed and the suspense-builders were spot on. Although not a close encounter kind of horror, it's a great game for a slow scare. And, it's free, which is always a plus.

I try not to go into games with the mindset of comparing it to other games however, given that the developers of C:LoS almost assuredly went in with a strong conviction to copy almost every aspect of God of War, I feel like I don't really have a choice.
The game is pretty meh. The story is a generic avenge/save your wife plot. The combat only occasionally feels kinectic. The locations though somewhat exotic, almost always feel like throwaways. You never stay anywhere too long and, because the game never really introduces any of the locations, you won't give half a crap about the scenary, pretty though it might be. The mechanics are cheap and nothing beyond functional and the game treats you like a half-blind toddler with all its hints, glowing objects and ridiculuously simple puzzles. Like the supposed enemies you have to fight, this game has no soul. If I were to place it in the GoW franchise, including the handheld games, I would still put it a little ways under Ascension. In non-GoW terms, maybe a 5/10. Given that GoW was the pinnacle of its genre, having tasted the extraordinarily tight everything of that franchise, I'm probably being extra harsh on this knock-off. For people who have never played GoW, I suppose I might bump this game up to a 6/10.
If you're buying this game looking to scratch your God of War itch, it's probably not going to satisfy you. It certainly didn't satisfy me. However, if you're new to the genre, I suppose there's worse ways of spending your money. Even then, buy it on a sale; it's not worth the full price.
Graphically it is not a bad game, but akin to games like "the force unleashed 2" and kid's games, It does not have a lot more difficulty than mashing buttons and "fill the gap" puzzles

I really wish Steam had a "Meh" or some kind of middling type option cause at the end of the day that's how I feel about this game.
It's not horrible really. It's a God of War type game instead of the usual Castlevania gameplay with Shadow of the Colossus sprinkled in for 3 fights. The music is pretty great, as is the art direction. The gameplay isn't really bad at all either.
The story isn't that bad, not that great but Castlevania isn't really a big story kinda game anyway so who cares.
But then come the annoyances the game just pulls left and right.
From the awful and annoying joke enemies (Chupacabras) that break the pace of the game since ya have to track them down in order to get your items back to complete the level to the constant annoying puzzles that slow the game down to a crawl sometimes. The bosses and companions who repeat the same dialogue OVER AND OVER AND OVER ("GET THE CRYSTAL GABRIEL").
The snails crawl pace the game carries on with that feels like it'll just never end.
The silly decision to map sprint to double tapping the analogue stick which sometimes wouldn't properly respond when I needed it most. The silly hitboxes on certain attacks that shouldn't have hit me whatsoever.
So many times I wanted to end the game. So many times I thought about quitting but I stuck it through because I wanted to understand why people actually enjoy this game.
All I got was a migrane and wanting to never play this again. If you want God of War on PC, this might be your thing. And if you're a huge Castlevania fan you might hate it I dunno. This sure as hell isn't Aria of Sorrow or Dracula X in any sense of the word. If someone had to ask me if they should play this I'd recommend any other Castlevania over this.

Saint Seiya: Soldiers' Soul is a anime-based game, the setting is as the following, five Bronze saints were gathered and trained during their childhood, when the time was right, they were fated to protect Athena, namely Saori Kido (the goddess) and fight for the just cause.
She was supposed to be residing in her Sanctuary with her army of saints (the Gold Saints and the Pope) devoted to her, however, instead, the Grand Pope Arles pulls the strings in the shadows and steals the influence she should have had over those said saints by revealing lies to them, such as Athena alread being in the Sanctuary (but not showing herself due to her high status as a Goddess).
They indeed believed him and thus, to make sure he'd keep his reputation clean, he ordered one of his minions to end Athena's life with a golden arrow, and so, the five Bronze saints' quest to rescue Athena begins.
Overview:
Gameplay: 7/10
Saint Seiya: Soldiers' Soul is a fighting game which involves two buttons combinations as a layout, light and heavy attacks, the purpose of the game is pretty simple once you get used to it. Nonetheless, there's a variety of combos and features that will get you hooked onto your gamepad, I found myself hugging the controller because I was pushed to make full use of it. Most buttons, more or less, have a purpose, whether it's to recover, guard, or go on the offensive.
The "ultimate" attacks, named Big Bang Attacks here, are quite satisfying. Being faithful to the anime/manga, the scenes are immersive and the effects are magnificent, however, some of them take quite some time to set-up, you might be missing a few of those due to how different their start-ups may be on several characters, and that's a good thing, it adds to the variety and the obligation to gather knowledge of each character.
Some characters, however, will be doubles as their basic movesets do not change but their ultimate attacks do, I can understand why in this case.
Overall the gameplay is pretty solid, you'll find it quite interesting but not as innovative.
Optimization: 9/10
Dimps pulled off another great PC port, this time for the cult and nostalgic anime Saint Seiya, the port is similar to Dragon Ball Xenoverse, the graphical options are multiple and the scenery is wonderful. There are also more graphical improvements compared to the PS4 version, which encourages PC gamers to pick up the game and have faith in future adaptations receiving good ports.
The settings are basic, some, however, are unusual, ranging from Shadows to Light effects, as well as Anti-Aliasing.
And that's encouraging enough for PCs of all ranges.
Soundtrack: 8/10
The music, some being taken from previous games, is quite fitting to the scenario, atmosphere and stages. You'll feel moved by some melodies and blood-boiled by others, each piece of melody that plays in a scene brings out the emotions that our Bronze saints are feeling. Joy, sadness, despair, and so on.
The menu BGMs are also representative of the old/Sanctuar-esque era with noble knights serving justice standing around. It's stylish, good for the eyes and a quite good fanservice for the Saint Seiya watchers/readers out there.
Graphics: 8/10
The graphics are loyal to the anime, facial expressions, backgrounds, character models and so on, they're very well made. The stages are superb and various, the background effect in them makes it easy to know which is which.
Although, certain cutscenes felt a bit rushed, to the point where the background was bland, the animations were clunky at times but you can easily overlook that since it only happens in a small handful of cutscenes, and they're barely noticeable, the slow movement makes it seem as if they were relaxed though.
But other than that, the armors were eye-candy, the reflection of them is wonderful, they're beautiful, both in design and effects, and when reaching the peak of your Seventh Sense (basically the Ultimate gauge), you'll want to not use it up just because of how splendid the armor set looks on each character.
Story Elements: 7/10
Elements were picked from the original manga, but despite that, a few of them felt rushed, namely the start of the game. You're thrown quite rapidly into the Sanctuary with a brief explanation on what happened previously and a small mention of the Bronze saints' background.
Some scenes will leave the new players discovering the anime confused because some elements were skipped to drive the scenario closer to its objective.
Still, if we put that aside, the explanations are well put together which makes it easy to remember and understand the general plot altogether.
Conclusion: 7.5/10
In the end, Saint Seiya: Soldiers' Soul delivers a quite solid fighting experience with some fan-service added on-top and challenges that will keep you busy for a while.
Unlockables and purchases are made in-game with the only DLC being Original Color Editions of two characters, Hades and Athena, and these barely matter to those who haven't watched nor read Saint Seiya yet.
There is plenty to collect and to complete as well as achieve with a decent list of achievements.
The Online Battle Mode is alright, it's composed of a Player Match menu and a Ranked Match one, one for stress-free battles and the other affecting the Leaderboards.
The game has a decent amount of hours to put into and the optimization is top-notch, Dimps has outdone themselves once again.
For newcomers, I do recommend the game if you like main scenario, which I recommend you to read to a point where you can judge whether to purchase the game or save the money for some other title.
For Saint Seiya fans, this is a must-buy as the optimization and the work put into the game makes it more than worth-while.

I recommend on getting this game if you're  a fan of RPG's. One thing I love about the game more so than the elder scrolls series and some other RPG's is the fact that once again, the combat system is fantastic(although they are using xbox control pop ups instead of teaching you what does what with the keys unless you check the keybinding and learn some things and set it up for yourself). They brought back some of the older weapons, and they are even better, with a new animation to the chaos blade and the other classic weapons, you'll enjoy them even more this time!
The level designs look awesome although the graphics are passable, it's not next gen or mind blowing, but if you like dark souls at all, you'll love these new map designs. As for the enemies, they look pretty good, especially the bosses which by far are some of the best bosses I have seen lately in any game! Not only do they look cool, but they will kick your♥♥♥♥♥as well if you make the wrong move but anyone who has played dark souls one, or demon souls knows that learning their attack pattern and forming a strategy and not over button smashing will go a long ways, and to be honest, I find most bosses in Dark Souls 2 allot harder than the first one of the series although I have to say the last boss is easier to beat than Gwyn from the first game.
The flaws the game has besides xbox buttons being shown on the screen is far little to complain about. One of the cons I didn't like was needing to go back to Majula over and over to level up(tho you don't need to level at all if you're good) but I'm complaining about this just because there is hardly anything to complain about, I mean the graphics aren't next gen as you'd think they should be.  One thing that is a legit complaint is the possible story to the game. Just like the other Dark Souls,  the game doesn't have many cutscenes at all(which can be good to some) but with an RPG as good as Dark Souls, they should start throwing in more cincematic scenes to give you a better  description on what the lore is about being the enemies, and the player. I will say Dark Souls doesn't disapoint with the difficulty because once again, you are thrown into the game with almost virtually no help and no clue on where to go and speaking of that, the game is a little linear at first but gets tricky after the first two, maybe three areas and there is tons of secrets in the game, so  at some point, you going to have to find a guide.
Another thing I can complain about is the scaling of the enemies and bosses because it seems no matter how much vitality or  vigorance you have, all bosses which drop you dead in one or two hits, maybe three tops. So what's the point of upgrading these stats if they are irrelevant? Also mages are once again have a easier time although they are very slow at first because of there being no spells to buy at the start worth while, and you'd have to constantly be conservative and not waste all the spells before the boss. So I made a mage first, I noticed it was tougher at the beginning of the game because of this but balances out, or should I say becomes overpowered later on, and oh any faith build using lightning spear which is a OP spell that can be gained from contributing to the sunbro covenant. As for melee classes, they seem pretty steady throughout the game but can struggle on some bosses but by far in my opinion the best starting class at first until later where the mage will out perform, especially in PVP.
I like that you can dual weild swords or greatswords, or just allot of combo's like having a staff in one hand and a sword in the other, or a shield, but there isn't too many good weapons that is gained in new game compared to new game+.
Overall, the game is  a solid RPG, I personally think it's as good as Dark Souls, if not better than Dark Souls, and you all should pick it up sometime and try it.

throws you into a dark world of suspense and mystery from the very beginning - that is, if you let it. The ambience is astounding both visually and audibly - rising music, sounds of the house shifting, shadows cast over the unknown territory; all of sound and sight leave you feeling lost and endangered. Even better (or worse), the sanctuary of city lights glow just past the property, giving you hope whilst simultaneously taunting you. Other than a few glitches with the visuals,
does a good job of pulling your attention.
The voice acting isn't really the best, but it has it's moments. While the tones sometimes don't carry the urgency necessary, it certainly isn't the worst and it still aids gameplay.
The plot didn't consist of much, and was actually a bit confusing. The characters aren't very developed, but there isn't much need for an involved storyline anyway. The whole objective is to escape somehow, and
becomes a "do this, to do this, to do this" kind of thing which is prevalent in video games, and I enjoy it a lot in shorter ones! Whereas I, personally, put a lot of emphasis on ambience, the easy-to-follow objectives make it easy to submerge yourself into the world and get things done. Solving problems as they come is understandable in gameplay and it does not require involved characters.
The controls were interestingly - and enjoyably - simple, especially considering the open-world feel of the mechanics. It uses the basic walk, run, flashlight, and interact abilities but offers a lot of interaction with other objects. As unnecessary as this capability is for completing the game, it makes the player more mentally involved without complicating gameplay or ambience.
Overall,
was very enjoyable. The scares were well-timed and the suspense-builders were spot on. Although not a close encounter kind of horror, it's a great game for a slow scare. And, it's free, which is always a plus.

I played a couple of hours a long time ago and I stop playing because back then I did not really want to play this game. Today I decided to try and play again from the beginning, but for some reason, the developers thought that no one would want to start playing the game again or start a second playthrough, so there is no option to start a New Game. What kind of stupid game feature is this?
Of course, you can start a new game by deleting the save files manually, but you also have to disable the Steam Cloud so there will be no more save sync and save backups. Thank you but no. This is not an option for me.
As a result, I have another garbage game in my library that I cannot restart properly from the beginning to refresh my experience because I completely do not remember the plot, how the game started and how to play.
I'm already tired of this game at the beginning of the second chapter, so I did not even bother to finish it. Especially after I played Lords of Shadow 2 which is much more enjoyable.
First of all the fixed camera is just terrible. Often an enemy will be attacking from outside of the borders of the camera, or the protagonist is not visible behind the big enemy, or the camera changes suddenly if you move to another location in the middle of the battle.
Secondly, Quick Time Events. For me, it spoils the gameplay and I do not like them in any game and this game has a lot of them. It's good that they can be turned off in the second game.
To this, I can also add manual confirmation of the loading last checkpoint after each death. Why not just do it automatically?
The combat is kinda OK, but it didn't get me like in the second part. Mostly because the weapon does too little damage even to low enemies and during a blow, there is no sense of impact, if you understand what I mean.
Also, you need to dodge a lot of time due to lack of stun attacks, so usually I had to roll around an arena to gather all enemies on it in order to quickly deal with them.
In general, buy the second game. It's not perfect, but it's better than this one.

If you take Dota and combine it with World of Warcraft.
That's what it feels when playing Arena in SMITE, atleast for me. Arena is 5v5 game mode and it's what you would expect from "arena" map. Pure, fast paced action.
Honestly, i don't really play other game mods, except events. If i want to play classic long game, i can play Dota. When you played so much of other moba games, you most likely look for something different. But there are also many people who play classic map (and it's really well done imo). To each their own, important is possibility of choice.
Of course there are other game mods, here is the list:
- Classic (3 lanes, 5v5, doto style)
- Joust (1 lane, 3v3, smaller doto)
- Assault (1 lane, 5v5, ARAM)
- Siege (4v4, 2 lanes, siege towers)
- Arena (5v5, try not to die, kill everyone, have more tickets in the end)
- MotD (different each day, some crazy stuff here)
Each mod is 100% playable, no imbalanced sh.t going on (except MotD) and people play them all.
You can buy these items:
- gods (heroes)
- god skins
- voice packs
- portraits, ward skins, border frames, announcers, pedestals... (all of these are the least important imo, save your Gems for skins and voice packs)
There are two ingame currencies: Favor and Gems.
Favor is used to buy new gods and some skins. You earn Favor by playing games and loging daily.
Gems are premium currency. You can buy them via real money, or you can get them for free during various events and also by loging daily. With Gems you can buy everything, naturally you should buy the things you can't buy with Favor.
Game itself is absolutely NO PAY TO WIN. Real money can get you only cosmetic items.
I can't but recommend this game. It's really great. Try it, you might like it. And remember to take the daily bonuses!

An Amazing Moba with frequent action packed gameplay. The game mechanics are friendly to anyone willing to give this "down-to-earth" camera angle moba game a legitimate chance. It isn't league, It isn't Dota 2, Its smite and its- its own game. There is no point comparing the three.
one of my favorite features I like about this game is its ability to rent gods. You may rent gods temporarily using the in-game reward money similar to influence points in League (But they are called "Favor" here ) and play the god for a predetermined amount of time (and after the time is up, you can just do it again! ;D ) You can also buy the god with the same Favor points or use Gems (The paid currency) to buy the god quicker then earning it.
The previously mentioned Gems can be bought using real money or earned by playing during special events and by Logging in for the login reward. (So technically you can get anything in the game for free in due time..)
Every God has a special set of skins that can be bought with both Favor or Gems and other skins that can only be bought using Gems. Every god has prestiege skins that are unlocked by prestieging (collecting worshippers by winning) these skins can be bought for favor after you unlock them.
Gameplay
----------------------
Smite gives you six different gamemodes:
-A circular arena map
-A jaged Single lane map with no recalling (similar to howling abyss)
-A semi stright single lane map with two connecred jungles
-a two lane map with a single jungle in the middle
-a three lane map with a surrounding jungle for each lane connected
and a random gamemode that changes every half a day.
You have your typical Mid, Top (long lane)  and bottom (short lane)
Aside for that the rules are similar to any other moba so I will not go into that.
anyways 9/10 would definetly play again.

Go ahead and take a cliched non-existent ''America Fu*k Yeah'' 80's action movie story about bunch of macho Americans liberating someone/something. Add some Metal Slug rapid action that meets Contra along the way. Add all destructible terrain that will either help you or completely ♥♥♥♥ you up. Add every single ultra macho action hero of the 80's as a playable character. Make it easy at first and then pretty hard later. What you get? A platformer with balls. Broforce hits and it hits hard in the eye - using action nonsense cliches paired up with some arcade shooting, you're getting an awesome platformer that makes you want more and more. It will bring out your inner 80's hero, it will make you grab that VHS rip (or even the tape if you still have it) of your favourite flicks and rewatch it with same enthuisasm all over again. For all of you kiddos that don't get it - no, "The Expendables" is not an original idea. Yes, it is a parody based on previous movie careers of all the actors.
Broforce takes you back when political correctness was non existent and there was no gender correct language nor ''other'' option in gender section. Males were males, females were females, we've fought hard and loved hard. And Ripley was one hell outta chick, just as she is today.
Full Broforce release packs more force, it's polished, bug free and hard when it comes to surviving later levels.

I have played every game in the series since CoD2 (my favorite) and I can honestly say that this title is right up there next to my favorites. The new mechanics of the game and future tech change up the gameplay enough to keep it interesting and avoid just being a re-skin of older titles in the series. Some players may dislike the changes but I think for most it will breathe new life into Call of Duty, and it may attract new players to the series because it isn't just a restamping of last years game. The story is pretty decent for CoD and is well structured. The acting quality is also quite good including Kevin Spacey’s character.
Performance wise the game is great. It is very responsive and has many PC specific options. I have had no issues holding a steady 60 fps on max settings. There have been moments in the game that I needed to remind myself that this is a CoD title. It is miles ahead of Ghosts in the performance and visuals department. (and every department) Overall just a great PC port.
Multiplayer is great and really mixes things up. It is faster than previous games though and does it well, just feels a little different. However the HUGE CON of this game is that there are no dedicated servers, so lag and hacking are major issues right now. If MP is your gig you may want to hold off for now!

I haven’t played a ton of CSGO. But in what time I’ve spent with it, there is one incredible and unexpected play that stands out from the rest.
The game started out as any other. I was a terrorist, playing Dust II on casual, warming up for a competitive. It was your typical pre-round warmup, and a couple of CTs tried to rush the spawn through B Tunnels. They picked off a couple of our guys, but not before retreating to the cover of Bomb-site B. They didn’t go without a fight, and one threw a nade, which had no effect (or so I thought).
Taking my fallen comrade’s M4A1, I ran down to Outside Tunnel, about to proceed to get rid of the CTs at B. It was then that I noticed something that shouldn’t have been there. It was just sitting there, right in the middle of the Tunnel Entrance.
It was the soccer ball.
Now, I have no doubt that if you play Counter Strike then you know which one I’m talking about. It’s the one outside of Terrorist Spawn that moves when you shoot it or run at it. So anyway, moving on. Why was it there though? Well, somehow it got blasted down by the grenade that the CT threw, and then kicked into the tunnel by one of our guys. Instead of trying to get rid of the CTs at B, our job was simple; Get the ball to bomb site B.
So we did. Almost. Completely forgetting that B was where the CTs were, we ran through like idiots, to be shot, of course. But we were so close that I could almost taste the glory. I could almost smell the glory, and hear the cheers of glory, and see the crowds of people cheering gloriously, and yeah, you get the point. We were really close. But a warm-up was nothing compared to the real thing; no one really tried in it. And now CTs were going to push back.
But so were we.
“Guys,” I typed into the team chat, “Help me get the ball to B.” One guy, reluctantly said “Ok, I’ll help,” before another said “Me too.” Wait, that was it, you ask? Just us three? Well you’re damn right it was. And so started our mighty crusade for glory, little to no recognition and a long journey through blood, sweat and soccer balls.
As soon as the game started, we pushed. Despite everyone else going for Long Doors and a couple through Mid, we proceeded to B. It was a trouble to even get it down the stairs, let alone into Tunnels. And in our attempt, we were killed by a CT. This was going to be just a tad bit harder than we had first expected. Now it was second round. We ran for the ball. A couple guys didn’t really understand, thinking it was a game and kicking it the wrong way. Once we explained the very grave situation though, they very politely stepped out of the way, and even helped a bit.
Now it was third round, and the third that CTs had won. We were almost there this time, only to be stopped in our tracks by an Incendiary thrown our way. The ball was in the Tunnel, and we were outside still. The clock was ticking. 47 seconds (well actually, it probably wasn’t that exact number, I just chose that because it sounds more dramatic to have a specific number). As soon as that fire cleared, we were on the ball in an instant. Nothing would stop us, not even the guy camped out next to the entrance who shot one of us in the back. There were four of us left to carry it now, until two CTs from Lower Tunnels came to finish us off. One of the Terrorist threw a smoke before he died, and the two of us left were now concealed to finish this fight. There was one guy at B, who killed me, but fortunately my team-mate shot him with an AWP. The ball was nearing towards B, and let me tell you, glory tasted like a friggin three course meal.
That was, until, we heard the sound of the knife stabbing into his back, and heard the “Ughff” of failure and saw the ‘COUNTER TERRORISTS WIN’ screen.
Now I don’t remember much about the rounds after this really, as they were pretty forgettable and unimportant. Also we were just really focused on the ball to care about anything else, so to save you the time (which clearly you don’t need as you’re reading my insanely overlong story), I’ll just skip to the final round.
So it was the final round, and here we were with two wins and the CTs with seven. This was the decider. It was now or never. It was all or nothing. This time, five others came to help us, and so did the other two after they realised what was going on. Without them, we may not have gotten past the Tunnel Entrance; they cleared for us, died for us, scouted for us, threw nades for us and stuck by us. But now things weren’t looking so good. It was down to the three of us that this whole mission (goal, if you will) started with. If that seems unrealistic that’s because it is, I’m still not entirely sure why it was us but it was. I’ll also call them Rob and Mike so as not to confuse the two.
There were six CTs left. Six. Damn. We were struck with the realisation that we may not finish this after all, and had a mini 4 second breakdown. But we could do this, and by gaming glory if we could do this, then we would do this. Rob went out to clear B. Nothing to do really, as surprisingly there were none there. But wait...
We heard the shot before we knew what was going on. Rob had been shot with an AWP. In rage, I ran to shoot the sun on a beach; lined up my crosshair, pulled the trigger. Bam. Dead. I ran back to Mike, who was standing with Rob. Wait, standing WITH Rob? It was then that the realisation hit me that Rob wasn’t dead. He took that shot like a freakin legend, right up the Valley too, if you know what I mean. It was just us three and the ball. Everything went into slow motion (okay, no, it didn’t actually, but it’s more cinematic for you to see it this way).
One final kick was all it would take. Mike kicked the ball. It rolled through the Tunnel; past the bodies, past the littered guns, heading towards the light at the end of the Tunnel. The proverbial one, not the actual Tunnel. And it rolled like a beast, to greatness, to glory. We followed it intensely, not paying attention to our surroundings. Until we saw where we were; in bomb site B.
YES! WE DID IT! We started shooting the air and each other like maniacs, dancing around, jumping on the blocks, spray painting. And then the CTs came. I can almost imagine their conversation.
“Well, I’ll be damned,” says one. “They actually did it, the suns on beaches,” says another. And then they threw away their guns; everyone did. It was knives only, and they started dancing around as well. It was majestic, everyone dancing around happily in a circle. And then we had cake and—
Okay, well, none of that actually happened. I mean, we got the ball to B, yeah, but the CTs didn’t start dancing. In fact, the CT’s conversation probably went more like this.
“What the hell are those idiots doing?”
“They look like headless chickens.”
“Who gives a damn, just shoot them.”

Castlevania: Lords of Shadow still looks great for a game released in 2013, and it runs surprisingly well on my low spec i3 laptop. Top notch voice acting from Robert Carlyle and Patrick Stewart, good musical score, immersive environments, sheer hack and slash fun with a chain-whip, and the climbing is actually pretty good. It played really well with my FC30 Pro xinput compatible controller too.
There's a lot to love about this game, but the camera is not one of those things. I get that a fixed position camera was chosen to give the game a more cinematic quality, but I'd rather be fighting a badly implemented camera that I can control with the right thumb stick on my controller than having no manual camera rotation at all.
The only other negative is that the bonus DLC content included in the "Ultimate Edition" felt a bit sloppy. These extra chapters use concept art animated into cut-scenes, force you to play as another not-very good character for some sections, and has some of the worst fixed positions for the camera in the game. Ultimately the bonus content felt like a let-down after a game that got so much right.
Castlevania: Lords of Shadow is a great game if you can deal with the use of a fixed position camera. I did, but only just.

Castlevania: Lords of Shadows is a bitter sweet symphony that could deliver either a satifying or frustrating experience, depending on what you find enjoyable in an action-adventure game.
The overall design of this game is brilliant (characters, enemies, environments, items, interfaces, music, etc.) making this game a true gem from the gothic art style. Alongside, the story it shows is interesting (even tough the main character motive is rather weak). Just these reasons are enough to actually give this game a try and, if you find these aspects appealing, this game will not disappoint. One thing to mention tough is that the game has a segmented narrative, in which the player will need to use the imagination to connect the dots between segments and follow the stotyline.
However, it lacks considerably in its gameplay and  its mechanics. Castlevania: Lords of Shadows offers 3 main gameplays scenarios for the player (exploration, puzzle solving and combat) and it fails to deliver in all of them.
Exploration is used to find power-ups and other collectables the game offers. It hinders this process with a system that forces you to contantly re-visit levels over and over again, until  you finally are equiped with the right upgrade. But probably the most dissapointing aspect in this regards is the abuse of invisible walls that make exploration limited and, in some special levels, it punishes the player for exploring, making impossible to backtrace along the level and forcing to start of all over again if you accdentally went to far ahead on a path. This mechanics may encorage re-playability, but it does it in a disappointing, frustating and uncreative way.
Puzzle solving is found all over the game. They are in itself very visually appealing thanks to the beautiful design scenarios, but the depth and complexity if the puzzles (with very few exceptions) are pretty much non-existent. Most of the puzzles are so obvious that they are already solved by the game showing you a cinematic of the surrounding area. The game try to improve this very superficial complexity by throwing you hordes of enemies while trying to activate a swicth or turn a pillar, or by playing unfair against the player, changing the rules of the puzzle if you are doing good in it (I'm looking at you beast chess).  It feels that this puzzle element was added to the game in order to add more content, but what it does is leaving the player with false sense of improvement and annoyance.
The main mechanics of this game is its combat. It offers a wide variety of combos, secondary weapons and upgrades, all of them combinable with the 2 kinds of magic. This gives a considerably big variety of options for the player to experiment. However, this in practice become pointless thanks to the simplicity of how combat is implemented. The overwhelming majority of the combat in this game follows 2 predefined recipies: 1. If it's an small enemy, pull them to you and the game will trigger an action-secuence in which, you press a button and the enemy is dead or 2. hit them with your basic attack 2-3 times and dodge. The worst is that these patterns apply boss fights as well. At the end, the game has a very elaborated combat system that gives the illusion of depth and strategy, but is useless thanks to the way combat is presented to player.
Overall, Castlevania: Lords of Shadows is a game that is visually astonishing, simple, accesible and offers a facelift to one beloved franchise. However, it has such detrimental flaws in the fundamentals of its video game mechanics, that it may give a rather poor experience to more experienced players.

Finally a game that simulates the part of my job where I'm snooping around other people's homes and got chased by the owner.
But in all seriousness though, this game is pretty well made, and possibly the best free indie horror games on Steam recently after Medusa's Labyrinth.

I know it's free and all but... it is very buggy. The voice acting makes me cringe (the cop does a better job than the main character). And with there being absolutely no instruction, I grossly underestimated the complexity of the puzzles in the game. But then once I figured out the first one, all the rest were way too easy. I found the first ending, going over the scaffolding. I tried to get out the garage for another ending, but I got hit by the guy, and when it loaded my check point, I kept falling through the floor into nothingness. So, I have no idea how that will end. But don't really care enough to play it again...
Also, devs, as cool as lens flares are, if you're trying to make it a realistic first person experience, keep in mind the human eye doesn't see lens flares. So unless you're supposed to be seeing all this through a camera, there was no need for a lens flare on the moon.

Despite some intrigue early on and a somewhat creepy atmosphere at certain points, the story makes very little sense from what we're told, and the puzzles all rely on making sure you actually found all the tiny pieces required to complete them rather than any real tests of logic. There's definite potential, and I'd encourage the creator to keep trying, but Blameless is a resounding "meh."

First of all I have finished a lot of runs in Dishonored 1 and from the start picked very hard and went for non lethal ghost.
The Story starts off interesting for people who played the first game but I can see it not being so good for players who have not played the first one. After the main plot has pretty much revealed itself it gets a lot more like: who is that guy and what did he do? Do I know her from the first game and how is she back in this one? All these questions had me going strong into the first hours of gameplay where pretty much none of these are answered and even more characters are introduced. So it is like every story from Bethesda games. But fear not you will get all your answers once you get past the 5th mission.
I would give the story a solid 7/10 for players who like the whole returning characters thing.
If you just take the story as it is without any prior knowledge I would think a 6/10 would still be in it.
The graphics look very similar to the first game but I think that's a good thing. It feels like Im still in the same universe but everything is just a bit brighter, which makes sense seeing that we are in the south. Non or less some textures look squishy or not even fully finished but that's a minority and you don't really notice it while playing. The lighting effects in this game are quite pretty and not overused so a bonus point from me since I don't like god rays blinding you everywhere.
So the graphics get a 8/10 from me.
Obviously the gameplay is the most important thing and I have to say it outdid the first game.
When playing as corvo you pretty much have the same powers as in the first game just with more fancy upgrades.
But the real fun is playing as Emily imo. Her Powers are innovative very different from corvos and give the experience you play a whole different game. The upgrade system is well made and lets you plan ahead. And as always you can build your character around your playstyle. Some of the combos with Emily´s abilities are so much fun. For example the Domino ability is not only useful but can be used for trolling too. Tie the executioner to the victim and once he killed his victim he dies too. Gave me some good laughs.
One of the coolest new features is the "timepiece" which you get near the end of the game. It lets you shift between the present and the past. You have to solve puzzles in the past to move forward in the present and so it becomes a kind of time travel game which brings a lot more to it and I really hope to see more of this in future DLC. What you do in the past has effects on the present for example you burn a dead wolfhound in the past which is infected with bloodflies so the nest does not grow in the future and you can enter the room in the present. This comes to shine when you make the final decision in this mission but I will not go into that too much as it would be a huge spoiler. I am gonna say that much, whatever you do to your target will change the present drastically.
Where we come to the multiple ways of solving thing. It has been in the first game that you can decide to kill or neutralize your target which is pretty much just the same but in more creative ways I would say. And when you spare key persons instead of killing them they will sometimes evolve the story even more and give you something in return. So think twice about who to kill and who to spare.
The gameplay is great. It feels slower than the first game but at the same time more dynamic which makes it better than the first game imo. I would give it 9.5/10. Why not 10/10 you ask? That's only because some of the abilities are not doing what they are supposed to some of the time which is annoying but forgivable even if you play ghost non lethal.
Lastly I would like to finish of with the performance. All I read here is terrible optimized. This game is unplayable. Don't buy it till its fixed and stuff like that. Sure its not perfect but I can play it on stable 60 fps most of the time. Some of the areas it drops to 40-50 and only in one area I had it around 30 which was only 1 or 2 minutes. I have a medium class PC with a gtx970 and a I5-4590 and I can play it pretty smooth. I have no input lag at all and when you turn out mouse smoothing it feels good.
Sure its not constant 60fps everywhere like other AAA games but they are gonna fix it soon so I would not get into this too much and try it out for yourself. I give it 6.5/10 for performance as it is but I will change this review once it is fixed.
My end result is that Dishonored 2 is a great game with a good story and incredible gameplay. It is a good experience for every FPS or Sneak player out there and even with its current performance you should give it a try.
Its a must have for fans of the first game and I for my part have a blast playing it.
Trying to get all the achievements next that I have the 2 most annoying out of the way.
Have fun playing this awesome game and if you look past the performance you can give it a thumbs up yourself to counter all those negative nancys out there.

Go ahead and take a cliched non-existent ''America Fu*k Yeah'' 80's action movie story about bunch of macho Americans liberating someone/something. Add some Metal Slug rapid action that meets Contra along the way. Add all destructible terrain that will either help you or completely ♥♥♥♥ you up. With about 15+ hours, depending how much you explore, how often you fail and how high or low you set the difficulty, Lords of Shadow is perhaps the most atmospheric brawler I've ever played. Setting, design, story, everything here is pretty enjoyable and even brilliant at times. This edition includes 14 chapters with a varying amount of levels, in which you jump, fight, explore, solve puzzles and fight mighty bosses. And boy, those bosses are all pretty varied and fun. Most enemies even require you to change your approach and they all fit thematically into the various, gorgeous landscapes. The story is one of tragedy and hope, and I won't spoil anything here for obvious reasons, but it's gonna be quite a ride. Narration and cutscenes are all pretty neat (well apart from maybe that one cutscene that seemingly never ends and revels too much in itself...you'll know it when you'll see it).
Combat is pretty straight forward at first with only 2 attacks available, but the more enemies you defeat, the more puzzles you solve (and don't auto complete, which is a thing for most), will earn you sweet currency with which to unlock more and more combos and moves. Through story progression alone you will also get new special abilities that are required to beat the game. Enemies are also vulnerable to different special attacks. Lycans for example don't really like silver daggers, while vampires just die to holy water. And the game lets you pull up an overview of the monsters and their weaknesses at any time. So, all is well, right? Unfortunately...not.
Let's start with the combat system...while a healthy amount of combos and upgrades and special abilities is nice, I often found myself not able to use them properly, because combat is often so hectic and you are mostly surrounded by swarms of enemies that using those powerful abilities isn't really possible. Most have a decent wind up time and any hit will cancel the move. Others will drain your complete mana storage in about a second and getting that back requires you to hit things while not getting hit yourself and then absorb the magic...or find limitless wells of magic, of which there are a few in most levels. In the end I had to resort to a few basic moves and combos like the "chainsaw" or whatever it was called . Many of the bigger enemies also take way too much punishment. And remembering all those different moves is another matter, but luckily you can always look them up conveniently.
The second big offender is indirectly tied to the combat...the controls in this game are not rebindable (at least for controller, but I think mouse/kb is the same). Just an example: block and dodge roll are on the same bloody button. Blocking in this game, however, is pretty essential I'd say, but as soon as you try to block and move the left stick your character will roll instead. This causes numerous issues: a) you just didn't block and open the enemy up for a counter attack, b) you just rolled somewhere and got hit and c) several special moves also require you to press the left trigger + something else...but you just dodged, because your brain was trained that characters need to be facing a certain direction and that you could change that direction while blocking...nope. This really annoyed me. There's a special attack with your gauntlet, but positioning your character, then stop moving and pressing that combination of buttons is atrocious and never really worked for me. The whole control scheme would need an overhaul in my opinion. Have a dedicated block button and a dedicated roll button or use the right stick for something...oh and pressing the sticks to collect magic during a fight is also...meh to be honest.
Then there are the puzzles which require you to recall that you have a move, that apart from learning it 10 levels ago you've never used, is required here. Shadow magic daggers anyone? Had to actually check the internet for 2 or 3 of those...and if the only hint is "maybe you can break through here", well screw you...Gabriel has at least a couple moves that would suggest a breakthrough were possible.
Another frustration is movement itself. The game generally does not allow you to move outside of its strict bounds, until it requires you to do it. That moment when you just fell to your death, because suddenly your character would NOT stop at the edge...uuuuuuuuuuuugh. Jumping and platforming in this game is also pretty terrible thanks to the camera, which I will get to in a moment. And when you get the double jump...ugh...it's the weirdest double jump you've ever seen and it ♥♥♥♥ed me over more than once.
On to the camera: it's fixed. Always. Most of the time it doesn't do a terrible job, but it regularly ♥♥♥♥s up your movements, when there's a sudden screen change and your forward now becomes your backward or left or whatever. Extremely annoying. This also means you can't look around and look for hidden collectibles, you just have to trust the camera. You don't have those camera stuck in wall issues as in other games, but this solution is also not so great.
Quicktime events: I can understand adding those to a game, but when any one mistake in such an event means repeating the whole section of (usually) a boss fight, they're just not that well designed. In this game you are required to press X when the bigger circle enters the smaller circle. Too early or too late and you have to do it all over again. Happened a few times. Oh, and pressing RT to hold on is ok the first few times, but after minutes of hanging onto a boss it gets kinda old and annoying.
Brotherhood Arks include upgrades for your weapons. I've gotten one of them. They are not required, but it is still annoying that you can't get 95% of them in your first playthrough, because you don't have the necessary abilities...it just means you will have to replay those levels at a later point in time...and who does that? Let's be honest. Maybe in a second playthrough, when all levels are unlocked...until you get a new PC and all your saves are erased anyway most likely. Just not good design in my opinion. At least you can get all the gems in each level without backtracking.
Finally, the DLC bridges the gap between the actual ending of the game and you defeating the final boss. Suddenly there's an even greater evil you need to vanquish, yadda yadda....the story is meh, the presentation is ok, but it gives some important closure and re-introduces a fun character that you can even play for a few moments. It adds 2 more chapters with some more unique puzzles and a pretty intense, multi stage, boss fight that also includes platforming to an extent. Once you realise what the boss can do and HOW you can actually do more damage to him (don't use the charged attacks...just jump and regular attacks in the later stages...another boss fight that makes combos completely useless), he's actually pretty fun, but also a bland villain, unlike the ones in the main game...still an enjoyable 2 to 3 hour experience.
Reading all of that I should not recommend this game, but still I do, because of the atmosphere and because the game can still be easily completed by most people.

The worst Call of Duty title so far. It's more on the rails than ever, with invisible walls and level resets if you try to get creative. Flanking? Not in this game, solider!
Near invincible enimies with specific kill mechanics make a bee line for you (ignoring all other NPCs) but then stand on the spot obliviously why you take the time to them with the level's chosen mcguffin. If you go off track enemies can wipe you out instantly - forcing a checkpoint restart - but stay where you're supposed to and it's a cake walk - in fact your presence is barely required to move the story along (although graciously the friendly NPCs let you do almost all the actual shooting as you follow the Adventure Line to the end - certainly don't count on them to take the heat off you; they don't register at all with the enemy AI).
Much of the time it's one quicktime event to another (press E, then F then Space, then the left mouse button, then E again!). Wioefully, even the quicktime events are often bugged, forcing a replay (objects you are supposed to interact with have a habbit of getting stuck throughout the game). Half the time you won't know if you are suppose press, hold or repeatedly mash the given key, it doesn't always say what it want's you to do, you just have to trial an error through the replays and figure it out. Sometimes you get a choice of button to mash! Don't worry, the same scene plays out either way. Isn't choosing buttons fun?!
Of course you'll get to do all the things - man the mini-mech-suit foreshadowed early on, drive a tank, a boat and a bike and pilot an aircraft; except none of these things are actually a choice. You'll be forced to use them, only at specific times and only until you reach the invisible triggers. The obligatory "stealth" and "oh no, all your weapons are gone" stages are there, only worse than they've been before. Good: They are not even annoying. Bad: It's all just awful.
The unskippable custcenes with the out of sync and inaudible dialog where the FPS nose dives for no good reason were perhaps the most memerable apect of the game.
In case you are wondering if it's saved by the multiplayer - no; if anything it's worse. It barely works and everyone was goading each other into quitting it was THAT TEDIOUS and poorly executed. I'm not sure why the tiny maps with poorly mistextured objects have such bad FPS in apparent attempt to squeeze out any hope of joy, but they do and there is nothing fun about any of the modes. That's assuming you can find enough people online to paly against - if indeed you can login at all (it took me half a dozen tries each time - things are really not well with the Online Multiplayer Service).
Instead of buying this, why not ask a friend to come over, tie you to a chair and have them shoot you with a paintball gun at close range? I promise it'll be more fun than enduring this.
I won't be further indulging this franchince - not even the considerable talents of Kevin Spacey can save it.

The groundbreaking predecessor to an even more groundbreaking sequel. Good combat, an emersive story, and a game engine that always comes to mind whenever I think of physics in video games. At least, this version. The engine this game was originally on is just an after thought. If you haven't play any of the Half-Life games, start with this one. Then play Half-Life 2, so you can be sad there's no part three, like everyone else. Enjoy!

With Black Mesa out it's hard to justify purchasing Half Life: Source. The lighting is better, and there's some higher quality sound effects from HL2. However the "chrome" effect (on things like security guard helmets) from HL1 looks off and the mix of HL2 and HL1 sound effects is strange. Havok physics are added but they hardly play a role. Maybe one puzzle involving some hanging crates is a little different, gibs bounce around using the new physics, and there are ragdolls. Some weapons have new recoil effects which can be annoying. The MP5 in particular bobs up and down when fired. AI is improved a bit and friendlies can keep up the pace better.
But what are you getting overall? It's HL1 with some visual novelties like ragdolls but with no support for the extensive amount of HL1 mods. Just get HL1 which looks mostly the same, or get Black Mesa which is a much more ambitious and impressive visual update to HL1 than Half Life: Source.

The game itself is fun.  I enjoy the gameplay.  It's the player base that stinks for the most part.  It's a great time waster and when I am fortunate enough to join a server with a group that knows what they are doing and know how to execute the little concept called teamwork, I have a lot of fun.
I took a six month break from playing it and I was pleasantly surprised to see new maps, weapons, and sounds were added.  The gameplay itself is simple really.  Avoid the fast runner zombies and pick them off at a distance if you can.  Never let yourself be surrounded and don't be a resource hoarder. The most important aspect is to listen to the more experienced players and help out.  If you run out and do your own thing, you'll die and become a problem for the other players when you turn.
Graphics are decent enough for lower end systems, some of the game mechanics are a bit wonky (nailing boards), but there is nothing to write home about visually on higher end systems.  Overall, this is a game I frequently turn to when I want to have a little fun with endless action while still requiring some thought in execution.  Best of all, it's free!

Go ahead and take a cliched non-existent ''America Fu*k Yeah'' 80's action movie story about bunch of macho Americans liberating someone/something. Full Broforce release packs more force, it's polished, bug free and hard when it comes to surviving later levels.
MUST BUY.

I've played a lot before adding this game to steam. I recommend this game, but there are few "but"s.
1) Balance. In MOBA you have to play current meta-based champions. I mean, the gods that are more powerful than others during the current patch. You won't be able to play every god you want and have fun if you can't deal with unfairness. You will probably rage-quit ( for newbie it won't be visible, but when you are good with this game, you'll know what i'm speaking about ). So, it depends on your "perception of the world".
2) Donate, Don't get me wrong. It isn't concerned with the balance. The terms: some skins can't be bought that easily. You'll have to buy icons, frames, some unnecessary stuff you won't ever need to get the skin. It's kind of irritating and i don't support that kind of policy.
3) Community. This community hasn't gone far away from the community of tha game, that begins with the letter "D". And there is all that can be said about it.
If you are ready to face this, this game can give you a lot of fun. If you are looking for MOBA, but you aren't a fan of the games begins with the letters "L" or "D", give it a try.
