Let me get this straight, you want me to tell you a review about this game? Whoever you are, you might as well go to the curators, because if you've come for a review on this game, you've come to the wrong place. However, if you have come for an outstanding chocolate chip cookie recipe, you've come to the right place.
---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Ingredients
1/2 cup (1 stick) unsalted butter
3/4 cup packed dark brown sugar
3/4 cup sugar
2 large eggs
1 teaspoon pure vanilla extract
1 (12-ounce) bag semisweet chocolate chips, or chunks
2 1/4 cups all-purpose flour
3/4 teaspoon baking soda
1 teaspoon fine salt
Directions
1. Evenly position 2 racks in the middle of the oven and preheat to 375 degrees F. (on convection setting if you have it.) Line 2 baking sheets with parchment paper or silicone sheets. (If you only have 1 baking sheet, let it cool completely between batches.)
2. Put the butter in a microwave safe bowl, cover and microwave on medium power until melted. (Alternatively melt in a small saucepan.) Cool slightly. Whisk the sugars, eggs, butter and vanilla in a large bowl until smooth.
3. Whisk the flour, baking soda and salt in another bowl. Stir the dry ingredients into the wet ingredients with a wooden spoon; take care not to over mix. Stir in the chocolate chips or chunks.
4. Scoop heaping tablespoons of the dough onto the prepared pans. Wet hands slightly and roll the dough into balls. Space the cookies about 2-inches apart on the pans. Bake, until golden, but still soft in the center, 12 to 16 minutes, depending on how chewy or crunchy you like your cookies. Transfer hot cookies with a spatula to a rack to cool. Serve.
5. Store cookies in a tightly sealed container for up to 5 days.
For a Rocky Road Bar:
1. Lightly butter a 9 by 13-inch baking pan. Make the batter as per cookie recipe and fold in 1 cup chopped walnuts along with the chocolate chips. Spread batter in prepared pan. Bake until the edges are light brown and the batter sets, about 45 minutes. Cool slightly and cover surface with 4 cups marshmallows and 1 cup chocolate chips. Broil at least 8 inches from the heat until marshmallows turn golden brown, about 2 minutes. (Keep an eye on the marshmallows, and turn the pan frequently--they go from golden to char in a wink.) Cool, cut and serve.

In my 3 decades of gaming, never have I wished so hard that a game would just END.  Many of the mechanics and conventions in Lords of Shadow have not held up over time, turning what could have been an enjoyable Castlevania-Lite experience into an exercise in tedium.
On the positive side, the story and production value is top notch.  The graphics are outstanding.  The characters are relatively intriguing and have interesting visual designs.  The environments are detailed and varied.  The musical arrangement is appropriately epic. The in-game and bonus artwork is great.  Some of the boss battles are entertaining.  Combat feels decent, if somewhat overblown.
The main negative is pacing.  This game is overly long by a huge, huge margin.  There are 3 interchanging gameplay conventions here: Platforming, puzzles, and combat.  By the halfway mark, I was rolling my eyes when presented with yet another slog session for any of the three.
Platforming cribs heavily from Prince of Persia and Shadow of the Colossus, but lacks those titles' precision and fluidity. You will get extremely frustrated with the inaccuracy of your double jumps and the clunkiness of Gabriel's clambering.
Puzzles seem to have been contracted out to the Umbrella Corporation.  You will push pillars into slots, fit levers into crank mechanisms, and fetch all manner of key and bauble to unlock gates or move platforms.  Rarely will you be able to do this, though, before first clearing out rooms and rooms and rooms of enemies.
Combat is almost entirely comprised of "defeat all enemies in room".  Here Konami channeled (copied) God of War, in giving you direct and area attacks that can be linked together in a million unnecessary ways via purchaseable combos.  I say unnecessary because it's incredibly difficult to consistently land most of these combos due to the amount of onscreen enemies and their lack of hit stun.  Your combo strings will be constantly interrupted either by a monster blowing right through your attacks or by multiple enemies overwhelming you, leaving you to rely for much of the game on your initially provided mash combos. The game's parry system feels slipshod, due to fixed camera angles that are often so zoomed out that it's difficult to distinguish the telegraphing of enemy attacks. There is also the standard God of War "grapple stunned enemy for QTE finishing cinematic", which gets old incredibly quickly and breaks combat flow, but is necessary for finishing off many larger enemies.
The story attempts to retcon Castlevania canon by setting up Dracula as something of an anti-hero.  Traditionalists might take issue with this. Personally, I didn't mind.  It would, however, be inaccurate to call the narrative an "arc".  I won't belabor the point, but suffice to say that the game climaxes in you DEFEATING SATAN, and then inexplicably tosses you back into yet another arduous platforming/puzzle/combat grind for three more chapters.  This is in order to explain, as an afterthought,  the most critical plot point of the entire game while squaring you off against a theretofore unknown Generic Armor Guy boss.
Overall, I can't recommend it. Maybe if you're strapped for cash, and incredibly bored, this game will give you your "money's worth" with its multiple layers of padding. For those of us who have less time to game nowadays due to real life obligations, it will be just another unfinished title mocking you from your backlog.

I played Rust over a span of 3-5 months with very long binge sessions. I can't think of the last game I played that made me forget what time it was, probably Vanilla WoW.
In Rust, you start with nothing, and usually end with nothing, but the magic in the game is everything that happens in between. Forming alliances and then breaking alliances, fooling a friendly player, and stealing everything hes worked for. Rust can bring out the sociopath in you. Even if you don't usually act toxic, this game will bring it out in you. But you must embrace it. Embrace the toxicity, because it will be all around you. You're in a giant sandbox to explore, build, hunt, kill, and loot.
I hope that one day Rust will leave Early Access because its a great survival game. I reccommend playing with friends, and if you're new, try to play with someone that has experience in the game to show you the ropes.
Remember, the only advice you need is to TRUST NOBODY.

---RUST REVIEW---
So far, after the 15 hours I have played Rust, I learned much about how the game works as well as the replayability and actual gameplay that players focus on.
---REPLAYABILITY---
This game goes by a clever(and quite cheap) concept that keeps on making the consumer(player) to play Rust more. The way how they do this is that you will end up building your own house and create a base. The hook to this however is that your character goes to sleep rather than teleports to the void, so you are still a killable entity. This creates a tense train of thought where you want to protect your character as well as your base at all times. Which becomes time consuming. Now of course, the Vanilla Rust servers have server wipes, which will also hook you into the game, because it gives you either another chance to build your 30 room megabase, or have a second chance at becoming better than the♥♥♥♥♥♥that build said megabase.
---COMBAT/EQUIPMENT---
The only thing to notice about the combat is that RUST uses a pretty cool locational damage system, since you can wear armors like the metal face mask, but being shot in a certain unprotected spot will have you take more damage as if you were naked in that area. The weapons and armor are pretty sparse in my opinion. And it would be enjoyable if there are different armors that give certain attributes rather than only protection against certain things. The weapons are fine, but it would be cool if there was a larger possibility to guns. Because at this point im sick of squealing children talking about how many AK's they have in their ♥♥♥♥ing base.
---Progression---
Progression in this game mainly points to the blueprint system and your base. The blueprint system is that the player has to find(or craft) certain blueprints for things like equipment and furniture. Honestly, this system is quite frusterating considering that id either have to risk my life constantly to get 20 scrap and a chance of an actual good blueprint or I can just walk to an area with 3 barrels and get safe but slow scrap flow like that. Considering the fact that people camp the monuments for no good reason other than to be a complete prick, choice 1 is my least favorite.
---Raiding/Base Building---
This is the real focus on the game when it comes to players(after they somehow survive from the onslaught of crossbow wielding psychopaths) The tactics in raiding is quite enjoyable on how I see it, but it would be nice if there are more unique raiding tools that use the player rather than slapping on a c4 and shooting everywhere(a chainsaw or some sort of drill would be fun). The types of traps players can use is enjoyable, like the airlock strategy where you can stealthily trap someone inside a room until they die, or if they just blow up the entire building.
---Playerbase---
Whenever I look at the chat i'd want to bleach my eyes considering that they all sound like 12 year olds playing COD after their parents bought them the game at christmas. about 90% of them are just complete dickweeds. Other than that, the 10% of the playerbase bring some interesting encounters as well as a potentially enjoyable time.
---FINAL VERDICT---
6/10
I really enjoy how rust works, but I can't get past on how cheap their replayability factor is. It's practically just forcing you to play if you want to enjoy the game with all your equipment, and it would wipe sometime soon so you just have to repeat the work you have done to get to that same level of gunplay you enjoyed in the first place. Don't take this review to hear however, this is only to official servers. I believe there are modded servers that are free for all based as well as more fast paced versions of the official servers.
TL;DR if you want a good survival game to sink your time into, this is the game. Other than that don't waste your money because it will just constantly hook you in even if you are unwilling to play the game. Because nobody wants to die when they have a cool gun in their inventory.

Pros:
Singleplayer - The story was good in my opinion. I enjoyed it was a bit longer than most usual Call of Duty games I have played previously.
Multiplayer - It's pretty fun actually. It has been a while since I actually enjoyed a Call of Duty multiplayer experience. The last time I actually enjoyed one was back during Modern Warfare 2.
Graphics - The graphics are amazing! I love how great the game looks!
Cons:
Singleplayer - The cutscenes are very laggy. I don't know why, but they are. It takes forever to get through the loading because of that.
Multiplayer - Some maps have a huge FPS drop which makes it a bit difficult to play sometimes, but it only happens on 2 maps.
Graphics - Can't play on max settings in graphics sadly. I am above the recommended system requirements. I have a GTX 760 with 4GB video card and all the other requirements I have something better. I still am unable to play on the max settings. I seen a article that GTX 690 can play max flawlessly so this is extremely disappointing. I checked if it was a issue on my side than the game, but it is actually a game-side issue and not my PC. It is clear the company did not work very hard on optimizing the graphics. They could have done better, but oh well. I guess the recommended system requirements is a bit misleading.
Overall other than the cons I would still recommend this game. In the end all of these issues can be fixed with patches and I know they will sooner or later.

Call of Duty: Advanced Warfare is a FPS shooter made by Sledgehammer Games, a studio branch off of Infinity Ward. This year was their first game, and they have been induced into Call of Duty's yearly cycle. I had my doubt about this game, but it came out really good.
In the campaign, you play as a U.S. soldier named Mitchell. He enlisted with his friend, Will. The game start out in North Korea, with you fighting to destroy an AA tank. Along the way, you meet up with an Atlas squad, in which one of your squadmates brings up that Will's father is the CEO on Atlas. Atlas is a PMC (Private Miltary Corperation), founded and commanded by Jonathan Irons. The mission ends with Will getting his arm stuck in the tank, and he dies with the tank blowing up. And for Mitchell, he loses a friend and his arm. At Will's funeral, you meet Jonathan Irons, who wants to give you a second chance, which means he's giving him a job and a new arm. There, you meet your new squadmates, Gideon, Joker, and llona. Atlas's job is to take down KVA, a terrorist group, and their leader, Hades. Hades wants to destroy anything technologic, meaning power, internet, phones, everything. Hades wins, and blows up power plants everywhere,  turning everything dark. 4 years of that and then Atlas was ready to take down Hades. Once Hades was gone and out of the game, you'd think everything is fine, right? Well lets just say, there's an enemy worse than Hades...
The gameplay is different than any other Call of Duty. The introduction of the exo suits, adds another element to the game. You're able to jump high, dodge fast, move things with the exo's strength. Every campaign mission you completed, you'd get exo upgrade points, to make your exo more powerful and more useful. Like for example you could upgrade your armor, reload speed, how many grenades you could hold, your spring speed etc. The things you could upgrade on your exo were a pretty wide range of things. In the campaign, the exos are very helpful, but the exo movement shows more in the mulitplayer. (I'll go over that later on) AI is a lot harder, but not sure compared to Ghost, because I didn't play that game. The exo abilities and exo types in the campaign brings something new. Plus, since this game is in the future, there are a lot of things that can be added that don't have to be real, like for example a sniper drone, or a hoverbikes. This game pulls off futuristic warfare pretty well, but then again, not all the guns are lasers and♥♥♥♥♥♥like that. That would make it too futuristic, it'd turn into Star Wars after that.
The graphics in this game are amazing. I never knew a Call of Duty could look so good. The surroundings of the maps, the level design and the character models....oh my. The cutscenes, I knew they were made in the engine the game is based on, but it looked so realistic. It took me so long to find out that wasn't real, but just a rendering. The faces on the people were so realistic, not to mention that they actually took the likeness of every single main character. People thought it was just Kevin Spacey, giving his likeness to the game, but no, it wasn't. I see this as what is going to happen to all other games now. Sooner or later, every game character will look like the person in real life. The gun models are pretty good, most of them are different from other guns, while some may have similaries to another gun.
The mulitplayer in this game is great. They introduced a new gamemode, Monentum and the exo suits. The exo suits, explained a bit above, adds a new element or play style to this game. It makes the game more fast paced than the other Call of Dutys'. Your movement speed is increased by a lot, because of the exos, you can now dodge in any direction, and not to mention, double jump. It also adds something to the level design, because of out of reach places that may require a ladder or some sort of step block, are accessable without those blocks or ladders. The exos in the mulitplayer also have different abilities such as, exo cloak, exo overclock, exo stim, exo ping etc. It pretty much replaces some grenades or other items that were needed to pull any of those things off. Another thing that was added this year, was customization. You could choose from a number of player models, male or female, most characters from the campaign. You could put helmets, masks, glasses, pants, exos, shirts, shoes, about everything that you have to put on in the morning to go to work or to school. (Besides the exo) To get these items, they are dropped by supply drops or by completing challenges. Supply drops can give you all the things listed above and can also give you special weapons. The weapon may have decreased range, but more damage or accuracy. They are dropped randomly. Level cap is 50 and there are 16 prestiges counting Master Prestige.
Sledgehammer has also included the Exo Survival gamemode this year. It's like MW3's survival, but it's delivered a lot better than Infinity Ward did on MW3. The exos are the main course of this game pretty much. The game mode includes 25 rounds on mulitplayer maps, with exo types, light, heavy, specialist and weapon and exo crates. Once you reach round 25, the map "flips" meaning you restart, but the enemies are stronger. You can pretty much just keep going forever. It's a fun gamemode, but it gets boring after a while in my opinion.
Call of Duty: Advanced Warfare is one of the best Call of Duty's since Black Ops 2, I thought Sledgehammer was going to make a bad game this year, knowing that their staff was from Infinity Ward, but no, they did a great job this year. I enjoyed it this year, I'm willing to buy the next game they publish in 3 years from now. One thing I didn't like, is that half the guns in the game have to same sound effect and on the MP, the spawn points are messed up and there are no deciated servers, so that means lots and lots of lag. Besides that, it's a great game, they just patched the game to reduce the insane amount of long shots (500 for the last camo) on the assualt rifles. 9.5/10

Let me get this straight, you want me to tell you a review about this game? Whoever you are, you might as well go to the curators, because if you've come for a review on this game, you've come to the wrong place. However, if you have come for an outstanding chocolate chip cookie recipe, you've come to the right place.
---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Ingredients
1/2 cup (1 stick) unsalted butter
3/4 cup packed dark brown sugar
3/4 cup sugar
2 large eggs
1 teaspoon pure vanilla extract
1 (12-ounce) bag semisweet chocolate chips, or chunks
2 1/4 cups all-purpose flour
3/4 teaspoon baking soda
1 teaspoon fine salt
Directions
1. Evenly position 2 racks in the middle of the oven and preheat to 375 degrees F. (on convection setting if you have it.) Line 2 baking sheets with parchment paper or silicone sheets. (If you only have 1 baking sheet, let it cool completely between batches.)
2. Put the butter in a microwave safe bowl, cover and microwave on medium power until melted. (Alternatively melt in a small saucepan.) Cool slightly. Whisk the sugars, eggs, butter and vanilla in a large bowl until smooth.
3. Whisk the flour, baking soda and salt in another bowl. Stir the dry ingredients into the wet ingredients with a wooden spoon; take care not to over mix. Stir in the chocolate chips or chunks.
4. Scoop heaping tablespoons of the dough onto the prepared pans. Wet hands slightly and roll the dough into balls. Space the cookies about 2-inches apart on the pans. Bake, until golden, but still soft in the center, 12 to 16 minutes, depending on how chewy or crunchy you like your cookies. Transfer hot cookies with a spatula to a rack to cool. Serve.
5. Store cookies in a tightly sealed container for up to 5 days.
For a Rocky Road Bar:
1. Lightly butter a 9 by 13-inch baking pan. Make the batter as per cookie recipe and fold in 1 cup chopped walnuts along with the chocolate chips. Spread batter in prepared pan. Bake until the edges are light brown and the batter sets, about 45 minutes. Cool slightly and cover surface with 4 cups marshmallows and 1 cup chocolate chips. Broil at least 8 inches from the heat until marshmallows turn golden brown, about 2 minutes. (Keep an eye on the marshmallows, and turn the pan frequently--they go from golden to char in a wink.) Cool, cut and serve.

This game is fantastic.
Contrary to all the negative reviews that have been posted here since release, the game runs like butter on a hot griddle on my system (listed in my profile) with all setting on the Ultra preset @ 2K and the much reported and lamented mouse issue easily fixed using the in game settings.
I decided to play Corvo with powers for my first play through and for me, someone who considers Dishonored 1 to be their GOTY for 2012, it’s like stepping into a pair of warm comfortable slippers after a hard day’s work.  It just feels good.
Having Stephen Russel’s voice accompanying me on my journey is just icing on the cake.  And makes up for the idiotic decision Eidos Montreal made for Thief.
The game play is excellent, and I foresee my first play through taking a good amount of time due to me using blink to get to every open window or balcony I can reach.  And exploring is rewarding, as you fill out the rich story by discovering pieces of lore everywhere you go.  The game seems harder than Dishonored 1, but on the default difficulty setting it never gets too overwhelming as long as you plan in advance an escape route to use if the fecal matter hits the rotary cooling device so to speak.
The game has a real honest to god saving system HALALUJAH (I’m glaring at you Mafia 3) which lets you tryout different routes to achieve your goals without having to restart from the last checkpoint if you screw up.
Please also take note that anyone who says they finished the game in 4 hours is lying.  Even if that person is ignoring everything in the game and running from checkpoint to checkpoint they are not going to finish this game in 4 hours.  I have over 8 hours in and have only started chapter 2.  Also I don't think you can consider this game finished unless you have played the game all the way through with both Corvo and Emily.
So to wrap this up, I’m going to touch on the so called “gamers” here at steam.  I’ve watched these disgruntled whiny self-important “gamers” tear down one game after another lately and it is a sign that valve seriously needs to rethink how its review system works.
People, who have been playing games as long as I have, know that it is almost impossible for a game to work properly on every system out in the wild on release day.  And we know the best course of action is to give the developers enough time and cooperate with them to fix the issues, and as long as the developers stay involved with the players and show progress in patching, not to prematurely give the game a poor rating.
But that’s not how things work here.  For every person with legitimate issues you have ten persons who fall into one the following groups.
People with mid-range systems don’t use the recommended in-game setting and rage.  People with improperly cared for operating systems and outdated drivers who have problems with the game and rage.  People who can’t read the minimal recommended system and try running the game with old unsupported hardware have problems or can’t even get the game to run… rage.
So my advice is to take most of the negative reviews here at steam with a grain of salt,  in fact I recommend you ignore steam reviews all together (including this one) and look elsewhere to make your purchasing decisions.
That being said, if you are a fan of stealth exploring games, I cannot give this game higher praise.  It really is just that good.  And you will enjoy yourself.

This is among the worst games I've played, and here's a breakdown as to why:
- There is no health regen, or regular healing sources. You get a well every now and then, but they're rare and leave you running around with barely any health while you're trying to make your way to the next one.
- It has checkpoints. Normally, not bad for a game, but when you add in a lack of health sources AND stupid controls, you end up dying often and sent ages back to try to repeat what you'd already done.
- The combat is repetitive and clunky. You just spin around like a ballerina, trying to hit what you can, but if you try to dodge or jump out of the way of an enemy it's slow and clunky.
- The game expects you to just know what everything is. I left it alone for a while, came back a few months later, and when I got poisoned it said "use your light". Great, what button is that? Too many cases where you're in desperate need of a button to press but it won't tell you which.
- Quicktime events. There are loads and they're not fluid in battle.
- Enemies are just impossible. I just tried to fight a pig and the game made it clear that I should use it to ram the door. Except the pig never rams. It just runs at me and hits me when I try to jump out of the way. There's no way to dodge it, it just hits you and repeats. If you have to look up guides on these things, your game isn't built in a logical way. Same with those damn goblins and their bombs; you have to throw their bombs at a door to blow it up, but you either end up throwing them, or throwing the bomb the other way.
- Tiny corridor maps. Inbetween bosses are these thin, twisty "maps" where you just run along a path, jump a few gaps, solve a weak "puzzle", and the level is over. Next level, same♥♥♥♥♥♥
- Fixed camera angles. You don't get to control where you look, so you have to deal with just peering at your character at some funny angle from miles away while he fights.
- Stupidly long animations. Most times you pick up loot or open doors quickly. But sometimes, it wants you to join in, like the fun in the game is smashing a button to just open a door. To break a totem, I had to put my whip on it, then keep pressing up and down before it finally broke. That is not the interaction needed for a game. That's just time wasting.
Maybe I've just been so used to good hack and slash games, like Darksiders, but this game is so weak that I don't actually know why I bought it.

After the first completed playthrough I can finally sum up my experience with the game.
From the standpoint of a Dark Souls vet, I can genuinely say that I am thoroughly enjoying every hour I put into the newest addition to the Souls series. The PC version is surprisingly polished, giving the user an array of graphical and keybinding settings. The performance is
, no more Blighttown-like slide-shows on my laptop, as the game is consistently reaching 40-60 frames per seconds. Visuals are smooth and pleasant to the eye. Dark Souls II might be the most aesthetically pleasing game from the entire Souls series at this point, even though graphics never were really the main focus of its developers.
The storyline is brought to the level of the previous games. The world is diverse and engaging, there are still many mysteries yet to be unfold within the game world. Although some inconsistencies can be also pointed out, there is a metric ton of lore packed into the game as it is. The world is now a bit more accessible now, as it's surely easier to understand
- which is a good thing in my opinion. No more of that "
" kind of stuff.
The gameplay is engaging, further expanding the choices of loadouts, refining the level and gear progression, weapons themselves and useable armour sets. Although the gear disparity might not look more diverse than what we've seen in Dark Souls, it still delivers in regards to variety of possible ways of play the game. Bows are finally gameplay-viable and
useful, casters aren't as vulnerable with the introduction of varying cast speed and agility and so on.
There are few shortcomings, too. The current online matchmaking might not be the best system up to date. Although it's very solid from the technical standpoint (
), the introduced Soul Memory rule pretty much limits the ability of co-operation with your friends when you end up grinding too much. While it is a good measure to protect new players from twinks, it's consistently harder to invade people as a Red Phantom, unless you're in the NG+ or above. The NG and NG+ matchmaking is separate now, which with introduction of
new items in the second playthrough gives the game a bit more space to gain more playtime for the new explorers. All in all, the new matchmaking system might not be as strict as many people say - but for sure there's a few things that could be done to make it a better experience.
It is an outstanding experience, particularly once you figure out how the new things work. I found myself enjoying the game more in my second NG playthrough. I'd say it's the little things that matter.
It seems like Dark Souls II is the best entry point to the series, particularly with regards to the PC community. The port is very playable with mouse and keyboard. Short load times, solid framerate, good graphics settings and
performance (
) make the PC version of Dark Souls II the
version of a Souls game up to date. If you are a new player and feel interested enough to give the Souls series a try, go ahead.

+Great gibs

-+Weapons are generic and some useless
-Level design makes no sense. Why would you have a massive pit with hanging crates? Why does Black Mesa have a meat processing factory connected to a sewer?
-Games looked terrible for 1998. At a time where every year introduced marginal graphical innovations Half-Life was far behind the times. Quake from 1996 looks far better than this at 1080p.

After about 100 hours into the multiplayer (which is rather fun if you'd ask me), I feel like it's time to polish the original review I had posted.
I'll start with Pros:
-Graphics are familiar
-Gameplay is smooth (once you get the graphics to suit your system)
-Controls are fluid
-Decent variety of weapons at your disposal
-Maps are diverse
-Player customization allows you to create a unique soldier
-Exo-Suit adds to the gameplay to make it feel like a different game (almost)
and now for the Cons:
-Lack of (promised) dedicated servers
-(in my case) Can't even load into certain maps (i.e. Riot)
-some guns need major balancing to correlate with  Mouse/Keyboard controls considering the game was a console port
-matchmaking system occasionally takes forever to find a match (assuming nobody is playing the gamemode you wish to play)
-Framerate issues (overall stability could be better, I have a decent rig and would expect better frames than I am currently receiving)
-Emblem editor was obviously designed for one using a remote controller and isn't as easy to use as I'd wish with a Mouse/Keyboard
-Supply drops; Yes, they allow for random items to keep an inventory diverse, but I'm personally not a fan.
Overall I'd give the game a generous 7.75 out of 10. The only reason I'm giving it this high of a rating is because I trust Sledgehammer is working to release a decent patch along with their first DLC.
Would I recommend the game?
In its current state: no.
In a couple of months: yes.

This game is fantastic.
Contrary to all the negative reviews that have been posted here since release, the game runs like butter on a hot griddle on my system (listed in my profile) with all setting on the Ultra preset @ 2K and the much reported and lamented mouse issue easily fixed using the in game settings.
I decided to play Corvo with powers for my first play through and for me, someone who considers Dishonored 1 to be their GOTY for 2012, it’s like stepping into a pair of warm comfortable slippers after a hard day’s work.  It just feels good.
Having Stephen Russel’s voice accompanying me on my journey is just icing on the cake.  And makes up for the idiotic decision Eidos Montreal made for Thief.
The game play is excellent, and I foresee my first play through taking a good amount of time due to me using blink to get to every open window or balcony I can reach.  And exploring is rewarding, as you fill out the rich story by discovering pieces of lore everywhere you go.  The game seems harder than Dishonored 1, but on the default difficulty setting it never gets too overwhelming as long as you plan in advance an escape route to use if the fecal matter hits the rotary cooling device so to speak.
The game has a real honest to god saving system HALALUJAH (I’m glaring at you Mafia 3) which lets you tryout different routes to achieve your goals without having to restart from the last checkpoint if you screw up.
Please also take note that anyone who says they finished the game in 4 hours is lying.  Even if that person is ignoring everything in the game and running from checkpoint to checkpoint they are not going to finish this game in 4 hours.  I have over 8 hours in and have only started chapter 2.  Also I don't think you can consider this game finished unless you have played the game all the way through with both Corvo and Emily.
So to wrap this up, I’m going to touch on the so called “gamers” here at steam.  I’ve watched these disgruntled whiny self-important “gamers” tear down one game after another lately and it is a sign that valve seriously needs to rethink how its review system works.
People, who have been playing games as long as I have, know that it is almost impossible for a game to work properly on every system out in the wild on release day.  And we know the best course of action is to give the developers enough time and cooperate with them to fix the issues, and as long as the developers stay involved with the players and show progress in patching, not to prematurely give the game a poor rating.
But that’s not how things work here.  For every person with legitimate issues you have ten persons who fall into one the following groups.
People with mid-range systems don’t use the recommended in-game setting and rage.  People with improperly cared for operating systems and outdated drivers who have problems with the game and rage.  People who can’t read the minimal recommended system and try running the game with old unsupported hardware have problems or can’t even get the game to run… rage.
So my advice is to take most of the negative reviews here at steam with a grain of salt,  in fact I recommend you ignore steam reviews all together (including this one) and look elsewhere to make your purchasing decisions.
That being said, if you are a fan of stealth exploring games, I cannot give this game higher praise.  It really is just that good.  And you will enjoy yourself.

A review I posted in the forums that I feel may go well here
Pros
1. Awesome powers. The powers are for the most part a blast to work with. They are smooth and unique.
2. Pretty. The game updates the visuals of the first without straying too far from the first game to make it completely different.
3. Interesting gameplay mechanics. There was some things that were unexpected and unique enough to be interesting.
4. Two playable characters. Having two playable characters was a nice bonus especially since their powers are both very different, but similar enough to allow for cross playstyles.
5. Lore. The lore and books were interesting to read and provided a distraction.
6. Sprawling levels. The levels were vast and open enough to provide multiple points of completion, but not so large that they were daunting.
Cons
1. Broken powers. Remember the "for the most part" part? well some powers were convoluted such as the teleport for emily. It often gets stuck on nothing or outright changes on you with a minor twitch in your mouse. The powers in part 1 were much more smooth and made you feel like you were in comand of something great rather than fighting to get it right.
2. Too pretty. In an effort to, I assume, make the game more realistic, They removed some of the helpful features that made the game less of a task, such as distance highlighting of useful and valuable objects. By removing this feature unless you are up close, it makes the game tedious if you want to collect as much as you can because you get no visual clues to guide you thus making you have to scour every inch of the map.
3. Confusing gameplay mechanics. As referenced above in the spoilers those same unique mechanics are also quite confusing and tedious especially if you mess up along the way forcing you to backtrack quite a lot.
*This doesnt really fit under a specific category so I'll add it here, In part one you feel like a bad ♥♥♥, you can spend an adequate amount of time studying an enemy and get through fairly safely and quietly, I dont know exactly why it so much harder to do the same in part two but things are vastly harder. The game also suffers from a very annoying problem, You'll go through the mission doing awesome, knocking everyone out safely storing them and then get to the end to find out you killed 3 or 4 people somehow. If you do not directly kill someone, it shouldnt count against you.*
4. Two playable characters, Same dialogue. If you're going to go through the effort of having two playable characters, Having vastly different dialogue and gameplay would have been a touch that showed you really gave a damn about storytelling instead of pushing a product.
5. Lore. The lore and the interestingness of part two pales in comparison to part one. In part one you are shocked to learn some of the things you learn about the world and it's truly interesting. The world actually changes technologically as you play. In part two, there is very little that changes as you go through, the lore is stagnant and while distracting, ultimately pointless. In regards to morgan
6. Sprawling levels. With the levels as big and open as they are, it is very easy to miss so much even if you are trying to be a completionist. For instance, On my first playthrough I spent 5 hours on a chapter and I was very confident I did everything there was possible to do. At the end, with my confidence that I would have most if not all of the money as well as all the runes, bonecharms etc, I was shocked to learn I had collected just over half of the cash and missed 2/4 blueprints and 2 bonecharms even though the heart showed none left. That shows poor level design if someone could, due to a bad mechanic, spend so much time exploring and still miss so much.
All in all, If I rated part 1 and 10/10, I would rate dishonored 2 a 6.5/10.
It's a good game, it's funish, but compared to part 1, it's lacking in nearly every aspect. Simple fixes would bring the score up to an 8/10, but there would have to be major story and lore overhauls as well as more defined clues to guide to special loot to get back to the 10/10 status.
Overall, good job. It was worth the $60, but I wish it was more of a true successor to Dishonored.

This is absolutely a recomended game. It does compare to LoL, although LoL has better balance and being top-down avoids some issues that SMITE runs into. The biggest issue in SMITE, is the balance between gods. Some are just overpowered and do not see nerfs for months, and anothers have been in need of rework, but aren't getting any.
If you can get past these minor issues, the gameplay itself is fantastic. I love the fact that multiple gamemodes are support, and all feel equally well made. My personal favorites would be Assault, Arena, Joust and Siege.
Let's go through the issues regarding balance:
We get a new match of the day every day, but sometimes you have these 1v1 matches or god vs god matches and you know the game is already lost in the lobby. Why? Well, that is because Hirez thinks this is a balanced matchup:
God 1: 1 ranged stun, 2 escapes/engages that also deal damage, plus an ultimate that deals a lot of damage and stuns the target in place.
God 2: 1 escape/engage which does lower damage than the first of God 1's escape, 1 melee stun, 1 ranged easy to dodge attack that deals low damage unless the enemy is exactly where all 3 parts of this attack will land, plus an ultimate that makes her invincible for 3-5 seconds, but she can be reduced to 1 health in this time and will be instantly killed if she has a DoT on her.
Does such a matchup sound fair? You have just no chance to win as God 2 if both teams are of equal skill, but hey, this is balanced according to Hirez.
These are also the guys who think releasing Ah Puch with an innate slow in his ultimate was fine. No no no no. You cannot just have an enormous square slow people by 50% while it deals insane damage, in range of a god who has even more slow and already an impossible to dodge ability. I'm glad they finally nerfed the ulti to no longer slow, but his OP first ability still remains. To this day I have never missed it, because if the enemy is in range and does not have an instant escape, it will hit. I freaking hate that there are abilities like these in the game and that they get away with having ridiculous damage.
So yes, I still enjoy the game, but there are enormous issues when it comes to gods on their own, or when compared to other gods. Of course it isn't a 1v1 game, but comparing gods 1v1 can really let you know how broken some are.
Another 1v1 comparison:
Thor vs Hou Yi.
Thor stuns Hou Yi and uses his signature spin. Hou Yi escapes the stun using his escape and waits for the spin to finish, and then he lands on Thor using his escape, which stuns Thor in place. He then launches 2 basic attacks on Thor, and then uses his 2nd stun on him. By this time Thor is surely down to so little health an ultimate would kill him, or just a single crit.
Is that really fair? To give a hunter, a full all damage god, an escape with a built in stun ontop of him already having an easy to hit stun? The escape even makes him immune to damage.
Some more gods I'd like to compare:
Kukulkan: He has good damage and is really fun to play, but ALL of his abilities can be seen before they happen, predicted and dodged. The most difficuilt to dodge is arguably the shotgun because he has control over it, even after the enemy has noticed. So he has a problem where his only 2 abilities that deal good damage, are completely avoidable by anyone who has moderately good skills at the game. Then you compare his damage over time, easy to dodge tornado to someone like Chang'e, who has an instant aoe damage ability that does the same damage as kuku's tornado, if not more. How the fluff did this pass development?
Kukulkan used to be overpowered and I'm glad he was nerfed, but now you have other gods who are worse than him, when they really shouldn't be. With the same build Kuku's ulti is around 500 damage, over the course of 2.5 seconds, but Chang'e has the same 500 damage INSTANTLY, plus another instant ability that will deal over 700 damage, while also stunning the enemy, again INSTANTLY. How can this possibly be fair? If an ability deals damage over time, it should by default have increased damage due to the time it takes for it to be dealt, but even more so because the ability takes an entire second to actually come into play.
Where is the balance there? I hate the inconsistency when it comes to abilities vs abilities.
Another god I'd slightly like to mention is Neith. She just seems far too nimble. She can be basic attacking minions and still have enough movement speed to dodge any skillshot thrown at her. Why isn't she slowed enough to be hit? If she is in the center of an aoe when it is cast as she attacks minions, then she should surely have no hope of escaping, right? But no, she can just walk right out. Then ontop of that she has a really nice root, an insane backflip that makes her damage immune, and makes her leap backwards waaaaaay too far. Her ulti is okay though. I mean it's a really good map-wide stun, but it doesn't seem too imbalanced. Overall her kit is just too good, because it is better than average.
So by now I feel like I have reviewed the game balance rather than the game, from the standpoint of someone who loves the game, but hates how it's managed.

Best thing since Dark Souls 1. It feels a tad less polished than the original to be honest, still an amazing game by all means but it just doesn't feel as cohesive to me. I'm also not a fan of some of the MP changes, especially the PvP areas, which not only have enemies like normal areas, but you can get invaded at any time by membes of the relevant covenants, and not just one, sometimes multiple invaders... at once... In other areas you might suddently get dragged away into other peoples worlds as a "grey phantom", cept the world is on thier side, so your extra boned. Otherwise though, the summoning and PvP works a fair bit better in this one, probably the biggest improvement. Another thing in the games favor is that it's a lot less recycled than Dark Souls was. DS1 used A LOT of stuff from Demons Souls, but other than the odd sound effect DS2 looks and feels more original.
For those who haven't played Demons or Dark Souls, it's an action RPG that feels like a mix of a traditional cRPG and a fighting game. It has stats, elements, equipment etc. like a cRPG, but the combat is very focused on animations, invulnerability frames when dodging etc. and things like that. The game is reknowned for having brutally difficult combat, but it's actually not so tough, it's very systematic and once you learn the systems and get used to enemy attack patterns etc. it's actually pretty straight forward and has an EXCELLENT difficulty curve. Eventually it becomes necessary to challenge youself with special limits during gameplay, one of the most popular of which is the SL1 run. You have to finsih the game wtihout ever leveling up, and must start the game with the weakest class. Not only does this make you MUCH weaker, but it also drastically limits what items you can equip. After that, everything is about exploring the large open world, navigating environmental obstacles and not getting your♥♥♥♥♥deaded by the big nasties (some are pretty big too). Hunting for secret areas, exploring for treasues, trying to find where to go that wont get you murdered, it's all part of the game, and it's big enough to make your first playthrough last upwards of 50 hours (if you have no prior experience with the series at least).
All in all, it's one of the best games ever made, it's generally VERY well crafted, has great art direction and setting, even if the graphics aren't so great. The challenge makes it refreshing in an age of trivial toys and it's the kind of game you can play a dozen times over, trying different builds, challenge runs, just plain finding things you didn't know the first time... highly reccomended.

Taking on the Forces of darkness with Cross Whip, because why not?
Story:
You take control of Gabriel Belmont, a warrior of the Brotherhood of Light. Gabriel embarks on a journey to take on the Lords of Shadow - The King of the Lycans, The Queen of the Vampires and the Lord of the Necromancers - in order to save the world and hopefully ressurect his recently killed wife. During his journey he has to fight through trolls, Wargs, Werewolfs, Reapers and of course Vampires.
The story of this game is pretty much what you could expect from a Castlevania game - a Belmont embarks on a journey to stop the evil forces, even though this time it isn't Dracula. It isn't fantastic, but it is kind of playing through a gothic B-Horror Movie, which in my book is really entertaining.
Gameplay:
Castlevania - Lords of Shadow is a linear, static-camera, Hack'n'Slash game in the same veins as God of War (with a some influences from the Shadow of the Colossus) and has all the elements from those kind of games as you would expect. You do combos with the different attack buttons, block and dodges attacks, grab enemies and finish them off with cinematic QTE's. It does not bring anything new to the table when it comes to the hack'n'slash genre, but what it does really work - though not without some problems. The static camera does for the most  part follow you around well enough, but it has a habit of getting stuck in a position where it is impossible to see all the enemies - giving these a free shot at you because you didn't know they where there.
The game also focuses a lot on plattforming and puzzle-solving, and while the puzzles of this game are actually well made (and they even offer you a chance to get the solution to the puzzle for a small cost in case you get stuck) the plattforming in this game is horrible. The controls are way to floaty and Gabriel has too much hangtime in order to make precise jumps - and yet they make whole levels focusing on plattforming without any enemies to fight at all.
The Best Part:
The bosses of the game are really cool.
The Worst Part:
The plattforming. With too floaty controls to make any precise jumps these part of the game is so frustrating - and nowhere is this more obvious than the level "The Music Box". This element should've been cut out of the game entirely.

I really like this game but theres problems this game is plagued by. First off is Map design. There is some maps which really shouldnt be in the game. Its those pesky square formed maps. More precisely its those with sharp angles between planes. Its nice that the edges are soft but it doesnt really solve the problem. When you use a camera which is using perspective projection theres bound to be angled planes which cant be shown. That is fine as long as they arent adjacent to the plane you are on.  Because that creates situation where you go from one plane to another and get insta killed from enemies who you couldnt see or predict they were there. For example I shot to plane I plan to go to and I expect there arent any there but right when I go there spawns one and I get instakilled. This is the second problem spawning enemies. This is less of a problem and more of a difficult aspect of the game. The problem is that enemies spawn and you happened to ignore it and where were it spawned and got killed. Its a bad feeling knowing enemies can spawn right under you and you cant help it for example if you get swarmed or something else. Luckily you can deal with it with a limited blast. I think the better solution would be to make it not possible for example by delaying or make the spawn pushable. If you think this is wrong tell me why? If you are of the same mind tell me if there is something else which is also bothering you?

Geometry Wars; ah, memories back on the Wii is when I first played it. I thought it was mostly a casual shooter about math. Yknow. Childlike innocence. And then I got home and played it. For the most part, I was right. It is a pretty simple game about shooting geometric shapes, but it was really fun. Now for this game? This game feels like..like a bit of a rushed one.
I'll give it that it LOOKS beautiful. the game is one that uses a bit of wireframe-style artstyle in combination with calling itself geometry wars, it just feels like that combination was brilliant.
In the Wii version of Geometry wars, called Galaxies, you traveled around various solar systems to different planets and suns, fighting enemies for a big score on them with different types of drone functions you could upgrade. Now, Dimensions adds a bit to the drones, giving them super moves; these add a different ability along with the passive effect, such as firing missiles for a small time or becoming a black hole to suck all the enimies in range. For the levels, instead of various planets with levels, you've got kind of an adventure-style, liner path through the game, with bosses at various points.
Now, the addition of bosses was cool, and the linear story-like gameplay is neat, but there are two other modes that have this aspect, but increase the difficulty a bit; Hardcore, and Ultimate. With Ultimate it's a little different, and you usually have less amounts to use your super-powered drone ability, and Hardcore is where you have no drone. But..really..these are just modes that could have been switched with a button, or even more levels on Adventure, just harder difficulty. It's seerate menus that make the game SEEM like it's longer than it is.
That's not to say I didn't have a blast trying to beat all the bosses and get 3 stars on each level; I'm still working on getting the stars, but my idsue is the AMOUNT of levels. There's only so much I can play on it, and each level has a simple objective; usually just survive and get a high score. There's 110 levels to beat, but after each end boss of each mode, the end end boss, a strip of lined color acts like I can keep going; like there's more secrets, but having me get ALL the stars just to see that? I'm an avid player of this game, but it's difficult to do.
Onto the ship..The ship got a downgrade. Now, it always shot in 2 little tiny peashooter shots, then it got an upgrade to shoot more, usually either in a spread or machinegun-like fire. Now it only shoots 3, has a somewhat larger spead, with the introduction of 'super states' which include both the time-based switching or the weapon from the other games, alomg with new ones, but here's my problem; THE WEAPON DOESN'T STAY. It's a time-based ability, and this ability isn't allowed on bosses, severely ramping the difficulty when at the harder levels and trying to get those 3 stars. I would rather have the survival-based weapon upgrades than a 'super mode'. The ship itself is still the same while the multiplayer mode gives you a look at the others; when will we get to play single-player as ome of the others? Just gibe us a choice! I personally like player 3's ship better than the default.
All in all, I'd say it's a good game to push how good you are at twin-stick shooters. I'd see if you could het it on sale, though..it's not a lot of new content in comparison to Geometry Wars: Retro Evolved 2, and that was an Xbox 360 arcade game. It's a pretty game, yes, but that's all it's got going for it right now. Maybe 4, if it gets mde, will have more content.

This review is for people who want to know about gameplay. If you want to see people ♥♥♥♥♥ about day-1 optimization, then keep scrolling.
This game is the sequel to Dishonored (wow shocker nice observation there santa), and it sucessfully brings back most of the gameplay functions that made the original so great, and even managed to improve on some. This time, you get to choose one of two protagonist, the royal protector, Corvo, equiped with the powerful abilities from the original, or the emperoress herself, Emily, with a brand new array of equally-devestating powers. The chaos system still applies in this game, meaning your actions (killing or sparing enemies) will have a drastic effect on the world that surrounds you. Each level has great level designs which has several secrets, side quest, and different methods to complete the level.
The following is a list of changes I have noticed (sorry that its in a random order).
+The overall movement system feels both faster and more fluid, allowing you to transverse the rooftops with even more ease.
+The new ability system adds more passive abilities, such as the ability to block/deflect bullets, and the new system even includes a new branch system to replace the original 'Tier 1/2' system. This system allows for specific powerups such as Daud's freeze time blink, summoning multiple rat swarms, and more.
+Getting a 'perfect block' is harder, but even more satisfying with more dynamic, epic executions!
+Even if you end up in a fight, you can now use a KO as a way to nonlethally deal with enemies
+As mentioned above, you now choose between 2 different characters, each with different abilities and thoughts on the situation
+There are far more citizens in the maps, which both adds a layer to life in the game, and another threat (they will call for guards)
+The new black market allows for upgrades and different items allowed to be purchased
+Bloodflies are the new rat swarms (with wings!)
+You can now select a rune / bone with the heart to see even without the heart equipped
+They kept the 'currupted bonecharm' function from the 'Knife/Witches of Dunwall'
+You are now able to craft your own bonecharms
+Optinal gamemode which removes all your powers
+The original 'Dark Vision' is now a squirmy pulse instead of the solid white filling, feels more balanced
+Picking up a bottle to throw now stays in your right hand instead of floating in the middle of your face
+You can now set timers on clocks for timed distractions
+Peak system now allows you to peak over things as well as around
-Peak system is a toggle, which feels annoying after replaying the original's hold system
-Guards don't constantly say 'Shall we gather for whisky and cigars tonight?'
-Has the good old rusty Bethesda polish, with its wide array of bugs and glitches
-Has one of the ugliest menu's I've ever seen in a game
-The game looks horrible on low settings (more so than others, to the point you can barely read writing on objects)
-Optimization patch (given)
-Allow the option for 'hold' peak like the original game, for the 'toggle' feels weird
-Bring back the 'Favor' system that was in 'Knife/Witches of Dunwall'
-Bring back the 'ChokeDust' grenades which were in 'Knife/Witches of Dunwall'
-I feel like this is a missed opportunity for a 'Cross-Game Save Data' system, changing the game's initial chaos setting based off the previous game
-Considering you get to choose from one of two characters, it would be nice to be able to do some co-op with a friend
-Suprised they didn't think of any new gadgets, like shock arrows or gas mines
The gameplay is an amazing 8.5/10, however I'm going to drop it to a 6.5/10 because its optimization is pretty bad. If the game releases a patch which fixes the optimization, I will boost it back to a 8.5/10.
Hope this helped 'on-the-edge' gamers, and shall we gather for whisky and cigars tonight?

It didn't take very long to realize just how disappointing this game was going to be. I admit I had pretty high hopes, being a fan of the series, the genre, and the aesthetic, but before even the introductory level was halfway over I was already frustrated with the camera and the controls.
The gamepad controls feel all backwards, especially "use" and "dodge" being on the trigger buttons, and it would take so much practice to get properly aquainted with the bizzare control scheme the game honestly didn't hold me long enough to get there.
The marjority of the difficulty comes not from gameplay but from the camera, which is constantly locked at the most inconvienant angle the developers could find. There's also a heavy reliance on the character being agile, with timed events, dodges, and parries being integral, but the controls simply aren't responsive enough and the character regularly fails to execute those maneuvers - which makes the boss fights, which often demand them, especially frustrating.
The combat in general is not at all balanced: most enemies are so underpowered that they might as well not be there, to the point that just mashing the attack buttons at random pretty much kills everything (even the enemies that you didn't know were there because the camera angle was hiding them); meanwhile, larger eneimes are generally unjustifiably punishing - one-hit kills and traping/stunlocking moves abound among the higher-tier enemies and bosses.
There are also mounted levels, but you'll wish there weren't. Which sorta works out, since the riding mechanics are so poor they decided to have you be on the ground for most of them anyway.
Finally, the menus, meant to simulate the pages of a book, are clunky and annoying because of poor design and the painfully long animations between them, and the majority of the story is told by rote narration over slowly scrolling text which, though the voice acting is rather good, is so slow and drawn-out that you get tired of listening to it very quickly.
There's potential with the story and the design, but the execution overall is just frustrating and unengaging. Pretty much every time the game offered me something new, my response was, "ok, that's a thing, but can we just be done with it now?"

I have over 2 k hours on my account. Used to play and absolutely love this game. That was back in 2011 and 2012.   I've stopped playing the game in 2013 because every patch the fps kept getting lower and lower. Basicly devs started working on engine upgrade to release the game on consoles and because optimisation was incompatible with upgraded engine they removed it. Or so I heard. Now in late 2013 they made a blog post saying that engine upgrade will come in Q1 of 2014 and it will improve the game visually and increase performance too. 2 years later engine upgrade still not released.
I used to get a steady 100 fps with no drops. Last I checked now my fps is 38-70. Usually arround 45-55 (even worse in Waterfront district) and it feels very unsmooth. Also at first the game used to run perfectly fine on 4 gb ram but in 2013 it started needing  more ram and on 4 gb ram setups there were freezes and lags. I have upgraded to 8 gb ram. It was a day and night difference performance wise (no freezes) but this did not fix the fps issue. Since the game matchmaking is based on your skill it constatly puts you against similar skill level players. I simply got tired of losing fights even against lower skilled players simply due to the fact that my fps is unsmooth and keeps jumping. Got tired of waiting for an engine upgrade that is never released. Unless you have a i7 oc'ed to 4.5 GHz I do not recommend playing this game. Sure its doable at bronze and silver levels but once you hit gold threat all your fun will go away when you try to kill somebody with 144 fps on his i100 and 1000 gb of ram. Random server-side lag and teleportations do not help either.
Oh and back in 2013 EU1 had ~3000 active players and EU2 had ~1700. Now they merged EU servers together active population is even less of that that EU2 used ot have so the population speaks for itself. Perhaps in 2050 when Half - Life 3 is released and APB Reloaded receives it's engine upgrade I will remove this negative review and start enjoying the game again because right now it's impossible to do so.

Best thing since Dark Souls 1. It feels a tad less polished than the original to be honest, still an amazing game by all means but it just doesn't feel as cohesive to me. I'm also not a fan of some of the MP changes, especially the PvP areas, which not only have enemies like normal areas, but you can get invaded at any time by membes of the relevant covenants, and not just one, sometimes multiple invaders... at once... In other areas you might suddently get dragged away into other peoples worlds as a "grey phantom", cept the world is on thier side, so your extra boned. Otherwise though, the summoning and PvP works a fair bit better in this one, probably the biggest improvement. Another thing in the games favor is that it's a lot less recycled than Dark Souls was. DS1 used A LOT of stuff from Demons Souls, but other than the odd sound effect DS2 looks and feels more original.
For those who haven't played Demons or Dark Souls, it's an action RPG that feels like a mix of a traditional cRPG and a fighting game. It has stats, elements, equipment etc. like a cRPG, but the combat is very focused on animations, invulnerability frames when dodging etc. and things like that. The game is reknowned for having brutally difficult combat, but it's actually not so tough, it's very systematic and once you learn the systems and get used to enemy attack patterns etc. it's actually pretty straight forward and has an EXCELLENT difficulty curve. Eventually it becomes necessary to challenge youself with special limits during gameplay, one of the most popular of which is the SL1 run. You have to finsih the game wtihout ever leveling up, and must start the game with the weakest class. Not only does this make you MUCH weaker, but it also drastically limits what items you can equip. After that, everything is about exploring the large open world, navigating environmental obstacles and not getting your♥♥♥♥♥deaded by the big nasties (some are pretty big too). Hunting for secret areas, exploring for treasues, trying to find where to go that wont get you murdered, it's all part of the game, and it's big enough to make your first playthrough last upwards of 50 hours (if you have no prior experience with the series at least).
All in all, it's one of the best games ever made, it's generally VERY well crafted, has great art direction and setting, even if the graphics aren't so great. The challenge makes it refreshing in an age of trivial toys and it's the kind of game you can play a dozen times over, trying different builds, challenge runs, just plain finding things you didn't know the first time... highly reccomended.
I won't call it easier or harder but.... YOU DIED.

My video review:
Fantastic twin-stick shooter, and honestly the farthest the space-themed geometry-based twin-stick shooter sub-genre can be taken IMO. Better than its copycat cousin Waves by a comfortable margin.

tl,dr: Mad fun, endlessly stimulating and worth the sticker shock, probably the best title of the franchise, disappointing soundtrack.
I was a huge fan of the Geometry Wars title for the old DS, and this pushes all of those buttons--even more successfully.  The stages are short, challenging, and significantly different from each other in most cases:  you could say that this is perfectly designed to soothingly accomodate your standard millenial gaming-induced adult ADD.
This iteration of the series has a couple of features that really extend replayability.  One:  incremental plus-up-your-drones-and-supers skinner box works exactly as planned,  Two:  knowing what I really want out of a leaderboard, it displays your Steam friends' scores -first-, so you have a sense of meaningful competition against other mere mortals (and instantly deployable bragging rights.)  Three:  I'm a sucker for three-tiered score challenges, I guess.
Anyway, it's my favorite game in the arcade genre.
Some mild criticism:  The soundtrack is extremely limited.  I like all the music I've heard, but I feel like I've only heard about four tracks, three of them very same-y.  There's one (1) boss level track, but the game seems to be pretty into its gem-themed array of bosses.  The soundtrack for the DS was excellent, so this is an unexpected letdown.
Criticism the second:  I've played about two thirds of the bosses, and they don't feel especially different from one another.  On the other hand, essential difference between levels in this game is largely a matter of different game modes and level parameters,

This is absolutely a recomended game. It does compare to LoL, although LoL has better balance and being top-down avoids some issues that SMITE runs into. The biggest issue in SMITE, is the balance between gods. Some are just overpowered and do not see nerfs for months, and anothers have been in need of rework, but aren't getting any.
If you can get past these minor issues, the gameplay itself is fantastic. I love the fact that multiple gamemodes are support, and all feel equally well made. My personal favorites would be Assault, Arena, Joust and Siege.
Let's go through the issues regarding balance:
We get a new match of the day every day, but sometimes you have these 1v1 matches or god vs god matches and you know the game is already lost in the lobby. Why? Well, that is because Hirez thinks this is a balanced matchup:
God 1: 1 ranged stun, 2 escapes/engages that also deal damage, plus an ultimate that deals a lot of damage and stuns the target in place.
God 2: 1 escape/engage which does lower damage than the first of God 1's escape, 1 melee stun, 1 ranged easy to dodge attack that deals low damage unless the enemy is exactly where all 3 parts of this attack will land, plus an ultimate that makes her invincible for 3-5 seconds, but she can be reduced to 1 health in this time and will be instantly killed if she has a DoT on her.
Does such a matchup sound fair? You have just no chance to win as God 2 if both teams are of equal skill, but hey, this is balanced according to Hirez.
These are also the guys who think releasing Ah Puch with an innate slow in his ultimate was fine. No no no no. You cannot just have an enormous square slow people by 50% while it deals insane damage, in range of a god who has even more slow and already an impossible to dodge ability. I'm glad they finally nerfed the ulti to no longer slow, but his OP first ability still remains. To this day I have never missed it, because if the enemy is in range and does not have an instant escape, it will hit. I freaking hate that there are abilities like these in the game and that they get away with having ridiculous damage.
So yes, I still enjoy the game, but there are enormous issues when it comes to gods on their own, or when compared to other gods. Of course it isn't a 1v1 game, but comparing gods 1v1 can really let you know how broken some are.
Another 1v1 comparison:
Thor vs Hou Yi.
Thor stuns Hou Yi and uses his signature spin. Hou Yi escapes the stun using his escape and waits for the spin to finish, and then he lands on Thor using his escape, which stuns Thor in place. He then launches 2 basic attacks on Thor, and then uses his 2nd stun on him. By this time Thor is surely down to so little health an ultimate would kill him, or just a single crit.
Is that really fair? To give a hunter, a full all damage god, an escape with a built in stun ontop of him already having an easy to hit stun? The escape even makes him immune to damage.
Some more gods I'd like to compare:
Kukulkan: He has good damage and is really fun to play, but ALL of his abilities can be seen before they happen, predicted and dodged. The most difficuilt to dodge is arguably the shotgun because he has control over it, even after the enemy has noticed. So he has a problem where his only 2 abilities that deal good damage, are completely avoidable by anyone who has moderately good skills at the game. Then you compare his damage over time, easy to dodge tornado to someone like Chang'e, who has an instant aoe damage ability that does the same damage as kuku's tornado, if not more. How the fluff did this pass development?
Kukulkan used to be overpowered and I'm glad he was nerfed, but now you have other gods who are worse than him, when they really shouldn't be. With the same build Kuku's ulti is around 500 damage, over the course of 2.5 seconds, but Chang'e has the same 500 damage INSTANTLY, plus another instant ability that will deal over 700 damage, while also stunning the enemy, again INSTANTLY. How can this possibly be fair? If an ability deals damage over time, it should by default have increased damage due to the time it takes for it to be dealt, but even more so because the ability takes an entire second to actually come into play.
Where is the balance there? I hate the inconsistency when it comes to abilities vs abilities.
Another god I'd slightly like to mention is Neith. She just seems far too nimble. She can be basic attacking minions and still have enough movement speed to dodge any skillshot thrown at her. Why isn't she slowed enough to be hit? If she is in the center of an aoe when it is cast as she attacks minions, then she should surely have no hope of escaping, right? But no, she can just walk right out. Then ontop of that she has a really nice root, an insane backflip that makes her damage immune, and makes her leap backwards waaaaaay too far. Her ulti is okay though. I mean it's a really good map-wide stun, but it doesn't seem too imbalanced. Overall her kit is just too good, because it is better than average.
So by now I feel like I have reviewed the game balance rather than the game, from the standpoint of someone who loves the game, but hates how it's managed.

We all know about MOBAs. How there's (generally) 3 lanes split up by a jungle in-between. How there's the 5 major roles:
-Bruiser / Warrior
-Guardian / Tank
-Hunter
-Assassin (Generally the Jungler)
-Mage
Well, in SMITE, this is no different. However, SMITE adds a completely new perspective -- third person. This will throw off even the most seasoned MOBA veteran for the first few games. You will hear sounds behind you as you're running away, and you need to use those sounds to better dodge abilities. When you're getting ganked, you might hear a sound to your left or right and that's your que to bail out.
All in all, SMITE is a unique game and has it's own vibe to it. It's immensely fun to play if you put the time and effort into properly learning MOBA ettiquette.

I've played over a hundred hours of Smite prior to its Steam release and before that I logged nearly 500hrs in Dota2.
Smite is a Moba, its core game mode (conquest) has a map much like Dota or LoL - 3 lanes, jungle between them, towers and bases.
The main point of difference with Smite is the 3rd person perspective and the action rpg inspired combat. This gives the game a much faster paced feel and makes you feel more a part of the action.
The learning curve is much more gradual and the game is far less punishing than Dota but there is still plenty of depth for the players you want to take it seriously.
I would recommend this to anyone new to mobas who is turned off by the isometric viewpoint that most use or to established moba player who want a change of pace.

By now, PC gamers everywhere have grasped full comprehension of Half Life. This monument of the videogame medium as a whole was VALVe Software's very first product; one that was by no means easy to produce, but was eternally rewarding. Half Life is still being played today and enjoyed by many people, and deservedly so. For it is one of those titles in videogame history that is recognized by many; even those who might have very little experience with the franchise or its modded stand-alone offsprings.
Half Life puts the player in the shoes and HEV mark IV Protective System of everyone's favorite mute, crowbar-wielding, monster-slaying, marine-fighting theoretical physicist Gordon Freeman. The plot takes a humble beginning, as Gordon arrives to work--late--and prepares for what seems like a regular day at the Black Mesa Research Facility in the underground desert landscape of New Mexico. Perhaps a regular day, if not for the "deviation from standard analysis procedure." The player is let loose to briefly explore parts of the facility, allowing for a brief settlement before the experiment you are taking part of goes horribly wrong and all of a sudden that elevator you rode is out of order, that corridor you walked through is now covered in blood. That security guard you talked to is trying to revive a scientist you had just run into 5 minutes ago, and that other scientist you talked to has turned into some weird mutant that is now walking towards you, though no longer with any interests of making small talk. Everything that the player had seen and gotten used to is now part of a horrific thrill ride; one that is action packed and will only get better from there.
The game's story telling is absolutely fanstastic. It delivers a truly immersive experience by never leaving the first person perspective of the player and Dr. Freeman. It sacrifices cutscenes and cinematic mumbo-jumbo for first-hand experiences and uninterrupted gameplay. Said gameplay is very satisfying. There is a very good mix of firefights of varying intensity combined with puzzles and first person platforming. The puzzles can be a tad difficult at times, but just the right kind of difficulty to encourage perseverance and reward the player for their astuteness. Firefights are also quite fun; you start out making your way through waves of hostile inter-dimensional beings and later on fight none other than the few, the proud, the Marines, who pose quite an intimidating threat. The Marines really shine in the AI department, they're aggressive but smart enough to know when to retrieve. They have a sense of personal preservation unlike anything I have ever seen in any other videogame. They will try their hardest to kill Gordon, using any tools at their disposal, but they don't want to die, and will thus will make effective use of cover and defensive tactics.
I would highly recommend purchasing the Source version of Half Life due to some added features such as much better particle effects, improved lighting and water effects, as well as the intergrated ragdoll physics. Those not interested in such added details could easily overlook the Source version and buy vanilla Half Life, seeing as how it is the same price on Steam as the Source version, but I would highly recommend getting this version for those who haven't experienced Half Life and are looking to get into it.

Although this is an Early Access game, i feel that we can get a pretty decent feel on what the game will be when its properly finished. And that will. be a very enjoyable Arcady action platformer, with tons of explosions.
I havent found anything wrong with the so far, no issues with controls they work fine whether or not you are using a 360-pad or the keyboard, no graphical glitches (at least for what i have seen) and i havent encountered any bugs.
Graphically, the game looks like an old arcade-game. Meaning somewhere around 16-32-bit craphics and although some people have a problem with this, i feel that it serves its purpose. It gives this game, a feel of nostalgia if you will. A reminder of those classic Arcade games you spent several weeks allowance money on. I remember getting over 20€ on slots and then spending most of it on the Star Wars: Original Trilogy Arcade Cabinet that was right behind me.. Dont look at me like that, i was very impulsive as a kid. But besides the point...
The game has a multiplayer, unfortunately i haven't gotten enough of my friends together to have a blast-a-thon. Since very few of my friends actually own this game, might need to get a 4-pack and distribute that to the most deserving plebia... I mean, closest friends.
But anyway, summarization..
Arcade-Cabinet craphics, rather basic soundtrack, tons of explosions, Many, many, 80's 90's action heroes with "BRO" put into everyones name for enhanced humour value, EXPLOSIONS! And in the latest update there is a copter you can control on the main-map and vaporize seagulls.
So, i think... Taking account that the game is unfinished. Broforce gets..
An undetermined score.
What ? I simply cannot give a decent score without making someone mad. Alright if you insist.. I think i can settle for a..
B+  Just because it rubs me the right way.. Dont go blaming me for bias over that.
