I'm sure everyone is aware that there are plenty of top down arcade shooters in the market both new and old, but none of which were made like this. Unlike other arcade shooters where you play on a 2D plane, this game allows you to play on a 3D plane. This drastically changes how the game is played to where you can easily wrap around the stage without having to akwardly run into enemies and projectiles, although that can still happen but just for other reasons. You don't need to play the games before this one to like it, and you'll likely have a hard time finding them on Steam anyways.
Although the main focus in this game is the 3D planes, you can also play on the classic 2D planes with all of the same gimics by going into classic mode. Also there is a story mode witch is just a long string of levels with certain gimics in them like: survival, enemy waves, limited ammo, time trails, ect. with most of the levels in story modes using 3D plane of some sort You earn stars based off of how well you perform in each stage with the maximum stars per stage being 3.
These stars will add up to your overall total where you will slowely unlock boss stages that are manditory for progressing further in the mode. Once you complete story mode you will unlock a harder story mode called "Ultimate" which is essentially new stages in themselves. After that are three bonus levels basically using the gimics mentioned above with the added benefit of being an endless mode. Finally there is multiplayer where you can play online (there's nobody online) or you can play local coop with a friend and go through a string of levels like in story mode.
There is no shortage of content here and you will likely get you're money's worth if you decide to try out everything the game has to offer. This game is no doubt hard, but satisfying granted that you are good or just get better over time. This is probably one of the best arcade shotters of its genre and is a must play for someone who enjoys these kinds of arcade shooters.

Performance woes aside, Dishonored 2 is a strong continuation of one of the best stealth-action fanchises out there. The story is satisfying and the characters are stellar, though the overall plotline lacks a bit of impact compared to the first game.
The game gives skilled pacifists plenty of nonlethal tools to ghost their way through the game's many complex levels, but it's the lethal and chaotic options that truly shine. In my more reckless playthough, I:
-Leapt 100ft off the top of a building and slam-dunked an unsuspecting witch's face into the bonfire she was warming herself by.
-Decapitated a powerful killer robot and watched it slice through an entire squadron of guards.
-Released a swarm of demon wasps into a crowded allyway, then sat back as they stung everyone and everything in sight to death and made nests in their corpses.
-Yanked a man through a window from the streets below with my tentacle hand, then kicked him in the balls so hard he fell right back out to his death.
In conclusion: If you play like an unrepentant psychopath, this game is a 10/10.

First of all I'd like to clear up that G1 as developers are somewhat incompetent only seemingly wanting cash and money from players. So I will put a disclaimer that this review is leaning more into the aspects of the game or the game overall rather than the developers of the game and the decisions made by the company itself.
Now that I've invested quite the time with the game and as the time Im revising this review I have played for about 300+ hours of this game. I feel as if I was a bit too harsh and judgemental about my previous review of this game as I was critisizing the game way too harshly and was a bit biased due to my first experiences with the game.
Having invested a great amount of time into this game I have found that it wasnt as bad as I originally thought it was. The community is active in forums and are fun to socialize and interact with on most cases. Im not gonna lie that there are times when a player or two engages in the activity I like to call "Who can be the best assh*le" in the game but they're only occasionally seen.
My best tip at this point would be to learn about the game in order to progress as APB Reloaded is a game that not only rewards you if you learn about secret routes or special hiding places for cover but also helps you progress through the game due to the help of the community itself.
I will admit though that before sinking 300+ hours into this game I painted a very biased opinion about the community making remarks that its cancer and toxic. Having personally interacted with the community in order to learn from veterans of the game and learning about tips and receiving advice from fellow players I then came to learn that it wasnt as bad as I originally thought it was.
Yes, the players online are very different from the ones in the forums and I can assure new players that it is not a turn off. The blend is quite well and sometimes even a good pair up. I will say though that if you dont have the patience to get better and invest some time into learning how things work with this game you'll end up having a very frustrating time blaming everyone else or everything else in the game rather than your lack of knowledge of it.
I whole heartedly feel that APB Reloaded is a game that I can recommend now, The graphics may be a little bit dated but that doesnt mean the game isnt enjoyable or playable. The community is helpful and fun to interact with and even though you get the occasional trolls you shouldnt get turned off by them since they are rare encounters. I would also like to state that there are barely any hackers in-game and I think people are mislead about the topic.
APB Reloaded is a moderately unforgiving game. Yes, I will say that it can seem unfair due to other players having upper hand due to the pay 2 win aspect but that has NEVER stopped me before. I have a character in Jericho server which had never seen any money invested to it and is now a Rank 100 Silver threat character with no premium and no overpowered guns at my disposal. The renting system is quite helpful since renting out guns that suit your playstyle can help you compete with various other players that does have premium guns and have invested money.
I also want to say that people think players are hacking but in all honesty those are the results of body modification implemented in the game. Just like in a MMO RPG, APB Reloaded has a system to benefit those who work on unlocking buffs for their characters. For instance there is a series of mods called Kevlar Implants and Clotting Agent. Both are health based modification used by many experienced players that give them an advantage over people. This isnt even part of the premium pay 2 win aspect as the body modifications I just mentioned are available to EVERYONE. Working up the ladder of whichever faction you chose to go with does reward you by unlocking these body modifications. Not only that but you can even get modification to give your guns more edge. BUT WAIT! it doesnt stop there! you can even put modification on your vehicles to suit how you drive and play! Of course you can customize your character but you can also implement skins on guns and even customize your vehicles!
Not only that but you never have to invest anything in the game as there is a system that lets you buy premium guns in exchange for in game currency earned through events such as Fight Club. This system is called the Joker Ticket system which lets players who dont have cash to invest in the game or just dont want to invest money to have an alternative way to get permanent items such as weapons, clothing, and even special vehicles and kits in a FREE way. Completeing objectives to save up Joker Tickets is a great alternative for those who want to play the game but not invest any money into it.
Take it from me who literally has a character that was built without the help of premium or OP guns. Just pure work put into the character and getting good in the game overall. As I said multiple times in this review, the key to APB Reloaded is to master the maps and to learn more about how things work in order to get better in the game.
Anwyays Ive been typing long enough so I will say this before I end this review. APB Reloaded is not a bad game at all. The learning curve is somewhat difficult and may take time to get used to. However, with the help of the community and fellow players you can get better at the game and advance. Try the game out and sink some time into learning how to play better and trust me it will be a great pass time if not a great game to enjoy overall.

I've played Smite for a very long time now and am very happy to see it show up on Steam.
Smite is a MOBA for people who like the gameplay/idea of MOBAs but may not necessarily be big fans of RTS controls, a category which I happen to find myself.
I tried very hard to like Dota 2 and LoL, and there really was a lot to like about those games but I just never really got a good feel for the controls.
Having been an extremely avid MMO player in the Vanilla WoW days, I already had a pretty good feel for a third perspective PvP game, so if this type of perspective/playstyle is to your liking then you should give Smite a try.  This comes with a drawback however, as you cannot see behind you with much distance so getting flanked is that much more dangerous.
The main point that really drove Smite home for me was that most abilities in the game require a skillshot to some degree, and all auto attacks do.  No longer was I pressing an attack button and focusing on getting in range to use my abilities.  When auto attacking, where I personally aimed had an effect on whether or not it landed.  When using abilities, a translucent display of the area/direction of the attack would appear and I could place it dynamically based on the type of move it was.
After a short time playing with the starter gods and enjoying them immensely I purchased the "God Pack" and have not looked back since.
Pros:
+ Attractive graphics, character models and animations.
+ Several game modes to enjoy for casual and competitive players
+ Third person perspective
+ Free to Play
+ Microtransaction items are aesthetic in nature only
+ Starter Gods are pretty well rounded characters and see high level competitive play, and more can be unlocked by ingame currency if you want to stay Free to Play.
Cons:
- Just like every highly competitive online game, you will run into some pretty toxic players.
- Still runs with Direct X 9?

Ignore all of the negative reviews from before August 2016 complaining of bugs. The game has been patched since then, but these people never changed their reviews. Just give them thumbs down so they get buried.

A beautiful side-scrolling shoot-em-up with a gorgeous soundtrack, with numerous unlockable weapon and option configurations. While challenging, the control scheme is perhaps not as complex as, say, GundeadLigne.
As of the August 23rd, 2016 update, most of the bugs (including the constantly firing bug and text issues in some of the screens) have been fixed.

Taken as a whole, Diadra Empty is just that little bit better than passable that warrants a recommendation--but just barely. Do not be deceived by the screenshots; Diadra Empty is not your standard sidescrolling bullet hell shmup. Compared to other offerings in the genre, the gameplay is immensely complex. Rather than traveling a linear route from left to right, the game takes place in a large arena, and your task is to defeat as many of the enemies as possible in order to gain the currency required to level up your abilities and defeat the occasional boss. Not only is there a significant variety of standard attacks, there is also an additional layer of strategy that requires you to use your money wisely and purchase the upgrades that will optimize your playstyle.
The game's learning curve is ridiculously steep. There's a written tutorial, but for those starting out, it makes little sense. The inclusion of an interactive tutorial would have done a lot to alleviate the lingering confusion of your two different shots, your dash, your dash attack, your option, the finer points of strafing, the limits of your invincibility frames, your three different types of bombs and the different controls for using them, the leveling system, and all the other crap you're expected to know going in. Do not be surprised if it takes you a very long time to get the jist of how to play the game, and expect it to take a couple of hours before you've grasped the finer points firmly enough to play the game well.
The investment of time and effort required to learn how to play Diadra Empty does eventually pay off, just not in huge dividends. It's a fun enough little game. It's just debatable whether it's fun enough to be worth learning its myriad intricacies. It has a good soundtrack, and I found it just barely fun enough to be worth learning how to play at some level of proficiency. I recommend Diadra Empty, but I qualify that with a warning that your mileage may vary.

Autofire bug has been fixed, and ESC no longer hard-closes the game.
Diadra Empty is one of the most unique shmups I've ever played, and one of my favourite. I have history with this game, so my review's going to show some bias.
Undeniably its strongest point is the gameplay. It does a lot to set itself apart from other shmups.
As you play through each stage you'll collect coins with which you can unlock new upgrades. Multiple playthroughs will unlock new weapons. Combining these lets you experience some really different playstyles. Mastering the game is a matter of making the best use of these, and learning how to best collect and spend your coins. There are more mechanics to master, but luckily the in-game manual does a good job of telling you as long as you remember to check up on it as it unlocks.
The game is a refreshing kind of chaos in motion. It has a lot of nice touches, but its age also shows. It was first released nearly 10 years ago at C73. It was made by a small team of people before the term "indie game" was even really being thrown around.
It's not very well optimized. It has limited resolution settings. It doesn't have real custom keybinds. Nearly every screen is very informationally dense. Most if not all of the soundtrack, while being expertly picked, consists of freebies from sites like sentive.
None of those things stop me from loving and playing this game again and again. If you're curious, I really recommend giving it a shot, especially on sale. See if you can use your 2 hours to get to stage 5, where the game will reveal a good chunk of what it has to offer.

OK, My ADHD has been kicking in something ugly for weeks, and have not been able to realy sit down and get into a game, a few days before this, I was mindlessly running through my "que". In two days I racked up over 900+ views! Yup that distracted.
Among the que was this game. I was thinking about getting into a vidual novel, but did not know what one, so I followed most of them. VOICES FROM THE SEA came up free, so I downloaded it and started it. For a moment, I thought my ADHD was going to steal my time away again, but something made me keep "clicking" and reading. Maybe it was because I could related to the boy in the story. Or maybe when I was his age, I wished something like this would have happened. Regardless of the reason, I blocked out the world, and kept reading.
After a couple hours, I finished it. The last few minutes had me running for the tissue - as it was one of those rare(for me) moving stories - the emotional climax will hit you fast - the timing was perfect.  You didnt realize it was going to happen until it did. And even though, you might have suspected the ending, it was OK. It was just the way it was supposed to be.
I was so glad this one was free, as it will definately make me take a look at some other visual novels. But I think I might savor the memory of this one for a bit, before I mash it with another story.
While the gfx are colorful and "cute", the storyline, is very mature (in a matter of speaking), and not the typical visual novel - this one would be good for your children - to make them realize just what they REALLY have in life that is important.

The arcade mode unlocks a character skin for everyone you beat it with. These skins are actually individual characters that have important roles in the story modes.
To be honest I haven't tried playing this with any friends yet and I don't know how fun it would be since a lot of moves can be really abusable, but if you're on the same level as your peers, I'd definitely think it would be a great 1v1 experience.

Overall I would highly recommend this game to anyone who likes 2D fighters and value for their money!

Geometry Wars 3 is a very pure video game.  Aside from the wonderful graphics, very little about the game is far beyond the older games it draws inspiration from: iconic Twin-Stick Shooters like Robotron and visual design elements from Tempest.  Although GW3 does have a ton of content (including a huge free update that came out long ago, the Evolved update), you'll find all of that content involves moving your ship with the left stick and shooting all around you with the right stick.  It's a fun game but the core experience never really changes, so you can know if you'll love it or hate it just from watching the trailers.
I love it.
There are a ton of different modes and a nice mix of enemy types with several cool boss fights as well.  Almost all enemies in GW3 do not shoot at you: this is not a bullet hell.  Instead they just try to collide with you and you die in one hit.  Enemies vary in their AI / movement speed / health and are easily identified because they are distinct shapes and color-coded.  Initially the game can seem quite easy but you'll find that a lot of the endless modes can get downright insane.  Also there's a big difference between barely finishing Adventure Mode once... and 3-starring every level like I did for the achievement.  Make no mistake, you get a lot from this game for the price.  The graphics are amazing, but the music is only so-so.  I recommend turning it down and playing your own music instead: that enhanced the experience for me.  The story is... what did you actually expect a story?  You shoot everything.  Also it has multiplayer and online leaderboards for what that's worth.
Console version is amazing, but this is a poor port.  144fps reported, yet its choppy and with input lag.  Do not recommend.

The other Souls games were challenging, but fair. While I love the brutal difficulty and crave more due to the sense of accomplishment, the difficulty actually served an artistic purpose in the other games. They weren't just hard for the sake of serving as a marketing gimmick (I'm talking to you Namco). They existed to create tension and immerse players into the world. They wanted you to feel the sense of dread, curiosity, and punishment for carelessness. This game shows exactly what the gaming medium can accomplish because it is pure. The story is simple and the lore of the world is in the background waiting to be discovered by passionate fans. Why can't this become the normal practice for modern games?
In Dark Souls II you can feel the absence of the former design director because the game does not feel as polished. I could give some examples, but they are too small to really complain about. It's not a masterpiece. This game is ultimately an expansion that brings nothing new to the table and I'm perfectly fine with that and more than happy to pay 50 dollars for and put 100 hours into. An overall excellent SHMUP.  Some of my thoughts on the game:
- Not quite bullet-hell in the way most may be used to.  Rather than micro-dodging elaborate patterns, you're avoiding the main avenues of fire while shooting the smaller 'chip' shots out of the sky before they reach you.  You have a Strafe that gives you limited invulnerability to break through large walls of fire/enemies to reach a more favorable position.
- Art direction is lovely, although it's hard to make out exactly what some of the small sprites are, haha.  The visual effects can be a problem in the insanity toward the end of EXTRA, but otherwise it's okay as long as you're paying attention.
- The soundtrack is incredible, and the entire reason I became interested in the game.  In particular, 'Nebula', the theme from the crazy-to-reach-let-alone-clear EXTRA Stage 5, has become one of my favorite tracks in games, period.
- As others have noted, the are unfortunately several bugs in this port, and it's unknown if we'll get any fix.  None are gamebreaking and there's a few workarounds, but don't expect to get a good read on your scores.
- There's a lot of customization in your shots.  3 Turbo styles (Hold, toggle, side shooting), fully mappable buttons, 12 shot types, etc.  Some things are locked at the start, and are unlocked after a certain number of cumulative level ups across all playthroughs.  It's also controller-friendly if you prefer.
- Since it's based on macro instead of micro dodging, movement feels a bit too floaty.  You'll also move some on the screen even if you aren't telling it to.  Something to keep in mind so you don't ram a wave of bullets.  Derpy dragons can't hover it seems.
Overall, I recommend you give this a try.  It's not my favorite SHMUP, but it's not one I'm going to forget.

Summary: Hori bullet hell with upgrades
Multiplayer: No
Completion: 3 hrs
Cards: Yes
Cloud: Yes
In a nutshell, Diadra Empty is a horizontal bullet hell style game, with the ability to upgrade your weapons and defenses between rounds. An obvious analogue to this is the Touhou series, except imagine that horizontally. You play in a single, large rectangular field with no terrain obstacles, and the ability to face and move backwards. The field does not wrap around, so it's quite possible to get cornered. Fortunately the game provides you with a "turbo" boost that you can use to become temporarily invulnerable, and a handful of bombs (called "Storm Savers") to convert enemy bullets on-screen into cash.  Between rounds, you are given several categories to upgrade your character using coins you gathered throughout your journey. I like that every weapon undergoes a visible upgrade, so you feel like you are getting stronger.
The story is about a girl, Nyalra who sets out to find her sister whilst riding atop her dragon, Minimi, though you wouldn't really get that unless you looked at the store page or manual. The narrative is told through occasional sentences at the start of each stage and the ending sequence. It goes for a somewhat minimal, artful approach, which isn't really my thing, so I'll just leave it at that.
Diadra is a rather pretty game, if you can stop and appreciate the bazillion bullet patterns on the screen. I haven't experienced any slowdown like I have in some other titles, so that's a good sign. On top of that, Diadra boasts some nice relaxing music, mostly somber piano scores or upbeat electronica. One criticism I have is that the story font is really tiny. The game is always in a 4:3 aspect ratio, which results in side bars on a widescreen monitor. I have to get up close to the screen to read the story text, which is displayed on the screen very briefly. It's hard on the eyes and by the time I realized there was text on the screen, it was usually gone.
The game offers three difficulty levels. Each must be unlocked in ascending order by completing the previous one. The easiest difficulty is a nice pace. It's not too hard and not exactly a cakewalk either. But after that, the game goes all out and goes nuts with the bullets and enemy health. Surprisingly the difficulty settings set up each stage differently. It's not just a simple damage and health multiplier; more enemies spawn, different ones show up, and more bullets are fired faster. And bosses galore.
I'm not entirely sure what the process is to unlock new weapons and features. I presume it all boils down to "play more", but I don't know how much more they expect me to play. I would have liked the game to explain the requirements for unlockables.
There's not a great deal of replay value, other than trying to unlock stuff. I rate Diadra Empty a 7/10. It's short, cute, and hectic. As far as bullet hell games go, this is one of the better ones.

In Diadra Empty, you take the role of Nyalra and her faithful dragon Minimi. You embark on an incredible quest to save your sis-MINIMI? Is Nyalra Dr. Evil? Did she take one look at this dragon and say "Breathtaking. I shall call him... Minimi."? What the heck kind of title is Diadra Empty anyway? Is Diadra Nyalra's sister? Why is she Empty? Maybe the developer didn't want to call it "Diadra is Missing" because it sounds too much like
. Besides, Diadra Empty is a perfectly acceptable nonsense-name for a doujin 2D shooter.
This is another shmup, and you know what that means; all of the plot is removed so there's room for more bullets. Unlike other side-view shooters, Diadra Empty is free-roaming. If you're using a controller, you're more or less forced to use the analog stick. Oddly enough, it's a sensible design-decision in this game. There will be millions of bullets, but you have an invincible wing-smash move to scoot through everything. You're expected to become attached to this maneuver, because monsters will come from every possible direction. It also helps to keep an eye on your defender-esque radar. Not only does this beauty keep track of you and the enemies, but it also accounts for projectiles, which is absurd but also amazing.
All you really need to do, in order to finish this game, is maximize your gains. There's a shop in-between stages where you can purchase upgrades. In order to get money you have to kill stuff. It helps to keep your finger off the fire button. Nyalra opts to fire away regardless, and you'll absorb cash from further away. The right combination of weapons is also very important. When you first play the game, your offensive options are pretty limited. As you progress, new weapons, formations, and even special config options will unlock. In my opinion, it's better to focus on raw power. Weapons with a lot of range sound nice, but they're either too weak or slow to do much of anything.
Everything else in this game can be handled with a little practice. The average play-through is about 20 minutes, so you'll have an easy time memorizing what spawns in each stage. Even the last boss and its multiple forms of increasing ludicrousness isn't too bad once you know when & where to wing-smash. It's also nice that the weapon-selection and upgrade paths lend unique qualities to every play-through. Eventually the natural level of difficulty will feel too easy. If that's the case, then it's time to move on to True difficulty. This mode is not to be taken lightly. I went with some poor weapon choices. This led to situations where I had to hide in the corner until all of the big mean monsters got bored and flew away.
If that still isn't enough, there is an Extra mode. Basically this is where the developer threw a bunch of bosses and enemies together. At this point it's just absurd, with bosses spawning on top of bosses. The final stage is also a serious test of endurance. This mode is accompanied by some awesome music as well. The entirety of the soundtrack is great, but the high-energy tunes in Extra are sublime. It's a shame that the last unlock is a stage select. I guess it's good for practicing - you can set upgrade-levels too - but I would have preferred... well... something else. It just seems sort-of anti-climatic, after all the insanity in the True and Extra modes.
The real flaws in this game are due to the Steam port. Some issues (like hi-scores not showing up) don't make any sense at all. I was able to trigger full-screen by setting it in the options, then restarting the game, but I've heard of players having other screen-related difficulties. Nyalra is also not supposed to fire all the time. It could be considered a minor problem, unless you're going for the "wing-smash only" achievement, then it becomes impossible to deal with. The publisher mentioned a patch, but they've been quiet for the past few months. The game is still enjoyable regardless. However, If anyone thinks that this port is inexcusable, then they're perfectly right. I'm not too happy about it either.
Diadra Empty is a really good shooter. It has cool ideas, great music, and the balanced difficulty makes for a tense but still very enjoyable game. Unfortunately, you have to approach this title with the mindset that its various port-related issues may never be resolved. Playing for a hi-score is part of what gives a shmup long-term appeal. It's total crap, when the incentive to learn the scoring system is lost due to shoddy programming. Online leaderboards would have been a tremendous addition, but I guess that's a distant dream at this point.
The game is still mostly playable, but it deserves better.

Right, to pre-face this review I'd just like to point out that I have fully explored and completed the game.  This review may have some bias because A) I like thrillers and horrors and B) I'm human.  Humans are basically greedy pigeons in people-form and go after things they're most likely to like.  That said, I do try to make constructive and honest criticism.
(minor spoilers, nothing not given away by it's description)
You are a struggling architect called out to a prospective clients place at night.  Whereupon you must solve puzzles in order to get through the house and leave.  Is this really a client?  Is it some elaborate set-up by a killer?  Hasn't the owner ever heard of DIY or basic tidying up?  Only you will ever be able to guess.
Primarily it is a guess.  You solve puzzles by using items in the environment, occasionally on other items.  That is it.
* The sound design is actually very accomplished, with materials sounds, effects in the environment and the odd sound from your character being incredibly close to perfect.
*Understated but charming music, a bit light on horror in some areas but still good and enjoyable.
*Voice acting - in-game speech is pretty good, the character reactions are believable.
*Good use of assets and the game areas are nice and consistent.
*Opening and closing cutscenes are very much 'tell' not 'show' and, in my opinion, tell too much.
*The story is basic.  There's some tantalising ideas there, real stuff that could be fascinating, but they're not delved into leaving it as little more than a 3d escape the room game.
*Load times can be awful.  The game seems to struggle to load from a continue in a timely fashion.
*Still buggy too.  Should maybe have spent some time in Early Access to get more issues worked out before release but the dev is approachable, fixes bugs and crashes as quickly as humanly possible and engages with their community.  With so many Indie and triple-A developers treating player communities as a personal Fiefdom this is a genuinely refreshing change and one that deserves recognition.
*Oh my goodness the voiceacting.  In-game is good but the two cutscene ones bounce between a ponderous bedtime story and a poorly done police cliche.  I laughed so hard.
Clues as to what is going on are hidden around the house but nothing is baby-fed to you with the exception of the opening and closing scenes.  This I like.  It feels, despite being a short and simplistic puzzle game, like the developers actually trust that gamers have brains and can think for themselves.  The opening and closing scenes are exposition shotguns, with a lot of telling rather than showing but you can get a good sense of what the developer was going for - black and white stills are done alongside a narration from the main character.  Dumping some of the information and getting 3d models or much more stylistic imagery to do parts of it would improve the immersion as well as the sense of dread.
There's little in the way of a threat but there is an almost palpable sense of something being wrong or out to get you.  This is often due to the really quite nice sound design - the soundtrack is good too.  Graphically, it looks very 'Unity' or 'FPS Maker' but the use of lighting effects and well-placed assets that look as if they fit together, so it may not be beautiful but it is functional and is by no means ugly.  Pacing is good in regards to the set events although I would have liked a bit more tension and orchestral stress-building music prior to them.
Controls are the standard ones for a first person game.  WADS for movement, F for flashlight, C for crouching and Shift for running.  Mouse for looking around and investigating.  They're responsive though it is possible to pick items up through the walls (rarely, but it can happen) and the head-bob is only slight - a boon for those of us who find it irritating and over-used.  When you move it feels like there's some weight to your character, they're not too floaty and the sound design helps with that.
Bugs and glitches are being sorted as they're reported and quickly too.  The only ones I came across were the flashlight being held oddly by the character, rending it nearly useless (you don't really need it), being able to pick up some slabs from outside whilst looking at a cupboard in the shed and an odd tendency to crash if I attempted to move during the first autosave.  The dev is approachable, reaches out to players and does seem to be listening to their community to make this short experience as good as possible.  EA and certain other teams (like non-terrestrial murder (I know, a joke for all the Jim Sterling fans there - I really don't want to be sued because of telling the truth) could genuinely learn a thing or two about player engagement and making the community feel involved.
I recommend this game.  Yes, it's short, has issues and has nothing on games like The Room when it comes to puzzles.  However, it has a spark of something and I hope the dev continues to work on this concept and improve.  So much is right or nearly there that I am pleased I played this very short game.  I feel that it was worth a few minutes of my time in spite of its issues.  Yes, it's free but it still costs time and that isn't enough to give a game a free ride.  This feels like an old-school demo for something greater, and I would not mind that at all.  Particularly as there's so many developers who sell an even shorter or non-functional game for ridiculous sums when the demo route has more honesty to it, in general.  For a first release everyone involved should be proud - first releases are often awful, this one may hedge on the mediocre at times but by no means is it bad.

ASTRONEER is an early access space exploration game.  Just keep in mind that this is my opinion based on my experinces in the game and what I look for in a game.
I will start with what I do not like and what makes me uncomfortable about the game and then go into what I do like.
-Being an Early Access game there is a chance the game will never actually be finished staying in early access forever.  Which is a pretty big shame when it happens to games especially games that show a lot of potential.  The game is in Pre-Alpha and updates with patches once or twice a month.  So it looks like it will be in early access for a while.
-Lack of content.  Being an early access game based around exploring a procedually generated worlds there is a lack of actual content.  The game at the moment consists of building a base to produce the recources for space travel and go to another world to do it again.  That is the actual physical content, the rest of the game is based around exploring and seeing cool things which I will say there is cool and interesting things to see.  Another thing to mention, because of the lack of content you reasonably have a few hours of playtime before you start doing things over and over again, 20 dollars may be a bit much for the time.
At the current state of the game those are the only major negatives I can think to point out, now onto the things I like about the game.
-While not super important, I am in love with the graphics of this game.  Everything has a cartoony look.  All the terrain, rocks and such are really nice looking low-poly models (and I will say I am a sucker for both cartoon graphics and low-poly models).  The lighting is really pretty and differs greatly depending on the planet you are on.
-The controls of the player is really nice and I don't often get frustrated thinking to myself "I didn't mean to do that!".  If I fall into a hole it is because I pushed the buttons to do so, not becuase of the game's controls.
-Building bases is kind of simplistic just being modules that extend from each other but you can also carve or create terrain to be whatever you need/want.  I could be missing something but I have never seen a game that allowed you to mess with the world in such a way that didn't involve blocks.
-Another cool thing about the game is the physics.  Physics are hard to really get excited about it.  Either physics are okay and nothing to shout about or they are terrible and should be shouted at.  ASTRONEER has what seems to me dynamic gravity depending on the size of the world you are on and how far down into the world you are.   Digging down into the core of the world I think perhaps could put you in a state of gravity where you are just floating around.  You might not care but I think that is awesome.
-Multiplayer, the game is so much fun with a friend or two and it is really easy to connect to each other (literally hit join game on the friends list).  Either the two of you are trying to reach a goal or just messing around.  An example of something that had happend; me and a friend were playing and he was new to the game and I had found a chair in a crashed space craft and he wanted it.  He sat in the chair when I brought it back and I carried it straight up into the air so that if he jumped out he would die from the fall damage.  Another thing, we were having trouble triggering an explosive (as it was a bit bugged) and somehow I had triggered the bomb on his back and he ran to me when it blew up and we both died.  Really good times.  If you have a friend that also has the game and has played it, I highly recommend that they hold your hand to teach you how to get started, but let you discover things on your own at the same time.
So all in all I recommend this game especially if it goes on sale.  You have any questions about the game I will be sure to answer them as unbias as I can.

The story wasn't too surprising, but it was filled with interesting bits the whole way through that kept me wanting more. The non-lethal eliminations for key targets were far less... horrifying than the original game's. It was less about destroying their lives, and more about taking their power away. I felt like my character really was doing her best to fix things, and the main character being reasonable does wonders for immersion.
The characters were well-acted and had a lot to say. The gameplay gave even more options than the original, especially for non-lethal combat. The addition of a second playable character is awesome, not even considering how much more customization each character has with more upgrades, more bone charms, and even bone charm crafting.
Graphically, it was very nice. Nothing amazing for 2016, but you'll be hard pressed to find texture or models that are offensive, and the big picture has a great aesthetic. Unfortunately, this comes with the sour note of "bad FPS", which hopefully can be improves over time. I might rate the graphics more highly if I could actually run it on ultra or very high with a tolerable framerate.
Length-wise, it'll last you about 10 to 20 hours for one playthrough, depending on how you play and how much you explore. With different endings, different characters, and different solutions to every problem, I imagine this would be a good game to revisit.
Overall, it was a great game. I think I'd give it a 8.5/10, because it gave me basically everything I wanted with no huge flaws, but failed to really blow me away.

This game is pretty cool. I love the 90's fighter game aesthetic it has. I got it on a good sale for .59 cents and even at full price its not a bad deal, I know I dropped way more quarters than that into Street Fighter 2 arcade games when I was a kid.
Arcade mode I found to be pretty easy, I beat it in a little under half an hr.
Survival mode I found more challenging since you only have 1 life and its not best out of 3 rounds.
Story mode is kinda cool also for something a little different. Each match has conditions you have to meet to win rather than just  free for all beat em up. You start out only using  punches and kicks on the first guy, then you might have to utilize a combo or one of your special attacks to do damage on another, or you have to try and avoid the enemy  until the time runs out for example.
There is no native Linux port so I had to play it through WINE. Any of the issues I describe in this next paragraph are only in relation to that. Windows users most likely won't have any of these issues!
My only disappoint was  a limitation in WINE which doesn't allow me to use my X-Box controller to play it. This problem is across the board and not unique to this game though.This kind of game is made for playing on a controller, but its still playable on a  keyboard.
I also had a few random crashes which seemed to coincide with getting trading card drops.All my cards for this  game have dropped now, so I am curious if there will be anymore crashes going forward. I will update this review if I still have random crashes.
*EDIT*
Random crashes still happen even after getting all the cards. I am downgrading WINE support from good to fair. It doesn't always crash, but has happened multiple times now fighting the last boss which is pretty annoying.

I will admit though that when I saw that this game was funded by Kickstarter I was very wierded out by this. For one thing people actually paid for this to be made? I mentioned that the art was good.... but all you have is small portraits of characters, backgrounds, and a bit of art. I don't think all that is worth 1, 2, $4,509! Now if this all went towards the DLC maybe that would make sense but I have not downloaded the DLC and I don't really plan on it either. What's worse is that if these guys would have waited they probably would have been able to make it easily with the Visual Novel Maker that just recently came out. They possibly could have made this game for about $15 (Or at least the free version, again no exposure to the DLC).

ORIGINAL REVIEW (Recommended at the time):
Diadra Empty is an obscure and awesome free-roaming bullet hell shooter unlike most other games in the recent years.
The game allows you to use up to two different weapons to shoot stuff, in which you will even unlock more as you keep playing. You are also allowed to dash to be temporarily invincible to cover against most bullet waves and can be used as an attack. Should you get hit by an enemy or a bullet, there's a Defense mechanic where shields you from losing a life once until it recharges back to full. The game also has an upgrade system where you use up gathered coins to power up certain things such as your weapon shots or movement speed. You will definitely be playing this game more times not only to unlock more weapons to choose from but also to unlock other game modes (haven't tried them yet as of this review) and as well as more useful tips in the main menu. There are a few bugs here and there (Results Screen displaying incorrectly is one of them) but none of them affects the gameplay so far. Also, you should
hit the Escape button if you play this game with your keyboard.
The soundtrack is also pretty good and it blends in with the game's atmosphere.
There's not much else I can say here and it's extremely hard for me to express the game in words. I'd recommend watching the trailer in the store page to see it for yourself (There are a few gameplay videos of this game on YouTube, but there's also a longplay of it by Rockin' Android if you're interested.). I don't know if there is a demo present, but you're free to explore around to find it. This game was on Steam Greenlight but there was no mentioning of the game's release for over a year. Thus, the game became obscured within the depths of Steam.
This review may be updated once I've play a couple more times in this game and/or something else happens here.

Game control 6/10
Pausing mechanism is slightly annoying that you have to use S key to pause instead of ESC key. Which this ESC key directly brings you back to your desktop and results in you staring at your desktop for full 10 seconds and asking yourself isn't ESC the pause key?
Game play 8/10
Standard bullet hell game, however, it does introduce an upgrade system allows you to upgrade your character's abilities. Since you can only control one character, the game provides you new weapon every time when you level up 3 full levels until you successfully unlocked every type of options. As for game play itself, screen full of bullets and enemies are expected. However, the game uses turbo movement(makes the character move faster) instead of precise movement(makes the character move slower), results in easier to escape from enemies but harder to fight the bosses since it gets harder to approach bosses while avoiding bullets. Overall the game flows really well as a bullet hell game, however, I do not appreciate the game throws three bosses into my face in a row.
User Interface 5/10
It is user friendly, shows all the controls upon player starting the game. However, a major problem is the game provides you the option to use ESC to exit the game and P key to pause the game. This is not really a problem until players realize using ESC to exit the game will not save the player's status. In order to save the status, player is required to use the Exit option in the menu, rendering ESC key completely useless or downright annoying. Art style is enjoyable.
Background Music 7/10
It fits the genre of bullet hell games, which is similar to Touhou project in my opinion. An audio setting option will be nice though, really.
Overall 7/10 Slightly annoying UI
Otherwise, this game should be a refreshing game if you like bullet hell games or want to try this type of games.

Dishonored 2 is a great example of the phrase "If it's not broken, don't fix it", as in, it feels a lot like the first game, but provides enough new content to make it worth your time and money. Dishonored 2 has you play as either Emily or Corvo, and depending on who you choose, you receive different powers, or you can go for no powers at all. You can choose to play stealthily, or all out combat, and you can also choose to pursue lethal or non-lethal ways to take out your enemies, which lead to different endings respectively. The story is great, and has a good pace to it. The combat feels satisfying, and the graphics are beautiful, retaining the same visual style as the first game, but upgraded. The only issue I ran into when playing this game was the bad optimisation, which led to lag in some areas, but the developers have already said that they are aware of the issue, and looking into it. If you enjoyed the first game, then you'll definitely enjoy its sequel. It's also a must buy if you're into stealth/action games such as Thief and Assassin's creed.

When I heard Arkane were finally making a sequel to my beloved Dishonored I peed my pants a bit then I cried a bit because sequels to your most beloved games are often♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ take Dragon Age II for example, a game I came to love but made me sick to my stomach after Origins. I was terrified that they would change it too much, try to be trendy and keep up with the kids, maybe include Minecraft inspired settlement building or an Angry Birds level or some other equally horrible commerical balls. However, I am ecstatic to say that Dishonored is still Dishonored, it still has the same lonely, gritty atmosphere, the same beautifully realised world, hidden secrets, tragic and incredibly drawn NPCs and is as rich in lore and intrigue as the original. The stealth and combat use the exact same mechanics too which means I was able to pick up my controller and hammer away at the buttons and die just as easily as I did the first time around.  I will say that I am finding it much more challenging this time, but that is probably only because I played the original to death and need more practice.
I've chosen Emily for my first playthrough because it seems natural for the story to follow her events. She has some incredible new powers which I am still getting to grips with, particularly Doppelganger which projects a copy of her that the guards are supposed to chase leaving you to get away clean. My Doppelganger, however, runs towards me drawing the hostiles  This is me being hopeless and drunk rather than the game I think...
The voices are wonderful, I was particularly worried about Corvo being voiced since he is supposed to be the classic silent protagonist but Stephen Russell (Garrett, Nick Valentine and Mercer Fray among othersl) is suble and somehow lovable in his role, as is Erica Lutrell as Emily. She manages to sound both like Chloe Moretz (young Emily) and like her mother, Jessamine Kaldwin voiced by April Stewart in the original.
Overall it is harder and creepier than before.  Playing with headphones makes the guards' footsteps almost unbearably scary and there is this screaming, insane woman.. The tension has been ramped up along with enemies' lethality - be warned it seems to be much harder to escape when you thought you were just gonna smack that guard over the head with a whisky bottle...
A quick word about performance - yes I've been having issues with horrible lag too and no I don't play on a potato, or a toaster or microwave. My rig is top notch, although my best GPU died recently, my second best is still above and beyond recommended settings. Having said that its not, like, unplayable - it lags and stutters sometimes and combat is bloody difficult because of it, but I am still over the moon because it is Dishonored and they will make a patch and it fills my sad and lonely life with joy so peace out my gameplaying friends.
Dislikes: I'm not keen on the Outsider's new voice he sounds like he is on a combination of Helium and Caffeine, he needs to sound more mysterious and menacing, we're not having a chat in Starbucks, we're supposed to be in the goddam Void for chrissakes. I can't remember the others because I am drunk. Oh yeah, I die a lot but that's probably because I am drunk.
TL;DR Just buy the damn game already, unless your computer really is a potato.

This cops & robbers themed 2D fighter is shallow as a pool and about as wide as one as well. The fighting mechanics are stunningly simplistic, to a point where brawlers from the 90's, such as the Streets of Rage series, offer a far more enjoyable experience. Hell, the game offers achievements for precisely two fighting related things: getting a four hit combo and winning a fight in 10 seconds. That should be an ample summary of what the combat is like. The only interesting thing on display here was the handcuff mechanic for the coppers, and the sticky bomb mechanic for the robbers (or at least the one robber I played). What that, or the "Wasted" mechanic did however, I haven't the foggiest. Probably has to do with the story mode, but the gameplay isn't interesting enough for me to spend any more time with the game, so I suppose I'll never find out. Ultimately, it wouldn't make the combat any less shallow, so it doesn't matter.
It's not that it's a bad game. It's well made and has that nice retro aesthetic. It's just that I've seen mobile games with more depth, and in a fighting game the gameplay needs to come first, and everything else third. I played through the arcade mode once and that was enough for me. Half of that would've sufficed, but I powered through in hopes of seeing something more, but I found nothing that would ever have me come back to this again. Doesn't matter if it costs 3€. You can get better stuff for that money, and if you're looking for a cops & robbers game with fighting, I think I'll stick with recommending Streets of Rage 1, which sounds, looks and plays better.

This review is aimed primarily at MP.
The campaign section of the game is pretty much what you can expect from any COD game.  Well crafted, enjoyable with expceptional graphic fidelity.  Oh, with an added Spacey here and there.
Ok it appears that I have not suffered the lag or FPS issues that it appears many users have  so I cant comment on what alot of people have said the games main failing is. With that said there are a host of positives about this game.....
Ive played many of the COD editions, I also thought Ghosts was terrible.  However AW sufferes from none of its issues.
The MP with Exo suits is frantically fast and requires mastery of a whole new set of skills.  Exo doge, exo jump, exo doge jump, exo slide and a host of exo abilities like cloak, speed boost or increased health adds a whole new layer of MP complexity.
You will not look at a MP the same way when you can vault over walls and obstacles to boot slam some unwary opponent right in the back of the head.   Mmmmm crunchily satisfying.
The loot drop and customisation options are virtually endless.  New gear drops regularly in three classes of quality, green, blue an yellow.  You can even drop elite versions of weapons with different skins and stats which can fit different attachments from their vanilla variants........ awesome.
Scorestreaks can also be customised in a myriad of ways.  For exampe carpackages can be trapped or even have the scorstreak tally survive through death.  Thats right, you no longer need to chain 3 or four kills to get one.  It does come with a cost however as it will require a larger score to earn the package.
Personally in the 80 hours Ive put down this game already Ive not seen anyone that I can say hand on heart was hacking.  Ive come up against some consistantly good players but  Ive also seen them have poor rounds. So the endless cries of hackers everywhere to me rings false.  No doubt they have been there but they have not impacted my enjoyment of AW at all.
The game does not yet have dedicated servers but apparently its coming.  Im easy either way.  I dont much mind lobbies, but im aware that this is an issue for many people.   Its coming, but I fully acknowledge the argument that it probably should have been there day 1.
Im quite surprised at all the negative reviews.... This game is a MP masterpiece. Honestly if you like twich MP gameplay then look no further than AW.  It is absolutly worth every dollar.

Blind Trust is a free to play Two-Person CoOperative exploration game.  It worked on Win 10, looked ok , played ok, sounded ok.  It Requires active steam friend to play, has peer to peer servers.  I used my second steam account to play some of this game.  Nobody hosting servers out there at the time of writing review.   Has steam achievements, some easy ones.  Has a short tutorial that you Have to complete before you move on to the rest of game.  The graphics are simple polygon shaped and crude character models.  If 1 player dies then it is game over.  Sound fx are ok.  Has a background music that the soldier hears that sounds ok.  Oracle Require Headphones that can do 3D directional.  Has low computer requirements.
It is a LAN Game only. Worked good to have your main computer host server and play the Soldier then if you have a separate laptop with other steam account to play the Oracle.  This way you could speed up play some by just directly viewing the movement of the Oracle.  You might could use a voice over ip connection to speak instructions to your partner and Hamachi for remote connection across the Internet.
CONS:
- No directions after you finish the tutorial.
- Can be buggy.
- It is a LAN game, you have to use Hamachi if you want to play with people across the Internet.
Try it, only if you have two computers on a LAN.

I have never really written a review for any game on steam, but this game breaks that mold, in fact it breaks lots of molds in the MOBA genre in all. Its a MOBA game that uses a third person camera at all times, while this may seem like a quirky gimmic that makes the game uninteresting in a few moments of gameplay it does not. It always keeps my attention and I waste hours playing this game without even realising it and thats the thing. Whenever I try to play any other MOBA game (Dota 2/League of Legends) I get bored quickly because I feel like the action just isnt there. This game on the contrary is always filled with excitment and im always on my toes when I play this game. All of the Basic attacks are whats called "skill shots" meaning you have to aim in order to kill anyone in this game. Unlike other MOBA games you do not click on the ground to move, instead you move with the WASD keys and you have to option to re bind them to something else. Currently the game has about 69 Gods to play as from different pantheons. Gods are essentially your character that you can choose to play as or a "Champion" if you will and they all look and sound Great! Hell the entire game looks amazing even when everything was turned down on low! The game modes vary from conquest (5V5) to Joust (3V3) and if that isnt enough you have a MOTD or a "mode of the day" which should add a little something to your life if you ever get bored of Classic 5V5. A MOTD is a random mode with the rules changed whether it be Extra money or all one character or a mode where everyone is already to the max level. In the end I could keep going about how amazing this game is ( I have played this for like a gazillion hours before it even came to steam) Or I could just end on saying, if you want to try a MOBA game thats a little diffrent but still fun Smite is your game!

Half-Life: Source is a science fiction first person shooter gamer developed by Valve Software for the source engine, obviously. It follows the misadventures of a guy with glasses as he shoots aliens with guns, in HD! Sort of.
So in an attempt to hype up the source engine, which Half-Life 2 was developed on as well, Valve went on ahead and ported Half-Life, a GoldSrc game, to the Source engine, obviously. Sort of. See the thing is, it's not a perfect port, and it's imperfect for a ton of dumb, easy to fix reasons. It baffled me, walking through the halls of "HD" Black Mesa, seeing scientists hover above their chairs, guns dropped by enemies wedged into the walls next to them, and various times where the gameplay didn't trigger causing me to have to reload. These problems are generally specfic to the moments they happen in, and would take 14 seconds to fix, literally. Those scientists doing their xen yoga tricks (see what i did there?) above their chairs are props, not npc's, what's stopping Valve from just realigning them so they actually SIT on the chairs?
The slightly higher definition textures and lighting effects are nice, I like that metal shine for sure, but if you're anything like me then the graphics of vanillla Half-Life hold a lot of charm, and if you're not like me than the graphics of HL: Source don't upgrade enough to impress you. If you want to get into classic Half-Life but think it hasn't aged very well, (who can blame you?) than I recommend Black Mesa instead, it's a much more solid remake of Half-Life and eons more care went into that than went into this. It's really baffling that, for all the playtesting Valve holds dear, it feels like they never actually tested this product to see if it holds up.
There are worse ways to spend your money, and this tends to go pretty low in price during sales, but I'd honestly pass on this.

I didn't want to write a review on this game until I had beaten it at least once, so I didn't contradict myself in my review.
Now that I've beaten it, let's talk about Dark Souls Dos.
Dark Souls 2 brings a lot of new elements to the Souls series, without poisoning the Souls experience. A lot of the new features are good, whilst some are a bit... eh, but they're not terrible changes.
Some of the changes are actually necessary for this game to be good, like the bonfire teleportation. Since you can't level up at bonfires, you have to go back to the main hub. In some areas of the game, this is impossible since you have to take a route that makes sure you can't walk back.
The bosses in Dark Souls 2 are a tad bit stale when in comparison to Dark Souls 1, but they're not terrible bosses. Yes, a lot of them are "Dudes in heavy armour" but if you actually read through the story of Dark Souls 2, you'd know why. There are a fair share of tough bosses, along with simple ones but all of them are unique in some way (excluding boss duplicates.)
The main gripe I have with this game, however, is the level design. In Dark Souls 1, it didn't feel like a chore getting to each boss because you memorized enemy spawning patterns, traps and room layouts. However, in Dark Souls 2, I mostly just ran through entire sections of the game because they were tedious as ♥♥♥♥. Heaps of enemies just before the boss area does NOT mean it's good level design. Yes, I know Dark Souls 2 is supposed to be hard, but when you're faced against a plethora of enemies just before you enter a boss room, that's a bit unfair. Yes, I know that enemies can de-spawn, but you have to kill them 12 times. That's twelve long trips to the boss area that I can just sprint to and ignore everything.
The PvP in Dark Souls 2 is vastly superior to Dark Souls 1. Less lag, better connectivity and you can talk to players that you're helping. A lot of people dislike the voice feature, but I think it's great, because you can warn the host of traps coming their way before they kill themselves and boot you out of their world.
Is Dark Souls 2 worth your time? Yes.
Is it better than Dark Souls 1? No, but it's not terrible in comparison.

Easily, unequivocally, absolutely, undoubtedly, undeniably, one of my favourite games ever, ever, ever - did I mention ever - ever! Here are just some of the many reasons as to why this game is so great:
PROS:
The Leading Man - Something has to be said about our main protagonist - he's an absolute badass reminiscent to that of Solid Snake. From his scar-riddled body to his gruff and gravelly voice every ounce of him oozes cool. I want to be him. Women want him. On initial impressions you might think he will turn out to be a monotone bore, void of personality but this also couldn't be further from the truth. Geralt can always manage to deliver great lines of dialogue from witty quips to interesting introspectives. In truth he is a great leading man.
Game Within A Game - While some games like to add some extra little minigames to their game that can prove to be entertaining for a couple of minutes at best Witcher 3 went the extra mile and added Gwent - a fully fleshed out card game that adds dozens and dozens of hours of extra gameplay. This card game itself is entirely optional within the game, but whole sidequests go unfulfilled should you choose to ignore it - which you really shouldn't - because it's a lot of fun. Northern Realms is best deck!
The Writing - There's always a special place in my heart for games that manage to give a choice of not black and white options - but the all too common and ever uncertain options of grey. You know, the choices that don't have a clear cut good answer or bad answer. The choices which, all to often is going to hurt SOMEONE. Witcher 3 has plenty of these and even goes the extra mile of luring you into a "good" choice only for outcomes to go horribly wrong. It makes me question my choice, makes me feel bad, makes me reload previous saves, makes me love it all the more.
A Good Looker - Straight up this game is GEORGEOUS! There have been plenty of times where I've just stopped in a beautiful glade or mountainpass and just thought "Wow" as I take it all in. Even the cutscenes in the game can be so pretty, the characters even have their intricate little flaws and detals like tiny marks, bumps and cuts on their skin and faces. I can only appreciate the sheer amount of work that went into making a game of this beauty.
The Celtic Influence - Ok this one, well I'm Irish so I can already appreciate the heck out of it. It's blatent celtic cultural influence is just a joy to see and makes me think of a simpler time. Props to the Witcher 3 staff hiring Scottish & Northern Irish voice actors for basically the entire populous of Ard Skellige.
I could also mention other things like how the game does a great job of handling lore of fantasy - delving into a whole host of mytical creatures or how the fighting mechanics of Witcher are a technical joy, having to read up on creatures weaknesses and using useful concoctions in the heat of battle are a must for higher difficulties, but I won't say anymore I can't praise this game enough - PLAY IT.
CONS:
Haha, no.

First CoD game I've owned on PC, and the first I've played in years.
Haven't played much Single-player but it seems fairly enjoyable. The story so far is pretty standard and nothing special BUT KEVIN SPACEY!
Multi-player consists of arcadish,  player-vs-player style gun combat with additional player abilities seemingly drafted from the likes of Cysis or Titanfall. There are several multi-player game modes of which I've only played a couple so I can't comment for all of them but I found team deathmatch to be fun. Currently multi-player does not benefit from dedicated servers and is instead hosted by players, so connections can be unreliable. Being forced to wait more than a minute to find yourself unable to connect to a host is frustrating and for a triple A title which heavily relies on its multi-player mode as a selling point, this isn't really OK.
The game is fairly well optimised and runs fine on one of my two R9 290s which I have. It's a shame that AMD has not yet released a crossfire driver for this game, but it doesn't appear to need it. I cannot speak for Nvidia.
Worth a look if you're into your CoD, but I find it hard to recommend this over Battlefield 4 which is ultimately a much better game and released a year prior. Still a decent game though, so gets a thumbs up from me.

I have never really written a review for any game on steam, but this game breaks that mold, in fact it breaks lots of molds in the MOBA genre in all. Its a MOBA game that uses a third person camera at all times, while this may seem like a quirky gimmic that makes the game uninteresting in a few moments of gameplay it does not. It always keeps my attention and I waste hours playing this game without even realising it and thats the thing. Whenever I try to play any other MOBA game (Dota 2/League of Legends) I get bored quickly because I feel like the action just isnt there. This game on the contrary is always filled with excitment and im always on my toes when I play this game. All of the Basic attacks are whats called "skill shots" meaning you have to aim in order to kill anyone in this game. Unlike other MOBA games you do not click on the ground to move, instead you move with the WASD keys and you have to option to re bind them to something else. Currently the game has about 69 Gods to play as from different pantheons. Gods are essentially your character that you can choose to play as or a "Champion" if you will and they all look and sound Great! Hell the entire game looks amazing even when everything was turned down on low! The game modes vary from conquest (5V5) to Joust (3V3) and if that isnt enough you have a MOTD or a "mode of the day" which should add a little something to your life if you ever get bored of Classic 5V5. A MOTD is a random mode with the rules changed whether it be Extra money or all one character or a mode where everyone is already to the max level. In the end I could keep going about how amazing this game is ( I have played this for like a gazillion hours before it even came to steam) Or I could just end on saying, if you want to try a MOBA game thats a little diffrent but still fun Smite is your game!

I have the right to remain charmed by this silly cops 'n robbers fighting game.
It's simple, and one of those fighters where you can just kinda flail your kick around and win every round, but there's a fair bit of inspiration in here. The pixel art is honestly pretty good and something to appreciate as someone who's trying to improve in the medium, it's a good benchmark that isn't top-of-the-line gorgeous but gets the job done and shows love and effort put in. Character designs are a bit silly but overall fitting of the concept, background art fills the scene nicely and has some movement to it so the game feels active and not just slapdashed together. I love that there's a dedicated handcuff button; sure it's just a grab move with a short effect afterwards but it's great to suddenly handcuff your enemy in the middle of a match and just wail them down.
Hardcore fighting game fans will probably find it laughable and people who don't care for fighting games will, well, not care, but if you appreciate the genre and aren't too concerned with balance or competitive play it might be a fun romp with a friend who's also not super amazing at 'em. Best game purchase I have made in a long time. I have had no interest in recent fighting games but seeing the 90's arcade style of art and game play, that was dripping out of Verdict Guilty, I had to try it out. The handcuff feature makes the game so incredibly fun and it adds an interesting dynamic to the game, beyond the standard kicks and punches. I also appreciate that the special moves are also pretty easy to learn and I don't need a graphing calculator to plot out some combos. Some people might shy away from the lack of online multiplayer but there is local multiplayer, and leaderboards if you're into that kind of thing. I will note that the game is kind of easy (certainly not a complaint) and I was able to tear through most of the story modes and arcade modes in a couple of hours. My only complain is that some of the pixel art is kind of inconsistant and a few of the characters look extremely cross-eyed.

I really wish there was a way to give a mediocre score to these instead of a thumbs up or down.
Verdict Guilty feels like it's attempting to be something old and new at the same time while tripping over both.  It definitely has a sense of 16 bit style, but the artwork feels a little off at times.  The interface is simple enough (strong and light punches and kicks and a grapple button), but the combo system is a joke and the entire control system feels somewhat stiff.  I'm hesitant to say it's a BAD game, just kinda generic.
And honestly, with so many better choices in fighting games, especially here on steam, I would recommend only checking this out when it's on sale.

Fresh off the public hype of EVO 2017, I check the daily specials and notice this hidden gem of a fighting game. The name "Verdict Guilty - 유죄 평결" alone was enough to pique my curiosity.
I purchase the game, dive into the options, and go into training mode to test out characters, and get a feel for the game's mechanics.
I used a PS4 controller, and switched to keyboard controls on occasion. A simple 4 button fighter with a block and grab mechanics. The grab is what really stands out. As you can handcuff your opponent, or "dizzy" for maximum damage potential. There are projectiles too: guns, grenades, vials, and animals. The only downside to thew mechanics are moves requiring you to "hold" a button/key in order for your fighter to a execute a move. I feel it is a second too long and stresses the button i'm pressing on.
The Story mode stages have "objectives" akin to Soul Edge (if I recall correctly) where you have to follow certain conditions to progress in a fighter's story arc. You are also taught combo strings and special attacks along the way. 8+ stages to clear per fighter.
Arcade, Survival, and Training mode are as expected of fighting games. While the three hidden modes unlocked after beating arcade mode for the first time freshen up the gameplay experience.
The fighters themselves are very fun and have their own combo strings and special moves to make them unique. At the moment, there is no way to play as the pallet swap versions of the fighters you encounter in story mode. A nitpick to the roaster is the lack of female fighters. If additional fighters are ever explored, I can envision a female forensic scientist, and female pimp (1 officer, 1 criminal respectively [feel free to use these ideas if you are reading Dev ;j]).
There is no online mode, however, your scores for each mode can be seen by others via the options menu (Stylized in a very arcade fashion).
Achievements for the game are very reasonable, easy, and fun to go for. I had the hardest time with the 7-hit combo achievement, with a peek at the forums, I was able to achieve it with ease.
I love the game so much, I bought the steam trading cards to craft the game's badge, tweeted this game out to Cheap A s s Gamer, and potentially gifting keys to my friends and favorite Let's Players. This is an excellent single player experience that is severely underrated in its multiplayer.

The concept of this game is brilliant - on paper. I'm afraid that I have to hesitate a little bit to call it a game. The potential for a game is here, but the technical hurdles involved in getting this to work, combined with the incredibly short amount of content really makes this more of a proof of concept than a game, per se.
The largest issue, by far and large, is that this game does NOT support Internet play. When hosting or finding a game - it's all done across the Local Area Network. So if you and your co-player of choice aren't on the same network (at home, in a dorm, at work, etc) - you're going to need to setup a VPN service to make this work. Some people have reported success with services like Hamachi - that didn't work for me, but I was able to setup a VPN on my particular brand of router, and get myself and a friend connected.
Once you DO get the game up and running - the entire content of the game can be played in under 30 minutes. For all the trailer talks about "solve puzzles" - there was only one puzzle to be solved.
A very unique experience, and one worth seeking out - IF you are tech-savvy enough to get past the hurdles. I'd love to see the concepts provided here fleshed out a bit more, and for more of a game to result.
