Castlevania: Lords of Shadow is with distance one of the best Action RPG's ever made!
Short:
The Story is excellent and it contains Love, Hate, Vengeance and Sadness, also is well told and full of Surprises.
The Gameplay and Combatsystem is fluid.
Graphically this game is maybe not up-to-date, but it looks really good and every level in this game is wonderfully designed and affectionately made.
Over time you get many upgrades which grants you more Ability's and skill's.
More detailed:
Story: The story tells of a member of the Brotherhood of Light, named Gabriel Belmont. His Wife Marie Belmont was killed and he wants Revenge for her dead [You will wonder who killed She and why].
Even the World has lost the blessing and protection of God. So Gabriel has received the Mission from the Brotherhood of Light to bring back peace to the World.
So his Journey begins ...
Gameplay/Combat: The Gameplay is really smooth and the controls are even really good and comprehensible. Over time you can learn more and more Ability's and Skill's which you can use by using the right button combination and timing. I played it with the Xbox360 Pad and it works perfect in all cases.
Enemys: There are many different Enemys. Every Foe has his unique style and his own behavior and/or abilitys and skills, which makes every Battle with an unknown enemy different from each other until you know them all =)
Soundtrack: The Soundtrack fits perfect to the game! It was made from a Orchesta.
Graphic: The graphic is outdated but this gameengine looks Awesome!
Environment:  You have beatiful surroundings in every Level [Maybe not the world of dead for some =)]. Every detail is well designed and looks really good.
Riddles: This game has many Riddles which must be solved to get further [with exception of 1]. Some are Easy, some Average and some Riddles are really Hard for the first time, but you can find hints in the same Areas where the Riddles are and you can let you show the solution if you want. But if you do it you will loose the Bonuses!
Over and all this Game is totally worth the Money! You will not make a wrong decision if you buy this game. Also you will need to spend 13 - 26 hours approximately to beat the game the first time.

There is so much detail put into the game world; you can see how weathered the walls are with their scratches and marks, there's tiny notches on the wood doors, scratches and marks of your metallic sword (with realtime reflections),  the scars on the NPCS, the ebb and flow motion of the water, and the gorgeous color scheme of skyline and shadows that reflects the time of day, etc. It looks freaking amazing. The game doesn't try to be photorealistic and improves on the art style from the first game. The dialogue from distinguished voice acting cast and animations are superb, the gameplay is open ended, and there's so much to explore that I know I won't be able to see it all in one playthrough. Its story and gameplay is done really well, a rarity as most games will do one portion effectively yet neglect the other.
If you're a fan of the Bioshock series, Thief series (excluding the 4th one), the first Dishonored, Deus Ex, or just love atmospheric games that focus on lore then this game is for you. Just keep in mind that this game is a bit demanding on the pc as even I get the occasional frame drops while running on a high end card. GOTY for me.
TL;DR
-Performance isn't that great atm but patches are underway
-Open ended Gameplay+immersive story are amazing
-Looks absolutely fantastic
-Can and should be replayed due to different endings depending on your decisions
Edit: I just tried the beta patch which is set to release around sometime this weekend. FPS performance has improved dramatically for me and the mouse issues are gone.
Also to the misinformed people writing reviews that keep saying this is a port, no it is not. Each version of the game was developed inhouse by Arkane.

Whether you are new to MOBAs or an expert at DotA 2 or LoL, you will love SMITE. Smite combines some of the best features from other MOBA games with an over the shoulder 3rd person camera angle, bringing you closer to the action than any other MOBA. I came to SMITE from DotA 2 and found the game incredibly fun. There are a wide variety of gods (heroes/champions) to choose from and they all have unique mechanics that contribute to the game. I have hundreds of hours logged into SMITE before it was added to steam, and I'm likely to get hundreds more.

Pros:
Great gameplay
Variety of modes
Variety of gods
Items choice
Cons
Lack of creativity
Matchmaking can lead to frustrating games
Sometimes bad servers/connections
I enjoy Smite. Its my favorite MOBA. Most of my friends enjoy DotA 2 or LoL. I grew up with FPS instead of RTS so i like the perspective of Smite so much more than other traditional MOBAs. Not to mention the $30 for all gods pack is an amazing deal considering its ridiculous how much I spent on LoL when it first came out.
Now the worst part of this game for me is the matchmaking. The matches are sorted based on your K/D/A from the previous game. This can lead you to stomping some newer players then immediately getting matched with some pro diamond-tier lvl 30 players and getting destroyed. This tends to happen back and forth over and over since you are catapulted up and down with with K/D/A success and failures. Another thing is that the Gods themselves arnt as creative as LoL or DotA. Maybe Hi-Rez is still in its infancy of creative since Smite is newer, but the items and gods themselves are all things we've seen before. On a final note, speaking of Hi-Rez, the company doesnt have a great track record when you take their previous endevors such as Tribes into consideration.
That looks like a lot of Cons. Dont let me fool you, Smite is a great game and my go-to MOBA for the past 10 months. I definitely recommend it if you prefer 3rd person over RTS style camera.

Slime Rancher is a fantastic little game with plenty of stuff to do and also surprisingly stable for an "early access" title. Relaxing and fun.

Slime Rancher is a fun, cute, relaxing game. Slime Rancher is reminiscent of a 3D platformer in that there is a lot of depth to the map (secret areas, locked doors, interesting landmarks, etc.) with a goal of collecting things (such as slimes, food, water, etc.). But, everything centers around your ranch. There, you may raise/breed slimes, chickens, grow fruits or vegetables, place decorations, sell your 'plorts,' or experiment with slime science.
Ultimately, the world is enjoyable, the gameplay is fun and fresh, the goals are progressive (but you are free to progress at whatever pace you like), and the cartoony visuals compliment the game's lightheartedness.

I've never been one of those who has to buy the latest COD or Battlefield game upon launch. In fact, I never buy them. However this time I splurged and decided to pick up CODAW to pass the time until Fary Cry 4 drops or I get my throttle and download Elite Dangerous. Because I haven't played 15 other versions of this, I have to say I enjoyed it. Sure, there isn't much that we haven't already seen in either film, TV or other games, but the gun play is fun, some of the exo abilities are cool, most of the areas are visually strong, the sound design is really sharp and, well, Kevin Spacey...pretty cool. Keyser Soze, lol. It annoyed me that the game decided which exo abilities you were armed with each time out because I would have picked my go-to setup and stayed with it. Minor issue. However, what isn't a minor issue is the fact that a company would charge me $60 for the privelege of stuffing my computer with an absolutly massive download file, and then, when I fire the game up (to run on a four-month old GTX 780ti) the first half of all the cinematics jerk and stutter so bad that they're impossible to watch. Jump into some multiplayer, you say. Ok, I'm actually typing this review while my character is lagged out humping a wall. I kid, but you get the point. Why in the world has it become the standard in the gaming industry to give the consumer a shoddy, incomplete experience with a premium price tag. I liked a lot of the game, but if you were asking me if you should buy it today, the answer is no. Maybe later.

This was one of the biggest gaming disappointments I have ever witnessed. When I first read they were rebuilding the original Half-Life title using the Source engine I thought it would be a proper remaster.
Like everyone else, I was a little depressed when I found out it was the same old blurry 90's game just on a newer engine. The physics were improved as well as the superb lighting and shadows you get from the Source engine. Oddly though, the one thing that did get new textures/meshes etc was the water. So you end up with this old school crappy 90's texture right next to brand new 2004 era water textures/meshes which made no sense at all.
I can look past all that above and just respect the fact that I can play the classic game on a newer engine with slight improvements here and there but...there is more to this story than just what we have read so far.

I played the first Dark Souls for many hours and I can happily say the sequal proudly lives up to the first one and improves it in many different aspects. For the agrument of the second one wont be as hard as the first there is some truth to it but that is only because i've completed the first game so many times. HOWEVER I have no shame in saying Dark souls 2 still kicked my a$$ many times and some of the new mechanics such as reducing health as you die definitly give a whole new tense feeling to death. For all the new good things Dark souls 2 gives something to counter it and keep it difficult. Examples: There are many different new healing items available when your Estus runs out so you start now with only one Estus and have to find more along with healing being a slower process. Weapon degrading is reset at bonfires but weapons degrade alot faster now and you'll need a backup on long stretches or repair powder.
I welcome all these new features and assure you they are smartly balanced to never give an unfair feeling. There are references to the first game especially in the bosses and if you identify it through an item description or some appearance quirk, it gives a sort of nice "I get it!" feeling, if that makes any sence. Covenants have a much larger role in Dark souls 2 and I got a deep sence of working towards something everytime I helped another player defeat a boss or get through a tough area as a Sunbro, because it helped that player and me. Ranking up in a covenant has much nicer rewards than before and even after I reached the final rank I still wanted to go refight bosses with another players for the souls.
New stats are able to make things like rolling and how fast you drink estus better and dual weilding is amazing! The game also changes very significantly in New Game+ by adding more items, enemies, NPC invaders and best of all new weapons you can only get in NG+.
I do have some dissapointments tho. The story is even more fague now, not that too many people payed attention to it in the first anyway but I do like to have just some sort of reasoning behind why im dragging my a$$ throught some of the hell holes in the game. Sometimes you will be kinda turned around as to where the next place is to go or how you should progress, but as you complete more of the many areas your path becomes more narrow and clear and that is only on the first playthrough anyway just like in the first game. My biggest let down was the final boss fight. Gwyn at least gave it a good effort but this one almost lays back and lets it happen. I killed another boss and the final boss fight instantly happened after I beat the previous one because I put off fighting that one earlier and I still managed to whip the final boss under a minute with reduced healing items and degraded weapon from the previous fight. They will probably beef up the last boss in a patch sometime.
I really loved Dark Souls 2 even more than the first despite some minor personal gripes and there is plenty of reason to keep playing this time since NG+ has many new features added.

A long time ago, I bought Geometry Wars Galaxies for the Nintendo DS. I absolutely loved it. It did everything right, and let me tell you using a stylus to shoot did not make things easy, especially for a lefty.
Years later, I bought this game (shortly after its release if I remember correctly). It was a decent price and I knew the graphics would have my eyes sparkling and my mouth puking rainbows. And I was right. Visually, this game is absolutely stunning. The many game modes and three-dimensional levels make it a huge step forward from Galaxies. Plus now my drone has awesome special attacks (called supers), and Super States give me a chance at getting a huge edge, if only very briefly.
So why can't I recommend this game?
It's a lot of things, but it mostly boils down to the fact that in this game, death means that you have to restart the level, either because (depending on the game mode) you only have a single life, or because while you have infinite lives, you have an extremely short time limit. Combine these issues with the following:
- Enemy spawn animations are very brief and easy to miss, especially when you're focusing not directly on your ship where they're spawning, but on the enemies you're currently shooting at.
- A lot of the levels, due their 3-D design, give you almost no visibility around you.
- There are many enemies whose speed makes them hard enough to dodge even when you can see them coming a mile away.
It doesn't help that you need those impossible-to-earn stars to actually progress through the game's single-player adventure mode.
In short, while the action is fast-paced and gorgeous, I can't recommend a game that has you spending hours on end just to make next to no progress. It would have been nice to include a few levels that worked like Galaxies, where you start with three lives, one bomb, one super, and can earn more of each by scoring enough points. The complete removal of this game mode (and mentality) has left me frustrated, and it's the type of game that ensures I'd get very, very fat if I had a swear jar (because I'd spend all that money on candy and ice cream).

This is the type of game which doesnt work and can't really be done in a way which would work. So ignoring the games obvious failing of not being able to play online without using Hamachi and the really mediocre graphics, lets look at why the gameplay fails.
The gameplay focuses around two players, a soldier and a oracle. The soldiers main purpose is to lead the oracle (Who is blind and can see nothing) and kill monsters. The oralces job is to follow the guidance of the soldier to create paths for theboth of you. The main issue when playing as the soldier is that it can be enormously frustrating attempting to guide an oracle who doesnt know what he is doing. All the soldier has to guide the oracle with is noise. I personally have a hard time disinguising the direction of sounds meaning its basically impossible for me to be the oracle, except for reasons I will explain later. Another primary issue with being the soldier is that your gameplay is extremely shallow. All you realistically end up doing is walking from place to place and occassionally shooting a few arrows.
Now the oracle has a whole different set of problems. The first being that you are looking at basically nothing the entire time you play this game. I understand that that is the point but that just factors in to the inability to make this concept work. Next up is the fact that the sounds the oracle hears range from jarring to extremely quiet. The tutorial section of the oracle has you listening to Bees Swarming. This sound alone gave me a pounding headache due to listening to it so often. The final issue which is actually an issue for both the oracle and the soldier is that after one run as the soldier, when you then play as oracle your soldier is basically useless. The map is incredible small and you can't die meaning that as an oracle you can just brute force your way through the game without even needed your soldier except to occassionally shoot an arrow or five. It completely destroys any replayability the game may have had as it becomes boring for the soldier who is doing nothing and boring for the oracle who is just walking.
So overall I can not recommend this game. The game hosts way too many issues just from a gameplay standpoint. When you begin to factor in all the time it takes to actually be able to play with your friends combined with all the gamebreaking bugs you encounter, there just isnt a reason to play this game. At best you might want to try it once with a friend if you find the concept interesting otherwise just skip it entirely.

I put hundreds if not a thousand hours into this game before it came to steam. I had a great time with it and made new friends. This game was very addicting and fun. Ranked matchmaking is really bad because it does not match you up with same level experience players. Example: I'm Gold and I will get matched up with 1 Silver, 2 Bronze and 1 Qualifying(Meaning they havent played ranked). The enemy team will consist of 1 Platinum, 2 Gold, and 2 Silver. The enemy team is superior because Platinum is better than all of these ranks. There is also 1 extra Gold, 1 extra Silver with no Bronzes or Qualifying players on the other team. And I'm sure many players had crazier, un-balanced matches worse than my example.
Also the fan base for this game is the most ridiculous, toxic and trolling fan base I have
ever seen of any game that I have played. Trolls pick wrong "class" gods for ranked games as well as disconnecting after getting into the game, therefore resulting in you wasting your time with an eventual lost. And there are plenty of toxic players because if you do any little thing wrong, your considered garbage. Just picking a God that is the "correct class" God but not top tier, then you will also be considered garbage because THEY dont like that particular God and think he is trash. Heres a few more examples to be clear. "Why do you have that item in your build? Your garbage." (Even if it works). "I have more kills than you. Your garbage." "I died less than you, so your garbage kid." And "You missed one skillshot the entire game? Your garbage bruh, go uninstall and kill yourself".
This is a
based game. How are we going to win if your complaining about me instead of simplying communicating teamwork to beat the other team and not being so competitive about how many kills you have towards me? Theres a reason there are different roles in mobas, hence an ADC (Attack-Damage Carry) should get more kills than most of the other roles.
You play this game and your just destined to get into arguement after arguement. I promise you that. Gods upon release are very unbalanced and can be weak but MOST of the time are over-powered. There is no middle ground with this game between its matchmaking problems to balancing issues to toxic fan-base.

In conclusion, you are able to play this game if you so choose. I however am going to save myself from many headaches and play many other great games. If you loved the first Dishonored you'll more than likely enjoy this one, of course no game can ever be as good as the first one but this comes pretty close in my eyes. Consider the questions below...
Did you enjoy the unique environment, art, feel, etc. of the first game? This game expands on that and continues with it, the world of Karnaca is absolutely stunning, even for as bad as my graphics are right now its still amazing to look at all the little details that make the world unique, can't wait for an update to hopefully make it look even better.
Did you enjoy the combat, customization, powers, etc. of the first game? Again this game expands on that and offers more ways for combat styles, new weapons, new upgrade, powers, etc. all feel really well done, if you were good at combat in the first game you'll still do fine in this one.
Did you enjoy the story and lore of the first game? Yep, again this one expands on that.
The idea of choosing between Corvo or Emily offers different play styles as well as outcomes so theres even more replay value than before.
The music is just as perfect as the first one.
Overall my best advice is to wait for further updates and fixes so you can experience the game in its full glory, if you can't wait then there's still plenty to enjoy as long as you can look past a few of the graphical eyesores.

If you played a lot of COD but "burned out" I suggest a no buy until you really feel like getting into the COD scene again.
But for me, this game is all good, brainless fun.  Its not perfect, but worth the $60.

I like Geometry Wars. It took the gameplay of Robotron and expanded it, while at the same time simplifying it.
The action was frentic. The enemies, while simple in their AI, had a tendency to gang up on you and cause your inevitable demise. And games usually lasted short time enough that you could always just restart to have one more go at the high score.
Geometry Wars: Galaxies for the Wii expanded upon this by adding different shaped levels, medals to set you some goals and some mutators like certain types of waves in the levels to give you some variety over the classic Retro Evolved.
I hear Geometry Wars 2 did rather well as well, adding game concepts like checkpoints or bubbles in which you need to stay in order to shoot. Expanding on the original to add some flavour.
And now there's Geometry Wars 3. The main draw over GW2 seems to be the 3D angle, it's right there in the title. The graphics look a lot more futuristic and flashy. Gone are those silly vectorlike wireframes. Hello flat shaded 3D backgrounds, blurry lighting effects. The works.
Sadly this is what really soured the experience for me. The art looks really good, especially in motion. But instead of the lines coming together to form newly spawned enemies, you just get a faint intensifying glow before the enemy is there. Instead of having a good view of the playfield, suddenly you're limited in how far you can see, especially on the cubes and spheres where enemies will seemingly out of the blue turn a corner and ram into you, because the camera wasn't showing you that angle.
At its heart, this game is very much an extension on Geometry Wars. With game modes from GW2, and slicker graphics. But for me it just turned to frustration to once again get spawnkilled by a powerup because I missed the slight glow. Or to get run into by an enemy coming around the corner I was moving towards. The third dimension, for as awesome as it seems, almost completely ruins the game for me.
80% of the deaths I died felt like a graphical gotcha. I died not because I lost track of where the enemies were, not because I stupidly wandered into something because i was looking at where I was, or because the enemies had surrounded me. I died because of something I didn't have a chance to see before it was too late. Or because I missed a bit of coloured light in the middle of multicoloured explosions.
It's a pity really. I really wanted to like this game, and on the flat levels this game is almost as much fun as the old incarnations of the game. But as it is I can't recommend getting GW3. Go play the old ones instead, they're hard enough without falling back on optical trickery to kill you.

An amazing game that is marred by questionable design decisions and obviously untested elements, especially in PvP. It may be longer than Dark Souls 1, but a lot of the game seems either as filler or doing exactly what Dark Souls did (and doing it worse). In the end its a good game, but if you haven't already, I recommend going to play Dark Souls 1 first.
In the first game, you fought gods and demons from the beginning of light itself or fought worse things that crawled out of the Dark; all of this happening in a decaying world on it's last legs. This game you fight mere shadows of such beings, or more often, just variations of "dudes in armor," and the desperation and gloominess of the coming end of the dying world seems remote and far away.
The game lacks the "tightness" that the original had; many of its enemies and bosses are particularly uninteresting compared to the original; the level design is hit or miss, and some parts of the game seem totally shoe-horned in; the story/lore is just lackluster and missing that wonder that the first one brought forth (and a lot of it is more or less confusing); but primarily the game messes up the frustration/reward factor, the breaking down of the wall of resistance (with your face), giving weak rewards and more often the reward is more like an arrow sign to continue forward to the next boss to repeat the process.
Even for a good game, a lot of it felt more like a slog than actual fun.

I'd like to start this off by saying I am a big fan of the lore behind Vlad the Impaler, both fantasy and historic, so the story of Dracula that castlevania tells has always held a special place for me.
This series of games is a retelling of the Castlevania story and the origins of Dracula for the game, and honestly it's probably the greatest fiction that's been told on it that I've ever had the pleasure of seeing (I will post no spoilers).  With that in mind I HIGHLY recommend playing this game, then immediately jumping into Lord of Shadows 2.  I have no knowledge on mirrors of fate as I have just received it, but those two flow beautifully.
Bare in mind I say this knowing full well there are people out there that disagree with me, and that's fine, that's what is beautiful about video games, there are so many countless choices we can all like something and it doesn't have to be for the same reason.  Disagree? Awesome man! And I really mean that, I don't want us to all agree, because then life would be boring!
Now that I can stop gushing (probably not) over the story, let's move on to the rest of the shenanigans:
The controls in the game are akin to God of War, Quick Time Events and all.  I actually didn't mind several of the 3D Castlevanias so it gets a passing grade here for me.  The movement feels solid enough and didn't have any kind of sluggish feel to it, nothing stuck out to be fantastic but it did the job just fine.  I haven't attempted using keyboard/mouse controls as this is a game I feel best enjoyed on a controller anyway, so with that, your mileage may vary.
The graphics are.....well, it's pretty enough.  There are a few spots that do make you go "Oooooh, Ahhhhh", but most if it is good enough that it holds emmersion, but not so pretty you want to stop to look at every detail...maybe only a few.  (All video settings set to max with fullscreen 1920x1080)
The settings are....abyssmal, there really is nothing to select.  Vsync, AA, full screen/window, resolution, and that's about it.  I'd have liked to see a more enhanced menu in this day and age.  Yes this game has a few years on it, but let's be serious, we all know the settings of a console to pc port when we see them.
The audio is fine, my Sonos Playbar and sub handled it quite nicely and it did well to hold the emotion that should have been with the particular scene.
The voice acting was hit or miss sadly....some characters sounded like they fit better than others, by large margins, and it really is a bit unpleasant; however, this is all countered by one fact: Patrick Stewart is narrating the game.  You tell me you don't want this man to read you a bed time story, I dare you.
Gameplay: Not to bad actually.  It has a good mix of easy and hard puzzles, and some really well hidden secrets.  There's also some replayability with the backtracking to collect new items as you gain new abilities and the trials modes, as well as harder difficulties.
TL;DR:
Story: Epic, especially if you combine this game with Lord of Shadows 2 story.  Again, not everyone feels this way, that's ok.
Controls: They're fine, there's nothing good/bad about them.
Graphics: Eh, pretty enough.
Audio: Good enough, sounded pleasant to my ears.
Voice Acting: It could have been so much better, it was really super hit or miss.  But remember: Patrick Stewart narrating.
Gameplay: Has a few spots of "What the hell game...." and "Oh jesus christ I pressed the jump button right at the edge I should have made that!" as most all Castlevania games do, but as we all would NEVER admit outloud, we know in our heart of hearts we didn't hit that button at the right time, they game was just better than us that day.
Conclusion: Story weighed so heavily for me on this game, and I believe that to be the biggest contributing factor on me recommending this game.  As I've stated a few times, I understand some people may not agree on this. That's. Fine. With. Me.  I truly don't mind that, if you don't believe story is that heavy a weight for you, use the other information to form what you believe you'd like.  Best case scenario though, steam does have refunds now!

Been looking for a while for a local co-op game to play with my 8 year old brother. After a few weeks searching, I found the perfect one: Broforce. With more explosions than a Michael Bay movie, prepare yourself for for one of the most fun games this year.There is no plot to get in the way: instead, take control of one of dozens of action heroes with weapons ranging from Neo's fists to the Terminator's minigun. It was fun explaining each hero and their lore to my brother and using their unique powers to tear through hordes of enemies. The levels are huge ( there are 15+ with 3 stages each), filled with rideable propane tanks, explosive barrels, moveable cover, destructable terrain, breaking bridges, and burning barrels. What's more, nearly everything is interactive, from working elevators, to rideable pigs, and coconuts to throw. Prepare to spread freedom with 4 friends local or online, or go head to head in multiple game modes.
Edit: It only got better with updates. Fantastic Arcade game, and the level builder is very clever.

Lazy, lazy, lazy.
First of all, I'm 90% certain this is a FPS Creator game, and if you buy a lot of indie games, you're probably already aware of the limitations and reputation of that game engine.
The game is full of horror game cliches, none of which are even remotely scary. There's items that don't work (and would be pointless if they did). There's sudden jarring changes in art style (like cartoon characters suddenly appearing in the game, and a couple sci-fi textures). There's hovering tables, hovering signs, overlapping textures which produce that lovely flashing effect when you walk near them. Lighting doesn't work half the time, and when it does work it's harsh and ugly. Load times are terrible (one of the clues to me that it's a FPS Creator game). You can easily complete the entire game in 20 minutes, and there is absolutely zero replay value.
Almost everything in the product description is an ludicrous exaggeration. "Living world", I guess, means that two of the (tiny) levels have creatures that walk around in them? "Multiple open area levels", well I guess they're open but they're like maybe 1200 square feet in size. "Unique story", hah! It's nothing but cliches piled on cliches.
Just all-around an amazingly lazy and uncreative game.

Half Life, the game that revolutionized the entire FPS genre for the last 18 years. While many said that Doom did it first, Half Life was the one that started it all. Although I never played the original game, I guess its Source engine port has served well enough to present the joy and fun of playing this well crafted game that Valve created in 1998.
At first glance, you arrive at the Black Mesa facility in a train transport as Gordan Freeman, a working scientist there. You are tasked of having to handle some dangerous, alien material, which suddenly goes horribly wrong and opens a portal to an alien world. Then, you are to seek out the source of the incident and try to end it. The story of this game is very simple and the tasks and puzzles are quite challenging if you have never played a Valve game before. Sure enough a lot of other games nowadays like Bioshock provide a lot of depth and variety in solving a situation, but remember that this game came out in 1998, so not many other games provided the same kind of FPS experience to gamers at that time.
I’m 17 years old, so for me to be playing a game that is older than myself was highly unlikely. But after hearing the franchises appraises and accolades and playing through this right now, I feel sorry to not have picked up this series earlier. Its core gameplay and simplistic mechanics made this game really enjoyable and fun to play, the setting of the game also made sense and really spawned a new era in the entire genre and set a great example for the games to come. Other similar games around the same time period like Doom, Wolfenstein and Quake were also what inspired the creation of Half Life and its sequel.
From the surprise elements such as headcrabs waiting for you around the corner of a vent, marines suddenly appearing from another room and the zombies camping somewhere to eat you alive, each part of this game had its own unique style and way of solving something but at the same time did not limit you to the part where you felt forced to do something and instead brought you on ride of salvation and survival in a destroyed facility infested with lethal elements that will harm you instantly if you take one wrong step. Half Life is not afraid of punishing players who try to go in recklessly and promotes players to take a smarter approach because Half Life doesn’t want you to go in guns blazing like Rambo and wants you to understand that you are Gordan Freeman, a scientist trying to survive from the dangers of his once workplace. Along the road, headcrabs, zombies, alien grunts and other alien manifestations as well as marines will try to take you down on your journey to Zen to redeem and reclaim yourself.
Half Life also made Valve to become a giant of the industry with other huge successes in games such as L4D2, TF2, Portal franchise as well as the E-sports scenes with games like Dota and CS:GO. Although Valve may never learn how to count to 3 or even worse, make another game themselves since they already have so much up on their hands at the moment, the Half Life franchise will still remain their first game and for that I think that it is enough to signify their influence in the entire gaming industry.

I'm writing this to hopefully counter some of the negative reviews because this game doesn't really deserve the harsh criticism just because some folks are having trouble on Ultra settings. I'm running an older 8350 paired with a 1070FTW edition gpu and a 34" acer predator and on the settings the game picked for itself, it's running just fine. It may very well be poorly optimized at ultra settings but my suggestion is to calm down and wait for a patch. It's not the end of the world to play at slightly less than ultra.
So, about the game itself. There's things that I like and things that I don't. I'm a little surprised at how much it *feels* like Fallout. The place is mostly trashed and there's a lore reason for it that I won't spoil, but it doesn't change how fallout-y it feels.
The controls are pretty good, at least for the 360 controller. I wish that we could remap the buttons ourselves instead of choosing their three presets (that's me wanting to map my 'sneak' button to the same one Fallout and ES uses), but it's not game breaking.
I am really enjoying playing as Emily and I'm pleasantly surprised at how prominently she's featured. She feels like a real character of the game, not the token woman just to check off a box. Her story is compelling and interesting and it's clear they put a significant amount of time into developing her.  The player can really care about and empathize with her. She has real motivation to go out and right the wrongs that have been done, wrongs that don't feel arbitrary *cough cough fallout baby cough cough*. Yet, it's not a situation where you're going to completely forget the main quest to start a garden somewhere because *too* much of the roleplay was taken away and you just can't care about it. This is the perfect balance of having a character with a backstory that you can still make your own.
The super powers are pretty fun as well. Movement feels fluid and it's especially satisfying to pull yourself behind an enemy and assassinate him.
There's only a couple things that I can think of right now that I don't really care for. One is the character models. We're in 2016 but you're going to feel like you're in the early 2000's when you get up close to talk to a character. If they are sitting on the floor, forget it. Out of proportion hands, strangely skinny and gangly bodies, it makes our complaints about Bethesda faces seem like overreaction. These are just weird looking npcs. It's what you see on mainstream crime dramas when they decide to write in gaming stuff using an old id Tech engine (and mostly get it completely wrong).
The other thing is the lack of treasure, and by treasure I don't mean valuables. I mean there's an awful lot of things laying about and you're going to strain your eyes piacking out what is actually actionable. There's too many 'pick up and throw' items littered about, though some interesting pieces are strategically placed. Truthfully it's just a minor gripe coming from someone who is a big fan of Fallout and ES and the ability to pick up literally every piece of junk laying about.
Menus feel too flashy and there doesn't seem to be an easy way to open the map. That could just be me getting used to the controls and not quite having that one down yet.
In all, it's been a pretty fun game so far. If you really only care about graphics, wait for the patch. If you like story and just stealthing around and leaving bodies in your wake, go ahead and get it.

Dark Souls II: Still one of the best games I have played with amazing surroundings and great scenery! It has improved gameplay wise since Dark Souls:Prepare to die edition and fixed some of the problems and it is a great port now but the keyboard and mouse controls are a bit clunky so I recommend a controller.
The game in general is great but it disapointed me in some ways. Quite a few bosses were just big guys with some kind of oversized weapon but I should also consider the fact that there are some great and unique bosses and the concept of a boss chasing you instead of the other way around. The world is great looking but a bit unlogical. There is a lava castle on top of a windmill (when you will play the game you will know what I am talking about) and you can see Anor Londo 2.0 (just looks like it) from Firelinkshrine 2.0 but when you try to go there the way there is a lot shorter and the last example from a castle where all kinds of experiments have happened you somehow get to some flying islands. Even though everything looks so great it's just a bit unlogical.
The game does not feel really balanced yet. As a faith user you have 3 (v1.05) lightning spears but sorcerers have like 10 soul arrows. If it had any tracking ability it would have been a good change but you can just walk and dodge no need to roll (there is a bug when the spear will just turn around and hit the enemy). There are some unbalanced enemies in the game that are some giant knights and ussualy you expect them to hit hard and swing slowly, nope instead they hit hard and swing all day not allowing you to hit making ranged combat or avoiding them the best decision. Some bosses are just too weak and others have just some undodgable attacks and others have been made harder by simply adding some minions around them.
Lore-wise it's confusing... I don't know.
They also just CTRL-V , CTRL-C some places from Dark Souls (original) and edited them a bit.
The game is kind of buggy when we come to PvP. In PvE poise works just the way it used to but in PvP even a dagger can stagger you when having maximum poise so stunlocks are just sooo annoying. What the hell are hitboxes? I don't even know. PvP seems like a bit mess right now.

Conclusion: Great game but for the souls series it feels a bit disapointing. It has great ideas but some were not applied the correct way. It also felt like the developers were a bit "lazy".
EDIT: All of the DLCs were amazing and the only problem with them might be the "dudes in armor" thing but that is not much of a deal. The DLCs seem better than the actual game and have been more fun. The only real problem was the co-op areas they are really hard to solo and the bosses are NPCs and retextured bosses.
Dark Souls (original): One of my favorite games and the best RPG I have ever played. It is one of the most punishing games and complex and realistic combat. The story is quite hard to understand since you have to look for it since it won't be obvious. The world named Lordran is great looking and it is has havenly looking palace to a hellish pit full of demons. Death will come from any direction and there is no real way to tell if you can survive something or not the only way to find that is by trial and error or looking for messages and bloodstains on the ground and learn from others mistake. The story (if you manage to understand it, but there are people who have channels devoted for the lore of the Souls series like VaatyVidya) is really dark and sad. The game has also an unique multiplayer aspect. You can summon other players into your world to help you or fight other palyers for souls and humanity (or get invaded and killed). The way to "unlock" multiplayer is by using a humanity and reverse hollowing, but there is one problem: Games For Windows Live... the servers are horrible but the same person who made DSfix also made a mod to fix the conectivity: DSCfix.

Conclusion: The game is great but it is just has a poor tutorial (but it managed to show something in the tutorial and that is that you will die, a lot) and it is port for PC.
If you get the mods to fix the port and a gamepad and you won't rage quit with ease then the game will be a great experience oh and... Prepare to Die and don't forget to Praise the Sun!

I've logged over 300 hours before the Steam release, so keep that in mind.
With that being said...
Smite is fairly unique in the MOBA genre.  The first thing that you'll notice is the camera angle (TPS-style instead of RTS-style), but the differences go much farther than that.  There's a plethora of game modes, so if Conquest (traditional 5v5) isn't your thing, there's still several other modes that might interest you.  Also, I've found that from a design standpoint, Smite is much friendlier to newer players.  For example, tower range is always shown, jungle timers appear automatically if your team has vision of it dying, assists on minion kills (last hitting is still rewarded), no Runes/Masteries equivelant, as well as an optional Auto-level system for skills and an Auto-buy for items until you familiarize yourself with the store.  These features mean that the skill floor is significantly lower for newer players, without impacting the skill ceiling for seasoned players.
The monetization is extremely reasonable.  5 Gods unlocked to start, with 5 more on rotation each patch.  You can buy every god with in-game currency (favor), or you can buy the Ultimate God Pack which gives you access to every god (including future ones) for $30.  Granted, DOTA gives you them all for free, but many other MOBAs make you buy them all, and $30 is incredibly reasonable considering that.
Overall, it's a fantastic game, especially if you're looking for something different from the MOBA genre.

<VVGH> Have fun!

Geometry Wars 3 is possibly the gold standard (or at least silver standard) for twinstick shooters on Steam, polished to a sheen and packed to the gills with content.  The bulk of the game consists of "Adventure" mode, a linear progression through 50 maps.  Lucid Games did an admirable job injecting an impressive amount of variety into each of the levels.  The result is that you usually won't feel like you're trying to achieve the same objective over and over again (for 50 maps).  There are a few duds in the mix--I've never been a fan of the missions where you see how long you can prevent enemies from completely "painting" the arena--but the game makes up for it with a lot of missions that are genunely fun to replay.
Reaching certain goals and milestones unlocks upgrades for your ship (like buddy drones and super weapons) while obtaining higher scores grants you a sort of currency that can be used to improve these upgrades.  While you'll ultimately have more points to spend than things to invest them in, you can only take one of each type on a given mission with you, so you need to think about the level you're going in to and what will benefit you most.  Maybe a defensive buddy is important for a 1-life survive-as-long-as-you-can mission, but a gem (point) collector drone is better for a timed mission.  Similarly, certain super weapons are better on certain maps than others.  The ability to customize your loadout helps add some depth to the game.
In addition to "Adventure" mode are three other main modes:  "Ultimate" mode, which plays like a crazier, 40-level version of "Adventure" mode; "Hardcore" mode, which is primarily levels from "Adventure" and "Ultimate" modes, minus the ability to use drones/super weapons, and "Classic" mode, which is simply the ability to choose from the 6 primary mission types featured in previous Geometry Wars installments.
As the game is all about stars, points, and high-scores, it can really create a "one more time" itch for people who like seeing how high they can get on the leaderboards.  The game itself provides a reasonable challenge--I wouldn't qualify it as an especially difficult twinstick shooter by any stretch--but for those who are looking to score 3-stars (or beat friends/global scores) the game can put up enough of a fight that you probably won't sleepwalk through levels.
Package it all up in a coherent lo-fi arcade art-style and you've got a solid twinstick-shooter timesink that likely offers more content than the average person will be able to tackle.  I probably wouldn't recommend taking it on without a gamepad of some sort, though.

I'm writing this to hopefully counter some of the negative reviews because this game doesn't really deserve the harsh criticism just because some folks are having trouble on Ultra settings. I'm running an older 8350 paired with a 1070FTW edition gpu and a 34" acer predator and on the settings the game picked for itself, it's running just fine. It may very well be poorly optimized at ultra settings but my suggestion is to calm down and wait for a patch. It's not the end of the world to play at slightly less than ultra.
So, about the game itself. There's things that I like and things that I don't. I'm a little surprised at how much it *feels* like Fallout. The place is mostly trashed and there's a lore reason for it that I won't spoil, but it doesn't change how fallout-y it feels.
The controls are pretty good, at least for the 360 controller. I wish that we could remap the buttons ourselves instead of choosing their three presets (that's me wanting to map my 'sneak' button to the same one Fallout and ES uses), but it's not game breaking.
I am really enjoying playing as Emily and I'm pleasantly surprised at how prominently she's featured. She feels like a real character of the game, not the token woman just to check off a box. Her story is compelling and interesting and it's clear they put a significant amount of time into developing her.  The player can really care about and empathize with her. She has real motivation to go out and right the wrongs that have been done, wrongs that don't feel arbitrary *cough cough fallout baby cough cough*. Yet, it's not a situation where you're going to completely forget the main quest to start a garden somewhere because *too* much of the roleplay was taken away and you just can't care about it. This is the perfect balance of having a character with a backstory that you can still make your own.
The super powers are pretty fun as well. Movement feels fluid and it's especially satisfying to pull yourself behind an enemy and assassinate him.
There's only a couple things that I can think of right now that I don't really care for. One is the character models. We're in 2016 but you're going to feel like you're in the early 2000's when you get up close to talk to a character. If they are sitting on the floor, forget it. Out of proportion hands, strangely skinny and gangly bodies, it makes our complaints about Bethesda faces seem like overreaction. These are just weird looking npcs. It's what you see on mainstream crime dramas when they decide to write in gaming stuff using an old id Tech engine (and mostly get it completely wrong).
The other thing is the lack of treasure, and by treasure I don't mean valuables. I mean there's an awful lot of things laying about and you're going to strain your eyes piacking out what is actually actionable. There's too many 'pick up and throw' items littered about, though some interesting pieces are strategically placed. Truthfully it's just a minor gripe coming from someone who is a big fan of Fallout and ES and the ability to pick up literally every piece of junk laying about.
Menus feel too flashy and there doesn't seem to be an easy way to open the map. That could just be me getting used to the controls and not quite having that one down yet.
In all, it's been a pretty fun game so far. If you really only care about graphics, wait for the patch. If you like story and just stealthing around and leaving bodies in your wake, go ahead and get it.

This review is written shortly after completing my first playthrough, which I played as Corvo
Dishonored 2 is damn near everything you wanted from a sequel to the legendary Dishonored, even if it might have it's own flaws. With it's updated engine and new technology available to the devs, the visuals and physics are absolutely stunning. Each mission now has even more ways to go about your goal (not more ways to deal with key targets, that still either lethal or nonlethal) and lots of tiny little details and side-quests scattered throughout. Everything from the level layout to all the tiny little things make this game absolutely stunning, and well worth the wait for fans of the original game. On top of all of the way to tackle a mission, there's an entirely new character with new powers to do it all again basically doubling the playtime you would've gotten anyways. That is not to say, however, that the game does not have it's flaws, albeit tiny ones. Honestly my biggest complaint with this game was it's sound design, as it just felt so much weaker than the first game's. The pistols no longer have that meaty explosive sound to them, and instead sound like somebody put a silencer on a real-life flintlock, a shame considering the spark effects from the firing of the pistol are glorious to look at. Also related to the sound design, and this might just be Corvo, but your character will occasionally (actually quite frequently) make a little jingly noise as they walk. This of course being everything they're carrying, but it's super distracting and I mistook it for a guard many times. These however, as I mentioned, are just tiny things. Another problem I had was that it seemed they removed the special assassination animations for specific targets. No matter who the key target (mission objective) the animation is always you stabbing them in the shoulder, snapping there neck, and then removing the blade. In the last game each target, even the optional ones, had their own cool assassination animation. Once again a tiny thing, but the kills don't feel as special as they did. One other problem I had with the game was how SHORT it was! I get that they're putting a♥♥♥♥♥♥ton of detail into these levels; writing journals and books, hiding secrets, making sidequests, and polishing it all around, but the game is only 9 levels long. This was the same length as the first game, regardless of the much larger hype and budget behind this game! My final grite with this game would be the odd lack of the Clockwork Soldiers (the big robot dudes invented by this game's Anton Sokolov/Pierro Joplin esq mad inventor, named "Kirin Jindosh"). They spent so much time talking about and describing these dudes before launch, yet you only see about 9 of them (not an exaggeration) in the entire game, 7 if which are all in the same level! Again, these are just tiny problems, and that didn't stop this from being one of my favorite games to drop this year. It's a definite return to the amazing gameplay of the first game, and I can't wait to play my second playthrough as Emily! Once they fix the performance issues (Of which I had none) this is a MUST BUY for those who enjoy anything about the last game, or stealth in general.

A game like Broforce only appears once in a great while: it's smart, fast, detailed, and hilarious. The campaign mode (still a work-in-progress like the rest of the game) starts out small - you've got a couple of bros to play as, and the levels are short and sweet affairs with minor explosivity and a gentle learning curve. However, the levels soon become massive, beautiful layers of falling structure and exploding barrels filled with many hapless terrorists - and their many, many stray bullets. Be prepared to die; it's going to happen a lot.
The playable 'Bros' are the heart of the game's charm: each is a loving shoutout to an 80's or 90's character, and each come equipped with their own weapon and special ability. It's great to see all these homages in one game, and especially one whose pixel graphics and over-the-top demeanor make it believeable.
The fully-destructible environments are a great feature, though to the unwary: death. As I said before, you will die a LOT. If there's not an explosion going off at any given moment, eating away at the level, you probably haven't started moving yet. With many structures physics-enabled, as well as all explosions having the possibility of causing a chain reaction, Broforce is a 1 million on the Hectic Scale.

For fans of the hack & slash types of RPGs, this came is the cream of the crop
Rebooting a classic franchise is hard. Even moreso when you're leaving the classic formula it's built on (2D hack & slash platforming), but if you're going to do it, this is how it's done.
The storyline in this game is phenomenal. Emotionally charged, well developed, and deeply invested. With narration by Sir Patrick Stewart preceding each chapter, even loading screens are beautiful and worth the wait.
The aesthetic of the game is stunning. Each level carries forward some quality of gothic design, from classic, sharp-edged castles to towering forests, to the most beautiful music box you can imagine. The music always suits, carrying with it that sense of an epic struggle of good and evil. Heroic battles await you around every corner. The soundtrack is epic enough that I listen to it regularly, even when not playing.
Gameplay follows a God of War style feel, but improves on it significantly, creating a solid skillcap that you can grow into. At lower difficulties, the game is easy enough to progress the story. At higher difficulties, the game is challenging enough to give you a good run for your money. While the platforming aspects are straightforward (this is no Prince of Persia), the puzzles are quite brilliant.
Originally bought this on the Xbox360, have 0 regrets about buying it again for PC. One of my favourite action RPG games.

It's the year of the Lord 1047, and the Pope just released the encyclical "About the use of shadow magic, and the embedding of barbed whips into 'crosses and other s..t'": the Holy Communion is down, and going around kicking demon asses is up.
This is the intimate alternate interpretation of the middle ages, where our hero, Gabriel Belmont lives (a view that seems to be perfectly coherent with Japanese's view of Christianity, until you find out that the developer is actually Spanish).
Unibrow, neckbeard and just two facial expressions, he is a broken man, devoid of mercy, untouched by evolution, on a quest for revenge and hope, to vindicate the death of his wife and, possibly, bring her back to life.
This portentous story, introduced at the start of each chapter by the voice of Patrick Stewart, who plays the role of one of Gabriel's comrades in the "Order of light" (which is a shorthand for "Order of the ⇓⇘⇒ + Light punch", I guess) basically consists in a lot of platforming and a decent amount of "monsters♥♥♥♥♥kicking" (amen).
During each mission, our hero will find the bodies of some of his fallen companions of the order, who died in this same quest before him, leaving behind scrolls with advices (as if following the advice of a dead man was a good idea…), or occasionally some precious life and magic gems that will help him on his holy quest.
That's for the plot.
As far as the game goes, I admit I liked it: the combat is perhaps not as satisfying as DMC, but can hold its own once you get to master it a bit, and there is some variation in settings.
There are some minor issues with the size of the main character, which is just too small in some panoramic takes, and forced me to squint to find my bearings, but the camera worked well overall, and the settings are beautiful.
The platforming is decent/good, though not being fond of this particular game mechanic, I found deeply annoying how much the game relies on it, often inappropriately, possibly as an homage to the primitive aspect of our protagonist.
Just one example.
You enter in a level that clearly introduces a boss battle, reach the enemy which towers you from afar, and just when you are ready to hit it… Oh, no! f…k. It's a platform boss *again*!
Yep. There are the "platform bosses", aka the "bosses you can mount" (keep your expectations low, you dog!), which means that 3 of the most important bosses in the game are actually platform levels in disguise, where you grapple on some giant f…er, search for magic sposts and pound on them, trying not to be dismounted. Deja-vu, anyone?
As for the rest of the game, the campaign is very long and satisfying, although the quality is often uneven, and you get the occasionally boring or frustrating level section (usually platforming…), but what really impressed me the most, is the amount of comedy this game unintentionally provides, for example:
- Gabriel has only two expressions: constipated, and that of a caveman, to whom someone has given a pocket calculator
- The comrades of the order of light are so evenly distributed around the world, they are a damn ecological issue. You can't litterly turn a corner, or enter a cave without finding one of those dead fuc…ers littering the ground
- even though Gabriel can jump 2 meters off the ground, perform 6 spins in the air, and land on some unsuspecting enemies like a cataclysm, large suspended beams are his bane: when he encounters one, he almost falls at every step (even though he could just normally walk on them. They are that large)
- Gabriel is barely human. Seriously. I know that not everyone can be as cool as Dante, but this guy? I cannot honestly identify myself with this guy.
- Patrick Stewart narration is great, but repetitive. After all, what can you say that's new after, like, 30 chapters of button mashing?  Here is a list of stuff you'll hear over and over:
* Gabriel's rage knows no limits
* Gabriel barely sleeps
* Gabriel never poops (just kidding on this one…)
* in his fury, Gabriel killed a X. The X was the last of his kind
* the glorous race of Y was thriving until the demons arrived
* the last of X of the glorious race of Y died at the hand of our WWF-enthusiast Gabriel
* did I mentioned how Gabriel's rage is boundless?
That said, I really enjoyed the game: just try hard to avoid the 2 DLCs, which you will probably play anyway, but are crap.
PS: oh, and I almost forgot: there is also an infamous, mood breaking "the cake is a lie" reference. Seriously, guys???

I've played over 1,500 hours of SMITE before the steam release and I could play 1,500 more.  This game in a short summary is the most skilled MOBA you will ever play, nothing is an auto lock ability and auto attacks even take skill to hit.
Pros and Cons:
Pros:  -Multiple gamemodes for different types of players (you don't ever have to play the classic 3 lane map if you don't want).
-All gods are usable, meaning that no ones is complete garbage and you will be shunned or hated on for using him.
-The META is constantly changing, always keeping laning and jungling fresh.
-Every god can be used in every lane if you are good enough, and no one will be mad if you do use a Tank in mid lane.
-The store currency to buy skins can be obtained through special events and through weekly awards, meaning if you are patient enough, you can get a skin you want.
-Game is completely free to play, you will never have to spend money on it if you don't want to.
________________________________________________________________________________
Cons:  -All new gods on release are either: 1. completely broken and will infinently destroy you, or 2. super garbage and need a buff immediatly.
-Some gods are better than others, such as Bellona, Au Puch and Khepri, and Hi-Rez won't balance them.
-Servers are constantly kicking you out of games and going offline randomly.
-Community is very toxic, luckily you can mute people though.
-If someone does something wrong, Jungle always gets blamed, so you better be damn good at Jungle unless you want to get roasted hard core.
-Game does not have an in-game voice chat, you have to download an external client called "Curse" to talk to people in League matches.
-Favor (the in-game currency to buy gods) is extremely hard to obtain, making you want to buy the godpack more and more so you don't have to deal with trying to get it.
________________________________________________________________________________
Overall, this is my most played and favorite game of all time, and I most likely will never stop playing it, no matter how unbalanced Bellona is.
OVERALL RATING FOR SMITE: 9.25/10

Okay, so I just finished the game. Here are my thoughts:
Pros:
-Very good story line (if you played the first game).

-Gorgeous art-style (look a lot like the original game).
-Keeps the feeling of the original Dishonored, but got a welcomed twist with the new character Emily.

Cons:
-I experienced a couple of audio bugs and some bugs, specifically with Emily's ability "Far Reach", when it sometimes just simply wouldn't get you to your desired destination (Elevator shaft, I'm looking at you!).
-Quite a few FPS drops, that really shouldn't happen, since I've got a preeeeeeeetty good PC...
Conclusion:
When it comes down to it, I think that Dishonored 2 is an extremely good game, but we shouldn't just overlook the very bad port, cuz there are A LOT of FPS drops, and the game simply just doesn't run very well on PC. I would still buy it though, and at no point did I regret buying this masterpiece of a game. If you don't have an extremely good PC, I suggest that you just wait till they have patched the horrible port out, and you'll stand with an (almost) perfect game.

Having played Dark Souls extensively, I have to admit, yeah Dark Souls II is probably not as good as the first. Though, it really is futile to compare the too. Saying that Dark Souls II is a dissapointment because it just isn't Dark Souls is like saying Psycho is a dissapointment because it just isn't Citzen Kane. DS2 might not be as much of masterpiece DS1 was, but it is still a damn fine game, and one of this years best. The game is easier than Dark Souls but in some ways it is more fun, there is better balance, better enemy AI, and more thought out/improved game systems. There is a great sense of exploration and dread permating throughout Drangleic's many and diverse areas. And, Dark Souls II still produces the cross world Co-op/pvp game play mechanic that is the hallmark of a Souls game and refines it. It will be really awesome to see how future pvp and cooperative play develops in the world of Drangleic. It's an incredibly well made game, for sure. Where DS1 was lovable but rough around some edges, DS2 feels more polished.
One potential problem aspect is there is a tendancy for this game to feel a bit more, for lack of a better term, video-gamey. The world in DS1 felt really lived-in despite being surreal. You felt like a small speck within a larger more dangerous and believable world, and all the worlds logically flowed into the next. DS2 areas, while some stand out greatly, feel more like worlds created for a video game. This isn't to say they are terrible of even bad, there is some really great level design here and some fairly clever visual design but they don't have the same sense of space and grandeur as Dark Souls 1. In this game you don't feel so much as a tiny ant among giants, which is one of the ways the predecessor felt so tense. I suppose it is unfair to critise DS2's world design against DS1 becuase the world design in DS1 is among the best ever to be created for a RPG or even all games in general. DS2's world design's only flaw is that it is just 'great.' Though I will criticize DS2 for feeling more video-gamey, I have to admit there is a kind of charm in that. Some areas gave me an old school video gaming vibe, almost like the early Zelda games. I dunno if it was intentional but it was nostalgic in a way.
The best thing about Dark Souls II is it is really a game for anybody. I'd recommend it to most game enthusiats in more ways than I would recomend DS1. Where Dark Souls was a game that fosters a devoted cult following, Dark Souls II is a much more welcoming game for all players. It's an awesome game and is likely a game of the year contender.

I've played over 1,500 hours of SMITE before the steam release and I could play 1,500 more.  This game in a short summary is the most skilled MOBA you will ever play, nothing is an auto lock ability and auto attacks even take skill to hit.
Pros and Cons:
Pros:  -Multiple gamemodes for different types of players (you don't ever have to play the classic 3 lane map if you don't want).
-All gods are usable, meaning that no ones is complete garbage and you will be shunned or hated on for using him.
-The META is constantly changing, always keeping laning and jungling fresh.
-Every god can be used in every lane if you are good enough, and no one will be mad if you do use a Tank in mid lane.
-The store currency to buy skins can be obtained through special events and through weekly awards, meaning if you are patient enough, you can get a skin you want.
-Game is completely free to play, you will never have to spend money on it if you don't want to.
________________________________________________________________________________
Cons:  -All new gods on release are either: 1. completely broken and will infinently destroy you, or 2. super garbage and need a buff immediatly.
-Some gods are better than others, such as Bellona, Au Puch and Khepri, and Hi-Rez won't balance them.
-Servers are constantly kicking you out of games and going offline randomly.
-Community is very toxic, luckily you can mute people though.
-If someone does something wrong, Jungle always gets blamed, so you better be damn good at Jungle unless you want to get roasted hard core.
-Game does not have an in-game voice chat, you have to download an external client called "Curse" to talk to people in League matches.
-Favor (the in-game currency to buy gods) is extremely hard to obtain, making you want to buy the godpack more and more so you don't have to deal with trying to get it.
________________________________________________________________________________
Overall, this is my most played and favorite game of all time, and I most likely will never stop playing it, no matter how unbalanced Bellona is.
OVERALL RATING FOR SMITE: 9.25/10

Here are the enemies! Let me shoot ya in the face!
Where am I?
Where are those geoms?
Where are the enemies?
Where is my cursor?
I think I need a controller.
Your ship shoots towards the position of your cursor. So for accurate aiming,
. Somebody might argue that you can just keep shooting and adjust the angle. The problem is, since the distance between your ship and your cursor isn't fixed (the cursor can be anywhere on the screen), most of the time the adjustment is super inaccurate if you do not keep an eye on your cursor position.

Most of the time you might focus on the enemies, especially those fast and/or small ones. Meanwhile, you should also locate the geoms, which is tiny green gems that increases your score multiplier. Geoms are dropped from enemies and will disappear after a few seconds, It is essential to catch enough geoms, otherwise you might even find it hard to get 1 star out of 3. If using a controller, it is acceptable to focus on these stuff. But if you are using the keyboard and mouse, you should also focus on the cursor, which is very distracting.

This game is the twin-stick shooter to beat. It is a treat of controls, visuals, audio, and difficulty. If I was forced to choose a small number of single player games to live with forever, this would be the admiral of the fleet. It's replay value is perfect. One stick moves, the other shoots. You have buttons for bombs, your basic panic button, and specials, which to me feel like sort of mitigation or back-up half-panic. In most modes killing enemies drops green pellets that you can pick up to increase your multiplier for sweet sweet points.
You are some sort of sharp edged open pentagon thing. You shoot bullets at over shapes, each of which behave in their own unique neurotic way. Many blindly move abut paying no heed to you. Some bumrush you. My favorite are the green shapes, that are skittish and will run away when shot at. There are also a number of bosses, and the boss music is incredible to be sure. I still nod my head to it and jam out. There's multiplayer as well, for some pew pew.
The aesthetic of this game is something like Tron, and there is this ague sense that this is all happening in some technological device. The music is great, and I wish there was more of it. I also wish there were more exotic geometries, as everything seems so Platonic and regular. Klein bottles? Eldritch higher dimensional planes? Anyone?

First off, The few hours I have played, I have enjoyed. Never cared for combat aspects, and in it's current state, it's perfect to relax and run around in most of the time.
Now for a quick overview
- The storm can toss blocks at you and kill you.
- Fall damage can kill you.
- plants shoot poison clouds that can kill you...
- Graphics are decent, but the game looks cartoonish.
- Playability, simple for the most part, and easy to get a hang of the given controls
- Building is far simpler than Space Engineers, reminds me a bit like Lego. Snap the pieces together..
Current failings - note: These are not game breakers, Just feel a few changes could be made to enhance them.
- Research : Requires you to locate these strange items, bring them back to base, With enough energy, you crack it open to either recieve some item or a blue print for making an item. To me that is not research, more of a roulette table for blue prints. * There is NO actual research to be done so far *
- The curvature of the planet is deceiving, It gives the impression that it is small, and would not take long to transverse the surface in a mostly straight line, after several hours of driving, My "home" location never showed up over the horizon. *This leads me to believe that the world is seeded and grows much like Minecraft does, tho I know it doesn't.* Also dropped a beacon after 4 hours, but it wasn't long before it vanished from view.
- No explored Map of any kind, to be able to at least retrace your steps to get back.
- Poison Gas Clouds, while wearing a space suit will hurt you? Wait, that's not right, should be a mild acid cloud, makes it more believable, in that it damages the space suit, and lets the poisonous atmosphere in. But it follows the player, so it's got a mind of it's own...
I would give the game an overal 6.5 out of 10 in it's current state. And even with my short "failings" list, when it goes to launch, I believe it will have achieved at least a 7.6, after reading the 'roadmap' of development plans.
* Personally, when they add Hostile encounters, for me, it will detract from the game, but that is just my personal oppinion on the matter, and hope they maintain a "safe play" mode that keeps encounters passive.

Castlevania: Lords of Shadow is a video game time capsule for the year 2010. Although the Castlevania series is about as classic as it gets, the previous attempts to modernize the games into a 3D space had been... iffy. So rather than reinvent the wheel to directly translate the Belmont's 2D action/platforming, MecurySteam took a long look at what was already out there and popular and generously borrowed elements from proven sources; the platforming is Prince of Persia, the combat is God of War, the puzzles are... pretty standard puzzles. Even some of the monster designs are ripped straight out of another property that shares the “Lord of” title... Throw some Zelda and Portal in there for good measure, and you've got Lords of Shadow.
  Even though you can't accuse the game of being original, it's still excellent. A surprisingly epic and involved story has the protagonist, Gabriel Belmont, on a quest to bring his deceased lover back to life. Told through highly produced and sometimes a little too long cutscenes (chock full of quick times events. Another mid-to-late 2000s staple.), you make your way through spooky forests infested with goblins and werewolves, dark caves, Frankenstein's booby trapped electric lab, hellish dreamscapes with shifting geometry, and a misleadingly minor stop at a vampire's castle. The rouge's gallery of Universal monsters and mishmash of creeps and haunts are well represented here. Even if the scarcity of classic gothic architecture is noticeable, it looks incredibly atmospheric and iconic when you're allowed to play in it.
  Fighting back the creatures of the night is enjoyable if a little shallow. You use your whip to strike either directly at an enemy or in an arc, and use experience points awarded throughout the game to unlock more advanced moves and combos. While the pages of upgrades looks intimidating and impressive, I didn't find much need to commit any complex combos to memory beside specific moves needed to manipulate the environment and progress the game. You're fine just focusing on timing rather than fancy buttonwork, dodging and blocking as necessary and parrying and getting damage in when you have a window. Getting hit usually drains an alarming portion of your healthbar, but you can regain some of it back by activating one of your two gauntlets (the other one increases damage) and striking back. It's certainly competent, though I don't think the system ever really hits it's stride and the difficulty tends to be all over the place.
  Navigating the sprawling levels is a highlight. There are secrets hidden everywhere, some of which you'll have to get to on a replay once your abilities have been upgraded. It's light Metroidvania, which is expected because of the later half of that genre. None of the backtracking is required, it's just bonus content for completionists or buffs if you're having trouble progressing straight through. The camera is fixed, which predictably leads to both beautiful shots and frustrating movement problems. The environments are almost uniformly gorgeous in a dark fantasy kind of way, although the proliferation of invisible walls can dampen your curiosity. You'll also be blocked by many puzzles which vary from gameplay mechanics quizzes, adventure game-type static screens, and a variation of chess. A few of them seem a bit too complex and involved, forcing you to completely stop for long stretches and shift gears to an entirely different genre, but they are satisfying to tinker with. There is also the option to basically skip them with a massive hint, which will forfeit your experience rewards for solving them.
  Lords of Shadow is an all around solid game, a massive old school single player adventure that puts it's massive budget on the screen. It is a bit of an odd duck with it's nebulous genre hopping and shifts in tone, but the upshot to that is you're never doing the same thing for long. If you value variety, Lords of Shadow won't disappoint. The only truly negative things I have to say is about the DLC included in the “Ultimate Edition”; it's clearly much lower budget than the main game with unfinished “motion comic” story boards replacing the previous beautiful cinematics. And the last boss is absurdly difficult; a multi-stage nightmare that will remind you why you avoided aerial combat before and curse some poorly placed checkpoints and the game's refusal to refill your life after each chapter. Oh, and those chupacabras... probably the worst enemy to disgrace any game I've ever played. Not only do they steal all of your relics (temporarily to the point of it being useless but still annoying), but they're some awful failed attempt at comic relief in an otherwise deadly serious and straightfaced game. They'll taunt you with an obnoxiously high pitched, grating voice as you hunt them down and they don't stop. And you can't kill them. Seriously, ♥♥♥♥ those things.

This game is quite challenging when you are playing alone. But when you play it with 1-3 friends, it gets just crazy. Prepare for explosions everywhere, enemies getting chainsawed, their heads blow off, wiped to death, set on fire or just crushed by all kinds of things.

Even in the early state that it is in at the moment, it's already incredibly polished and fun to play. -in this game, you recibe a threat level (it indicates how good you play). green,bronze,silver and gold. you're put automatically inside a district that is supposed to gather players from the same threat level. for (reasons), this doesnt happend. silver district is full of golds and bronze district is full of silvers. this creates something interesting: 2 worlds. the bronze district, where bronze and silvers hang out, a more newbie friendly place to learn the game. and the silver district, full of silvers that likes to take a big challange and golds. the silver districts will be hell on earth for all new players, they will be put against very strong oposition and wont have any chance of winning. yet, silvers and golds of the bronze district wont be as good and strong as silvers of the silver district.
