Overall the game is fun, exploring while trying to maintain the ranch and fighting of the Tar and feral slimes. but there is a current glitch that is blocking me from even playing the game anymore, after you walk off of the elevated spawn area you fall directly into the ground and drown in the slime sea, this has accoured in the path to the lab too! please fix this so fellow players and me can actually play the game.

This game starts off with a simple premise: get slimes, make money. After a brief tutorial on basic mechanics (press WASD to move, SPACE to jump, etc...) it throws you right in. The cycle of gameplay is centered around your ranch, your home base where you keep slimes in cages and feed them terrified chickens. There's a number of empty plots that you can purchase upgrades for, essentially the choice of plot boils down into Farm, Chicken Coop, or Slime Pen. Each plot costs money to upgrade, but money filters into your account at a decent pace, so you're constantly upgrading.
The best part of the game I've seen so far is the various types of slimes, and how you can mix them together. The way you make money in this game is through slime plorts. Essentially slime poo. The easiest type of slime to keep, the pink slime, makes pink plorts, rock slimes make rock plorts, tabby slimes make tabby plorts, etc.. If you feed a slime a plort from a different type, the slime transforms into a larger mixed version. If you don't know what you're doing early game (like me) and you keep all your various types of slimes in the most basic corral (like me) you'll end up overflowing the farm with massive fat adorable and annoying mixed slimes, which will inevitably eat all your chickens and crops. The easy fix to this is euthanasia, essentially launching the adorable ♥♥♥♥ers into the ocean to drownd. Later in the game, mixing slimes becomes a more challenging and more profitable alternative to smaller slimes.
Beyond the ranch is the wide open wilderness of slimes, where you'll find wild slimes to vaccum up and shove into corrals back at your home base. This is the most rewarding aspect of the game. Pink slimes, the ever annoying pests, swarm throughout the first few areas in the wilderness, tainting other slimes with their plorts, and being generally terrible to be around. They're especially annoying when they mix with rock slimes, because then you have randomly exploding giant balls of adorable trundling along after you. The one good thing about wild pink slimes is that they drop plorts almost nonstop, so it's one of the easiest sources of ingame money, despite the pink plort's low selling point.
Eventually, you're bound to come across some massive stationary slimes that you can forcefeed until they love you, and some locked doors. I'm mentioning these together because I'm possitive that they're somehow related, but I haven't tested any further.
The level design out in the wilderness can occasionally be something like Dark Souls, a twisting labarynthine area that contains some hidden areas, crates of goodies to uncover, and a plethora of various slimes. Sometimes, it's confusing, especially since little open areas of slimes are connected by essentially long twisting corridors, but getting lost is part of the fun.
Venturing out into the night reveals new slimes, ones that die horribly if exposed to sunlight, and some kind of evil tar monsters that eat slimes, but don't mind trying to kill you too. These can be dealt with by hurling them into the ocean before they split apart and become twice the threat, but you're likely to be quickly overwhelmed by them if you aren't careful.
The colors are lovely, the slimes are adorable (especially the tabby slimes), and the item descriptions are cheeky fun. There's a real time display of what plorts are in high demand, and which aren't. If you're not careful you'll flood the market and crash the price of some plorts (mostly pink plorts, because they're everywhere).
I'm not sure if I'm happy with the 20$ price tag, but the game is still eary access, so I'm hoping that more is added to boost the value. As is, I'd say there's a full 15$ game worth of content here, but I might just be a cheap old ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥.
In short, absolutely buy this if you have a heart, or buy it if you want to commit genocide on the pink slimes, because they deserve it.

(Please note I have clocked about 15 hours of multiplayer at the time of writing, and this will be a review about the multiplayer portion of the game)
*sigh* This is truly a disapointing title. And I'm not saying this because it is yet another CoD. Not at all, in fact it breaks the mould quite nicely I would say. A simple addition in the form of the exo-suits changes the dynamic of the game quite significantly, offering a whole new learning curve and and interesting twist on your standard firefights. This is really the only significant change made in this title, but it REALLY can't be emphasised enough the difference it makes.
Exo-abilities are also quite a nice change. Instead of the standard of having tactical and lethal grenades/equipment you have lethal equipment and an exo ability. Exo abilities essentially are like new perks (in some cases old perks) but with a twist to them; they have a limited amount of battery life, meaning you must use them wisely.
So far things sound like its not too bad, right? Wrong. It is no good having improved gameplay if the game isn't playable. This is where we get to why I will not recommend this game.
1) No dedicated servers. As it is there are no servers, and since they haven't been here on release I have no reason to believe this will change, so you are stuck with P2P. Those P2P connections as they currently are very sporatic. You really don't know what is going to happen with them. And this is absolutely unacceptable in a real time pvp game like this where split second reactions can save your life.
2) Optimization. This game is far superior to Ghosts in this department but it still cannot be ignored that this requires far greater hardware than it really should (imo, but I'm sure many will agree). In fact this is the strange issue with the game. I could if I wished run many of the settings on extra/high and would have a playable fps in the 60s, but this makes the game unplayable for me as the stuttering as the game renders the level is ridiculous. This is something I have never had in any game series other than CoD, and I'm starting to believe this is a serious issue with their engine, at least on PC.
It should be noted I am writing this from a lower spec end of the PC spectrum but you will find people are having problems with various hardware configurations, even PCs that should easily run the game. It seems to me the general thing with this game is it is consistently poor on machines that are below the recommended requirements, possibly more so than it should be... and even those on recommended specs or higher have had enough problems for me to deem necessary to note here.
Then there is also the fact this game only utilizes 2 cores, but locks out PCs which don't use 4 cores/threads. Terrible and pointless practice.
The overall verdict is if you want/must play Advanced Warfare, play it on console - where it was intended to be played. Probably a more enjoyable experience anyway, since this (and all CoDs really) was clearly made for casuals. Maybe patches will make the PC version more bareable and enjoyable, but lack of dedicated servers will seriously hurt this game in the long run.

I'll get this out of the way first thing: they tried REALLY hard to make this a true successor the the original NES Castlevania's and even Super Castlevania. On the hardest difficulty (which you unlock when you finish the game on any difficulty) is brutal and you pretty much have to go through the entire game again without being hit (especially by bosses) [and much like the original Castlevania where one hit killed you].
The only thing keeping this from being a great homage to the series is the music. It's not that I DISLIKE the music in Lords of Shadow, it's that it's not Castlevania music at all. No catchy themes or different themes for different areas. While this would normally irritate the hell out of me (being a HUGE old school Castlevania gan) the music that is in place does the job just fine. Some of it is actually pretty good. It's just that it's got a feel that is closer to lightly orchestrated/gothic as opposed to Rondo of Blood or Symphony of the Knight. It's there just enough to notice it, but it's not strong enough to stand out.
Now that we have that out of the way, was the game worth playing to 100% completion? If I had to give it a rank I'd give it a 7/10. The combat sections are phenomenal and require real skill and strategy to got past (especially on Paladin mode). There were times when I got stuck, but I was always aware of what I did and why I failed.
Where the game falters the most are the platforming sections. I'll be frank, the platforming sections are a pain in the♥♥♥♥♥ Often time the camera doesn't focus on what you're supposed to see and other times the next objective is almost entirely off screen, leaving you wondering where to jump to next. The 2.5D sections are a serious pain as you still have full 360 degrees of motion but are being directed on a "two-dimensional" plane. Additionally when the camera changes to a new perspective the controls don't adapt. Meaning if you're going through a tricky platform section you can easily miss a step if you try to adapt to whatever the game does to the controls when you reach your destination.
Overall though, I don't regret playing it to 100%. It's definitely one of the tougher games I've played (I'd put it up there with some of Alan Wake's tougher achievements) and I definitely felt a sense of pride when I finished off the very last boss (from the Resurrection DLC which is included in the Ultimate Edition) in Paladin mode which essentially ended my play through. There were moments where I got bored (platforming, again) but I did have a good time with it. It's out for legacy platforms and I don't know about it's backwards compatibility status but if you're looking for something to scratch that God of War itch with a Castlevania setting then look no further.

08-Jul-2016 : Finished main story + extras
Equipment : MSI GT80-2QE Notebook
REVIEW :
I really enjoy this game. The graphics are a little bit outdated but still good enough for a 6-year old game (originally released in 2010 for console). The music soundtracks are great and really captures the dark victorian atmosphere, The characters and storytelling are interesting with good voice acting, The locations are varied from chapter to chapter with great artistic level design. The puzzles are great and challenging but not too hard so they won't distract the player from the quest and story pacing. The puzzles also have in-game solutions so player can choose to bypass them if necessary. The boss fights are great and epic. I had a hard time putting down this game before I finished it because I really felt like I'm in an epic quest.
Things I dislike, let see... the fixed camera system. Some platforming parts were really frustrating because of that. And then there's the story itself. Although I like the storytelling, some parts of the plot were silly and the ending was badly written. I don't want to spoil anything here, so you just have to start your own quest for glory.
CONCLUSION :
Recommended on full price, a must-have on sale price.

The good:
- I like the lawless theme and gritty world of the borderlands.

The not so good:

I bought this game 6 months ago, and I found it an interesting single note, with the promise of being a beautiful symphony (one day).  However, it just didn't have anywhere near enough content when I started to play it, and it grew boring very quickly. I ran through everything in about 15 hours, and stretched it to almost 30 to not feel like I wasted my money ( I did).  Early Access and all aside, there have been 0 patches in these 6 months that, from my perspective, that have added content in a meanigful way, or encouraged me to re-install the game since my first playthrough. I have lost faith the developers are pushing hard enough to add real innovation to this game at this point.

Now, If you feel that about 15 hours of game play is worth the game's current price, this a good game.  It has a good artistic look, not too buggy, seems reasonably polished and playable for what little this title does. Just expect to set it down after about 15 hours, unless this game REALLY, REALLY fits your playstyle, or redundancy in gaming is your jam.
For someone like me, who is a variety gamer and has a large number of Steam games and varied interests, you may be coming into this with the exxpectation of 20+ hours of game play for a game in this price range, and/or some fierce and innovative game mechanics from an indie gem in the rough.  Two Early Access games that demonstrate what I am saying here, Factorio or Rimworld, where $20 couldn't be better spent, sale or not, and you could spend literally over 100+ hours in either one of those games and still not be bored.
If this kind of gamer describes you, I will tell you what I have told several Steam friends already.  watch this game, wishlist it even, but WAIT until it this game either leaves Early Access, or when you see a MAJOR patch come through that clearly adds a HUGE amount of content.   In the meantime, if you have to look at an Early Access game, and it has to be space, and buildy, and multi-player, and you hate the bugs of Space Engineers and want soemthing more playable, in this price range, I'd look at Avorion.

There is so much good in this game but there are only a few problems I ran into.
- Rovers are glitchy when used in multiplayer.
- The what I will call "plantlife" which is really just some blocks, tends to respawn in the air if you tear the terrain up.
- There is a bit of a hit detection error where you cannot shield your base from storms if you build a wall around it.
Apart from those problems I enjoyed every minute of it. You can discover large objects like a massive solar panel that you can link to your base for power, or you might run up on a crashed lander with free supplies like a seat for your rover, or perhaps you just might find more of a resource that you have been looking for. In the current state of the game it is very much playable, but I might not return until I know that the annoying issues are fixed. The only issue I have is how the rockets are controlled in space.
Really fun for the first hour or so... Then, it already starts feeling a bit repetitive. I hope they add more content soon.

So far, this has been a very good game and had the potential to be the best space discovery game out there. That being said, if the devs don't speed up on their work, this will end up like the numerous early access games out there.

Advanced Warfare brings in a lot of changes to the COD formula, while still keeping it familiar enough to be COD. The campaign, though still pretty linear compared to Treyarch's Black Ops II, is definitely top-notch, and is a huge improvement over Ghosts' mediocre campaign. Sledgehammer definitely put in a lot of effort to make a good story, and they did it right. All of the main actors (Troy Baker, Kevin Spacey, Gideon Emery...) contributed a lot to making this campaign enjoyable with their acting, and their characters are well-designed. My only gripe is that Baker's character, AKA the protagonist Mitchell,  doesn't actually speak during gameplay (I prefer the way Treyarch does it with their protagonists for Black Ops and Black Ops II). But I can live with the way things are right now.
The multiplayer component is now even more intense and frantic than ever before, thanks to the Exosuit movement added in the game. It adds a lot of "verticality" (quoting SHG dev Michael Condrey here) to the COD formula. Here is a COD game where skills actually matter. You don't just jump in guns blazing and hope that you can end up on the top of the leaderboards. There are tactics involved. Sledgehammer has also learned a lot from Infinity Ward and Treyarch, and improved upon the best of each developer. With the right kind of balance and tweaking, Advanced Warfare multiplayer has potential to be the best MP game since COD 4.
At the time this review is written, the game is still in need of several fixes, especially optimization for connectivity, but overall it is a solid product, and I wholeheartedly recommend this game to anyone, specifically those who have quit COD and are looking for a reason to come back.

The new powers you acquire from the Outsider are a lot of fun and give even more options when it comes to play styles. The game has a very different feeling from the original; Karnaca is a lively, populated city  with a lot of character, a stark contrast to Dunwall. Civilians and guards roam the streets, keeping you on your toes and ready to call out for help if you seem suspicious or are seen comitting crimes. The story feels engaging and well thought out so far, definitely a game I would recommend to existing fans and new players alike.

So I was looking for a dark Castlevania type game.  At first glance this game looks like Assassin's Creed or God of War, which was a turn off for me, but as I got into it, it's very much Castlevania.  Each area is explorable, usually a puzzling path to try and find, and monsters.  That's pretty much classic C. in 3D.
Controls.  I scoffed a bit at people who said you need a controller, As I could play just fine without one.  Until the later levels :(  You can definitely play and enjoy without a controller, but for smoother control and less missed jumps, you should use one.  Not a deal breaker though.  (spoiler-free hint:  when it says: wasd(spin) just do wasd twice at normal-fast typing speed.)
The game is extremely long especially with the DLC's in this edition.  A fair amount of exploring, That's a big plus, and you have a rediculous amount of attacks to learn so I find the replay value very high.
The graphics are 9/10.  They are amazing if you look at it from a design perspective, But no DOF or anything like that.  It sits somewhere between last-gen and current-gen.  Lots of well done specularity and normal maps.  In a given scene you may see hundreds of items, enemies, scenery and they all have very well done texturing.  The architecture models are absolutely mind blowing.
People complain about the camera.  In this game, the camera follows you on a set path.  I rarely found it to be a problem.  Maybe once trying to find a platform but other than that I kind of applaud the camera angles.  It goes from closeup battle and jumps to side-scroller.
Pros:
Great cinematic experience.
Very long game.
The monsters are pretty fresh, definitely not derivative.  C. is making it's own style.
The fighting AI is actually pretty smart.  I feel alot of my moves and blocks feel almost predicted. (even more so in LOS2)
Great replay.
Cons:
Music.  I really wish the music had some of the Munsters-like "pop" that the old games had instead of orchestra music.  That would make this game near perfect.
Conc:
Glad I spent the money.  It is a great story, with great battles.  Def worth it.

If you're looking for a quick horror game to play today, look no further than Blameless; a short 20-60 minute puzzle-solving mystery game that has a unique tinge to it. You're a freelance journalist who has been led by a potential client to a house that is under construction. As you follow him into the seemingly abandoned home, you're hit over the head with a metal bar and knocked unconscious, only to awake a few hours later. Can you free yourself from your dark confinements, and escape your pursuer?
There's a tight aura of relentless tension that will surround you from the beginning until the bitter end with this title. The entire time you're left questioning if you will run into your captor while exploring the small, unfinished corridors and rooms of the house. Your first task is to escape the basement that you were left in, and it's in those few minutes that you will understand that Blameless has a different take on investigation and exploration. It takes some critical thinking and scavenging to solve the few puzzles that are present, and it's all very reminiscent of the game INFRA; although the atmosphere here is much more sinister.
The optimization of this game is excellent; it ran at 60 FPS at all times for me on my GTX 1080/i7 6700k combo. The assets and textures look crisp and fresh, the overall title looks really good. Even the voice acting for the intro, ending, notes, and dialogue is extremely well executed; a rarity for a free horror game. There have been some in-game bugs and glitches that've marred the experience of some players, but the developer is very active in the community and a day after the game launched he released an update patch. I played the game after this update patch, and I can confirm that I did not encounter any bugs or glitches during my playthrough.
At the end of Blameless, we are led to believe that this short ride is part of a much bigger project, and that this is a test to see how well it would do on Steam. For one, I think that we need more titles like this on Steam, as the only real "investigative" games that we have are Murdered: Soul Suspect and INFRA; neither of which have a horror element to them like Blameless. TL;DR: Overall a good game, despite a learning curve that will take a few hours of trial and error.
The game itself is great. The map is huge and interesting, yet graphically demanding (I was getting about 40 fps on the highest graphics settings w/ a 1080Ti and 7700k).

It took me probably three hours to really start doing well, but it all came to an end when a group of guys with rifles gunned me down and took all I had (you start with a rock and a torch, obviously giving those with guns an upper hand). That's the fun of it, though.
My complaints would be the following:
- Stone is an important resource, yet it is pretty hard to find. It is not nearly as abundant as wood, sulfur ore, or metal ore. I often found myself with large amounts of those three resources yet scavanging for stone.
- Scrap metal is harder to find than it should be. You'd think it would be in or near rusty cars, but it's not.
- Grass and branches go through buildings.
- Weird issues with shadows where they'd appear and disappear depending on my camera angle.

The original Geometry Wars (Retro Evolved) is one of the best twin stick shooters around and this third entry in the franchise is much better than that gold standard by improving upon it in every conceivable way. There are dozens of modes, over 50 levels, a superb concept of a 3D grid folding back upon itself to open up new ways to travers the grid and take down enemies all mixed up very well with constant rage-quit preventing variety (bored of one level? play another!). You also have power-ups in the form of drones and special pickups granting temporary enhanced shots. I found the difficulty fair if at times a bit on the hard side. The game is an excellent PC port that runs fluidly with pulsing bright, colourful and smoothly flowing graphics all punctuated by excellent music setting the tone for the frenetic gameplay. I read reports of people encountering technical issues but I never experienced any myself, most likely since the game has been patched since release. Speaking of patches, the developers released a free content pack several months after release along with a patch that many recent games would try and sell as DLC, just shows that they actually respect their players and they really deserve to be supported. If you like arcade shooters and like good value (hours upon hours worth of content here) you really should try out this game. I recommend playing this with a gamepad as twin stick shooters generally control better with a gamepad but the keyboard and mouse controls are also very well done.

I'm going to go ahead and recommend this game, because in my opinion it is my favourite Call Of Duty so far. The graphics are great, and it runs well for me on max settings on a 770 and an i7 with 16GB of RAM. The campaign is your standard Call Of Duty so don't expect any surprises, but I still thoroughly enjoyed it.
However, there are a few glaring issues with the game, mainly with multiplayer.
- No dedicated servers, and because of this, lag. I've found myself suddenly teleporting around the map, shots that clearly hit other players are not registering, then I suddenly die. Once I watch the killcam I see that on their screen I didn't even fire a shot.
- Hackers. Today I joined a match where when I got a kill I was awarded 65000 XP, which boosted me from level 44 straight to 50 and I could prestige. I was having a great time legitimately leveling up towards the goal of prestiging only to have that happen, and I'm pretty sure there is no way to reverse it. I then joined another lobby which had the exact same XP hack later on.
- No FOV slider for single player. This didn't bother me personally but I thought I'd point it out.
People have been mentioning mouse acceleration issues, and apparently the fix is to set your polling rate of your mouse to 125Hz. I have done this and I don't have any problems, although I now play with a controller as personally I feel I play better with it.
However, when there is no lag and a full lobby of legitimate players the game is a blast. Its the most fun I've had on a Call Of Duty in quite a while. So yes I do recommend this game, but it might be best to watch videos and do your research before buying, and wait for a few updates.
tl;dr: Great game when it doesn't lag or get hacked, same old campaign but still very enoyable. Kevin Spacey.

One of my least favorite parts about the campaign of Advanced Warfare was it was short, and felt very rushed, I completed it in 6 hours and I am not fast at completing campaign modes of games. I felt that they could have spent more time on parts of the story and more missions. Also I thought that them bringing in Kevin Spacey meant something that so much of our modern world is entranced in right now, the chance to play the bad guy. Considering our recent obsessions with shows like Breaking Bad, Game of Thrones, and House of Cards I feel that it would be obvious to Activision to finally give us the chance to be the bad guy in a game..instead of playing (America killin dos nasty terrorists, russians, or some guy trying to take over the world). To me, I assumed Kevin Spacey meant we would be playing w/ Atlas the entire time, even though they are the bad guys, or even better, a choice at a key point in the game giving u the chance to side w/ Jonathan Irons (Kevin Spacey) or siding w/ America. What I did like about Advanced Warfare was the maps and environment you get to fight in, such as Antartica, Golden Gate Bridge, and New Baghdad. These futuristic representations of these places we know today were very interesting and fun to fight inside of, and defin. a positive part of the game, just like how fighting in Washington D.C in MW2 was such an amazing part of the game. So overall I give the Campaign a 7/10, meaning I think it was fine, I don't feel ripped off by Activision, but I also don't feel super excited for the next Advanced Warfare. The Multiplayer i actually feel is a big positive to the game, because for the first time in ever, they have changed both the movement and the gameplay of the game. Now to be honest it has become very similar to Titanfall, but that doesn't really bother me because at least i'm having fun in the multiplayer now. Also it is important to note that it is very fast paced now, w/ no respawn timers, somewhat small maps, and the ability to fly across them fastly you can respawn, kill, and die in less than 10 seconds. Whether this is a positive to you or not is up to you, but for me I enjoyed it, so i'd give the multiplayer a 8.5/10. So should you buy this game, I think so, but just keep in mind its defin. not the best game out of the Call of Duty franchise.

I've always been a big fan of this franchise, and even after slogging through all their other 3D entries, I still love the series. The N64 and PS2 entrants are more than enough to make most folks give up on a non-side-scrolling entrant for the series being any good, but I think they got it right modeling this after GoW.
The stroy is damn good, and that silky CPT Picard narration is the icing on the cake, for sure. Controls can be a bit squishy, but I think anyone comming from Dark Souls would say that about any game. Boss fights and environments are pure epic, and the puzzels aren't too maddening (plus you can just spend coins to unlock them if you get stuck, or... you know, youtube it). I've got to say the platforming leaves something to be desired, as it mostly just feels punishing due to the afore mentioned rough controls, but the brutal combat and feeling of accomplishment as you gain more power-ups makes up for it to me.
The game also encourages you to revisit previous zones to collect more power-ups that were locked behind previously locked areas due to not having specific abilities, much like the earlier metroid-vania style entrants, so that's a nice nod to the past.
Overall, this game as aged well IMO, and is worth the price of entry when on sale, for sure.

Great game! 4 out of 5.
Pros:
Great graphics, sound, and gameplay make for a solid action 3rd person hack and slash game.
Combat feels rewarding enough to push through even the toughest or most boring fights.
Navigation through the games "world" is more like navigating your harddrive directories than anything else but each stage description gives you the right information if you're looking to get 100% completion or just to go back and get that one extra power up.
Voice acting is seemless with facial animations bringing the characters to life. You get a real sense of emotion from this to build further upon the story telling.
Also, Sir Patrick Stewart's soothing voice narrates a brief prolog before each stage which almost never gets old.
Cons:
The combat system does not stand out on its own as it feels much like other notable hack and slash titles, most like God of War.
The story doesn't follow previous games however uses characters and other elements to write its own version of the Castlevania universe. This may be a con for some, I personally didn't mind.
Some stages, puzzles and enemies tend to become annoyingly difficult and unforgiving even on easy. Though not many, it may impact your decision to collect 100% of the items and powerups.
The cutscenes are plentiful and if you're looking for a quick way to skip cutscenes like other games, this one will annoy you by requiring you pause the game, then select "Yes" to skip the cutscene, instead of pressing or holding a button.
Overall despite the problems this game has I still enjoyed it enough to justifiy the rating 4 out of 5. I love Castlevania, the story was deep, and the game was rewarding. I've played through the game twice now, once on 360, second time on PC, however it may be some time before I revisit this title.

I was a little reluctant to pre-purchace given the influx of frame rate issues people seemed to be having but I took the plunge any way and was not disappointed.
I run a GTX 1060 with i5-3330 CPU and haven't had any issues so far; my FPS has held at a steady 60 (and much higher in some areas of the game), even in the more populated locations with the majority of the settings turned to very high the frame rate has still held.
I've played through the tutorial and first 3 missions and have been loving every second of it; there is much of the original Dishonored gameplay and mechanics which I loved but there are also enough new features and additions to keep it feeling fresh and interesting. The new powers you acquire from the Outsider are a lot of fun and give even more options when it comes to play styles. The game has a very different feeling from the original; Karnaca is a lively, populated city  with a lot of character, a stark contrast to Dunwall. Civilians and guards roam the streets, keeping you on your toes and ready to call out for help if you seem suspicious or are seen comitting crimes. The story feels engaging and well thought out so far, definitely a game I would recommend to existing fans and new players alike.

Though I'm not recommending Lords of Shadow, it's not necessarily bad. It's just not worthy of playing when there are better titles out there in the same genre. If you've played all of those then LoS could still be worth a purchase for you.
My biggest complaints are the following:
1) The game feels too gimmicky. You acquire several new abilities that you'll need to progress in the game. It doesn't feel fun or clever when using the abilities. It feels like a pointless roadblock.
2) The fixed camera can be extremely frustrating.
3) Combat gets tiring as the game continues on. The purchased abilities pale in comparison to something like Devil May Cry. The game can be finished using primarily attack patterns purchased early in the game.
4) While not bad, the music is weak compared to other Castlevania titles. None of the tracks are very memorable. And no Bloody Tears? What?
5) Quick time events are...well...quick time events.
The voice acting and visuals deliver a strong sense of immersion. The story is decent enough and the characters are OK but nothing that will win an award. Lords of Shadow is obviously a well liked game, but it's not something that makes my recommendation list.

The main quest line is linear, but you can go back through levels you have already completed at any time for any reason so it is not completely linear. Indeed sometimes you will come to things that you cannot get until you get a weapon or item from a later level and are forced to come back or miss the item. The game is long also with challenges that show up after the initial completion of a level to add further playability to it, as well as having steam achievments and cloud support which is always a bonus for me. All in all I would rate this game an 8 out of 10. Definitely worth picking up!

I'm going to frank about this. If you love, to run-around, blowing up absoulutely EVERYTHING on the second plane of dimension, this is the game for you. It has a wide, and widening, group of playable characters. The mechanics are solid, animation is great, and as I write this, the development team is most-likely fixing bugs and adding features.

The maps, as well, are well-made.
Overall, it is a very fun game, but, like some others, tires quickly. After the hour-or-so long campaign, you're limited to the user-made levels. These range from single-texture messes, to works of almost-art.
Despite all of this, I do reccommend the game.

Single Player Campaign:
I haven't finished it yet (about 2 hours into it), but it's tedious. Simply tedious. Your exo suit gets nerfed on each mission, which is just irritating; the QT events are poorly designed; you STILL play follow the leader the majority of the time. But the most offensive thing about it? The LOOOOOONG cut scenes that precede each mission CANNOT be skipped. In the past, this was because it played during loading. But this time around, the loading actually STOPS during the cut scene, then resumes AFTER the cut scene ends, forcing you to stare at a black screen save for a small progress bar at the bottom right of the screen. This wouldn't have bothered me very much if it weren't for the fact that quitting and restarting later makes you sit through the WHOLE thing again (feels like about 2 minutes). And don't even THINK about trying to adjust any video settings during campaign mode--the game restarts for EVERYTHING, which then forces you to watch the ENTIRE EFFING CUT SCENE AGAIN.
Multiplayer:
I've spent about 15 hours playing this mode so far. This is, in most cases, the real reason people buy this game, and it's fine. It's definitely far better than Ghosts, but the peer-to-peer servers are still a ridiculous joke. Also, in typical CoD fashion, spawn points are inexplicably bad as well. I can't tell you how many times I've spawned right in front of an enemy soldier entering the room or how many times an enemy spawned in front of me. The exo suit powers add a nice change to the gameplay, and matches feel faster and more frenetic as a result. The downside is that every split second counts that much more now, which makes the crappy server situation all the more irritating. The maps are mostly well-designed (with the exception of Ascension, which mostly consists of a long corridor that snipers call home), and verticality is definitely taken into consideration. That said, it's ridiculous that there are invisible walls and "Out of Bounds" messages still. You don't give a player more power of movement and then put invisible walls. For goodness' sake, make the roof higher and out of reach, or put a meaningful blockade so I can't reach it. But an invisible wall in a place where I *should* be able to jump? That's just lazy.
The reviewers who gave this a 9/10 are clearly fans who grew up on the series and were just thrilled to feel like they're playing something that isn't a TOTAL retread. A 7/10 seems fair to me. Enough is new. Too many annoyances are FAR too old to the point where there's NO excuse than an annual franchise can't fix it.
Do I recommend this game? Do you like CoD? Then you should probably get it. Do you just want single player or are you not a fan of CoD? This isn't going to change your mind.

You know, it’s never easy nor a good feeling to come away from a passion project without being able to have mutual feelings for the dedication behind a small-team. Having played many far greater RPGMaker games of greater and lesser quality and knowing that this version is a more polished “release” than the one-month challenge original, Save Your Mother simply feels like an amateur project. It’s not nearly as amateurish as Lamia Must Die, but it showcases a lot of gameplay design pitfalls when making an entertaining game. There are simply far too many problems to recommend SYM in spite of its own charm, which is a shame because in small bursts of moments SYM can kindle some affection.
While I cannot attest to the merits of Tuomo’s other titles like Strangers of the Power or the upcoming Adventures of Dragon, these games are likely more polished due to the fact that they appear far more focused on what makes them different from other games and they are benefited from the experience of learning how to make games. As a creator/critic, it’s easier to find faults with past projects than when you create them of the moment because everyone has to start somewhere, and I can only hope that whatever lessons are to be learned from Save Your Mother are carried on to future success and to any aspiring developers who should learn how not to make an JPRG.
Normally I avoid using gaming armchair terms that may only serve to make me sound pretentious, but Save Your Mother suffers from two core issues, the lack of conveyance (in gameplay and in storytelling) and the amount of gameplay contrivances. Some of these issues can be excused with the fact that the game was originally part of a contest, but these blunders should have been addressed in its rerelease similar to how OneShot ironed out its RPGmaker flaws.
In talking about conveyance, or simply the ability to communicate ideas to the player, let’s start with the storyline’s greatest problem, the introduction. Immediately after the game begins, the player is learning about the mythos through many abstract terms in a quick text-scrawl before the human elements of Alice and her sickened mother are crammed into this massive exposition dump. It also manages to tell us everything we will ever know about Alice and of her mother in the first cutscene through expository text with no dialogue. While all this info is necessary and relevant, SYM chooses the worst way to frame its beginning by doing the opposite of what it should do. Instead, the game should have began with the two characters conversing and showing us how Alice is incapable of curing her mother, thus establishing her as a scholar pushed to her limits, then letting the player discover the textbook which informs the player not only of the mythos but also of Alice’s goals.
This kind of oversight reappears throughout all the small little details that keep cropping up the farther you play. Why are the particle effects obscuring so much of the screen all the time? Why are dead/knocked-out characters laid vertically when horizontal bodies better convey this information in 2D? Why are the many side-characters glossed over before you can learn their names? Why are dungeon traps so pixel perfect obstacles (like lava bits that blend into the background)? Why is the elevation drawn so vaguely it is hard to see it through the snow? Why do so many dungeons feel punishing towards people who forget to save by making players replay large chunks of a short game, especially when a puzzle offers no second chances? These are the types of questions I would expect game-testers or other quality-assurance groups would point out as suggestions for improvement, and it’s the main sign of the overall lack of quality behind SYM.
The other major issue is how many things feel contrived, and none for good reasons. Many mechanics and systems are included into the game to add “content” without considering how these aspects benefit the game. Things like the fishing mini-game, which is only required once; the coffin ride for one ride; and the scattershot usage of puzzles that often give little information are all pimples of a game in its adolescence. As much as I enjoy subversions from Earthbound-inspired games, this is the kind of problem you would find in AAA games that create content first and contrive “reasons” for their existence after their creation. Even when these elements do fit in such as the puzzles, many can be too punishing and time-consuming like the math challenge because the clues are scattered in a maze and you will reload your save file if you mistype the answer. These puzzles don’t feel rewarding because they feel more like busy-work to keep the player from progressing.
What bothers me is none of these added mechanics—aside from the puzzles that show ingenuity—flesh out Alice’s character to show the player she is smart, resourceful and capable because the game doesn’t utilize the mechanics to flesh out her traits. These concerns are all laid on the wayside as the art and music attempt to make for an emotionally bonding experience almost anyone could relate to with going on a journey to save their mother. Except it never really reaches the heights it could have achieved because neither the game’s storytelling nor the gameplay truly commits to making that bond a priority over simply making what feels like any other RPGMaker game.
While I could continue describing many other problems such as basing a JRPG as a one-man combat system becoming quickly stale, those concerns seem less important from the more crucial problems that robs Save Your Mother from being an emotionally heartfelt experience. Underneath the charming exterior and the emotionally manipulative set-up to invest players almost cheaply from maternal feelings, this is one experience that I cannot say will remain memorable nor will it retain any fondness in its desire to evoke these feelings. I wouldn’t say the game is a failure nor broken; its ambitions seem too high for the capabilities of the developers to achieve them. It's simply a case where a game did not work out the way they hoped it would plan out.
Perhaps for the developers and for their families Save Your Mother does resonate with them more strongly because they have that connection in every line of code, in every pixel and picture drawn, and in all the memories embroidered in the development borne from that same passion that manifests itself more strongly than I ever could imagine.

I realised I haven't wrote a review of this game, but I feel like I should as it's still in my library and I have played it.
I've played this before version 1.43, but given the changelog, only balancing changes happened for the most part, so what I speak should generally still apply.
I originally thought this game was the absolute worse, but now reflecting back on it, it isn't so bad, but it's not very good either, not good enough that I would recommend. But there are far worse games than this.
So, the good part of the RPG is it presented itself with a lot of oppurtonities to subvert your expectations and writes in a lot of set up seemingly specifically for it and the choices that can potentially explore various ideas to provoke your thoughts.
That's where the bad part comes in, despite all the setup, the game never takes advantage of them, it never really explores morality with the goals of the main character which is really unfortunate.
This results the game not being very engaging, making it for a very forgettable experience. It's also marred by the fact that it's an RPG Maker game clearly, giving players expectations that it's very cookie cutter as most games are in RPG Maker
It's expected of them to bring something strong to the table, and most respond with a very strong story as an RPG Maker game. This game doesn't have a very strong story because it's not engaging.
Story aside, the combat is very basic as you only control a single character. The first boss can be summed down to spamming the fire spell you get at the start to win. The the alternative route you can take is grind for hours to just beat the boss without the fire spell which is an odd design choice of offering a choice.
The most tactic you can get out of this is maintaining full health and throwing out your strongest attack. OFF by Ghost Mortis had more depth, unfortunately.
There were other mechanics in the game that were thrown in without ever being very developed such as the mining. If that idea was played through the entire game with a few tweaks to make it stronger, it would have made ore hunting fun and rewarding, but it ended up only in one section of the game with the sole purpose to inflate you with money.
In short, this game had a lot of potential it didn't build upon storywise and mechanic wise, which is a shame.
Edit: Also an addendum to this review, this game is beatable within 6 hours of casual playthrough. That is if you're not collecting stuff for the gallery, which is another underdeveloped part of the game. Rewarding you with art. But it doesn't feel very rewarding in the way they do it.

After getting a coupon for -90%, I figured why not, but having played through the game I couldn't help but see a bunch of problems that kinda need attention, as well as general criticisms that I don't think will change but I still did not really like.

* Really do not like the combat. Combat is real time which isn't necessarily bad, but because what you could do was typically very limited and only could be done at certain times, it felt really bad.
For example, in a fight you could basic attack, cast a spell, guard or use an item such as a healing potion.
However, fights would typically devolve in to mindlessly doing two things - casting your strongest spell and occasionally topping off your health and mana. There was very little variety in how to play fights because you didn't have time to think and plan what to do, and you objectively had a strongest attack which you'd just spam in order.
As such a lot of bosses and enemies just felt like stat checks, since there wasn't really any thought in to beating them it was just "Spam this as much as possible and either kill the enemy or die".
Combat definitely needs work in some way, whether it's dropping it down to be turn based to slow things down and let the player plan how to play, or overhaul the items and attacks the player could use in order to make things less binary.
* Controls were clunky and could probably do with breaking up some of the buttons which were "press this to do everything", and also there were times in the game which handled REALLY badly. One that springs to mind was the lava lake section, where sometimes the character wouldn't move as you wanted which was really frustrating.
* Some things felt fanservicey. I know some people like that, but personally I do not.
* Game felt very linear with not much side questing or exploration to get up to. There was a gold collection mechanic too, but never really anything to buy so it would just turn in to "well I can buy hundreds of this thing and I've got nothing else to purchase, so ok".
Overall I feel like the game does have potential, but currently isn't really fleshed out enough to justify buying.

I logged in. I spawned with nothing but a rock, a bow, and a few trusted arrows. My inventory was meager, but I did not let this diminish my ambition. As I looked over the horizon I saw a man. He was medium built and naked down to the boot. The only thing identifiable about this man was the look of hatred in his eyes when he turned towards me from over 200 meters away. Although we locked eyes for only a moment, we both had a silent understanding. We knew that only one of us could walk away alive.
The next thing I know I am sprinting towards this man with all the energy I could muster. The only thing on my mind was spilling this man's blood. As we approached eachother I pulled out my bow and nocked one of my few trusted arrows. I aimed the arrow high above his head and gently lessened the grip of the arrow until it jettisoned from my bow into his skull. In almost the blink of an instant my advisary was on the ground and screaming like a wounded deer.
I knew I had to put my prey out of its misery. As I gradually approached the injured man I recognized I had to dissociate this man as another person. I had to rationalize them as an animal in order to sever any doubts in my mind to finish the job. I then raised my rock high above my head and slammed it into his skull. A man no more. What was once a man is now an empty cadavar; a desolate shell.
As I gleefully looted my prey and took his items I heard a warcry from behind me. As I turn around I see a naked man about 100 meters away from me jumping in sheer jubilee. The last thing I see is his wooden spear flying through the air directly towards my head. I did not move. I stared blankly into my computer monitor, wondering what I had become.

I finished this game a few times now and I am still loving it.
So first of: This is no classic Castlevania. As you maybe took from the screenshots this game takes place in a 3D enviroment and you can choose the diffrent stages in a world map / chapter screen.
But this game does not need to be a classic Castlevania. It tries to revive the the franchise, it starts an entire new timeline.
So lets get to the gameplay: You use only one main weapon throughout the entire game but you will get upgrades for it  from time to time. Additionally you will acquire 4 sub weapons while playing through the game and to types of magic you can  (and will) use in combat. One will buff your attack strength and one will heal you every time you hit an enemy.
Each killed enemy will grant you XP but they are not used to level up like you would imagine. You use them to buy new combos (or concept arts). All of this (and the possibility to block / parry / dodge) and a challenging enemy design build up a simple to use difficult to learn combat system.
I will not spoiler any detail about the story but I will say that the last cinematic shocked me (not counting the to DLC chapters) and makes every effort throught the game's story worth it.
Finally I would really recommend this game to any Castlevania Fan, Hack'n'slay lovers and story obsessed gamers as it provides a great storyline, great combat system, great music and a great new beginning for a Castlevania timeline.

Short version: Go buy Black Mesa. If you want to know why this game is a ♥♥♥♥ing joke, by all means, proceed.
HL Source is the only bad Valve game ever released. It's honestly unbelievable how awful and fundamentally broken this one is, Valve managed to take their most iconic game- not to mention the one which launched their company to stardom, and absolutely deprive it of quality. For 10 bucks, what do you get from HL Source? An unplayable mess full of broken scripted sequences, broken NPCs, unbalanced weapons and damage systems, infuriating glitches, levels so broken you can't win, levels so broken you can't lose, just a total disaster. I hate to repeat myself so much, but this game is a broken mess. Even the Garry's Mod content is pretty lackluster, you'd be better off with a free mod like Half Life Renaissance. Oh, and for fans of the HD models that came with Blue Shift, don't even bother. For one they seem to be modified from the original release (why bother with such tiny changes?) and most importantly, the models are incomplete showing wireframes, and even the sounds on the guns like the M4 and SPAS-12 are missing altogether.
The "selling points" of HL Source include a HL2 style chapter select, improved Source Engine lighting, HL2 style water, and ragdoll physics. That's it. For ten bucks. How could Valve have gone so wrong? Counter Strike Source and Day of Defeat Source offered complete Source remakes of their predecessors, so why are we stuck with this awful port instead of a real remake, like the mod Black Mesa? And more importantly, why hasn't Valve even bothered to make this garbarge at least functional? It's full of little distracting mistakes any HL series veteran will notice immediately. Just a mess.
I will say the Deathmatch multiplayer is fun. You can actually get this in a pack of other Source multiplayer titles without having to get HL Source. DMS has a lot of the same problems as Source, but luckily the abudance of great community made maps makes it worthwhile.

Orign Of Destiny is a free rpg that is easy to just pick up and play. It's your typical generic rpg that takes elements from other games and does them well for the most part. Of course there are flaws but nothing major. A few flaws i would mention is no wait option for tactical play and the lack of variety of monster in some areas and low exp rates, which makes things a bit of a grind. Some may not mind this.
There is the option of three difficulty settings. Easy, medium and hard. Easy mode is if you just want to breeze through the story with little challenge, medium provides a serious challenge and hard mode is just insanity.
Graphics are your basic rpg maker kind of graphics with sprites that we expect from these games, which is kind of that Snes nostalgia era we all once knew an loved.
Overall it is a very well produced game that offers challenge and story in a free rpg to download, and to play.
6/10 from me. Solid for what it is.

Dark Souls 2 is a great hardcore RPG that will give you more than your money worth of play time and entertainment. If you have played the first Dark Souls game then you know what you are getting into. An unforgiving combat RPG that thrives off of quick reflexes and perfect timing, and deaths. Lots and lots of death are the means to learn what makes the enemy ticks. With plenty of different armour combinations to make your character unique and a new take on the way you level up which has creating your characters stats build even more involved than in the first Darks Souls there are more RPG elements than you probably will take the time to see to its full extent! When I first started playing to be honest after a while I hated the game, but the more you play the more you see just how thought out the game developers made the game and how wrong I was. Take the Blue Sentinel covenant for example. Upon finding and joining the faction like group you are tasked with playing as the "good guy" as far as slaying strangers can be considered good. You can help other players in the world by placing summon signs on the ground which draws you into their world for a limited time, or boss battle to help them in their adventure. Upon finishing helping them you recieve an item that you can use in the covenants chapel to spar with other covenant members. The one who wins, which would be considered the stronger of the two, recieve an item that allows them to use in the world to invade the world of sinners who have killed innocent people to exact justice. You also recieve a ring that allows you to be pulled into the world of a member of you sibling covenant the Path of the Blue. When a Path of the Blue member is invaded by a would be sinner you come to their aid to fight them off. All of this which when slowly being introduced to you over hours of explorations and trial can seem uncessecary and odd but when you look back on the process as a whole it reveals itself to be a thought out RPG style way of interacting with the world and multiplayer community. The game does have some flaws like the story line becoming very obtuse later on luring you away from the action and to online guides to end the search for that one statue you passed by 30 in game hours ago and 4 real life days ago that had no use then but now is the only way to continue on. Even with the flaws there is so much good in this game that they are heavily out weighed by the moments of joy like when you choose to start a New Game plus with harder difficulty and new items to find, just to see that there is also new enemies to fight, and new enemy placement to keep things just as fresh as the first time!
TL:DR
I am loving this game from the PvE to the PvP and recommend anyone who is willing to lose days worth of time getting lost in its world should pick this game up!

Castlevania: Lords of Shadows is an action adventure game, developed by MercurySteam and published by Konami Digital Entertainment. Releasing in August 2013 on PC, Xbox 360 and PS3. The game is set in South Europe during the Middle ages. This was a reboot of the Castlevania series, where you play as Gabriel and you follow his quest to revive his wife.
Gameplay is played from a third person perspective. Your main weapon consists of a retractable chain, and you can learn up to forty different combos to use in the hack and slash combat system. As you progress through the story mode, you will learn new abilities along the way, as well as picking up new unique pieces of equipment which boast uses in both combat and non-combat situations. Gabriel will learn how to muster magical powers of light and dark. Light powers enable the player to heal any damage taken in fights by hitting enemies, whilst dark allows the player to deal extra damage. You are able to renew these magic powers by hitting a high string of attacks together without being interrupted, which will release magic orbs for you to collect. You will encounter tons of different types of enemies, from trolls, zombies, and spider’s right the way up to gigantic titans. Each enemy has their own strength and weakness which you will be able to use to your advantage.
The boss fights throughout the game are some of the most intense scenes I have played in a game. Each boss has multiple different phases of fight, each requiring you to act in a different way. The titan boss fights are long processes which normally also require an element of platforming. These can become a little bit of a pain when you first start out the game as you are still learning how to use all of the mechanics but by the last titan boss fight, it shouldn’t pose any problems for a veteran titan killing machine.
Whilst the game does have an element of platforming in a few boss fights, the game also has small amounts of platforming included throughout the story mode too. Of course jumping puzzles are always going to be my biggest enemy, and sadly they also make an appearance and are as frustrating as usual.
Graphically, Lords of Shadows is stunning; it is difficult to think that this game was released in 2013. It looks gorgeous. The cut scenes are almost a step down in graphical fidelity compared to the in game graphics. There is a huge different in how the game looks on PC compared to the consoles though. Animations throughout the game are all fluid and perfectly designed too. The sound effects are spot on, with some brilliant voice acting to be heard also from the likes of Patrick Stuart.
The game has various levels of difficulty, and you can also change them on the fly. The easy mode is essentially just a way to see the story as the combat poses no real threat. Paladin mode is the game’s hard-core mode, where enemies are more dangerous and Gabriel is significantly weaker than usual. This will add an extra layer of replay ability to a game that already boasts over twenty five hours of content. On top of the lengthy story mode, each stage also has a “trial” for you to complete as well, these can be simple tasks such as completing the stage in less than a specified amount of time, or more challenging such as not being able to use your magic’s throughout the stage.
I initially thought I would be able to play the game on 4k resolution given the age of the title, but unfortunately, I was not able to, not because my rig was not powerful enough, but because when setting the resolution to anything over 1080p, the screen in game began to flicker violently – this required a hard reboot of my system before I was able to get back into the game to change the settings back to 1080p. I would also strongly recommend people play this game on a controller; it plays perfectly on an Xbox controller and the keyboard controls would just become a huge chore to anyone regardless of their skill.
Overall, Castlevania: Lords of Shadow is an underrated title that is definitely well worth your time in checking out. The game’s price tag of £19.99 is perfectly matched at the game’s length and production values. Fans of the series will be pleased with the amount of lore and plenty of tributes to older instalments in the franchise.

Judging by how it looks and plays, I can't say that its one of the most ambitious RPG maker games out there, but it's not half-a**ed either. There's definitely plenty of interesting and customized features here that puts it above the more generic titles, so if you're into RPG Maker games but are tired of playing the same thing over and over again, then this is definitely worth a try.
It has puzzles, challenging side bosses, interesting lore, mini games and secrets to discover. Although these are no doubt great to have in games, I think the game's overall length is what kept these individual features, especially the mini games and the lore from standing out on their own since there's simply a little too much to feature in such a short game. The length also hurts what I think is an ambitious in-game lore, seeing as there are plenty of explanations given in the game but the player is given little-to-no opportunities to explore it even further through gameplay.
That's not to say that a short game is bad. It's short enough for a rainy afternoon or a lazy week end that I think none of what the game throws at the player will ever get old(besides the mining "mini game"). It's short, charming and fun, and if it were a tad longer, then I think I'll appreciate it even more.

Gabriel is a member of Brotherhood of Light who recently went through sad events - his wife was murdered. As there must be some big evil behind it, he journeys through the world to kill three lords of shadow, to kill everything evil with his holy battle cross, and to steal powers of each lord. That's all you need to know about the story, which is poor. If you read through all notes and background texts in the game, you'll be looking forward to see the depth of the unusual fantasy world on Earth (many years after our civilization has fallen), but in the real action the story just lets you cringe, as things only happen to move the plot forward without proper explanation or sense. In the end, it's all about killing evil things and keeping the decreasing faith to God.
It's a typical hack'n'slash console game (released on 2010 for consoles) with purely linear gameplay - the whole game is split into chapters and levels. While there are some parts where you can choose a path, there aren't many of those, so you'll mostly be just walking forward through corridors or climbing and jumping on the ledges (with only one right path) like in Tomb Raider series.
Many people hate the game for the fact that you can't control the camera. Every place has static camera that feels annoying and may cause some problems with controls (when you move between two scenes where the camera angle change), but I felt it's important for Castlevania's level design, as there are many secrets based on you trying to explore places where the camera isn't showing you can go, many secrets are located behind the camera. Other secrets are usually made in a way that you can't get to them in your first playthrough, as they require some late-game core item. Replayability is also encouraged by various bonus objectives, which you can see after your first playthrough of each level.
The action gameplay is enhanced with ability to mount big enemies, which is usually mandatory to move forward - e.g. you have to mount a huge spider to let him make a spider web bridge for you, or you have to mount a big troll to destroy a stone wall. Otherwise there's nothing unexpected or extra original, the game's offering classic hack'n'slash combo system with unlockable skills. Besides health, you'll be working with light and dark magic - light magic makes your attacks heal you, dark magic boosts your damage; and that's all.
There are totally 4 difficulty options, I played on the second one (similar to "normal") and the base game, 12 chapters, felt easy. The final two chapters (which are DLC content on consoles) has much bigger difficulty, especially with the final boss that took me 3 hours to beat him. Boss fights can take more than 10 minutes, but you don't have to be afraid of repeating the whole battle - there are always few checkpoints.
The game, for a console port, is optimized fine, I haven't met any critical problem through my play. Graphics are pretty for a 2010 game, there are many beautiful sceneries which motivated me to make many screenshots; there are also nice details that you'll usually see thanks to the static camera. The soundtrack is good, to describe it I'd say it's classic fantasy melodies which definitely improve the atmosphere.
If you keep your expectations low, ignore the story and just enjoy the linear hack'n'slash gameplay, Castlevania: Lords of Shadow is a fine game that can offer you about 20 hours of entertainment for a single playthrough - and if that won't be enough for you, there are more difficulty settings and many secrets.

Battles take place in real time with a cooldown bar between each action. The game has a mix of puzzle solving along with platforming at times. Although the game may have been rebalanced as of now, when I played this game, I was unable to find a spell that was crucial to beating the first boss and I thought certain enemies and bosses needed some rebalancing. I did enjoy what I played of the game though and in my opinion the universe of this game is well thought out. Most reviews talk of glitches and bugs but I never encountered a single one. Maybe I was just lucky or maybe the reviewers were lying. Who knows.
But anyway. I wanted to check out Half-Life since I got sucked into the Portal universe (and hearing that Aperture Science and Black Mesa were linked somehow) and it was recommended that I get the Source version as opposed to the original. So I did.
I actually really enjoyed the story. An experiment at Black Mesa goes wrong and it's up to silent protagonist Gordon Freeman to set it all right again. And despite being a scientist, he's a damn good shot with a gun or he'll really smart you with a crowbar. The gunplay feels good and movement is good, though sometimes jumps can be a little floaty.
I never judge a game on graphics but either way, the graphics are good for a game of this agel, and a HD retexture is included. Both sets look good but graphics do not make a game.
The gameplay itself is good and the difficulty has good progression, so you start with easier enemies and then as the game progresses, you face tougher enemies. Occasionally the difficulty can spike in places but this is usually doe to miniboss encounters, which is expected.
Either way, this was definitely a fun experience and I would highly recommend it.

I've been a player on Smite ever since March 2013 (this was around the time that the Goddess 'Aphrodite' was released).
We're now in September of 2015 and Hi-Rez has managed to get Smite released on Steam, and this extra exposure is something that they as a company wholeheartedly deserve, as the game itself ever since alpha up till now has improved massively with implementation of new Gods and patches to allow for balance changes etc. If you're not familiar with Smite but are intrigued by the look of it I recommend you at least give it a try, and who knows; you may even decide spend money on it (if you enjoy it, believe me, you'll spend).
Simply put, best MOBA out there. Try it for yourself.

Smite is not a MOBA. Smite is an real time action RPG 3rd person shooter, with MOBA elements. If you want to compare it to anything, look more at WoW PvP than DOTA. In fact, don't even go into smite looking to play the normal game mode. That's not important right now. Download, log in, do the tutorial, and go to the Arena and learn what Smite really is. The only God that Smite worships, is the almighty god of the Team Fight!
DOTA/LOL/HotS would have you believe that the mechanics of a MOBA are more important than how you play. How can you have a MOBA without Creepscore? How can major objectives be taken 5 mins into the game? Why is ganking happening every 30 deconds! Why can almost every god play almost every role!?! Every DOTA fan that I have ever met says to me the same basic bullet points to justify playing one of the isometrics. We have heard it all, and when it comes right down to it, I always say the same thing. The one thing that no one can argue no matter how hard they try that Smite has over its competition.
SMITE IS FUN.
That's it. I don't care how complex your game is. How much more skill you claim to have because you play an Isometric Moba. I don't care how complicated your item system is. None of that matters to me, unless you can have fun as well. Smite doesn't care about complexity. Its complexity is in its simplicity. Here's a god, here's his kit. Be better than your opponent. Oh your opponent is outfarming you. Outplay him. Gank in duo lane and you are on the other side of the map. 30 second walk to the other side or fly accross the sky on your chariot of fire, or crash down on them with the power of olympus. Dodge, duck, dip, dive, and♥♥♥♥♥♥♥dodge.
I, along with all the Smite playerbase, can talk about this game for years, and I am not ashamed to say that my play time is 35 days, or 840 hours, and that's nothing compared to most players that I know. Hi-Rez studios is an amazing company that is very open with its fanbase, and the SPL (smite pro league) is amazing to watch. I can't wait for SWC 2, and to see what this game has for me next.
TL;DR Download this game, Play Arena. Play god.

I can see that many people have been complaining about the performance, but I have not encountered it myself so I can offer no comment on the matter. Playing on mid-range PC I can get a solid 60 FPS  @1080p slighlty below highest settings (Set it to max, tuned down two or three options), without major hitches.
There are however some minor cases of z-fighting that I've notices, and I have seen cases where the game loaded wrong version of an object - the lo-rez, long distance version instead of the hi-rez version.

There was only one area that made my FPS drop down to 25-27ish, but it was literally the only place where that problem occured within 3 first missions. If there are more issues in the future, I'll update the review.
----
Update 1:
19 hours in, Ended missions 7 right now.
Since the initial review I have managed to finish four more missions (well, as you could probably figure out by the count). The overall performance is still stable on my system. When sandstorms are coming in, the performance tends to dip for a few seconds, but past the initial drop, it recovers quickly.
I've encountered a single audio bug (the song sung by NPCs would only play out fully when I was facing them, otherwise it'd stutter), and sometimes on game load, the world state seems to be updating in a weird way - All the guards are suddenly aware of everything that happened up to this point. Not a big deal, just need to wait a few seconds for their surprise to fade.
Still a solid game, though I personally don't like how one of the levels takes away your powers and replaces it with another mechanic, for that one level only. (It has been heavily featured in the promotion, you can probably figure it out). Having a lot of fun so far.
----
Update 2 - Final:
Just over 23 hours. That's how long it took me to finish the game - not going for 100% (but collecting most of the collectibles and side objectives), not playing completely stealthily either. To adress the most common issue - I still have not encountered any major technical issues. I cannot tell anything more about them, they just don't happen on my system. I probably just got lucky at the sillicone lottery.
What's my final opinion on the game? It was good - really good. A truly worthy successor to the original Dishonored, bringing in a bunch of new mechanics, adding variedy, building up the game world even further. The pacing of the game felt generally good, though I do have some minor complaints about the final parts of the game.
The road leading up to the final confrontation is great. The final mission itself? Weeeell... Not so much. I get what they were trying to achieve, but I think that it is slightly underwhelming, and a small change (which would work with the exact same set-up) would make the feeling feel much more satisfying. But that'd require me to directly spoil how the game ends and I will not do that.
Even with slightly underwhelming finish to the whole game, I think it is really worth your time. If you run into technical issues right now - feel free to refund the game and buy it on sale once it's been patched. That's the smart thing to do.

So, Dishonored 1 is my favourite game of all time, and I have more than 640 hours in that game, and it is wonderful how Dishonored 2 actually improves on so many areas of that game. You can knock guards out in combat, the missions are bigger and better than ever, the AI smarter than ever, the characters are more interesting, and I can spend more than 4 hours playing a single mission trying to find all the stuff in it and still be missing a lot by the end, because the missions are just so wonderfully expansive, but in all honesty I just cannot recommend the game in its current state.
The performance is just godawful, it it has no right to be. It is playable, even enjoyable, and so far I have almost 20 hours put into the game, but as much as I love the rest of the game, Arkane Studios and Bethesda both deserve a Very Negative status until they fix the game.
If you are going to get the game, you should know that there is a good chance that you will experience performance issues, so make sure to enable the FPS display (Steam>Settings>In-Game>In-game FPS counter) and pay attention to what you are actually getting. During the intro cutscene I got around 40 FPS, most areas are somewhat better than that, though with some occasional stutter, and some areas go below 20 FPS. There are also mouse issues with sensitivity being tied to the framerate for some crazy reason (that has been fixed by the beta patch). So please if you do decide to buy the game, be vigilant and consider still leaving a negative review, even if you do enjoy, because this just shouldn't be okay.
If they do fix it, then this game is definitely worth the 60 dollars/euro/whatever they are asking for, and this review will probably be changed to a hearty recommendation.
Edit: Mouse sensitivity being tied to framerate has been fixed, as of the beta patch, and the game overall seems to run much smoother (though still not quite as good as it probably should). Arkane has showed that they at least seem to care about making the game run properly.
Edit2: So with more patches it might be worth looking into. It is not going to look at good as you might like, it is not going to play as well as you might like but the gameplay is still so damned good that you might just forgive it for that. Anyway with steam refunds if it doesn't run for you, you can always get your money back.
tl;dr: Play the original Dishonored and the latter two DLCs (Knife of Dunwall and Brigmore Witches) that are both absolutely fantastic games, and cheap as a bag of chips (3 to also get the DLC). If you hunger for more Dishonored 2 is probably worth looking into and if you don't like it, you can always refund it.

cons

* scripted events involving hostiles seem to trigger wrong or not at all ( "I killed twe-RECON! GO GO!" )
* wounded NPC's yell over and over and over and over at top volume.
* Source physics on the jumping puzzles have taken them from hard to impossible.
* Got as far as blast pit, which all sneaking tension is gone and replaced by an indestructable npc shooting the creature over and over again.
Half-life (non source) is an awesome game, and it sounds like there may be a better fan-made port in the works.  But stick with the old version if you want the story, and I'm surprised Valve would let anyone curious for the mythos of Half-Life play such a buggy version. It does become a little addicting once you start playing because you start at ground zero and have to work your way out of
