Played this game since June 2012, and still play it to this day.
One of the most popular Mobas in the world. And unique in so many ways. Uses a third person camera angle that give you immersion that you can't find in other Mobas. Usable Characters are all based on Mythology, with different Pantheons being present. As of right now, there are Egyptian, Greek, Chinese, Hindu, Mayan and Norse gods in the game. All the gods have lore-friendly abilities.
Another thing that I enjoy quite a lot about this game is the lack of purchaseables that give you a competitive advantage. Take League of legends as an example. You can buy Runes with the currency, which give you an advantage against an opponent that lacks Runes. In Smite, the only thing you can buy with the free currency are gods (characters) and some skins, that are mainly re-colors of the base skin of the god. This to say that if anyone dumps a lot of cash into the game, he/she gets no advantage over someone who doesn't spend a single penny.
You get daily login rewards, and the 6th and 7th day login rewards are 15 and 35 gems, respectively. This means you can buy a regular skin if you login for 8 weeks in a row, even if you don't play a game, you can just login and collect the reward. You also get Favor (free currency) with the daily rewards, that refresh after a week. Pretty cool too.
You can also buy a pack with all the gods in the game, be it available now and in the future, with one single purchase. When I bought it, it was something like 24€, for all the characters in the game, forever. It's a pretty awesome deal, if you ask me, since whenever a new god is released, you automatically get it without spending currency.
Definetely recommend

A great contender in the growing pools of the MOBA genre, SMITE is a very fun, action-oriented multiplayer game. The camera view is over the shoulder, 3rd-person, and there are no auto attacks on right clicks like DOTA 2, every single ability excluding some abilities and ultimates have to be aimed and fired, making player skill affect gameplay much more than other MOBAs. A very easy to pick up, hard to master game that is a blast to play with friends.
It is Free to play, sustained from micro-transactions coming from buying cosmetic skins like in League of Legends, but unlike League of Legends, you can get all 70 gods, PLUS all future gods, for $30 USD, which is an amazing deal if you enjoy the game. If you don't want to invest money into the game, you can purchase gods with the in-game currency, as well as having 5 free gods, plus 5 free rotation gods every few weeks. From my experience with League of Legends, SMITE has a much more fair and valuable deal with getting gods/champions to play than the former, but that is just my opinion.
I have sunk over 1600 hours into the game since March 2013 (
)when it was in Beta, and I plan to keep playing until Hirez shuts it down, hopefully not in the immediate future. It's a MOBA that is unlike the top MOBAs at the moment, and it has a bright future. It's worth AT LEAST trying. 8.5/10

TL;DR - If you've tried other MOBAs in the past (LoL or DOTA) and didn't like them because of community or gameplay style, give Smite a shot. It's different enough with a friendly enough community to reccommend.

SOTS is quite the interesting game. With many styles and ideas, this game excels in variation. You start small and build up to becoming shogun of japan. You have to amass armies, train with the sword, train your men, and even find a wife to bear a heir to your empire as you will age and retire. You also must gain honor and land to gain favor, and this brings me to one of my favorite features. Backstabbing your rivals. You can entice riots, insult their kin to fight a duel(so you can kill them) and a few other things. Don't feel bad. They will do it to you many times in the game as well without hesitation. But get caught and you lose honor, and maybe your life.
As I said there are many styles of gameplay, they are top down action, strategy, and dueling.
They vary in quality, the strategy portion has more tactics than it seems at first. You gain men with diffrent weapons and line formations, making you have to think a bit. The action portion is also well done, you have arrows and a sword at close range to fight off groups of thugs or ninjas. It's all about positioning as you can be overwelmed quick. I find myself going to a point with few paths to limit their assault.
The duel portion is unfortunately the weakest portion. The elements are there for a great match, side swings, overheads, parries, it's just the A.I isn't very good. They always fall for an overhead charge thats unblockable. Even on harder difficulties they only seem more aggressive, as there defense is still lacking.

The controls were an issue at first, as all of these styles of gameplay require different button imputs. But plug in a controller and it's much better. The graphics are very dated. There is a style being done with japan influences and it helps a lot. But realize it's not going to blow you away. This goes for the sound too.Dated but with a style that really helps.
You will reach a point where you will take lands from other rivals and it's well done. You need to take territories without attacking those with larger armies(until you build yours up at least) and your command of men will be tested at full here. The ending is also cool, as your ending varies on many factors like your land amount and honor. You could have no more than five years of rule if you jumped the gun on becoming shogun. Or if you play your cards right, it could last a century.

Played this game since June 2012, and still play it to this day.
One of the most popular Mobas in the world. And unique in so many ways. Uses a third person camera angle that give you immersion that you can't find in other Mobas. Usable Characters are all based on Mythology, with different Pantheons being present. As of right now, there are Egyptian, Greek, Chinese, Hindu, Mayan and Norse gods in the game. All the gods have lore-friendly abilities.
Another thing that I enjoy quite a lot about this game is the lack of purchaseables that give you a competitive advantage. Take League of legends as an example. You can buy Runes with the currency, which give you an advantage against an opponent that lacks Runes. In Smite, the only thing you can buy with the free currency are gods (characters) and some skins, that are mainly re-colors of the base skin of the god. This to say that if anyone dumps a lot of cash into the game, he/she gets no advantage over someone who doesn't spend a single penny.
You get daily login rewards, and the 6th and 7th day login rewards are 15 and 35 gems, respectively. This means you can buy a regular skin if you login for 8 weeks in a row, even if you don't play a game, you can just login and collect the reward. You also get Favor (free currency) with the daily rewards, that refresh after a week. Pretty cool too.
You can also buy a pack with all the gods in the game, be it available now and in the future, with one single purchase. When I bought it, it was something like 24€, for all the characters in the game, forever. It's a pretty awesome deal, if you ask me, since whenever a new god is released, you automatically get it without spending currency.
Definetely recommend

UPDATE:
I managed to find a workaround for the FPS, and the game is now playable, albeit at 60 locked fps, it works, with a few crashes throughout the story (was a certain point in the game which crashed a lot, seems to be related to msi gaming app however, after removing that, no crashes).
How to get 'maximum' fps from reddit credit to: \u\Ikarostv
First: I went into my NVIDIA Control Panel and set the "Max Pre-Rendered Frames = 1" Honestly not sure if this helps or not, because it never really did when this was the ONLY fix that I put in.
Second: Go on into NVIDIA Inspector. Open up the Profile for Dishonored 2. Since the game doesn't have an FPS Cap built in - go to FRAME RATE LIMITER and set this to 61.8 (odd choice, but shows less stutter for myself).
Third: This one I haven't heard mentioned other than people getting black screens with an Ansel error. So, scroll down and find ENABLE ANSEL and set this to ANSEL_ENABLE_OFF. This will eliminate any potential threat of this thing effecting us. NVIDIA Ansel is basically their fancy internal 3D Screenshot program. Not really needed right now as a "must".
Fourth: You can go ahead and download Process Lasso or Process Hacker 2 - either or. The game for most is set to LOW Priority for your CPU. With these programs, you can lock it to HIGH. This is netting anywhere from 10-30FPS gains for people. For myself, the game is running on Normal and setting to High actually made it worse personally. Very odd.
Fifth: Head on over to C:\Users\NAME\Saved Games\Arkane Studios\Dishonored2\Base\Dishonored2Config.cfg - Now I want you go head to g_mouseSmooth "1" - set the "1" to "0". This will ACTUALLY turn off Mouse Smoothing in the game. Whether it's set to 0 or not in the game options, doesn't matter unfortunately. Afterwards - right click on that .CFG File after it's saved - go to PROPERTIES and then set to READ-ONLY. Otherwise the game will overwrite the setting.

Just completed my first playthrough as emily high chaos. She seems to be the better fight for high chaos runs.
The game is fun, the lore and story is deep and interesting to read about, all the little bits in the game, such as if you use the heart to find oout if a normal civilian is a good little boy/girl or if they're secretly naughty is a fun addon. I used that to decide wether a person lives or dies. It upped the immersion quite a bit.
From a gameplay standpoint, emilys powers are fun, and brutal. The way she pulls herself forward instead of blinking made approaching certain situation differently as you'll be spotted if you traverse across enemies FoV. That is, unless you find a bonecharm which makes you invisible while traversing the land with far reach.
The world:
It works just as well as in the first dishonor. It's "open world" you get sent to a map, then you're free to choose what to do, and how to approach objectives. There's a lot of♥♥♥♥♥♥to explore, I keep getting side-tracked and without meaning to finding ways to pacify targets rather than killing them, just by exploring and not by intention, which is a good thing.
The game actively promotes exploration as you find various upgrades (albeit they are not needed, but adds some more fun to your arsenal) and runes/bonecharms just as before.
I advice everyone to pick up bonecharm crafting, it means that you can craft one bonecharm to have multiple effects, if you add a lot into this passive power, you can have bonecharms that grant you 4 effects, which is pretty ballin.
The story:
Overall story is great, couldn't tear my ear from listening to all of it, with added bonus from random NPCs in the world who talk, give you tidbits of information, some that you can use to your gain. (Hidden safes, weakneses, entrances) and the likes. Which makes taking your time to actually understand the story and listen to NPCs rewarding.
The ending, I must say is rather lackluster, might be because of my high chaos run, guess I'll see how my low chaos run is. Then again, it probably comes with, the fact that there are multiple endings, they might've chosen that there isn't too much to it.
Would I recommend this game?
Yes, definitely.
However, I still advice you to wait, the game is fun, it has a good story, and replayability just as the first, seeing as you can approach everything the way you choose, which in the end leads to another ending, makes it worth playing several times.
But the topmost information of this review is still relevant, the game has yet to be patched, I'll likely update this happens to give some thought on performance.
If you cannot wait, there are workarounds that might fix your FPS.
Hope some people benefit from this. And thanks again \u\Ikarostv for the workaround which made the game playable.

This is an amazing game that really should get some more honors or awards for its outstanding qualities. Every aspect of the game is just done so well.
ENEMIES
This game has one of the most interesting and challenging set of enemies that you'll ever encounter. The monsters know how to fight and have an arsenal of moves that will keep you on your toes. They are beautifully animated, and there are a ton of different creatures and monsters to encounter.
COMBAT
Combat is a total blast. There are many combos to learn, with a huge variety of cool moves that lead to fun combat, which also requires good combo skills to master. There are no pushover fights, and from the very start you will have some challenging and epic battles. You can also dodge, block, and use special powers.
MAPS
There are alot of maps to go through, and they are exquisityly designed and detailed. Everything is beautifully rendered, and a pleasure to look at. The settings are unique and interesting, and you will go through many different environments as you go through the story.
STORY
The story is interesting, and keeps you motivated throughout. The story is narrated by some great voice acting.
PLATFORMING
In certain situations, your character will need to jump, run, dodge, wade, climb, grapple, and smash his way through various areas. You can even capture beasts and have them smash doors or climb up walls with you riding them! It just adds to the fun!
PUZZLES
You will encounter puzzles now and again, and they offer a good challenge and will test your wits.
CONCLUSION
This is how games should be made. Fun, challenging, great combat, tough enemies, epic encounters, beautiful visuals, interesting mechanics. I can go on and on. BUY IT TODAY!!

As a simple rule: don't use a cutscene to do something that can be done with the player still in control of the character. If you think the player may need to notice something, like the path forward, then map a button to "focus" so they won't get lost. Spending 10-20 seconds or more out of every minute pointing me in the direction that I'm already going is just wasting my time and kind of insulting. I want so, so, SO badly to like this game, because I'm interested in the story and the sequels. But it's just not good. The presentation and lore is great, but the gameplay is PAINFULLY mediocre. I'm talking mind numbingly boring.  I'm torn between putting the game away for a time when I find myself without internet or a job (having time to kill) or just YouTubing the cutscenes and moving on to the sequel.
Pros:
-Amazing visuals. It's almost at the level of Trine 2, which was a 2D game.
-Interesting lore. Avenging love lost. Gothic theme. Dracula's origin story. I'm not versed in Castlevanie lore but this seems like a fine reboot of it.
-All-Star voice acting. Enough said.
-Journal offers bits of lore via beastiary entries and equipment descriptions, etc.
-*Seemingly* long. My playtime shows the time it took to clear chapter 1. From the map screen, it seems like there's at least 9 chapters.
-Out of absolutely nowhere, a little fairy appeared and showed me her boobs. This pleased me greatly.
Cons:
-Lacking soundscaping. The level of audio detail does not match the visual detail. For example, a big titan crushing it's fist into solid ice has no crunch to it, just a weak *whomp*.
-Linear level design. Every level is a corridor. No, seriously. It's like Crash Bandicoot. I'm not kidding you. You have branching "Y" paths that later rejoin to the same area. Just like in Crash Bandicoot.
-Simple combat. It's skill based character action, but it lacks nuance. It's not bad, but it's a total bore.
-Simple platforming. Think Prince of Persia: Sands of Time, but dumbed down for 6 year olds.
-Clunky controls. The game never stops showing what button you need to press to do what. The problem is that it does it for good reason. You aren't taught the basic scheme of the game via repetition. Buttons do unique things at every turn that you would have too much difficulty figuring out on your own. Climb on a big boss's arm. Hit the gem with "B". It's stupid that the game's still showing me tutorials, yet I'm grateful because I probably would have been lost as to what the game needs me to do. I didn't know I'm climbing to the gem to hit it. Ugh...
It's just a stupidly bland game. Most of all, it doesn't feel at all like Castlevania 1. You know what does feel like Castlevania 1? Dark Souls. Go play that instead.

Primitive game by 2017, somewhat dated even on release in 1989.  That said, the core concept and game there is fascinating, to say the least.  You're a low level samurai warrio making your way up to daimyo and, eventually, united Japan under single clan rule.  The game is broken up into two halves, the first being you living in a homestead, overruling a feif of rice tillers.  You can do things like raise taxes and raise troops, practice your swordsmanship in a primitive 1v1 fighting minigame, and send your troops to play war games in a fairly shallow real-time strategy sim that is somewhat easy to manipulate and light on options.
Or you can choose to leave your home.  You have options here as well.  Leave with your army to court women at your peers or your local over rulers aboad or respond to calls to military action or heroic deeds.  Of you can set off at the risk of being alone but recognized and attacked in an attempt to gain notoriety.  These minigames give you more "honor points", which let you rise up in your social circle.  You can challenge your peers to a duel to play the aforementioned 1v1 minigame.  Finally you can shoose to venture out as an obscure and unknown ronin which allows you to commit espionage against your peers.  This is a third minigame, an over the head action RPG-ish mode where you either swing your sword or shoot a bow.  You enter this mini game while in the field to, say, repell some bandits attacking a village, or while traveling to your enemy's home to wait for nightfall.  Espionage against the AI lets you do things like assassinate esteemed guests, plant stolen heirlooms, kidnap members of the house to hold ransom or, ultimately, assassination of the head of the house hold.
Ultimately the game is juggling gaining of enough honor points, recruiting soldiers, and correctly raiding or assassinating your enemy.  The system itself is shallow yet satisfying.
This game would really transfer to a fleshed out and in depth game if it were taken on by a modern day team with proper development.

Geometry Wars 3 is a twin stick shooter, which is a genre that I have to admit I'm not very experienced with. I played the original on Xbox 360 but that's about it, so I can't really compare the mechanics to other games, but I've mostly enjoyed my time with GW3 so far.
Its quite a simple game, with no story to speak of. The player controls some kind of spaceship and has to shoot a variety of differently coloured enemies while trying to earn a high score. Destroyed enemies will leave behind "geoms" which can be collected to increase the score multiplier. You die instantly if anything touches you and there are usually dozens of enemies on screen at a time, so its all about learning the movement pattern and speed of each enemy type, to avoid them.
There are 50 levels in adventure mode, which give you star ratings based on your score. Bosses are locked until you earn enough stars on previous levels, which normally I would consider to be a cheap way of extending a game, but GW3 gets away with it because most levels only last 2-3 minutes so replaying them isn't a massive inconvenience. There are also 5 "classic" modes that only have 1 map each, so their only goal is to set a high score.
The controls are designed to work best with a gamepad, so I used my 360 controller. You move with left stick and aim with right stick, and have super weapons on the two triggers which can be used a couple of times per level. You've got a supernova that instantly destroys everything on screen, and one other which the player chooses from a range of options. I liked the homing missiles because when the action gets really crazy, I didn't want to worry about aiming. I tried the mines and black hole but didn't really find a good use for them.
You can also choose between several drones that fly around and help you. The attack drone shoots enemies, and is useful when you need a bit of extra firepower, but I mostly used the drone that automatically collects geoms because the score multiplier is absolutely essential for earning stars.
The big feature for GW3 is the 3D design of the levels. While it looks impressive, it can sometimes have a negative impact on the gameplay. What I found is that many enemies spawn in places I couldn't see, so on small maps, fast moving enemies could kill me before I could react, and on large maps that have a time limit, hunting for an unseen enemy wastes valuable seconds.
The music is a good match for the fast paced action and I didn't notice any major bugs. Value for money is good. I finished the adventure mode in around 8 hours, and genre fans could probably spend countless more hours chasing high scores on the leaderboards for every map. And just before I was ready to post this review I've seen an article on IGN saying more levels will be released as a free update towards the end of March.
Overall I think Geometry Wars 3 is a pretty good game, and worth checking out if you're in the mood to just turn off your brain, relax, and shoot stuff.

UPDATE:
I managed to find a workaround for the FPS, and the game is now playable, albeit at 60 locked fps, it works, with a few crashes throughout the story (was a certain point in the game which crashed a lot, seems to be related to msi gaming app however, after removing that, no crashes).
How to get 'maximum' fps from reddit credit to: \u\Ikarostv
First: I went into my NVIDIA Control Panel and set the "Max Pre-Rendered Frames = 1" Honestly not sure if this helps or not, because it never really did when this was the ONLY fix that I put in.
Second: Go on into NVIDIA Inspector. Open up the Profile for Dishonored 2. Since the game doesn't have an FPS Cap built in - go to FRAME RATE LIMITER and set this to 61.8 (odd choice, but shows less stutter for myself).
Third: This one I haven't heard mentioned other than people getting black screens with an Ansel error. So, scroll down and find ENABLE ANSEL and set this to ANSEL_ENABLE_OFF. This will eliminate any potential threat of this thing effecting us. NVIDIA Ansel is basically their fancy internal 3D Screenshot program. Not really needed right now as a "must".
Fourth: You can go ahead and download Process Lasso or Process Hacker 2 - either or. The game for most is set to LOW Priority for your CPU. With these programs, you can lock it to HIGH. This is netting anywhere from 10-30FPS gains for people. For myself, the game is running on Normal and setting to High actually made it worse personally. Very odd.
Fifth: Head on over to C:\Users\NAME\Saved Games\Arkane Studios\Dishonored2\Base\Dishonored2Config.cfg - Now I want you go head to g_mouseSmooth "1" - set the "1" to "0". This will ACTUALLY turn off Mouse Smoothing in the game. Whether it's set to 0 or not in the game options, doesn't matter unfortunately. Afterwards - right click on that .CFG File after it's saved - go to PROPERTIES and then set to READ-ONLY. Otherwise the game will overwrite the setting.

Just completed my first playthrough as emily high chaos. She seems to be the better fight for high chaos runs.
The game is fun, the lore and story is deep and interesting to read about, all the little bits in the game, such as if you use the heart to find oout if a normal civilian is a good little boy/girl or if they're secretly naughty is a fun addon. I used that to decide wether a person lives or dies. It upped the immersion quite a bit.
From a gameplay standpoint, emilys powers are fun, and brutal. The way she pulls herself forward instead of blinking made approaching certain situation differently as you'll be spotted if you traverse across enemies FoV. That is, unless you find a bonecharm which makes you invisible while traversing the land with far reach.
The world:
It works just as well as in the first dishonor. It's "open world" you get sent to a map, then you're free to choose what to do, and how to approach objectives. There's a lot of♥♥♥♥♥♥to explore, I keep getting side-tracked and without meaning to finding ways to pacify targets rather than killing them, just by exploring and not by intention, which is a good thing.
The game actively promotes exploration as you find various upgrades (albeit they are not needed, but adds some more fun to your arsenal) and runes/bonecharms just as before.
I advice everyone to pick up bonecharm crafting, it means that you can craft one bonecharm to have multiple effects, if you add a lot into this passive power, you can have bonecharms that grant you 4 effects, which is pretty ballin.
The story:
Overall story is great, couldn't tear my ear from listening to all of it, with added bonus from random NPCs in the world who talk, give you tidbits of information, some that you can use to your gain. (Hidden safes, weakneses, entrances) and the likes. Which makes taking your time to actually understand the story and listen to NPCs rewarding.
The ending, I must say is rather lackluster, might be because of my high chaos run, guess I'll see how my low chaos run is. Then again, it probably comes with, the fact that there are multiple endings, they might've chosen that there isn't too much to it.
Would I recommend this game?
Yes, definitely.
However, I still advice you to wait, the game is fun, it has a good story, and replayability just as the first, seeing as you can approach everything the way you choose, which in the end leads to another ending, makes it worth playing several times.
But the topmost information of this review is still relevant, the game has yet to be patched, I'll likely update this happens to give some thought on performance.

Played this game since June 2012, and still play it to this day.
One of the most popular Mobas in the world. And unique in so many ways. Uses a third person camera angle that give you immersion that you can't find in other Mobas. Usable Characters are all based on Mythology, with different Pantheons being present. As of right now, there are Egyptian, Greek, Chinese, Hindu, Mayan and Norse gods in the game. All the gods have lore-friendly abilities.
Another thing that I enjoy quite a lot about this game is the lack of purchaseables that give you a competitive advantage. Take League of legends as an example. You can buy Runes with the currency, which give you an advantage against an opponent that lacks Runes. In Smite, the only thing you can buy with the free currency are gods (characters) and some skins, that are mainly re-colors of the base skin of the god. This to say that if anyone dumps a lot of cash into the game, he/she gets no advantage over someone who doesn't spend a single penny.
You get daily login rewards, and the 6th and 7th day login rewards are 15 and 35 gems, respectively. This means you can buy a regular skin if you login for 8 weeks in a row, even if you don't play a game, you can just login and collect the reward. You also get Favor (free currency) with the daily rewards, that refresh after a week. Pretty cool too.
You can also buy a pack with all the gods in the game, be it available now and in the future, with one single purchase. When I bought it, it was something like 24€, for all the characters in the game, forever. It's a pretty awesome deal, if you ask me, since whenever a new god is released, you automatically get it without spending currency.
Definetely recommend

A small game I bought months back when it was still on Desura. I was intrigued by the unique game play and I definitely got my moneys worth.
The game offers a unique "tower defense" like experience where one faction is trying to help their giant shark monster to the center of the city while another faction works against them. It’s a neat and enjoyable experience, especially when you experience the wacky flight physics of the fighter jets...provided you can get a good game running.
At the time of writing this, the population playing this game is almost nonexistent. It's been like that for awhile and that's a real shame. There was an explosion of players back when the game was new and there seemed to have been a jump in popularity when Youtubers like Nerd Cubed show cased the game.
One problem I have with this game is that it's a couple years old now and it lacks any sort of major updates. It's a simple, one level game with a generous map, sure, but part of the reason I stopped playing is there wasn't much else to do in the game. And I fear that’s one major reason why most stopped playing as well.
The major drawback is there are balancing issues. Teams are not managed to be fair. Sure, sometimes you get into matches where no one wants to fight Omegalodon, they just want to run around and blow stuff up, do their own thing. However, when one finally does decide to play the game like it’s designed to, there’s no way to balance the teams out for a fair match.
Often you’ll have one rambunctious newbie jump into the limelight and run around as Omegalodon with no supporting players to keep his health up. So he walks slowly down one track of the map until his life slowly drains to zero, allowing the slightest breeze to kill him. Once dead, it stops everyone else dead in their tracks and the round is reset. This can get rather annoying after the fiftieth reset and you just want to fly around in a jet for fun.
So overall, I would say it was a good game back when it was still new, but right now it’s mostly just a game gathering dust in my library. Occasionally I will jump into it and try to find a match, but often I’m not so lucky or don’t play it long.

A great contender in the growing pools of the MOBA genre, SMITE is a very fun, action-oriented multiplayer game. The camera view is over the shoulder, 3rd-person, and there are no auto attacks on right clicks like DOTA 2, every single ability excluding some abilities and ultimates have to be aimed and fired, making player skill affect gameplay much more than other MOBAs. A very easy to pick up, hard to master game that is a blast to play with friends.
It is Free to play, sustained from micro-transactions coming from buying cosmetic skins like in League of Legends, but unlike League of Legends, you can get all 70 gods, PLUS all future gods, for $30 USD, which is an amazing deal if you enjoy the game. If you don't want to invest money into the game, you can purchase gods with the in-game currency, as well as having 5 free gods, plus 5 free rotation gods every few weeks. From my experience with League of Legends, SMITE has a much more fair and valuable deal with getting gods/champions to play than the former, but that is just my opinion.
I have sunk over 1600 hours into the game since March 2013 (
)when it was in Beta, and I plan to keep playing until Hirez shuts it down, hopefully not in the immediate future. It's a MOBA that is unlike the top MOBAs at the moment, and it has a bright future. It's worth AT LEAST trying. 8.5/10

TL;DR - If you've tried other MOBAs in the past (LoL or DOTA) and didn't like them because of community or gameplay style, give Smite a shot. It's different enough with a friendly enough community to reccommend.

I don't normally recommend Early Release titles. Ususally, they're a relatively incomplete experience, or at least not worth the price of entry. And while I won't call Broforce a complete title by any means, it certainly seems to be well on its way, far better than many of its early release brethren. It is a simplistic, yet surprisingly interesting 2D shooter that can be equal parts blind run-n'-gun or clever pseudo-stealth platformer (don't let that title fool you though, there's still plenty of bloodshed.) You assume the role of numerous non-copyrighted action movie bros as you seek to liberate the world of evil. With guns, bombs, lasers, and anything else within arm's reach. But, that's enough summary, here's the key information.
First, some caveats. The only (for practical purposes) complete portion is the solo campaign. But, that can seem misleading. There are other facets, custom maps, test maps (if you're one to delve into such content), a fair amount of community maps, and even the new (at the time of reviewing) campaign map work better than the touted features of some "officially released" titles. However, there are issues. The networking, in particular, can be nightmarish. In my testing instances, my buddy and I requently lagged out, before eventually disconnecting, despite being quite literally 6 ft. away from each other. If you want co-op, I highly recommend doing it locally, on the same system. Using one player on a gamepad and one on the keyboard can work, or two gamepads, et cetera, whatever's comfortable.
Now, the stuff that works. And, there's actually a surprising amount of it. As mentioned earlier, most of the single-player content's pretty playable. As for control, both keyboard & mouse and gamepads are supported (I used a wired Xbox 360 Controller to test gamepad fuctionality), and both are workable. Some may prefer a gamepad, but once you get the hang of the controls, keyboard and mouse can be just as precise and enjoyable. Lastly, the characters/updates. There's a pretty large cast of characters considering this game's in beta, and even more are slated for release. From the simple Rambro to the "aghluaghla" -spouting Bronan, it's pretty interesting watching these various heroes tearing through terrorists. One minor dent, however, is the random nature you get these bros. Outside of the one time you initially unlock them, the bro you play as is always randomly selected. This can lead to difficulty, as some of the bros are simply either more useful in certain areas, or more useful as a whole. Being able to select a pre-set squad of five-or-so bros to always cycle through in a stage, or even the option to play as one bro only, would be nice, at least in single-player games.
To finally wrap this thing up, the real question: should you buy beta Broforce? As much as a cop out as it may sound: it's really a matter of personal taste. If you're a thrifty shopper, or only have a passing interest in run-n'-gun/retro-simplistic style games (think Hotline Miami), you may want to wait until this game goes on sale, likely at the time of full release. But, if you've seen the gameplay, seen the trailers, and like what this game is going for, then supporting the devs and getting your hands on this title early may make a bro of you yet.

This game has definitely held up to my expectations! I've played a lot of the first game over both my PS3 and PC and now I've already stacked up over 100 hours on the PS3 version of this game, and am only just starting with the PC.
Some Pro's:
-It's easier for beginners to get into, with an in depth tutorial that is easily skippable.
-Dedicated servers make it easier to engage in Jolly Cooperation!
-Keeps to the original games difficulty level, I've had my fair share of deaths.
-Arena mode for PvP seperate from Invasions.
-Multiple Paths from the beginning to choose how you want to go through the game.
-The Graphics are stunning; I always find myself stopping to admire the scenery.
-Amazing story and Lore
-Still a lot of replay value, even after beating the game. It only gets harder :)
-PvP is still a great time, despite a few issues...
-Dual Blading has been improved immensly with many new mechanics.
The Cons:
-Summoning and PvP Still Run off P2P connection, leading to lag and phantom stabs and lag stabs, it can be pretty harsh.
-Soul Memory, it isn't a big deal, but it can make it a lot harder to do co-op with one of your friends.
-The game seems more focused around you, instead of the world you play in. The NPC's are a bit stale but still have lore to them. (Other then Gavlan, for no other can Wheel and Deal like he does)
-In order to level up you have to go through the same 4 lines of dialogue, it gets annoying.
-You have to spam play arena mode in order to get Cracked eye orbs (Blue or Red) or by them for 10k souls, which can be ridiculous. They also removed the Red and Blue Eye Orb that gave you infinite invades.
Overall this game is absolutely amazing and I can't stop playing it, and neither should you. And you're sitting there like "But Condi, I don't own this beautiful game, what do?" Then go steal your moms credit card or something, because you NEED this game. It's like being that one guy sitting there envious of those kids at school who go outside during lunch and praise it, but you can't join them because you're a casul and didn't praise hard enough in the first place. God damn it man you have to praise harder if you wanna get anywhere in life.
TL;DR Get this game, it holds up to the standards of Dark Souls 1, and is amazingly fun as always!

Great Game with some serious issues holding it back.
The Good
-Solid fps and next to no stutter even in the more intense areas (2 boss fights that shall remain nameless dipped down into the low 50s/high 40s for a bit)
-All the tweaking options you would expect from a PC game
-Much higher texture resolution than console
-Great art Direction and solid atmosphere
-did I mention how great it performs because DS1 was abysmal
-Combat feels meaty
-Boss fights are for the most part (see The Bad) challenging but not overly difficult
-Most enemys, even in groups, are fairly easy to fight (you can learn their attack patterns and counter them farly easily)
The Bad
-While higher that console the texture res (specifically environmental) is fairly low and quite blocky.
-Skyboxes and distant scenery look HORRIBLE (I'm lookng at you, Heids Tower of Flame)
-Some ares have noticable frame drops, nothing serious though
-There are certain enemys *cough*zombie dogs*cough* that have broken attack animations, in otherwards you are hit before the attack animation plays (Zombie Dogs (big red ones, not black ones) Petrify rats, and in some cases the Heide Knights are some frequently encoutered offenders)
__
--[[ Really Bad ]]--
-Spell casting/ranged enemys are broken, like crazy broken
Spell casters at the moment have increadibly long agro range and have very broken played tracking mechanics. I have on many occasions ran around corners and had spells do full 180' turns to follow me. This makes a certain water filled are more difficult that it should be due to a mass of spell casters, large open areas, and movment inhibiting deep water
-NPC red and black phantoms
At the moment NPC phantom have increadible health and defence, near limitless stamina, and instant recoveries leading to what I have dubbed the relentless attack. NPC phantoms currently have the abbility to attack through staggers and shield breaks with about 1.5x the attack speed of a player character. This can lead to, in the case of Havel and Greatsword phantoms attacking with the speed of a longsword and the power of a Dragons Tooth/Ultra Greatsword with next to no recovery time between attacks.

I never could get into MOBAs until I tried Smite, I've played Heroes of the Storm, League of Legends, and a very small amount of dota 2. The main thing that I did not like is the isometric viewpoint, as well as the click to move aspect of the traditional MOBA. Smite Fixed all of the that, when you auto attack someone it's not you just clicking on them and the attack auto hitting them no matter what, In Smite it's a skill shot that they can dodge the same principle applies to most abilities.
You start off with 5 base gods for free + another 5 on rotation.
You can buy more gods via in game credits you earn buy playing and leveling up, purchase them with real money individually with gems, or get the ultimate god pack it's $30 and gives you every god in the game as well as every feature god if you plan on playing as lot of smite it's definitely worth it. The community is amazing for a MOBA.
The main con I can think of is the servers. I live 2 hours away from LA CA and always have over 100 ping normally 120 ish.
Some tips for new players.
Buy beads! You will hear this, a lot in arena it means you should buy Purification Beads from the store it's a cheap on use item that gives you CC immunity when used. As long as you have the auto buy on it should buy them for you.
Yes there is last hitting no there is no denying.
Learn some basic VGS commands
Don't worry about item builds at first. The game will auto buy a basic build for you (you can turn this off at the lobby screen before you enter a match) I recommend to play arena until you get the hang of the base gods.
The traditional MOBA map is called Conquest there is no bottom or top but long/duo lane for ADC and Support you can tell what lane this is because the towers will be farther apart and it will be the side with the gold fury, Then mid normally played by a Mage and solo/short lane normally played by a Warrior (or any god with good clear and sustain) this will always be on the side of the Fire Giant and will be either top or bottom depending if your home is the chaos or order side. Jungler will start off farming lane with solo lane (aka short lane)
If you have any questions ask in the comments and I'll try and answer as soon as I am able.
Finally! Now, to sync those achievments...

TL;DR: There are so many other games available now, play a different "competitive" shooter.
The Good:
• The gunplay is good for a third person shooter, winning is EXTREMELY satisfying
• The game has the BEST character customization out of any game I have played EVER
• Customization extends to cars and graffiti which you can tag around the map(a novelty feature)
• Open map everyone in a server plays on to complete missions
• Genuinely fun events every once in a while that shake things up
The Bad:
• Random blatant hackers who are able to play before hours(!) before being removed from the game
• Open nature of map allows players outside your mission to grief and help other team (example: crashing into your car multiple times so you can't reach mission objective)
• Mission placement and map balance is generally poor, MUCH better than release, but still not great
• Low player count, you'll be stuck playing against the same people over and over
• Poor MM, pretty much caused by low player count, mostly long time players are left and if you are new, you might have a hard time enjoying the game (tried getting my best bud to play once, he said nope, $*% this lol)
It's not a terrible game, but with all the other games available now, why would you play it? I'll admit the customization is the best ever, but it doesn't trump the boring missions, equipment grind, low player count, and mangled gameplay on the open map.

I don't think that all the hate on this game is unfounded. It is certainly a title that exists in a long line of games widely hated by PC players. This is the game's main disadvantage, in my opinion. Call of Duty: Advanced Warfare finally brings something new to the table for the series, and much like Black Ops 2 with its competitive oriented play style, people still don't like it.

The pick 13 system is awesome; letting me pick more attachments and perks in one class and better scorestreaks in another makes me a very versatile combatant on maps where the fast and the skilled dominate.
Tl;dr - give the game a chance before you sideline it. It impressed me in a way that a first person shooter hasn't for a very long time.

So just finished my first playthrough of this game and thought I should do a review of my thoughts overall. Obviously the first thing to note is the optimisation issues. There are issues indeed and many people are having frame rate drops including myself, but these issues are not as serious for a fair amount of people. The developers have stated they are working on a patch, so maybe hold off on getting the game for the next few days while we wait for these issues to hopefully get fixed.
Now onto my thoughts of the game, and I have to say, I love this game! Never was very interested in Dishonored, but thought I would get Dishonored 2 since pre-ordering also gave me the first game to try. Dishonored 2 has an amazing story which can branch different ways and give different endings depending upon which character you choose and how you approach each situation during the game. Having two different characters that do play fairly differently is a great aspect of this game too. There are many different weapons and abilities which you can use and upgrade to better your experiance through the game, all with different purposes. I especially enjoyed using the rat ability to consume my enemies. The game has a nice atmosphere and a lot to do. You can search for runes, bonecharms, materials to craft bonecharms and eaven recipes to upgrade your weaponry. I hardly scratched the surface of content within this game and plan to playthrough the game again.
Overall, I say do not be fooled my the mixed reviews. The game has some optimisation issues, but if you are willing to look past them and wait for the developers to (hopefully) fix them, you can see an amazing game that could be Game of the Year material.

As someone who has never played the old Castlevania games I went blind to Lords of Shadow. I didn’t knew anything about the story other than that it involved vampires. The only thing that made me buy the game in the first place was the huge amount of positive reviews. And, like I usually do, I waited until I got the other two Castlevania games on Steam to start playing the first one. A few hours into the game, I was having a blast.
From top notch music to gorgeous and memorable locations such as forests, gothic castles, desert lands and ruins from an old civilization, this game has it all. Combined witha fast paced action combat (with tons of unlockable combos) this made for quite the epic experience. Although enemy variety was somewhat lacking, certain locaitons had a specific set of enemies assigned to it, thus making it harder to forget those zones. As for the gameplay itself, as I mentioned before, it is quite fast paced. You have to adapt to changes in the enemy behavior, aswell as bosses, and use a variety of attacks to effectively defeat your foes.
The game itself is rather long, taking around 20-22 hours to play it through, which was rather a surprise for me. Of course, for all the completionists and collectible hunters out there, Lords of Shadow also has something in store for you. The game is divided in 12 chapters (+2 chapters corresponding to the DLC included in the Ultimate Edition), and each of those chapters is subsequently divided into several stages. It is in these stages that you’ll be able to explore and collect scrolls containing letters from fallen brethren of the Brootherhood of Light, and you’ll also be able to find gems that enhance your abilities. And if you’re into bigger challenges, you can try completing Trials for said stages which, I believe, reward you with an achievement. So yeah, not only the game is a blast on its foundations, but it also rewards exploration, which, in my book, is always a plus.
Now, enough talking about all the good things this game has, and lets talk about my only gripe with the game, the controls, or perhaps my terrible skills at precision platforming in a 3D game. I swear that sometimes the game just made me want to shove the controller through my monitor (anger issues perhaps?). Very rare were these situations, but they were infuriating when they occurred. I honestly can’t tell you if it was an issue with the controls, like the inability to control with precisio where you want to land or if I’m just really bad at jumping from platform to platform in a 3D game.
That said, I can’t recommend this game enough. It is an epic journey through some amazing landscapes and it has one of the most insane and thrilling soundtracks I’ve ever heard on a videogame. Please, do yourself a favour and do not keep Lords of Shadow on your backlog.
I hope these words accomplish my intended goal, which was raising awareness for a series that I feel that went under the radar for alot of PC gamers. Or perhaps that is just me, afterall, I have never played the old Castlevania games and I only played this one three years after its release, maybe that’s why.
PS: Sorry for the wall of text.

Many might criticize this game for having such old school graphics, but it dosen't matter. Despite being a little dated what is impressive about this game is how it managed create a depth of character for the player.
I thought the game well executed the experience of starting of as a local landord samurai who eventually ascends through ranks and later become capable of uniting Japan as Shogun. During this ascention there is plently of opportunities to display your might as a Samurai by crushing bandits, rescuing damsels, stopping assassinations, preventing kidnapping of your own family members, winning numerous duels, and winning numerous battles in the war for Japan. All the while you have to manage to rival clan members who also aspire to become daimyo or even shogun while also ensuring that your heirs are safe and capable of taking your place when you retire and thus can continue the campaign.
I must say for an old game, it did a really great job of immersing the player into the role of a samurai lord, what with the many adventures, risks, and responsibilities that becoming a shogun entails.
Do not let the graphics make you shy away from this game. Its still a worth while experience once you get into it.
I must say it is a shame that this game didn't get a modern remake. In fact i would say that if a game like this took its original immersive experience, and employed the graphics and fighting style like that of Mount and Blade, also managed a politics and dynastic experience similar to Crusader Kings II, and just maybe tried to employ some of the battle styles of Total War, then we got oursleves a really good samurai game right there.
Ahh heck, in all likelyness such a fantasy might not happen, if anything if we are lucky, Mount and Blade bannerlord might inspire a really good mod instead.

IMPORTANT NOTICE TO PEOPLE WANTING TO BUY THIS GAME:
DO NOT BUY THIS GAME! DO NOT AND DO NOT BUY IT WITH THE DLC CONTENT!!! THERE IS A NEW GAME COMING WITH ALL THE DLC AND GAME!!!!!
The Dark Souls Franchise have always captured me knowing every single bit of detail about the game, but this game is not something what I expected (in a good and bad way.)
Let me first introduce the positives and negatives throughout this game:
POSITIVE: The Content is outstanding!!!!!! There are mini-bosses after mini-bosses and the world is massive which is a treasure-cove of awesomness! I have clocked 45 hours of this game and I still think I have a long way to go. In each area, you are stopped possibly by a door that needs to be opened. It is ok, you can move on to another area where you can continue exploring, which is suppose to be Dark Souls main objective: "making" you explore other areas rather than the specified path. By using this objective, the game is not linear, it is an "open-world". If every game would follow this method, it will leave an insurmountable time of fun!
POSITIVE: The Visuals in Dark Souls II is A-MAZING!!! I love standing in Majula and overseeing the sea. The work in other areas is also amazing I must say because it brings you into the game whereever you may be. Words cannot describe but if you are to buy this game, you will put your controller down and stare at the beautiful scenery before your eyes. There are even mods that will enable you to have a gloomy and dark atmosphere like the original Dark Souls game. I know Durante is making a mod to work with countless games (still in Alpha) but it works wonders on the game. I have not tested it yet because if you are to modify or change, specifically, Dark Souls II's files in anyways you will be banned by VAC. I advise you to keep back for a while if you want to mod your game until From Software deals with this problem.
NEUTRAL: Covenanats (or online multiplayer) are awesome to be in now rather than Dark Souls (it was good but not as frequent when it came to invasions,) but the only covenants I would recommend are Bell Keepers, the Ratz, and Praise the Sun! (The rest are pretty much boring to say the least: the Blue Sentinals and Blood Brothers are useless!!!! The Blood Brothers have a minimal chance to invade since they do not have an unlimited supply of cracked red eyed orbs like the previous Soul games; thus, leaving the Blue Sentinals nothing to do. The only task they have is to grab a stick and draw circles on the ground.)
NEUTRAL: The Music is beyond clarity compared to the other Soul games. It brings out areas with melancholy and forboding environments that leave either you scared for your life or pleasantly happy to be in that specific area. It does not compare to the other previous games but still Dark Souls II has great music to listen to. (The last song at the ending is a pleasure to listen to!)
NEGATIVE: The Lore and Characters are terrible compared to Demon's Souls and Dark Souls. The previous Soul games have boundless backstories to each and every character you meet that makes you feel sadness, despair, grief, and empathy. You want to help them like any person would but nothing will help them, no matter how much you want to. (Maiden Astrea--*tear*.) Every character you meet "tragically" has a heart-wrenching ending that will stick to your mind forever leaving you hopeless. (Artorias, do I need say more?!) As for Dark Souls II, the characters are not memorable in anyway. Yes, you speak to them where they talk about their dark past but it does not even compare to the dark atmosphere of the previous games. Honestly, why take out the most vivid and memorable moments of the Dark Souls Franchise and make it in to a full-fledged difficult game (which is honestly not hard at all???)
NEGATIVE: The Bosses in Dark Souls II are, do I have to say, TERRIBLE!!!! If you are a veteran of Dark Souls and Demon's Souls you know what I am talking about. Almost every boss you meet is humanoid and has the same technique which is applied by easily moving around in a 360°. It tears my heart in how simple the bosses are. I do not know what the developers from From Software were thinking but the only thing that they implemented during this game was to make it as difficult as possible, and to do this is by pitting you against more than 2-3 more bosses or to include mini-units to make your life miserable. Basically a gang-bang of bosses and mini-units to pummel you. This is not difficult anymore. The only thing this game will train you to be is the most patient person ever! Also in the previous games, you have backstories to the enemy bosses (by reading their equipment or when you talk to NPC's.) As for Dark Souls II, we do not have that. Simply put, the monster or humanoid wants to kill you and that is it. One example I can say that actually uses Lore for one of the bosses is Sinner where he is one of the undead that started the first flames. Other than that from my current playthrough, that is the only information I have received out of the bosses.
Closing Statement:
I really do not have anything else to say, but if you are expecting a game that is better or up-to-par with Demon's Souls and Dark Souls, this is not the game. Even though I have played Demon's Souls and Dark Souls (countless hours) I must say, sadly, that this game lacks the essence of what made the Soul games a unique playing experience. I believe with the hype the original Dark Souls received with "prepare to die" of the "difficulty" made From Software focus on how difficult they can make this game. But in truth, they forgot the most valuable asset to their game: memorable characters and their mysterious lore.
SCORE---85

So, yeah, my eyes have finally stopped bleeding enough to write a review on this.  For those that have never heard of Geometry Wars, it started out as an in game freebie for PGR:2 on the Xbox.  It was addictive as h3ll back then, much simpler, bullet hell gem.  Its a twin stick command, one thumb moves and the other shoots in the direction of the sticks.  It had one goal, don't die.  Now it has time trial, original, maze, and drones that you level up (just to start).  The original would get so hectic and busy you could hear the xbox struggle with all the dots, waves and explosions, this one is much, much worse.  Now its 3d, so you get these little pills rotating, moving backgrounds, and everything bending and twisting.  I dont really have a lot to complain about, i have been a fan of the game since its inception and am glad i paid the 10 bucks for it.  But here it is:
The graphics are fracking amazing for a game less than 400 megs

So just finished my first playthrough of this game and thought I should do a review of my thoughts overall. Obviously the first thing to note is the optimisation issues. There are issues indeed and many people are having frame rate drops including myself, but these issues are not as serious for a fair amount of people. The developers have stated they are working on a patch, so maybe hold off on getting the game for the next few days while we wait for these issues to hopefully get fixed.
Now onto my thoughts of the game, and I have to say, I love this game! Never was very interested in Dishonored, but thought I would get Dishonored 2 since pre-ordering also gave me the first game to try. Dishonored 2 has an amazing story which can branch different ways and give different endings depending upon which character you choose and how you approach each situation during the game. Having two different characters that do play fairly differently is a great aspect of this game too. There are many different weapons and abilities which you can use and upgrade to better your experiance through the game, all with different purposes. I especially enjoyed using the rat ability to consume my enemies. The game has a nice atmosphere and a lot to do. You can search for runes, bonecharms, materials to craft bonecharms and eaven recipes to upgrade your weaponry. I hardly scratched the surface of content within this game and plan to playthrough the game again.
Overall, I say do not be fooled my the mixed reviews. The game has some optimisation issues, but if you are willing to look past them and wait for the developers to (hopefully) fix them, you can see an amazing game that could be Game of the Year material.

I'm usually quite the fan of the zombie survivor MMO genre, but this game would definitely fall into the categories of shotty, cheap and downright horrendous. With a lackluster world with even more lackluster mechanics, it seems
is just riding on the popularity of the genre. Don't get me wrong though, I'm grateful that this is a free game (as everyone else should be), and am only saying these things in the hope that the issues will be resolved. <3
My first time playing this game was... not very enjoyable. Besides being dumped out in the middle of nowhere (every... single... time...), I found it extremely difficult to find food or water, and therefore only had around 30 minutes (being generous here) of gameplay (i.e. aimlessly wandering) or so before I would die. Any food or water I did find usually came with some terrible drawback (i.e. dirty water = disentery). Not to mention it was a lot harder to replenish your hydration, as water was three times harder to find than food when looting (I never actually found any clean water).
Looting was also a nightmare as the majority of the items I found were components for crafting, which took up a lot of room in my pitiful inventory space. Better still, you needed blueprints to craft something as simple as a campfire... a campfire for Pete's sake. And these said blueprints are pretty hard to find at times if you don't know where to look. Though I know you can find better bags, it's either a hit-or-miss in finding them. Not to mention that if you died and had to find your better bag again, you have to empty it all before you can re-equip it, which is silly and risky. If there was an easier way, it wasn't very clear.
In terms of game mechanics, I had no idea what I was doing. There are no instructions, and everything just seems piled together in a awkward mass. I'm not even going to start on how bad the zombies' AI is. Good luck trying to fight those things if you're lagging... It's absolutely impossible with melee weapons. Oh, and don't expect to use firearms; there are many around, but they rarely, if ever, come with ammo or any useable ammo nearby (again, never found any lone ammunition either). But on the other end of the spectrum, you can sneak around the zombies with terrible ease. I could loot a whole gas station (finding nothing useful of course) without being detected.
In my honest opinion, I seriously wouldn't waste my time playing this game. It has insipid terrain, a needlessly complex crafting system, and you can't even drink water from a well or river when you're seriously dehydrated. I would even prefer Unturned over this; at least guns with ammo aren't as rare hen's teeth in that game. Better yet, unless you look on the forums, you're not going to have a good time trying to set up groups with other players.
Overall, I give this game a 3/10 for its poor mechanics, dodgey gameplay, terrible terrain, half-baked AI,  overly complex crafting system and non-existant player guide.
You could argue that this game is trying to emulate what a real zombie apocalypse would be like, but with this game's many, many flaws, I doubt anyone would even think of such a point in the first place.

A good, solid hack 'n slash action game with a combat system that is as deep as you so choose.
You could go through the whole game using only the basic attacks or you could use the advanced combos to tear through enemies and boss with ease.
The difficulty gradually ramps up through the game, and while the common enemies will rarely give you much of a fight, it's the bosses that make this game shine. I heartily enjoyed virtually every boss fight. The puzzles weren't terribly hard but a nice diversion to keep things from being stale. Platforming elements were not too frustrating, barring one or two areas.
It took me about 30 hours to finish on Knight (Hard) difficulty, which unlocks the Paladin (Very Hard) difficulty. At this time, I haven't played through on that difficulty yet, but in regards to replayability, there is a decent amount. To get 100% in this game, after you beat it you'll need to beat every level over again on the max difficulty and there is a trial that is unlocked after every level is finished that you will need to complete.
At the time of this review the price for this game is $29.99, and I would recommend it at that price, and doubly so if you find it on sale which seems to occur fairly often.

Loved the game. Leisurely completing the game and DLC with 44 hours. Amazing visuals, amazing story, and great soundtrack. It's what every 3D Castlevania wished it could have been.
It took some time getting hooked into the story though, because they let on very little in the beginning of the game, and slowly stream it in over time. By the time I got to the castle (5-7h?), you couldn't pry me away from the game. By the end of the game you are begging for more story and insight into the characters. Beating the game on 'normal' was difficult in boss battles with a couple of deaths (outside of DLC boss, died for hours), but just right during normal gameplay, never really dying but definitely had moments where you really needed to be aware of your health, your enemy types, and strategize your moves around that. The game felt like it was built primarily for the controller, I used both and keyboard/mouse was a joke. Playing on hard was difficult to the point of being extremely frustrating, you could die with any encounter of a 'heavy' opponent, and good luck on boss battles, I should probably mention that I was also using keyboard/mouse during this test.
After playing both this game and its sequel, I'm just sad that there isn't more.

Updating this due to new developments:
Dark Souls II is one of the most enjoyable gaming experiences I have ever had. I loved its unique system of chaotic multiplayer, wherin a seemingly random selection of fellow players are drawn into your world to help or hinder you. I loved its difficulty, which was brutally hard but (almost) never unfair. I loved its brilliantly subtle approach to the lore, where things are hinted at and implied but never outright said.
So, it pains me to say that buying this game on steam right now is the worst possible thing you can do with your money.
The game's devs, FROM, decided that they are going to re-release the game next year, complete with all of the DLC thrown in, and with a number of really cool new features which aren't accessible anywhere else. That sounds nice. It WOULD be nice. Were it not for the fact that the game is not even a year old yet, and that we have already paid $80 for the sundry DLC packs to enjoy the full experience as it were. Now they are releasing a few new features (which we cannot purchase seperately) just after we commited ourselves to this game and dropped our money on it.
This was a truly dissapointing move by the developers, and shows a real lack of fiber. This move was a hollow grab for money, and constitutes a betrayal of the game's loyal fans. When it is re-released, I hope you enjoy it. If you don't want to waste your money and support a very underhanded practice on the dev's part, I don't blame you in the slightest.

So just finished my first playthrough of this game and thought I should do a review of my thoughts overall. Obviously the first thing to note is the optimisation issues. Dishonored 2 has an amazing story which can branch different ways and give different endings depending upon which character you choose and how you approach each situation during the game. Having two different characters that do play fairly differently is a great aspect of this game too. There are many different weapons and abilities which you can use and upgrade to better your experiance through the game, all with different purposes. I especially enjoyed using the rat ability to consume my enemies. The game has a nice atmosphere and a lot to do. You can search for runes, bonecharms, materials to craft bonecharms and eaven recipes to upgrade your weaponry. I hardly scratched the surface of content within this game and plan to playthrough the game again.
Overall, I say do not be fooled my the mixed reviews. The game has some optimisation issues, but if you are willing to look past them and wait for the developers to (hopefully) fix them, you can see an amazing game that could be Game of the Year material.

Nine hours in playing as Emily and really enjoying Dishonored 2. Gameplay is extremely solid with just the right amount of difficulty. The addition of Emily as a playable character was a great way to expand gameplay without breaking from the formula that made the first game great. Arkane has designed the game in a way that greatly awards pre-planning as opposed to rushing in and winging it (although both ways are just as fun and sometimes necessary). Not knowing what is around the next corner really pushes players to stop and think about their next move as enemies are numerous, and players can be easily spotted and overrun if not careful. As far as the story goes, it is for the most part very engaging and worthwhile investing in, however Arkane has only just glanced over important details that link the first game to the second, as well as quickly rushing players through Emily recieivng her powers, leaving the player asking why one minute she goes from a well trained Empress, to a magically powered assassin for seemlingly no reason other than to add a second playable character that is similar enough to Corvo that the game doesn't lose any of its core mechanics. This unnecessary mystery does get explained a bit better overtime, but it should have happened much earlier in the game, and much clearer and more complete. I will say that much of this could be considered unnecessary detail to newcomes to the series, but as a lover of the first game I wish Arkane would have taken the time to scratch the story itch.
I have seen numerous players complaning of technical issues with the game, however I have personally experienced none of this. The game looks great, and frame rate is solid. I am playing on a farily high end system so I can't comment as to the issues that lower end to mid range PCs are having, but I can confirm that at least on my GTX 1080 and 6600k that the game is running perfectly. I have had a couple somewhat silly glitches such as Emily getting stuck floating in the air and able to fire down on the heads of enimies without being noticed, but I have had nothing gamebreaking or frustrating and intrusive to gameplay.
I definitely recommend Dishonored 2 to anyone new to the franchise, as well as anyone who played Dishonored 1. It may be worth it to wait a week or two (from today 11/11/16) for players running on low to medium tier PCs due to technical issues experienced by players on similarly powered systems, but I have no doubt that Arkane will patch these issues very quickly. A solid 8.5/10 for a game that had very big shoes to fill.

How does one explain without seeming a madman how dragging a flated stacked with other flatbeds from Linz to Salzburg can so narcotize the human mind?
How does one articulate the compulsion to traverse the same length of autobahn, east to west, west to east, east to west...  until it is suddenly Monday? Would you beleive me if I said its like the craps pit at Bellagio? Probably not.
So here are some fun bullets:
- Beautifully rendered, exquisitelty compressed , tourable abstraction of Central Europe.
- A ton of diverse equipment to drive, all meticulously simulated so you can taste every subtle difference: believe me when I say you will gladly bleed for every  upgrade to your rig , and you WILL care about the difference between raw horsepower and tractive effort ( in Kw of course )  .
-  Comulsively engaging but accessible small business simulator. Your skin is in the game, so get out there and make some $$$$!
- Beefy, affordable DLC's that literally add entire countries to your experience: this is NOT death by a thousand half-a$$ed cuts like another logistics sim I might mention.
My effort here is fruitless. Just look at the other reviews and buy this thing already.

Dark Souls II is one of the most enjoyable gaming experiences I have ever had. I loved its unique system of chaotic multiplayer, wherin a seemingly random selection of fellow players are drawn into your world to help or hinder you. I loved its difficulty, which was brutally hard but (almost) never unfair. I loved its brilliantly subtle approach to the lore, where things are hinted at and implied but never outright said.
So, it pains me to say that buying this game on steam right now is the worst possible thing you can do with your money.
The game's devs, FROM, decided that they are going to re-release the game next year, complete with all of the DLC thrown in, and with a number of really cool new features which aren't accessible anywhere else. That sounds nice. It WOULD be nice. Were it not for the fact that the game is not even a year old yet, and that we have already paid $80 for the sundry DLC packs to enjoy the full experience as it were. Now they are releasing a few new features (which we cannot purchase seperately) just after we commited ourselves to this game and dropped our money on it.
This was a truly dissapointing move by the developers, and shows a real lack of fiber. This move was a hollow grab for money, and constitutes a betrayal of the game's loyal fans. When it is re-released, I hope you enjoy it. If you don't want to waste your money and support a very underhanded practice on the dev's part, I don't blame you in the slightest.

I'm quite pleased with the outcome of a game that I heard mixed reviews of prior to its release. I was a big fan of the original GW and even played a ton of it when it premiered as an easter egg in Project Gotham Racing. I didn't play the subsequent sequels (I think GW2 and another one?), so my experience with the new mechanics in this is about as fresh as can be.
I like the variety and challenge of the main campaign mode: 50 levels of increasing difficulty, each with their own theme. The introduction of a little helper that can shoot extra bullets or help collect geoms is a welcome addition, as well as the new types of bombs available. I feel like the boss fights are well done and interesting as far as trying to get multiple stars on for unlocking later levels. Revisiting them with new power ups makes for a different experience as well. Some levels that can seem overwhelming at first make a lot more sense when you approach them with new or upgraded gear.
The other two campaign modes are also fun in their own right. Ultimate mode introduces a lot of new enemies and types of arenas to play in, as well as some interesting new game modes. Hardcore mode doesn't allow for the use of an alternate super or a helper; just you, bombs and super-states. Both new campaigns feel just right in their length and don't overstay their welcome with repeated or uninteresting game modes.
The re-introduction of evolved classic with the Evolved update is a welcome sight. No geoms to worry about and mostly classic enemies make for a simplified, albeit lower scoring experience. The old strategy of black hole management still works too!
There are local co-op modes available, which is a welcome sight to see for PC games. Even if co-op and the 'story' modes (there isn't really a story, just numbered levels, which is fine for this game) modes aren't your jam, there are still 5 different modes you can play in an arcade-style fashion to beat your friends scores at.
Like any game that has online leaderboards, the global top spots are sometimes riddled with hackers, so it's best to just compare how you do against your friends. I don't think the new campaigns have been hit by people hacking their scores into impossibly high numbers yet, so those might be more worthwhile to try to get a top 10 world record score.
All in all, a fantastic game, even at full price.

In this review I'm focusing on comparing this game between Geometry Wars 2 so this review for you - like me - had tons of fun with the second one and are trying to figure out if this one is worth a buy.
Why not compare to the first one? Because the second one was for me a direct follow up, improving the first one and not so many added features. This one should be approached as something completely different - mostly...
Geometry Wars 3: Dimension introduces "dimensions", which is not as fun as it sounds. Instead of shooting these ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ flying alien geometry-forms in a fenced rectangular area, you are doing the same but on 3D objects (/maps), sometimes a wavy format of the "original" rectangular map.
Don't get me wrong here, the concept is good, but in practice this get annoying to say the least. Problems like visability is encountered constantly on many, if not all maps. MAINLY because the map must always be just big enough so it can fit your screen, which often leaves out 40% of the screen for a wallpaper. And i get that if you don't have the "shape" of the map visible there would be problem to navigate. A fix to this could be to scale down everything on the map, but no, they have not even considered scaling anything down, maybe because of the PC-release with smaller monitors.
Except from this the theme of "dimension" is within every inch of your screen from the moment you start the game which unfortunatly came in the way of the beautiful background on the second game and replaced it with a moving grid which is just one annoying thing that draws your attention away from the basic gameplay.
You are (on every map i think) in this kind of pit or hole in the ground which is meant to reflect your impact on the surface of the map. I can go on for hours about these small details of theme-ruinment, but im not going to.
Instead your getting a list of + and -
-The theme of the game penetrates and destroys even basic gameplay
-Map layouts are mostly just a pain in the ***
-Music is more unseemly
-Spawn of enemies is more than ever overlooked and difficult to handle
+Music is still good
+You have and option for "classic" gameplay on original maps
+Online is an awesome feature
+Local still kicks a**
Conclusion
Is it better or worse? It's different
Is it worth a buy if you liked the first and second one? Yes

Top truck driving simulator. With support for TrackIR, wheels and pedals, this game has become a gem of the simulation genre.
Before having tried it, it's hard to see why this game will be so addicting. I suspect much of that feeling comes from the progression from a lowly truck driver not even owning a truck to a multi-country Logistics company owning a hundred trucks and employing as many drivers.
You "level up" various skills which improve the rewards you get from certain types of deliveries or open up more jobs such as longer distances or different categories of dangerous cargo.
Driving the trucks is a pleasure. It's surprisingly therapeutic driving from city to city, obeying the road rules rather than smashing things up like a madman. That said, if you disable the speed-limiter in options (90kph) you can get a bit crazy, getting as high as 150kph+ on some routes, a bit of a thrill considering the cargo you have in tow! Speed cameras will become your enemy though.
Unfortunately the AI of the other traffic can at times frustrate. In some instances such as in underpasses under freeways you can find intersections where the cars always fail to give way, probably because the intersection was not programmed correctly.
In any case, this is the most fun you can have driving a truck in a game. Having a controller or steering wheel would be highly recommended, and if you have head-tracking equipment it's icing on the cake.
